notes: 2026-09-24 ~16:30 director: CAUSE FOUND, not a game bug. title: Play pass 4 — answer the Phase 2 exit question
description:
The Phase 2 exit question is: is spending a hero's life a decision you actually feel? Unanswered after three play passes. This is not a code ticket — it is someone sitting down and playing the built game.

docs/TASKS.md has been saying this is the real next move for three sessions. The user's own sequencing was models first, then play; the models (P2b-09/P2b-10) have landed.

What a pass must cover, because no pass has ever met them: training, traits, buildings, gear recovery, and everything the fe1a74b arena/hub batch added. The 22 PROVISIONAL arena feel values have been played once as a whole (verdict: 'feels good for what it is') but never felt individually.

If the answer is no, the fix is design, not code.

Reference: docs/TASKS.md 'Phase 2 exit question' section, and the superseded handoff comment above it.
close_reason: Played. Answer: yes, spending a hero's life is a felt decision. Remaining gap is animation/combat feel, which is clunky; the two P1 feel tickets are now unblocked.

title: Caster presence: a role-aware measure and a winnable second point (SYSTEMS § Casters)
description:
WHY
ig-vl1.3's presence test found no stat offset that passes (the mixed team with the Mage slot swapped; seeds 1-8, medians, P6; logs in .agent-results/ig-vl1.3/). It judges the Mage on clear time and the Cleric on team HP, each against Knights, and Knights tank:
- The F Mage at offset 0 already clears faster than a C Knight (263.6 s vs 272.6), and faster still at every offset. But its team ends with less HP (1424 vs the D Knight's 2133.5). It passes D only from about 1.75.
- The F Cleric fits D..C on team HP only at offset 0 (2359.6). On clear time it is slower than a D Knight at every offset up to 2.5.
- Point 2 (C30 at Sundered) is 0/8 wins in every slot: a C30 mixed team has about 27% of Sundered's RP.
So vl1.3 ships the offset at 0 (director ruling 2026-09-25).

WHAT (design: game-designer)
1. A measure of presence that doesn't put unlike roles on one axis. For example: both axes for every slot, a composite, or a Knight-rank equivalent per axis. Say what "a caster at R lands between a Knight at R+1 and R+2" means on it.
2. A second point the mixed team wins (a rank, level and zone), so higher ranks get measured too.
3. Rewrite SYSTEMS § Casters' presence test, and ig-vl1.4's ACC 5, to use it. The engine lane builds it into tests/balance/presence_check.gd as part of vl1.4.
4. Say when the offset gets set: after the spells (vl1.4 zones, vl1.5 walls) change presence.

NOT
No tuning here. No engine runs.
notes:
DESIGN DRAFT (extra as game-designer, 2026-09-25). No engine runs. SYSTEMS untouched until vl1.3 lands; the text to paste is in part 7.

1. THE MEASURE: presence = the hardest fight the team still wins (its "break").
- Same team as before: the balance gate's mixed team (Knight, Ranger, [slot], Rogue, Knight), everyone else at the point's rank and level, bare supplies, seeds 1-8.
- Scale the zone's enemy power by m. Every enemy's HP, ATK and DEF scale with its budget (battle_simulation.gd:929-944, via Wave.from_zone -> zone.recommended_power). The roster and the enemy count stay the zone's own.
- For each seed, find the largest m the team still wins (outcome.status == "victory"; anything else is a loss). The slot's break = the median over the 8 seeds.
- Why it fixes vl1.3's problem: one axis for every role. Damage wins it by killing before the team runs out, tanking and healing by lasting, and zones and walls by both. It's also what a player means by presence: with this hero in, can the team take a harder fight?
- A crude guess says survival binds before the clock. At F1 Verdant with the D Knight in the slot, the team ends at m=1 with 2,133 of its 4,368 HP (hero HP x pace, battle_simulation.gd:988), so it loses about half. With the Mage in the slot it loses 61% (1,424 of 3,636 left). Damage taken grows about m^2, but clear time only about m. So the team runs out of HP near m 1.3-1.4, well before the clock (298 s x 1.4 = 417 s, against a 1080 s cap). The break is not a clear-time race in disguise. The run checks this (part 4).

2. WHAT "LANDS BETWEEN R+1 AND R+2" MEANS
- A caster at rank R passes at a point when break(Knight R+1 in the slot) <= break(caster) <= break(Knight R+2).
- The readout, so tuning knows how far off it is: the Knight-rank equivalent E = R+1 + ln(b_caster / b_R+1) / ln(b_R+2 / b_R+1). Pass = E in [R+1, R+2]. Printed as +1.4 etc.; extrapolation outside the band is fine as a readout.
- Noise: if b_R+2 / b_R+1 is under two search steps (1.044), that point can't resolve the band: print UNRESOLVED and re-run it on seeds 1-16. A crude guess for the gap is ~7% (one slot of five at x1.35).

3. THE POINTS
- Point 1 kept: F level 1 at Verdant (Knights at D and C). The team is 784 power against RP 900 (87%).
- Point 2: B level 30 at Ashfall Reaches (Knights at A and S; level 30 is under both caps). The team is 4,205 against RP 4,800 (88%), so both points start from the same margin. It replaces C30 at Sundered (3,111 against 11,500, 27%: 0/8 in every slot).
  (Power is compute_team_power with the Mage in the slot at offset 0.)
- The break doesn't need a win at m = 1, but matching margins keeps the enemies at comparable real strength at both points.

4. THE HARNESS (vl1.4 builds this into tests/balance/presence_check.gd; small)
- The scaled fight: hard = zone.duplicate(); hard.recommended_power = roundi(zone.recommended_power * m); create_run with hard. Nothing reloads mid-run, so the copy is safe. No game code changes.
- Per seed: a geometric bisection over [0.5, 2.0]. Widen x2 if it wins at 2.0 (up to 8), or /2 if it loses at 0.5 (down to 0.125). 6 halvings put the break within +-1.1%. Each seed's break = sqrt(lo * hi). About 8 fights per seed, so 64 per slot, 256 per point, 512 per offset. The Knight slots don't depend on the offset, so each extra offset costs 256.
- Lines: BREAK point= slot= offset= m=<median> seeds=[8 values] losses={defeat:n,timeout:n} wall_s=; then EQUIV point= offset= mage=+x cleric=+y gap=z% (UNRESOLVED if the gap is under 4.4%); then PICK offset= (part 5).
- Keep today's ROW line at m = 1 (seconds, hp, wins) as INFO: it's the caster's role profile, not judged.
- A TIMEOUT flag when most of a slot's losing fights are timeouts: then the break has turned into a clear-time race, and that's a finding for design.

5. SETTING THE OFFSET
- PICK = the smallest caster_rank_offset >= 0 where both casters pass at both points. Run offset 0 first; E says how far off each caster is, so sweep only near that (--offsets= exists).
- Never below 0. A caster above R+2 at offset 0 has a spell that's too strong: the spell numbers get cut, not the row.
- One row for both casters. If no single offset fits both, the caster that misses gets its spell numbers tuned (Rime Circle / Hearthward are per-class). Don't add a second row: class identity lives in the spells.
- DIRECTOR'S CALL, when:
  (a) Set the offset after zones (vl1.4) from the zones run, and re-set it after walls (vl1.5). MY PICK. Walls wait on pathfinding (ig-0qh), so otherwise casters stay at plain stats for that whole gap. The owner asked for strong casters.
  (b) Only after walls (vl1.5). One tuning pass, but casters have no edge until then.

6. THE RUN I WANT (vl1.4's first step, once the harness has the break; before any zone code)
One run at offset 0 on HEAD after vl1.3 lands, both points, all 4 slots. It answers:
- the pre-spell presence: the baseline zones and walls get measured against;
- whether the R+1..R+2 gap resolves (over 4.4%) at both points;
- whether the losses are defeats, not timeouts;
- the wall time (sets how wide an offset sweep can be).
If point 2's gap is UNRESOLVED or TIMEOUT fires, it comes back to me before zones.

7. SYSTEMS TEXT (replaces § Casters "Presence, as the sim measures it" and its 4 bullets; paste after vl1.3 lands)
**Presence, as the sim measures it** (`ig-vl1.6`). Presence is the hardest fight the team still
wins. `ig-vl1.3`'s test judged a Mage on clear time and a Cleric on team HP, each against a Knight,
which tanks; it passed no offset.
- Take the balance gate's mixed team (Knight, Ranger, Mage, Rogue, Knight) and fill the Mage slot.
  Everyone else is at the point's rank and level. Bare supplies, seeds 1-8.
- Scale the zone's enemy power by m: every enemy's HP, ATK and DEF, with the zone's own roster and
  count. For each seed, find the largest m the team still wins, to within about 1%. The slot's
  **break** is the median of the eight.
- A caster at rank R passes when its break lands between a Knight at R+1's in the slot and a Knight
  at R+2's. Its Knight-rank equivalent, R+1 + ln(break / break at R+1) / ln(break at R+2 / break at
  R+1), says how far off it is.
- Two points: F level 1 at Verdant (Knights at D and C) and B level 30 at Ashfall Reaches (Knights
  at A and S). Both teams start at about 87% of the zone's recommended power.
- Clear time and team HP at m = 1 are still printed. They show the caster's role and aren't judged.
- Measured at `battle_pace` 6 with the Knight's full kit.
> ⚠️ **PROVISIONAL** — the second point and the search range are arithmetic · **Settled by:** the
> first run at offset 0: the R+1 to R+2 gap resolves at both points, and the losses are defeats,
> not timeouts
Also the "Then the stats get set" bullet gains part 5's rules: the smallest offset >= 0 where both casters pass at both points; a caster above R+2 at 0 gets its spell cut; if no single offset fits both, the spell of the one that misses is tuned. Plus the director's (a)/(b) timing.

8. vl1.4 ACC 5 (replaces "The presence test at P = 6 ... then the caster_rank_offset cut, re-run, recorded")
5. presence_check.gd measures the break (SYSTEMS § Casters, ig-vl1.6). Run it at offset 0 before zones (the baseline; part 6's checks) and again with zones in. Record both in SYSTEMS. [If (a): then PICK the offset from the zones run, re-run at it, and record. If (b): the offset stays 0.]

9. REJECTED
- Per-axis Knight-rank equivalents, averaged: the weights are arbitrary, and the Mage's clear time is off the top of the Knight's curve at F (it beats C), so it's all extrapolation.
- A composite such as clear time x HP: the units don't mix, and the weights are a guess.
- The Mage against a Ranger: the owner named the Knight, and the Cleric has no match.
- Scaling the enemy count instead of stats: it would inflate a zone's area value against the real rosters.
Director ruling 2026-09-25 ~10:05: extra's draft ACCEPTED, with (a) and one reorder.
- Checked in code: enemy HP, ATK and DEF are each linear in the budget (battle_simulation.gd:940-944; the budget comes from Wave.from_zone, wave.gd:22). Hero HP x pace (:988). RPs: Verdant 900, Ashfall 4800, Sundered 11500. Ranks F D C B A S; caps 10-60, so B30 with A and S Knights is legal. presence_check.gd already passes a ZoneDefinition to create_run, so a duplicate with a scaled RP works with no game code change.
- TIMING: (a). Set the offset from the zones run (vl1.4), re-set it after walls (vl1.5). The owner asked for strong casters, and walls wait on 0qh.
- REORDER: the harness and the baseline run (part 6) move out of vl1.4 into this bead. high1 does them right after vl1.3, before eek.1. Why: if the measure fails its own checks (UNRESOLVED or TIMEOUT), extra redesigns while high1 builds eek.1. And a Mage already above R+2 at offset 0 would change the zone numbers before any zone code is written.
- RUN ADDITIONS: next to each median, print the slot's seed min and max (I judge resolution on the spread too, not only the medians' ratio). Print each point's team power against its RP, to check 784/900 and 4,205/4,800.
- DOCS: after vl1.3 lands, extra pastes part 7, part 5's rules and (a) into SYSTEMS § Casters (uncommitted). When the run reports, extra adds the baseline numbers and updates the PROVISIONAL. It commits with high1's harness, by path.
- CLOSE when: the harness is in; the baseline passes part 6's checks at both points (the gap resolves, the losses are defeats); the SYSTEMS text is committed. If it fails, it goes back to extra before vl1.4.
STATUS (extra, 2026-09-25): STEP 2 pasted, uncommitted, LF, § Casters only (:1416-1576). Presence block = part 7 (+ seed min/max and team power vs RP printed; 784/900, 4,205/4,800) with its PROVISIONAL; 'Then the stats get set' = timing (a) + part 5's rules; parts list item 3 says set after zones, re-set after walls; the offset row's 'the presence test (below)' now says ig-vl1.3's. Also synced accepted 0qh/vl1.5 rules: corner graph rebuilt lazily after any fresh decode; instant moves = every push and move skill, cut at the choke points; basic melee only, area skills reach across; cast-on-actors pushes downed bodies, carried moves with carrier, AI skips a placement whose push leaves anyone inside another footprint. Waiting on high1's baseline numbers.
high1 2026-09-25 ~09:45 STATUS partial: harness in, baseline run done; TIMEOUT fires at B30_ashfall on all 4 slots (design finding). HOLD.
HARNESS (tests/balance/presence_check.gd, only file changed): points F1_verdant (Knights D,C) and B30_ashfall (Knights A,S); the scaled fight is zone.duplicate() with recommended_power = roundi(RP x m); per-seed geometric bisection over [0.5,2.0] (widen x2 to 8, halve to 0.125), 6 halvings, break = sqrt(lo*hi); slot = median of seeds 1-8. Lines INFO/BREAK/TIMEOUT/EQUIV/PICK; old FIT/PICK removed. Scale proof: INFO scale verdant enemy max_hp m1 621.0, m2 1242.0, ratio 2.000. Nothing re-reads the zone by id mid-run (only BattleState.from_dict does; the harness never serializes).
BASELINE offset 0 (.agent-results/ig-vl1.6/presence_baseline.log, wall ~25 min):
F1_verdant: knight_D m 1.559 [1.369..1.664] losses def17/to10; knight_C 1.700 [1.628..1.737] def14/to11; mage_F 1.477 [1.176..1.628] def23/to3; cleric_F 1.646 [1.526..1.854] def14/to7. EQUIV mage +0.38 cleric +1.63 gap 9.1% (resolved). Power vs RP: mage slot 784/900 87%.
B30_ashfall: knight_A 2.938 [2.875..3.002] def6/to31 TIMEOUT; knight_S 3.221 [3.068..3.274] def4/to24 TIMEOUT; mage_B 2.783 [2.723..2.970] def12/to16 TIMEOUT; cleric_B 2.970 [2.938..3.035] def0/to36 TIMEOUT. EQUIV mage +0.41 cleric +1.12 gap 9.6% (resolved). Power vs RP: mage slot 4205/4800 88%. All m=1 rows 8/8 wins.
PICK none. BUILT: gate 0/0, GUT 919/919, 67 scripts, 22391 asserts.
Director 2026-09-25 09:45 PDT: high1's baseline (.agent-results/ig-vl1.6/presence_baseline.log, offset 0, seeds 1-8, ~25 min wall) verified line by line. Harness diff reviewed: matches parts 4 and 6 (scale proof: enemy max_hp 621 -> 1242 at m2).
- F1 Verdant: Knight D 1.559 (1.369-1.664; 17 defeat / 10 timeout), Knight C 1.700 (1.628-1.737; 14/11), Mage F 1.477 (1.176-1.628; 23/3) = +0.38, Cleric F 1.646 (1.526-1.854; 14/7) = +1.63. Gap 9.1%. Power vs RP: 837, 909, 784, 774 of 900.
- B30 Ashfall: Knight A 2.938 (2.875-3.002; 6/31), Knight S 3.221 (3.068-3.274; 4/24), Mage B 2.783 (2.723-2.970; 12/16) = +0.41, Cleric B 2.970 (2.938-3.035; 0/36) = +1.12. Gap 9.6%. TIMEOUT on all 4 slots. Power vs RP: 4543, 4942, 4205, 4102 of 4800. The m=1 fights end at 170-210 s with 27-39k team HP left; the clock is 180 s x 6 = 1080 s.
- Reading: both gaps resolve (Ashfall's seed ranges don't overlap; Verdant's barely touch). At offset 0 the Mage sits below R+1 at both points; the Cleric sits inside the band at both. PICK none (expected at 0; the pick waits for zones).
- FINDING (design): at B30 the clock binds, not survival, so part 1's premise fails there. Back to extra for a ruling before vl1.4. vl1.6 stays open.
RULING (extra as game-designer, 2026-09-25) on the B30 clock finding: (b), keep the clock. SYSTEMS § Casters edited, uncommitted.
WHY (b):
- The break becomes "the hardest fight won under the game's own rules". A player at Ashfall also loses to the clock, so this is honest.
- (a) would measure a fight the game never has. B30 barely binds on survival, so the break would climb far past real content, and it needs a stalemate guard and longer runs.
- (c) chases a point that probably doesn't exist today. Survival pressure fades with rank everywhere (the finding below), so a survival-bound B-rank point would need a harder zone than the team can win.
- Two points with different binds is a feature: point 1 leans on survival, point 2 on kill speed, and a caster must pass both.
- If the enemy threat gets retuned (the finding below), point 2 follows the game with no measure change.
THE HEARTHWARD CHECK (the director's question): it doesn't break PICK, but it exposes one corner.
- Hearthward still counts at B30: a downed hero stops dealing damage. The Cleric's team had 0 wipes and its break beat the A Knight's (2.970 vs 2.938).
- It counts for less at B30 than at F1, so a Cleric's spell widens the gap between its two points. The offset and the spell's size both move the two points together, so a caster more than a rank apart can't be fit by either. New rule in part 5: that goes to design as a change to what the spell does, not its size.
- At offset 0 the Mage's points are 0.03 apart, the Cleric's 0.51.
SYSTEMS CHANGES:
- The premise: "the clock included". A new bullet explains how losses split and why the two points differ (TIMEOUT is INFO).
- A baseline table with every number, the power lines and wall time.
- The m=1 HP bite at each point, with its cause.
- The PROVISIONAL rewritten. Settled by: the zones run keeping each caster's points within a rank, and the ruling on the finding below.
- Part 5 gains the spread rule and the Hearthward note.

FINDING (design, for gy0.9 or its own bead; not this bead): a matched fight bites far less at higher ranks.
- At m=1 a team ends F1 Verdant with 39-61% of its HP (seeds' medians: 2,133 of 4,367; 2,550 of 4,802; 1,424 of 3,636; 2,360 of 3,840). It ends B30 Ashfall with 87-92% (34,077 of 38,092; 38,777 of 41,990; 26,877 of 30,775; 30,074 of 32,989). Both points sit at 85-103% of the zone's RP.
- Cause: damage = ATK x 100 / (100 + DEF) (battle_simulation.gd:1961, battle_damage_defense_scale 100). From F1 to B30 a hero's HP and DEF grow about x7-9 (level growth x rank multiplier), but enemy ATK grows only with the RP (x5.3, Verdant to Ashfall; battle_enemy_atk_budget_multiplier 0.03). A B30 Knight's DEF of 236 cuts each hit to 30%; an F1 Knight's 26 cuts it to 79%.
- Why it matters:
  - permadeath: matched fights rarely down anyone from mid ranks on (KNOWN_ISSUES asks whether spending a life feels like something);
  - Knights and Clerics lose value as ranks rise, because the fight becomes a damage race;
  - the Early fixture's 18 battles were all victories with no moment.
- Not settled here: whether that's the intended curve (easier as you grow) or a gap. It needs the owner's feel and gy0.9's pace work. Levers: enemy ATK budget per zone, or DEF's scale. It's a balance change the director would call big.
DIRECTOR 09:55 PDT: extra's ruling (b) accepted. Its numbers match presence_baseline.log, and I re-derived the m=1 HP bite from the hero defs (same result). SYSTEMS committed as 50b4123. I made one wording fix: the doc now names the TIMEOUT line, and says both it and the wipes/timeouts counts are INFO.
THE CLOSE CONDITION CHANGED with the ruling. "The losses are defeats, not timeouts" is dropped: the clock is part of the game's rules. What stands: the harness is in (8564dac), both gaps resolve (9.1%, 9.6%), and the text is committed (50b4123).
The bite finding is filed as ig-ixh (waiting on the owner's call). vl1.4 is unblocked.
close_reason: Harness in (8564dac); both gaps resolve (9.1%, 9.6%); § Casters committed (50b4123). The close condition was changed by extra's ruling (b): the clock is part of the game's rules, so timeouts are INFO. The bite finding is filed as ig-ixh.

title: Economy: no brake and no target rate: teams, stones and pulls snowball past hour 3 (Early pulls 18 an hour)
description:
WHY
Found by extra (game-designer), 2026-09-25, from ig-eek's first Early run (seed 1, tests/fixtures/stages/early/run.log and ledger.jsonl, 700aef0).
- The bot pulled 36 times in 2 h of game clock, about 18 an hour. That is exactly today's rules: 300 starting stones + 16 Verdant victories x 150 + 2 Ashfall victories x 450 = 3,600 stones = 36 pulls, 0 left. Stone rewards are the P2-09 numbers x battle_pace (game_session.gd:2476).
- So nothing is broken. But nobody ever set a target. P2-09 priced pulls in clears and said hours can't be settled without a played build (SYSTEMS § Summon Stones, "What this does not settle"). ig-1jw kept earnings per hour. The bot is the first measure.
- It's well above the picture the rest of SYSTEMS assumes. § Stage saves guessed 5-10 heroes at 2 h and "the best team mostly C-B" at 20 h. The run's best heroes are A and B at level 30-33 after 2 h (23 fodder, 4 rank-ups).
- The rate rises with the zone: an Ashfall clear pays 3x Verdant, Sundered 8x. At Early's rate alone, the ~327-pull spine to a manufactured SSS is about 18 h of play. P2-09 called that spine "a reasonable long-horizon grind".

WHAT (design first: numbers are game-designer's; the feel is the owner's)
1. Set a target: pulls per game hour at Early, Mid and Late, and the level/rank a best team should reach by 2 h and 20 h. Ask the owner how fast a new hero should arrive.
2. If today's rate is off, pick the lever: stone_reward, summon_pull_cost, the x P on rewards, or XP. Record it in SYSTEMS § Summon Stones.
3. Knock-ons to check:
   - § Stage saves' checks (Early's were re-set from this run under ig-eek.3/.4/.5);
   - the Ledger. Summoned (tier 4) and died (tier 5) records were 59 of Early's 81, and they evict last. At this pull rate they fill a capped Ledger. 2.4's and ig-m6o.2.2.10's volume estimate (12 meetings, 8 meals, 10 battles an hour) counted none;
   - permadeath weight: a pull every ~3 minutes makes each hero cheap (KNOWN_ISSUES' open question on whether spending a life feels like something).

DATA (seed 1)
- 18 battles, all victories, none with a moment (all routine): the A pulled on summon 2 made Verdant a stomp.
- The pulled ranks were F 19, D 9, C 4, B 3, A 1.

NOT
No tuning inside ig-eek.3/.4/.5. No balance change until the target is set. A change here is "a balance change the director calls big" for the stage saves.
notes:
SNOWBALL (director 10:16 PDT). Found by high1's ig-eek.1 Mid run: seed 1, step 5 s. Log: .agent-results/ig-eek.1/mid_snowball_run.log.

The run, hour by hour:
- HOUR 1: wall 3.8 s, roster 8, orders 1, ledger 59.
- HOUR 2: wall 15.0 s, roster 23, orders 4, ledger 159 (Ashfall cleared).
- HOUR 3: wall 38.4 s, roster 28, orders 5, ledger 338.
- HOUR 4: wall 123.2 s, roster 78, orders 15, ledger 729. Stopped there.

CAUSE
- Nothing caps the roster or the orders. I checked: game_session.gd has only the per-mission hero_cap and squad_cap.
- The bot plays like a greedy but legal player: every 5 idle heroes make a team (stage_play.gd _form_teams).
- More teams bring more stones, more stones bring more pulls, and more pulls bring more teams.
- Each game hour costs about 3x the last in wall time.

It breaks Mid's checks by hour 4:
- 78 heroes (Mid wants 15-30 at 20 h);
- 15 teams (Mid wants 2-4);
- ledger 729 (Mid wants about 1,000 at 20 h).

THE QUESTION IS NOW TWO: a target rate (how many pulls an hour) AND a brake (what stops the growth). Early (2 h) doesn't show the snowball; it starts around hour 3. SYSTEMS says the bot is never changed to meet a check, so the brake has to be a game rule.

NEXT
1. extra drafts 2-4 brake options on paper. Each one comes with numbers and its effect on Early's numbers and Mid's targets. extra says which one it would pick.
2. The owner picks the brake, together with the rate.
3. ig-eek.1 depends on this bead. Raised to P1.
STATUS (extra as game-designer, 2026-09-25, on a53b7eb): the loop is mapped, four brakes are drafted with numbers, and I have a pick. Paper only: no engine runs, no doc edits. Model: scratchpad econ_model.py (a desk model, calibrated to Early seed 1; numbers are orders of magnitude).

1. THE LOOP, IN CODE
- Pay: stones_earned = zone.stone_reward x pace (game_session.gd:2476), for a victory only. Pace 6, so a clear pays Verdant 150, Ashfall 450, Sundered 1,200, Citadel 1,350, Frontier 2,250.
- Time: a battle order's route runs while it fights, and it's due when both end. Route = max(min x P, base x P / sqrt(r)) x ref/size (expedition_orders.gd:34-51), r = team power / zone power. For a 5-hero team: Verdant max(90, 360/sqrt r) s, Ashfall max(270, 1080/sqrt r), Sundered max(450, 1800/sqrt r).
- So one 5-hero team earns, per game hour:
  | Zone | r = 1 | r = 4 | at the floor (r >= 16) |
  | Verdant | 1,500 | 3,000 | 6,000 |
  | Ashfall | 1,500 | 3,000 | 6,000 |
  | Sundered | 2,400 | 4,800 | 9,600 |
  Citadel pays 1,350/h for 30 heroes and Frontier 1,500/h for 50: a sixth of a small zone per hero, so they aren't the snowball.
  Early seed 1 measured about 1,750 a team-hour (3,300 stones from ~1.1 teams in 2 h).
- Cost: a pull is 100 stones, flat (balance.tres summon_pull_cost). The start is 300.
- Payback: a hero in a team earns 300-600 stones an hour, so it pays back its own pull in 10-20 minutes. That's the snowball: team count x income per team, and both grow with pulls.
- A second, smaller loop: fodder -> rank -> r -> shorter routes, up to 4x per team (the floor at r = 16).
- LIMITS TODAY (none caps the count):
  - hero_cap (5/5/5/30/50) and the squad cap: size per mission only.
  - No slot cap, by design: SYSTEMS § Timed dispatch (:3857-3858, "without an energy system or dispatch-slot cap"). DECISIONS 2026-09-22 (:1051-1052) rejected "fixed dispatch slots unrelated to roster depth" and "a new stamina currency".
  - Housing: needed only for a workplace job. "Fighters and fodder need none" (GAME_SPEC :1140-1141, owner ruling 2026-09-23).
  - Food: only housed heroes at home eat (GAME_SPEC :1186-1187), so fighters and fodder cost nothing.
  - Offline: one run per order resolves while closed. Online has no limit.
  - The Safe forecast gates unlimited repeats (safety, not count). The Summoning Circle changes odds, not count.
- A RATE CUT ALONE IS NOT A BRAKE. It only stretches the doubling. For a player who keeps pulls to build teams, the roster doubles every ~12 min at A, ~36 min at B and ~80 min at C. At C with no brake, the model is at ~18,000 heroes by 20 h.
- Why the bot snowballed at hours 2-4, not at once: the bot feeds any remainder under 5 (stage_play.gd _feed), so a new team needs 5 pulls to land in one step. Verdant's 150 never does it. Ashfall's 450 (4.5 pulls, plus leftovers and the returning team) does it about every other clear, and Ashfall was cleared at hour 2. A player who keeps pulls snowballs from hour 1. So the brake has to hold for that player, and the table below models that player.

2. FOUR BRAKES (numbers from the model at rate A/B/C; Early = 2 h, Mid = 20 h; Mid wants 15-30 heroes, 2-4 teams, ~1,000 Ledger, best team mostly C-B)

(1) SQUAD SLOTS FROM THE TRAINING HALL
- Rule: orders in the field <= 1 + Training Hall level (1-6). Rescues don't count. A force order counts as one.
- Numbers: 2 rows (base 1, +1 a level). Assumed TH 0 at Early and 3 at Mid (the bot's hall order puts TH 4th).
- Early: 1 team, 7-8 heroes. Mid: 4 teams, ~23 heroes (4 teams + 3 workers; the rest is fodder).
  | Rate | Early pulls/h | Mid pulls/h (1 -> 4 slots) | Pulls by 20 h | Ledger at 20 h |
  | A | 16.5 | 18 -> 70 | ~900 (2.8 spines) | ~2,200 |
  | B | 5 | 6 -> 23 | ~300 (0.9 spine) | ~970 |
  | C | 2 | 2.5 -> 10 | ~120 | ~610 |
- Cost: dispatch_force and its preview refuse at the cap; the Gate panel shows "Squads out 2/3" and the reason (boundary #2). No save key (building_levels[2]). A legacy save over the cap loads and keeps its orders; only new sends wait (boundary #1 test).
  - DECISIONS 2026-09-22 needs an amendment (godot-architect), and SYSTEMS :3857-3858 changes.
  - The bot forms at most as many teams as free slots, and the rest are fodder. That's following the rule, not meeting a check.
- Feel: the gacha standard. "Raise the Training Hall to field another squad" gives halls a strong pull. A deep roster still matters: fodder, town workers, rescues and force zones. The cap on the RTS fantasy is 6 at once.

(2) A BED FOR EVERY HERO (Banished)
- Rule: every hero lives in a House, and a pull needs a free bed. The nth House costs 6 x (n - 1) wood (the first stays free; today it's a flat 10).
- Numbers: 1 row (the step). Bed count follows wood, not hours: quadratic cost against linear wood gives linear growth.
- Early: 1 team, 7 heroes. Mid: 5 teams, ~28 heroes (1 woodcutter, then 2).
  | Rate | Early pulls/h | Mid pulls/h | Pulls by 20 h | Ledger at 20 h |
  | A | 16.5 | ~51 | ~950 | ~2,300 |
  | B | 5 | ~17 | ~320 | ~1,035 |
  | C | 2 | ~7 | ~135 | ~670 |
- Cost: it reverses the owner's 2026-09-23 ruling ("fighters and fodder need none"). It does match their first words: "have the heros have their own house, city management like the game banished".
  - Code: summon_hero checks for a bed; the pull auto-houses; the house cost curve (town_rules.gd); fighters at home eat, so starvation can pick a fighter (boundary #3 weight); UI for beds and the pull button's reason; the bot stops pulling at no bed and builds houses.
  - A legacy save with unhoused heroes must load and keep them (boundary #1).
  - No new save key (residents are saved). About 6 files plus GAME_SPEC.
- Feel: the town becomes the brake, which is on-theme and deep. The risk is friction: "can't pull, build a house" in a gacha, and placing ~30 houses.

(3) CROWDED ZONES PAY LESS
- Rule: a zone pays at most one team's worth of stones an hour, split between your orders in it.
- Result: income is bounded by the zones you use, but the roster still grows linearly, since extra teams still earn XP and loot. Mid heroes: A 666, B 223, C 91. It fails Mid's 15-30 at every rate. Mid pulls/h: A 35, B 12, C 5.
- Cost: the split needs the order count at dispatch, stored on the order (a new order key, boundary #1). Counting at settle is gameable.
- Feel: "Verdant is picked clean" nudges spreading across zones, but it reads as hidden stamina (DECISIONS rejected stamina).

(4) THE PULL COST RISES WITH THE ROSTER
- Rule: a pull costs 100 x 1.1^(heroes owned): 259 at 10 heroes, 673 at 20, 1,745 at 30.
- Result: the roster self-limits (Mid: A 58, B 40, C 25 heroes), but pulls collapse (20 h totals: A 58, B 40, C 25). Fodder dies with it: the 327-pull spine is out of reach, and "manufacture, don't pray" breaks.
- Cost: tiny. The cost function, its preview and the bot read the live cost. No save key.
- Feel: opaque and punishing. You sacrifice before you pull. P2-09 already rejected pricing pulls on another axis (rank).

Dropped: upkeep per hero. With income linear in heroes on teams, an upkeep only lowers the growth rate. It holds a steady roster only when it equals a team's income, and then a new player can't grow at all. Its town form (fighters eat) is inside (2).

3. THE RATE WITH A BRAKE IN (A keep ~18/h, B ~6/h, C ~2-3/h; the lever is a new stone_reward_scale row, 1 / 1/3 / 1/7, at game_session.gd:2476. It keeps a pull at 100 and the start at 3 pulls. The other lever is summon_pull_cost 300/700 with STARTING_STONES 900/2,100.)
- A: Early 16.5/h. Mid climbs to 50-70/h under (1) or (2). ~900-950 pulls by 20 h means about three manufactured SSS by the end of Mid (327 pulls each); Mid's "mostly C-B" is gone by hour ~8. The Ledger is ~2,200-2,300 at 20 h, and summons and deaths evict last, so at 100-140 an hour in Mid they would fill the 10,000 cap alone in 70-100 h. A pull every ~1 minute at Mid makes a life cheap.
- B: Early 5/h (13 pulls in 2 h: 8 heroes, 1 team, Early's checks pass at the low end). Mid 6 -> 23/h, ~300 pulls, ~1 spine: my guess is a best team of B-A with one S-SS, above "mostly C-B". Ledger ~1,000 at 20 h matches Mid's row.
- C: Early 2/h (7 heroes in 2 h, 1 under Early's 8, and nothing to feed until ~hour 3). Mid 2.5 -> 10/h, ~120 pulls: "mostly C-B" holds. Ledger ~600-670, under Mid's ~1,000.
- Every rate other than A changes Early's rows (Ledger ~80 becomes ~35 at B), so Early and Mid get remade (a big balance change).
- The Ledger knock-on stands at every rate: summons and sacrifices are over half of Mid's records (~580 of ~970 at B). 2.4's and 2.2.10's volume counts none.

4. MY PICK: (1) squad slots from the Training Hall, at rate B.
- It's the only brake that pins Mid's heroes (~23) and teams (4) for any player at any rate.
- It separates the brake (slots) from the rate (stones), so the owner's rate answer is one number.
- It's the smallest build: one refusal, one UI line, no save key.
- It gives the halls their strongest reason to upgrade.
- B, because C starves Early's fodder loop and A spends the 327-pull spine three times over by hour 20. B lands Mid's Ledger on target, at one pull every ~12 minutes in Early and every 3-10 in Mid.
- Runner-up: (2) if the owner wants the town to be the brake. Its cost is reversing their own two-day-old ruling and about 3x the build.
- If slots, the host could be the Town Gate instead of the Training Hall (it's where dispatch lives), but the Gate has no level: a sixth building_levels entry is a save-shape change (boundary #1) and a new upgrade table. The Training Hall already trains squads (XP +15%/level, skill teaching).

FINDING (either way, its own bead): the route floor makes an easy zone pay best for a strong team. At r >= 16 every small zone hits its floor, so an over-strong team farming Verdant makes ~6,000 stones an hour (90 s routes plus stomps; Early's 18 battles averaged 64 s), against ~2,700 at Sundered with r = 1.25. A slot cap bounds how many teams, not how much each one makes. The fix, if wanted: stones x min(1, 1/sqrt r), which makes income flat in r above 1. It's the "rewards fall off" idea, tied to over-power, not to crowding.
DIRECTOR 10:31 PDT: extra's brake sweep is checked. The code facts hold: stones = stone_reward x P (game_session.gd:2476), summon_pull_cost 100, the route formula (expedition_orders.gd:34-51), SYSTEMS :3857-3858 (no slot cap), DECISIONS 2026-09-22 :1051-1052 (rejected fixed dispatch slots and stamina, under 'Owner approval'), GAME_SPEC :1140-1141 (fighters and fodder need no house; owner ruling 2026-09-23). The arithmetic spot-checks: a Verdant team at r=1 makes 1,500/h, 300/h per hero, so a pull pays back in 20 min. That gives exponential growth at any rate, so a rate cut alone is no brake. I agree with the pick, (1) slots from the Training Hall at rate B. BOTH leading brakes reverse an owner decision: (1) the 09-22 approval of 'no dispatch-slot cap', and (2) the 09-23 'fighters and fodder need no house'. So the owner decides, with 4 options: A = (1)+B (my pick), B = (2)+B, C = (1)+rate A, D = (1)+rate C. Brakes (3) and (4) are dropped: (3) fails at every rate, and (4) kills the fodder engine. The farming finding is filed as ig-ncz.

title: Live pulse: five active battles advance in one frame (tick 36.6 ms); spread them one per frame on the main thread
description: WHY: after ig-7sn.7 (b52bad5), five active: tick 36.6 ms p50 (decode 4.5, advance 19.9, encode 1.5, other 10.7) plus ~10 ms of handlers. 2-4 active is 33-37 ms, and 95 frames were over 33 in 30 s (.agent-results/ig-7sn.7/pulse5.log). ig-7sn.11 cuts the handlers to ~4 ms, but the tick alone is over 33. The threading ADR (DECISIONS 2026-09-25, item 7) keeps the live pulse on the main thread and names a later bead under ig-7sn for it, measured first. This is that bead. It stays on the main thread: one battle fits a frame (frontier 14.0 p50 / 19.4 p99 a pulse, ig-7sn.7/battle_frontier.log); five in one frame don't. WHAT: with five dispatched, no frame over 33 ms outside a settle pulse. Split out of ig-7sn.11 (extra, 2026-09-25).
design:
DESIGN (extra, 2026-09-25; threading ADR item 7 kept: the live pulse stays on the main thread).

WHERE THE TIME GOES (ig-7sn.7/pulse5.log, five active, p50): tick 36.6 = decode 4.5 + advance 19.9 + encode 1.5 + other 10.7. The handlers add ~10, or ~4 after ig-7sn.11. One battle alone fits a frame: watched frontier_march's sim is 14.0 p50 / 19.4 p99 a pulse (ig-7sn.7/battle_frontier.log). The miss is that all five advance in the same frame. Also, a returning order (battle over, route left) is decoded twice every pulse (tick_expeditions' look-ahead and _advance_clocks_in_memory) just to read its status.

MEASURE FIRST (pulse5, before any change): split "other": _advance_clocks_in_memory less its battle work, _land_battle_checks, _send_battle_checks, the scans in tick_expeditions (lost caches, incidents, starve_step, finishes_build), and the battle_changed handlers. Record each battle's advance time a pulse, by zone, and decodes a pulse, active vs not.

FIXES, in order. Re-measure after each; stop once the target holds.
1. No decode just for a status. A battle order that is not active reads "status" from its battle dictionary, the value from_dict would read. It decodes only to advance, or to check secured allies when the order is due.
2. Reuse last pulse's state. GameSession keeps an unsaved table, order id → [the battle dict it wrote, its BattleState]. At the next advance, if is_same(order["battle"], that dict), the state is reused with no decode. Every writer replaces the battle dict and never edits it (ig-7sn.5's rule), so identity proves it unchanged. from_dict and a cancel clear the table. This is allowed because BattleState holds nothing unsaved but derived caches (its zone; the corner-graph cache keyed by the wall set): the threading ADR's rule for derived caches.
3. One battle per frame. The pulse keeps everything else on its 0.25 s schedule. Battle advances move to the frames between pulses: at most one battle advances per frame, in order-list order. Each advances by the real time since its own last advance. The sim carries tick_remainder, so the ticks, and so the outcome, are the same as advancing at the pulse. The pulse's own frame advances no battle. The due check at the pulse sees each battle's latest advance, so a battle that ends is settled at the next pulse, at most 0.25 s later. That is the same lag a save already has between pulses today. battle_changed fires per advance, once a pulse per battle as today. A command still applies at once and replaces the battle dict (_issue_battle_command_in_memory), so the next advance decodes it instead of reusing a stale state.
4. Only if still over: the "other" part, by what the measure finds.

NOT CHOSEN: live-pulse jobs on workers (an item 7 amendment). A frame's worst case is one battle, and one battle fits. Threads would add a pulse of latency to the watched view and to commands for no gain. Revisit only if one battle's pulse passes ~25 ms (for example if walls pass their 2 ms pathfinding budget).

BOUNDARIES: #4: the same sim and the same Wave, only chunked differently. Proof: the balance gate's digests are unchanged, and a reuse-vs-decode run is equal pulse by pulse. #1: no saved key; the table is unsaved and cleared by from_dict. A save writes each battle's latest committed dict, at most one pulse behind real time, as today. #2: a watched battle's view still updates on battle_changed. #3 untouched.

title: Dispatch preview and until-stopped dispatch run whole forecasts on the main thread (~6x at battle_pace 6)
description:
WHY: GameSession._preview_force_data (systems/game_session.gd ~1100) runs a whole BattleSimulation.forecast (two battles) on every dispatch preview, with a fresh seed. hub.gd calls it through _selected_force_preview on every _refresh_dispatch_summary (about ten call sites: selection, runs, policies, loadout), once per selected team. _dispatch_force_data runs it again, and an until-stopped dispatch runs one more forecast with the real seed. At battle_pace 6 (ig-1jw) each of these is ~6x longer: ~0.6 s per verdant preview, over a minute for frontier_march, all on the main thread. Found while designing ig-7sn.6 and ig-7sn.12 (extra, 2026-09-24). Not measured yet: perf_baseline has no preview measure.
WHAT (after ig-7sn.13 and ig-7sn.6): the preview's forecast becomes a worker job, cached by its inputs (hero ids, zone, squads, policies, loadout, and a hero/Ledger change key), so the refreshes share one job; the preview shows "Checking" until it lands. An until-stopped dispatch creates its order in ig-7sn.6's "checking" phase instead of forecasting on the main thread. Add a preview measure to tests/perf/perf_baseline.gd first (ADR item 1: measure first).
NOT: dropping the Safe gate on until-stopped dispatch (a design call).
design:
DESIGN (extra, 2026-09-25; builds on DECISIONS.md 2026-09-25 "Battle sim threading" and ig-7sn.6's job table).

MEASURE FIRST (2026-09-24 performance ADR, item 1): before any change, tests/perf/perf_baseline.gd gains a "preview" measure on the same save as the others (100 heroes, Ledger at 10,000). It times (a) GameSession.preview_force for one team at each zone's hero cap (5 / 5 / 5 / 30 / 50) and (b) one hub _refresh_dispatch_summary with that team selected, per-team mode and combined. Record the numbers in the bead (and SYSTEMS § Performance budgets, Hub row) at P = 1.

APPROACH: the preview's forecast becomes a cached worker job, and until-stopped dispatch reuses the preview's seed. So no forecast ever runs on the main thread, and dispatch needs no "checking" phase.
1. The preview's checks (squads, caps, policies, loadout, reserve, route) stay synchronous. They are cheap.
2. The forecast part: build the snapshots as today, then look up a small unsaved GameSession cache (at most 16 entries, oldest dropped). The key is the exact inputs the forecast reads: [snapshots, zone_id, squads, policies, escrow], compared with == on a hit, never by hash alone. Each entry holds its seed and, once landed, the verdict (safe, reason).
   - Hit with a verdict: return it. Hit still checking: return checking. Miss: draw a seed, add the entry, send the forecast as two jobs (normal and stress runs), return checking.
   - Checking reads as: safe false, checking true, reason "Checking...". An until-stopped preview is not valid while checking; a fixed-run preview is valid as today.
3. Landing, at the pulse: the entry gets its verdict, and GameSession emits a new signal, preview_forecast_ready. hub.gd connects it to _refresh_dispatch_summary only. Not expeditions_changed, whose handlers cost 6-10 ms plus the town walkers.
4. Dispatch: _dispatch_force_data's own preview call is a cache hit (same inputs). An until-stopped dispatch needs a landed Safe verdict; its run uses that entry's seed and the same snapshots. So the real run's normal half is the forecast's normal run, exactly today's gate (a forecast with the run's seed), and no second forecast runs. The entry is consumed at dispatch, so a seed is never reused. A fixed-run dispatch never waits.
5. Anything that changes a snapshot (a level, gear, skills, a bond the Knight cover orders read), the zone, squads, policies or loadout misses the cache. A stale verdict can't gate a dispatch.

BOUNDARIES: #1 untouched: the cache is unsaved; no new saved key. #2 a new GameSession signal plus one hub connection, a "Checking..." forecast line, and Dispatch disabled for until-stopped while checking. #3 untouched. #4 the forecast is still BattleSimulation.forecast's two runs; the dispatched run uses the forecast's seed and snapshots, as today.

COST AFTER: a refresh builds the snapshots and compares keys: about 20-23 ms for a 50-hero frontier team (ig-7sn.4's number), under the 33 ms hitch line. A small team is a few ms. The verdict lands one battle's wall time later: frontier ~6 s at P = 1, ~40 s at P = 6.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Measure first: perf_baseline "preview" measure at HEAD before the change (preview_force per zone at its cap; one hub dispatch-summary refresh, per-team and combined), logged under .agent-results/ig-7sn.14/. Then the same script after.
2. After: a preview refresh runs no BattleSimulation work on the main thread. A refresh with a 50-hero frontier team stays under 33 ms. A second refresh with unchanged inputs sends no new job.
3. The landed verdict equals BattleSimulation.forecast run on the main thread for the same snapshots and seed.
4. Until-stopped dispatch: refused while checking (Dispatch disabled, and dispatch_force refuses). With a landed Safe verdict, the order's run uses the entry's seed and snapshots (its to_dict at start equals create_run with them), and no forecast runs inside dispatch. Fixed-run dispatch never waits.
5. A change to a hero's level, gear or skills, the zone, squads, policies or loadout misses the cache. The entry is consumed at dispatch.
6. No new saved key. A hub test: the verdict landing refreshes the dispatch summary through preview_forecast_ready.
7. BUILT green. Review: #2 and #4 (Sol).

title: ADR + prep: run the battle sim on worker threads (forecast, load catch-up, dispatched pulse)
description: WHY: owner 2026-09-24 asked how multithreading sounds for performance (and ig-7sn: 'threading, code perf audits'). The battle sim is the biggest remaining cost and grows ~6x at battle_pace 6: the repeat forecast (ig-7sn.6, ~600 ms), load catch-up (ig-7sn.12, ~40 s), the five-battle pulse (ig-7sn.11). Battles are independent pure data, so they can run on WorkerThreadPool. The UI (roster list rebuild, ig-7sn.9) cannot: the scene tree is main-thread only. WHAT: (1) ADR (godot-architect): which sim work moves off the main thread; only pure BattleState work runs there; no scene tree, no GameSession mutation and no save from a thread; results committed on the main thread; per-battle RNG, so identical results to single-thread (a GUT test compares digests). (2) Prep, behaviour-free: the six static scratch vars in combat/battle/battle_simulation.gd (_cover_victims, _cover_claims, _cover_nearby, _row_front, _row_contact, _row_threat) become per-call, or two battles on two threads corrupt each other. Balance 8/8 and all digests unchanged. extra's ig-7sn.6 and ig-7sn.12 designs decide whether they build on this.
design:
DESIGN (extra with godot-architect, 2026-09-25). ADR: DECISIONS.md 2026-09-25 "Battle sim threading" (PROPOSED; amends the 2026-09-24 performance ADR's item 5). Director to accept.

THE RULE: the battle sim runs on WorkerThreadPool; the UI, GameSession, the save and the scene tree never do. First users: ig-7sn.12 (load catch-up) and ig-7sn.6 (repeat check). The live 0.25 s pulse stays on the main thread for now (a later bead, measured first). The preview/dispatch forecasts are a follow-up bead.

PREP, behaviour-free (combat/battle), before any job runs:
1. The six static scratch vars (_cover_victims, _cover_claims, _cover_nearby :2209-2211; _row_front, _row_contact, _row_threat :2266-2268) become locals passed down, or non-saved per-state fields.
2. godot-architect's find: the sim loads the zone by name every tick. _update_objectives (:735) and _spawn_group (:890) call ZoneDefinition.definition_for -> ResourceLoader.exists + load. BattleState gets a non-saved zone reference: create_run sets it, from_dict callers set it on the main thread, and the sim reads it. No worker ever calls ResourceLoader. (It may also shave main-thread tick time; measure.)

THE JOB (one function, callable on the main thread too):
- Input: a deep-copied battle Dictionary (or create_run's copied inputs: snapshots, squads, policies, escrow, seed) plus the zone the main thread resolved. Advance in fixed 5-battle-second chunks. Output: plain data (to_dict() or the forecast Dictionary). Touches no Node, autoload, signal, Hero, GameSession or SaveService.
- Job table: a private, unsaved GameSession Dictionary, like _paused_battle_orders. No fourth autoload.
- Commit on the main thread at the pulse, each order in its fixed place, never completion order. A stale result is dropped: the order must still exist, still hold the battle Dictionary the job read (identity, the look-ahead pattern), and still be in the phase and job generation it was sent under. Identity alone is not enough (godot-architect): remaining_seconds, pause and stop fields change in place without replacing the battle Dictionary.
- Cancel: a shared flag checked between chunks. On quit, and in load_game before from_dict, set it and wait for every task (at most one chunk, ~0.2 s at frontier). Cancelled results are dropped.

WHAT THREADS CAN'T DO: shorten one battle. Its ticks run in order. frontier_march's ~38 s catch-up at P = 6 stays ~38 s of wall time; the fix is that it runs in the background after the hub opens (ig-7sn.12). The wins: nothing on the main thread, the five zones in parallel, a forecast's two runs in parallel.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The director accepts the ADR (DECISIONS.md 2026-09-25 "Battle sim threading") before any code.
2. Prep is behaviour-free: balance 8/8, every existing digest and checkpoint test unchanged; no static var left in battle_simulation.gd; grep shows no ResourceLoader or definition_for call reachable from advance/forecast.
3. Determinism GUT test: the same job run directly and on WorkerThreadPool gives byte-identical to_dict() (and forecast Dictionaries) for several seeds, frontier_march and fallen_citadel included, with two or more jobs running at once.
4. Quit with jobs out: the process exits within 0.5 s; GUT exits clean with no task left.
5. BUILT green. Review: boundary #4 (Sol, read-only).

title: Caster spells, part 2: walls (units path around them)
description: WHY: owner picked zones and walls (ig-vl1.2 note). WHAT: wall spells per the ADR ig-vl1.2, numbers from game-designer at battle_pace 6, on top of battle pathfinding. Then re-run ig-vl1.6's break with walls in and re-PICK caster_rank_offset (timing (a), ACC 6).
design: extra 2026-09-25. SYSTEMS § Casters 'Walls' and § The v1 kits: the Mage's Rime Wall (level 1, cd 30 s, range 8, length 6, thickness 1.2, lifetime 8 s; P = 6: 180 s / 48 s). battle_wall_cap 3 inside battle_field_object_cap 8, oldest wall ends first. Thickness keeps actors on opposite sides 1.85 apart, over melee reach 1.6 (walls block walking, not attacks). AI: an enemy melee actor 3.5-6 from a back-row ally (Ranger, Mage, Cleric) -> wall across the ally-enemy line, 2.5 from the ally; nearest enemy decides, ties by lower spawn index. Cast on actors: pushed out across the segment to the side they stood on; exactly on the line -> the caster's side (director default, agreed). No damage, no counter tag, heroes only. Choice to flag: walls go to the Mage (control); the Cleric keeps Hearthward. All numbers PROVISIONAL.
acceptance_criteria:

description: WHY: owner 2026-09-24: 'we're eventually going to need pathfinding anyways' (picking zones and walls for casters, ig-vl1). Must fit SYSTEMS Performance budgets (the frame that advances a watched battle (_owe_battles, since ig-7sn.15), five dispatched, load catch-up at pace 6 ig-7sn.12). The forecast sees the same walls. design: extra 2026-09-25. Per DECISIONS.md 2026-09-25 'Casters shape the field' item 5-6 and SYSTEMS § Casters 'Walking around walls'. (1) The wall kind of field_objects (data + validation) lands here, cast by no skill yet; tests place walls by hand. (2) No wall up: today's straight-line movement, gated by one check per battle per tick; zero behaviour change. (3) Footprint = segment grown by half thickness + 0.325 (half battle_separation_radius), ends included. (4) Blocked straight line -> next corner on the shortest corner path (4 corners per wall; ties by wall cast order then fixed corner order); corner-to-corner graph is a derived, unsaved, per-state cache keyed by the wall set, rebuilt on cast/end or lazily after reload; actor-to-corner and goal-to-corner visibility plus a small Dijkstra each tick. AABB pre-test before exact segment tests. (5) Goal inside a footprint -> nearest edge point on the goal's side. (6) No path -> hold until a wall ends. (7) One helper cuts every instant move at the first footprint edge: Charge, knockback, lane push, separation, Slip, Dust Roll, Turncoat Cut, evade. (8) Per-state only, no statics (threading ADR). title: Load catch-up at battle_pace 6: expect a ~40 s load after 8 h away
description:
WHY: ig-1jw (SYSTEMS § Battle pace) makes every battle ~6x longer. Offline catch-up simulates the run's battle-seconds, so it costs ~6x. At ig-7sn.7 (07e8013) the load after 8 h away was 9.8 s, 6.3 s of it frontier_march's catch-up; at P = 6 expect ~40 s. SYSTEMS § Performance budgets, Load row (no target yet).
WHAT: measure it with tests/perf/perf_baseline.gd once ig-1jw lands, then pick a fix with the director (time-slice behind the load screen, a thread, or a target). A fix must keep the catch-up's result identical (same seed, same outcome).
NOT: resolving offline battles by quick_resolve instead of the sim (changes the rules; a design call).
design:
DESIGN (extra, 2026-09-24; boundary calls by godot-architect; builds on ig-7sn.13's ADR, DECISIONS.md 2026-09-25 "Battle sim threading" (PROPOSED)).

APPROACH: catch-up on worker threads after the hub opens. Picked over a time-sliced load screen (~40 s wait at P = 6), a main-thread background slice (frontier ~150 s and it eats the frame budget the Dispatched battles row already misses) and quick_resolve (changes outcomes, breaks seam #4; the skills ADR item 2 keeps QuickResolve to legacy_v2).

WHY IT IS BOUNDED: catch-up already covers at most one leg per order. apply_offline_expedition_progress advances each active battle by min(offline, max_seconds - elapsed_seconds); the repeat then starts fresh. So the cost is the rest of one battle per order, plus the repeat's forecast (moved out by ig-7sn.6).

WHAT CHANGES (systems/game_session.gd; combat/battle only through ig-7sn.13's prep):
1. apply_offline_expedition_progress runs no sim. Each battle_v1 order with an active battle gets catch_up_seconds = min(saved catch_up_seconds + offline elapsed, max_seconds - elapsed_seconds). remaining_seconds drops as today. Nothing else about offline time changes (recovery, town and keepers stay live-tick only).
2. New optional order key catch_up_seconds (float >= 0). Missing = 0. Non-finite or negative = 0 with push_warning. SAVE_VERSION not bumped (the P2-23 / chains precedent).
3. The first pulse after load sends one job per owed order (ig-7sn.13's job function: advance in fixed chunks). While its job is out, the order is in the paused skip set: its battle clock stops like tactical pause. Its order card and battle view say "Catching up", and commands are refused ("catching_up").
4. One round: when every job of the round has landed, the main thread applies them together and runs today's commit path (phase returning, stranded capture, _resolve_due_orders_in_memory in _due_order_before order, notifications, one save), then clears catch_up_seconds. So settle order never depends on which thread finished first. Cost: small zones wait for the slowest (frontier ~40 s at P = 6).
5. Save mid-catch-up: writes the order as loaded, with catch_up_seconds. Quit: ig-7sn.13's cancel flag, then wait (at most one chunk). The next load adds the new absence to the owed seconds, capped at the leg's rest. Chunks start from the same saved state, so an interrupted catch-up ends at the same to_dict() as an uninterrupted one.

LOAD TARGET (SYSTEMS § Performance budgets, Load row): load_game after any time away costs no more than with none (345 ms at 07e8013; at most 500 ms on the owner PC). The hub takes input at once. The catch-up adds no frame over 33 ms. The round's commit is a settle pulse and counts in the Dispatched battles row (ig-7sn.6, .9, .10). Wall time to land at P = 6: frontier_march ~40 s, the other zones a few seconds. Threads cannot shorten one battle: its ticks are serial. Only a faster sim can (ig-7sn.7 was that).

BOUNDARIES: #1 one additive order key; acceptance below. #2 a "Catching up" state on the order card and battle view. #3 none: settles and kills stay on the main thread, in today's code. #4 the sim is unchanged apart from ig-7sn.13's prep; the job equals the main-thread run by ig-7sn.13's byte test.

ADR: yes. ig-7sn.13's ADR amends the 2026-09-24 performance ADR's item 5, which says building a threaded battle "amends this entry first". The new key rides in it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. After 8 h away (perf_baseline measure load, at P = 6 once ig-1jw lands): load_game <= 500 ms and no more than the no-time-away load plus 150 ms. The catch-up adds no frame over 33 ms while it runs (the round's commit is measured under ig-7sn.6).
2. Result identical: for every zone, the state after a threaded catch-up equals today's synchronous advance by the same seconds and chunks (to_dict() byte for byte).
3. Save round-trip through disk (boundary #1): save mid-catch-up, reload with no time away: catch_up_seconds survives and the order ends at the same to_dict() as an uninterrupted catch-up. A legacy save with no catch_up_seconds loads as 0 and catches up its offline time. A bad value loads as 0 with a warning.
4. Quit mid-catch-up exits within 0.5 s; no task left running (GUT exits clean).
5. A command, stop or recall on a catching-up order is refused or held, never lost; a stale result is dropped.
6. BUILT green; balance 8/8; the ig-7sn.13 determinism test green. Review: boundary #1 and #4 (Sol).
notes:
After ig-7sn.7 (b52bad5), pace 1: load after 8 h away 9.8 s (was 16.4), frontier_march catch-up 6.3 s (was 12.1), no time away 345 ms. .agent-results/ig-7sn.7/load.log.
STATUS (extra, 2026-09-25): done (design). Approach: catch-up on worker threads after the hub opens, one round, committed through today's resolve order; new optional order key catch_up_seconds. Load target now in SYSTEMS § Performance budgets, Load row: load_game after any time away <= the no-time-away cost (345 ms), at most 500 ms; hub takes input at once; no catch-up frame over 33 ms; at P = 6 frontier lands after ~40 s. Boundary #1: one additive key (acceptance has the disk round-trip and legacy save); #4: sim unchanged beyond ig-7sn.13's prep, byte test. ADR: yes, ig-7sn.13's (DECISIONS.md 2026-09-25, PROPOSED). ORDER CHANGE: this now depends on ig-7sn.6. Without it the round's commit runs the repeat forecast on the main thread (frontier ~76 s at P = 6). Engine order becomes ig-7sn.13 -> ig-7sn.6 -> ig-7sn.12. Deps added: .12 -> .13, .12 -> .6.

Director 2026-09-25: approved high1's change to design item 3 / ADR item 8. catch_up_seconds > 0 stops the battle clock at the paused-skip sites; the order is NOT put in _paused_battle_orders (the battle view's _release_live_binding calls set_battle_paused(false) on close, which would free it mid-job). Commands -> refused 'catching_up'; stop -> stop_requested, honored at the settle; pause -> the player's pause only. ADR amended (DECISIONS.md item 8). Landing reuses _battle_checks/_land_battle_checks with its own branch; perf_baseline's stale forecast column is dropped here.

Load runs no sim: active battles owe catch_up_seconds = min(saved + away, leg rest), rounded to whole microseconds so it survives JSON exactly (below TICK_EPSILON). Clock stop = player pause OR owed>0 (_battle_clock_stopped; not the pause set, director-approved). First pulse sends one BattleJob.run_battle per owed order into _battle_checks; the catch-ups land as one round via _land_battle_checks (generation + is_same + still owes), then returning/stranded + _resolve_due_orders_in_memory, one save. Bad value, or a key on a battle that is not active, loads as 0 with push_warning. Commands refused 'catching_up' before the commit (a rollback would restart the round); stop and pause are held. Perf load (ig-7sn.12-before -> -after): after 8 h away 8293.7 -> 350.8 ms; no time away 350.9 -> 314.0 ms; lands in 7.6-9.0 s at P=1; worst frame while it runs 33.0 ms, and the same 3 frames (~33 ms at 0.44-0.50 s) appear after a plain load (control), so they belong to load_game; landing frame 355-448 ms (5 legs settle in one commit). perf_baseline: forecast column dropped; load measure watches frames. Known: vs one advance() call, a battle that ends mid catch-up keeps a different leftover tick_remainder (fight identical; test pins it). title: ADR: caster zones and walls (saved field objects) and battle pathfinding
description:
WHY: ig-vl1's spells are 'battlefield shaping' (zones, walls, slows, mass heals or wards). A lasting object on the field is new saved battle state and a new sim mechanic: boundaries #1 (checkpoint save round-trip) and #4 (combat seam: both resolve paths, the forecast). The director asked for an ADR first.
WHAT: godot-architect writes the DECISIONS entry once the owner has picked the first shape (SYSTEMS § Casters). Settle: where a zone lives in the checkpoint, its keys and validation, determinism and actor order, how quick_resolve stays skill-blind, the forecast's cost, and the perf budget (ig-7sn). The battle has no pathfinding, so walls need their own answer or are ruled out.
NOT: numbers (game-designer, after the ADR).
notes:
Owner 2026-09-24 ~23:55 local: picked zones AND walls as the first battlefield shaping: '1 & 2, we're eventually going to need pathfinding anyways'. This ADR now covers zones and walls as saved field objects (boundary #1, #4) and pathfinding in the battle sim (movement, determinism, no RNG, forecast, perf budgets, Charge's lane and knockback against walls). Director order: zones first (no pathfinding needed), then pathfinding, then walls.
STATUS (extra, 2026-09-25): done (design). ADR written by godot-architect: DECISIONS.md top entry 2026-09-25 'Casters shape the field - zones and walls are checkpoint-saved field objects; pathfinding is a per-state pure function, not a nav service' (PROPOSED, lines ~10-85). Director to accept. Key calls: BattleState gains field_objects + field_sequence (additive, SIMULATION_VERSION 1); effects read from the const ABILITIES by skill_id (never ResourceLoader, so thread-safe); validated with the objective-state point/bounds/number checks, not the marker exact-match check. The closed set grows by one primitive, zone; a wall is a shape the movement code reads, blocks movement only (not attacks or sight), both factions. Fixed tick step, creation order, no RNG in pulses. A live-object cap (game-designer's number). Pathfinding v1: a visibility graph over inflated wall corners, next waypoint a pure function each tick, costs nothing with no wall up; a derived unsaved corner-graph cache keyed by the wall set is allowed (a hit equals a recompute, so reloads and worker copies stay identical). No NavigationServer; AStarGrid2D only after a measured miss. Charge, knockback and separation stop at walls; a wall cast on an actor pushes it to the side it was on. Verdicts: #1 allowed (additive keys, legacy = empty), #2 view draws from the checkpoint only, #3 untouched, #4 allowed (same sim, forecast sees it, QuickResolve/safety_forecast stay skill-blind). Open for game-designer: cap, geometry, durations; whether enemy kits get zone/wall in v1. Small gap for ig-vl1.5: an actor exactly on the wall's line needs a tie-break side (for example the caster's side).
close_reason: ADR accepted by the director 2026-09-25 (8b69558): zones and walls are checkpoint-saved field objects, pathfinding a per-state pure function. Numbers (cap, geometry, durations) next, game-designer, under ig-vl1.4 / ig-vl1.5.

title: Caster power: the caster flag and caster_rank_offset (ships 0: the presence test found no offset that fits)
description:
WHY: owner: 'a 2 star mage should have a battlefield presence of a 3 to 4 star knight'. Stats are the quick lever until the spells (ig-vl1.4) land.
WHAT: SYSTEMS § Casters. New balance row caster_rank_offset = 1.5. Hero.compute_final_stats multiplies a mage's or cleric's HP, ATK and DEF by 1.35^offset (not SPD, not crit). Enemies unchanged. Then run the presence test from SYSTEMS § Casters (the mixed team with the Mage slot swapped; seeds 1-4, medians; F level 1 at Verdant and C level 30 at Sundered) and set the offset so a caster at R lands between a Knight at R+1 and R+2.
ORDER: after ig-1jw (pace) and ig-zht (Knight kit), since both move the Knight it is measured against.
design:
DESIGN (extra, 2026-09-25; checked against 858b45d. game_session.gd refs are HEAD's: high1's uncommitted WIP shifts them by about 65 lines). Rules: SYSTEMS § Casters (the caster_rank_offset row, and "Presence, as the sim measures it"). It runs after ig-1jw and ig-zht (both still open), because both move the Knight it's measured against.

FINDINGS (director's call on both)
- Runs per point: the ACC says 8 runs per point per slot, but SYSTEMS says seeds 1–4. My pick is 8 (seeds 1–8): a median over 4 is the average of the middle two, so one odd fight moves it. If you agree, game-designer changes SYSTEMS to "seeds 1–8".
- The ACC's unit test pins 1.35^1.5, but step 3 below retunes the offset, so a pinned 1.5 would break the moment it's tuned. My pick: the test reads balance.caster_rank_offset. Then it passes at 1.5 today and at whatever the presence test picks.

1. THE ROW
- balance_table.gd gets `@export var caster_rank_offset: float = 1.5`, and balance.tres gets the row, the same as every SYSTEMS row.
- It stays PROVISIONAL in SYSTEMS (the marker at :1348) until the table is in the notes. After that, game-designer updates the value and the marker.

2. WHERE IT APPLIES: Hero.compute_final_stats (heroes/hero.gd:171-229)
- HeroDefinition gets `@export var caster: bool = false`. mage.tres and cleric.tres set it to true.
- Why a flag on the definition, not a def_id list in code: compute_final_stats and compute_team_power are handed the definition separately from the hero, and tests pair them freely. test_hero_stats.gd:84-98 gives a def-less Hero.new("Second", 3) the mage definition. A check on hero.def_id would skip that hero, and the test would pass for the wrong reason. The class is the definition's data (ARCHITECTURE rule 3).
- In the function, beside `multiplier`:
    var caster_scale: float = pow(balance.stat_multipliers[1], balance.caster_rank_offset) if definition.caster else 1.0
  Then HP, ATK and DEF are multiplied by multiplier * caster_scale. SPD and the two crit stats are left alone. Gear and traits then multiply on top, as today.
- stat_multipliers[1] is the curve's one-rank step (1.35, § Ranks), so there's no second copy of 1.35.
- It reads the balance argument, not preload(...).prop, so a runtime change to the resource reaches it (the constant-fold memory). The presence harness relies on that.
- Every consumer gets it through this one function: the sim snapshot (game_session.gd:1492-1493), quick_resolve (:44 and :47), team power and dispatch (expedition_orders.gd, game_session.gd:423), the arena (:750), and the stat panels (hub.gd:852, battle_view.gd:155). There is no second stat path to keep in step.

3. THE PRESENCE HARNESS: tests/presence_check.gd, kept in the repo
- SYSTEMS re-runs this test after zones and again after walls (:1289-1290), so it's kept, not thrown away. It's a manual SceneTree script like the other tests/*_check.gd. BUILT doesn't run it (GUT runs tests/unit only). It still has to import clean under the gate.
- Run it with a temp APPDATA, like GUT: the autoloads start with it.
- Snapshots come from GameSession._team_snapshots (game_session.gd:1484), fetched with root.get_node(^"GameSession") after a deferred start. So its keys (skills, chains, level, squad, a Knight's cover_order) can't drift from the game's. It reads the level from Hero.level_for, so the harness gives each Hero the xp for its level (C's cap is 30). The squads and battle loop copy the balance gate's (.agent-results/ig-uu7.3/balance_gate.gd).
- The team is the gate's mixed team (Knight, Ranger, Mage, Rogue, Knight) with the Mage slot swapped. Everyone else is at the caster's rank and level. The zone is from ZoneDefinition.definition_for. Supplies are bare (0 healing, 0 revival): supplies heal, so they would mask the Cleric. SYSTEMS doesn't say, so this is my pick.
- Two points: F level 1 at verdant_outskirts, with the Knight at D and C; and C level 30 at sundered_vault, with the Knight at B and A. The ranks are F D C B A = 0 1 2 3 4.
- Measures:
  - Mage: elapsed_seconds at "victory". A fight that isn't won counts as max_seconds.
  - Cleric: the sum of the allies' hp at victory, with downed allies at 0. A fight that isn't won counts as 0.
- It prints one table: per point and slot, the median of each measure, and wins out of N.
- The sweep: it sets the loaded balance.tres's caster_rank_offset at runtime (load() returns the shared instance) to 0.5, 0.75 … 2.5. That's 9 values, PROVISIONAL. The Knight rows are run once (they don't depend on it).

4. PICKING THE VALUE
- Take the smallest offset where all four lower bounds hold (Mage and Cleric, at both points) and no upper bound is broken. "Smallest" matches SYSTEMS' later rule to cut it as far as the lower bound holds.
- Write that into balance.tres and the balance_table.gd default. Paste the table into the notes.
- If no single offset fits both classes at both points, don't force it. Report the table: a per-class split is a SYSTEMS change for game-designer.

5. WHAT MOVES ON PURPOSE
- The balance gate's mixed digests change (it has a Mage); the starter_knights digests must not. Name both in the notes.
- Tests that build a Mage or Cleric through Hero may pin a number: test_hero_stats (573.26 at :96), test_battle_job, test_battle_simulation, test_equipment, test_expedition, test_expedition_orders and test_masterwork_draughts. Update each to the new value on purpose, never by widening a margin. The formation digests are hand-built snapshots, so they don't move.
- A battle in flight keeps its dispatch-time stats (the snapshot is fixed at dispatch). The next dispatch sees the new ones. No migration is needed.

BOUNDARIES
- #4: one function feeds both resolve paths (quick_resolve and the sim snapshot), so they agree by construction. Sol reviews it.
- #1: no new save field. HeroDefinition is a .tres, never saved.
- #2: two .tres edits (mage, cleric), plus one balance row. #3 untouched.

title: Knight skills: Charge (straight-line dash, crowd-control immune, knocks enemies aside) and Ground Slam (area damage and stun); the AI opens with Charge then Slam
description:
WHY
Owner, 2026-09-24: "skill addition for knights: charge -> charges in a straight line towards an selected enemy. immune to cc while in motion, and knocks aside enemies in between the target and knight. ground slam -> aoe dmg+stun around the knight. intended to be used after charge. AI should charge then ground slam as an opener"

WHAT (design numbers first, then engine)
- Charge (new mechanic): a straight-line dash to one enemy (the player picks it when casting by hand; the AI picks it on auto). Immune to crowd control (stun, root, knockback, slow) only while moving. Enemies in the lane get knocked aside, pushed out sideways. It builds on ig-36y's real knockback. A new move type (MOVE_TO today has only behind_target and away) and the immunity window probably need an ADR (boundary #4).
- Ground Slam: mostly data. Damage around_caster plus an interrupt stun (like knight_buckler_blow), with combo_after = the charge, so it follows it.
- AI opener: the AI charges, then slams, when it opens a fight or an engagement. Pick the charge target so the slam lands well (e.g. into a cluster).
- Director defaults (the owner can overrule): unlock early enough that the owner's current knights get both (they want to play them); the slam doesn't hit allies; knock-aside pushes without damage.
- Numbers go in SYSTEMS, set at ig-1jw's slower pace: cooldowns, damage, stun seconds, charge speed and range, the push distance, and the slam radius.

KNOCK-ONS
- Knights get stronger, so ig-vl1's caster target (a caster ≈ a knight 1-2 ranks higher) is measured after this.
- Balance cases and pinned digests change.
design:
SYSTEMS § The v1 kits: two Knight rows plus 'Charge and Ground Slam (ig-zht)'; § Learning note. Pace-1 values (x6 at battle_pace 6):
- Charge: ability, level 1, 15 s (90 s). Range 4-12. Straight line to the target's cast-time position, ending 1.2 short (inside 1.6 reach), bounds-clamped. Enemies other than the target within 0.8 of the line pushed 1.5 sideways to their own side (on the line: the Knight's right); all of § Knockback's rules (elites immune, no damage, no interrupt, clamp, no RNG, resolve then push). No damage. Allies passed through.
- INSTANT in the sim, like every move today (Turncoat Cut, Slip). The Knight lands on the cast tick, so nothing can CC it mid-dash: the owner's immunity with no timer and no saved state. The view draws the dash over 0.4 s. Fallback if it reads as a teleport: a timed dash with an immunity window (saved state, boundary #1, then an ADR).
- Ground Slam: ability, level 1, 15 s (90 s). 1.0x (6.0x) to every enemy within 2.5, 1.5 s (9 s) interrupt-stun on each. Opponents only. No counter tag. AI rule combo, combo_after = charge.
- AI: charge the current target (never retargets; cover holds) when it is 4-12 away and another enemy is within 2.5 of it, or it is elite (rule enemies_near_target, ai_count 2, ai_radius 2.5, ai_or_elite, min_range_units 4). Slam fires after the 1.0 s lock inside the combo window.
- Enemies don't get either.
- Schema, inside ADR item 1's closed set: move.to = 'charge' + lane_push; interrupt gets area (target | around_caster); AbilityDefinition.min_range_units; the combo rule allowed on abilities. No ADR needed if instant; ask godot-architect for a one-line check.
acceptance_criteria: 1) GUT: Charge lands 1.2 short on the cast tick; an enemy in the lane is pushed 1.5 to its side, an elite is not, the target is not; bounds clamp; no damage. Slam hits and stuns every enemy within 2.5 and no ally, and cancels a windup. The AI charges then slams on auto; it holds Charge under 4 away and without a second enemy near the target (unless elite). 2) A mid-battle save/reload repeats the same charge and pushes (determinism). 3) The ig-544 gate's 8 cases re-run: any loss or new downing in a supplied case goes to design. 4) Every skill .tres still loads under the primitive test. 5) BUILT green; Sol review (combat seam). Depends on ig-36y (knockback).

title: Casters ultra rare (1 in 100 each) and battlefield-shaping: a mage or cleric fights like a knight 1-2 ranks higher
description:
WHY
Owner, 2026-09-24: "i want magic in general to be rare but battlefield shaping, so mage and clerics should be ultra rare compared to the knights and rangers, but stronger, ie a 2 star mage should have a battlefield presence of a 3 to 4 star knight". Asked how rare: "1 in 100 each".

WHAT (design first; split into children when scoping)
- Summon odds: mage 1%, cleric 1%. Knight, ranger and rogue share the rest (director default: the rogue stays common). Today hub/summon/summon.gd picks the class uniformly (ARCHETYPE_DEF_IDS[randi() % 5]). Every other place a hero or a class is rolled follows the same odds; find them all (e.g. SYSTEMS :612).
- Power: the game has ranks (F, D, C, B, A, S, SS, SSS), not stars. Director reading: a caster at rank R has the battlefield presence of a knight at R+1 to R+2. Define "presence" as something the sim can measure (e.g. a team's clear time or its enemy damage with the caster vs with the knight), and tune to that.
- Battlefield shaping: few casts per fight, each one big. Area effects that change the fight (zones, walls, slows, mass heals or wards), with cooldowns set against ig-1jw's slower pace. A new mechanic (terrain, zones) needs an ADR first (boundary #4).

KNOCK-ONS
- The owner's existing casters get the buff (fine).
- New area effects add sim cost (perf budget, ig-7sn).
- Pinned digests and the balance cases change.
- The power targets are best measured at ig-1jw's new pace.
design: Split (SYSTEMS § Casters, § Summoning Class odds): .1 odds 98/98/98/3/3 (ship first; touches only summon.gd, balance_table.gd, balance.tres, test_summon.gd); .2 ADR for battle zones (godot-architect, after the owner picks the first spell shape); .3 power caster_rank_offset 1.5 on HP/ATK/DEF via compute_final_stats, tuned to the presence test after ig-1jw and ig-zht; .4 spells after .2, then cut .3's offset. Skill-book class rule amended (unbuilt): one share per owned archetype.

title: Combat pace 5-6x slower, toward a Total War: Warhammer 3 feel
description:
WHY
Owner, 2026-09-24: "i find the combat pace still too fast. I want the pacing to feel more like total war warhammer 3". Asked how much: "5~6x slower". Today a starting team of five clears Verdant in 62.9-78.6 s, so the target is about 5-8 min.

WHAT (design first, then engine)
- Targets in SYSTEMS: the clear-time band (5-6x today's), time-to-kill for trash, elites and bosses, attack cadence, move speed, and ability cooldowns (so spells don't fire 5-6x more often per fight).
- Director defaults (the owner can overrule): earnings per hour stay the same (rewards per battle scale up). The feel comes from longer time-to-kill and weightier exchanges, not global slow motion.
- This settles the ig-el4 PROVISIONAL band (played: too fast).

KNOCK-ONS
- The repeat's safety forecast simulates two whole battles, so it grows 5-6x (about 0.5 s). ig-7sn.6's time-slice becomes required.
- Offline catch-up grows with battle-seconds.
- The balance gate's 8 cases and the pinned digests get a new baseline.
- In-flight battles keep their old stats.

NOT
No change to the combat seam's contract (both resolve paths agree). No new autoload.
design:
SYSTEMS § Battle pace (ig-1jw, design 2026-09-24). One balance row, battle_pace = 6 (int: whole loot rolls; unscaled walk-in/windups/telegraphs land a clear near 5.5x).
x P: max HP of every actor at spawn (not a damage divisor: the max(1) floor); ability cooldowns (heroes and enemies; one place, BattleSimulation._skill_cooldown); an ability's ATK-based amount per cast (damage multiplier, heal, shield); the seconds of every status/control an ability applies (DR, stat changes, bleed/burn/HoT, stun, root, silence, taunt; per-second magnitudes unchanged); objective holds; max_battle_seconds; route base and minimum; rewards (stones, XP x P, loot = P rolls); recovery_lifetime_seconds (incidents and caches).
Real seconds: swings and interval, weaponskills and their statuses, passives, movement, windup, telegraphs/aims, delayed-area delays, dodge window, ability lock, combo window, chain timeout, status tick, carry, cover taunt, pushes, the tick. Supplies already scale (max-HP fractions, limited counts).
Saved: one optional battle checkpoint key 'pace' written at spawn; every x P reads it; missing = 1 (in-flight battles end as they began). SIMULATION_VERSION stays 1. Boundary #1 review. legacy_v2 orders read the live battle_pace.
Not changed: combat seam contract, six stats, hero_power, RP, quick_resolve, autoloads.
acceptance_criteria: 1) The balance gate's 8 cases at P = 6, seeds 1-2: all win; mixed 315-472 s; Knights 561-698 s; downings at most +1 per case; a new downing in a supplied case goes to the director. Under 315 s: try P = 7 and report, don't tune other numbers. 2) GUT: HP, a cooldown, a heal, a stun and a reward each scale by P; a weaponskill, the windup and a telegraph don't. 3) Save round-trip: a mid-battle checkpoint saves and reloads with pace; a legacy checkpoint without it loads as pace 1 and finishes at pace-1 numbers. 4) New baseline for the formation digests and the pre-skills checkpoint. 5) ig-7sn.6's time-slice and ig-7sn.12 (load catch-up) settled or knowingly waived by the director before export. 6) UI prints x P cooldowns/heals/stuns. 7) BUILT green; Sol review (boundaries #1 and #4).
notes:
