EXPORT HOLD from ig-1jw until ig-7sn.12 (load ~40 s after 8 h) and ig-7sn.6 (settle forecast ~6x) land, so the owner's feel test has no new hangs. The pace checkpoint key is boundary #1: Sol review, plus a real save/reload and a legacy checkpoint with no pace key. ig-eek now depends on this bead.

Added to ACC: re-run perf_baseline's load, settle and preview measures at P = 6; no new frame over 33 ms.
high1 2026-09-25 STATUS partial (code done, BUILT green; balance misses 2 ACC-1 limits, needs director call).
CHANGE: battle_pace=6 (balance_table.gd/.tres). BattleState.pace (checkpoint key "pace", missing=1; SIMULATION_VERSION stays 1). create_run(..., pace=0 -> live). xP: spawn max HP (heroes+enemies; checkpointed actors not rescaled), ability cooldown (in _spend_ability, not _skill_cooldown so _counters sort unchanged), ability dmg/heal/shield, ability status+control seconds (not dodge), telegraph dmg (only abilities start them), raid holds, max_seconds, forecast_leg, route base+min, recovery/lost-cache lifetime (live pace), rewards (session settle reads state.pace: stones/XP xP, P loot rolls seeded run_seed+i; legacy_v2 reads live pace). (2) Medium: a legacy no-pace incident's recovery window uses live pace (900 -> 5400 s). NOT changed: design says lifetime uses live pace; longer only, one-time for pre-update incidents. Director call. Combat seam: no defect found.
Director 2026-09-25 ~03:50 local, review of high1's STATUS: ACCEPTED at P = 6.

No supplied case got a downing. P = 7 is worse (balance_p7.log), so P stays 6. Measured clears are 4.7x-5.1x, not the design's guessed 5.5x: extra to record that in SYSTEMS § Battle pace.
- Sol finding 1 (unbounded pace -> loot rolls): fixed by MAX_PACE = 20 in validate_snapshot, test_battle_simulation covers 0, -1, 1.5, "6", null, 21, 1e9 and a JSON 6.0. Director read it; no Sol re-run.
- Sol finding 2 (a pre-update incident gets the live xP window): accepted as designed. Windows never shrink (_incident_lifetime and the cache lifetime keep the high-water mark), so a pace change can only lengthen a window, never expire a stranded hero early. Carrying pace into incidents and caches would add saved keys for no player gain.
- ACC 5: 7sn.6 and 7sn.12 landed. Catch-up after 8 h is now 27.0 s (was 7.4). The new mid-catch-up frame (41-67 ms at ~13.9 s) goes to ig-7sn.16.
- ACC 6: no UI prints a static cooldown, heal or stun (grepped); battle_view shows the live xP cooldowns.
- Balance baseline from here: .agent-results/ig-1jw/balance_final.log.
STATUS (extra, 2026-09-25): docs written, uncommitted: SYSTEMS § Battle pace. Why column: 'about 5x, measured (4.7-5.1x)'. New 'Measured at P = 6' paragraph (clears, both waivers, P = 7 worse, baseline log). PROVISIONAL now says 'measured on the balance gate, not played'. Earnings note: 'up to about 6 / 5'. The Ledger's 'about a sixth' left alone (routes are exactly x6).

title: Settle pulse: a pulse that settles a leg takes 321-422 ms (the repeat's forecast)
description:
WHY: Measured by ig-7sn.2 at 0df0e29 on the owner's PC (1920x1080, vsync off, 100 heroes, Ledger at 10,000). Numbers and method: .agent-results/ig-7sn.2/baseline.md; rerun with tests/perf/perf_baseline.gd. Budget: SYSTEMS § Performance budgets (p99 8.3 ms, no frame over 33 ms). A fix cites before and after with the same script. Dispatched battles row. A pulse that settles a leg (a battle ends and its report lands) took 340 ms with one battle out and 447 ms with five, against 33 ms. It happens once per leg per battle, so a repeating order hitches every leg.
WHAT: split the settle pulse's cost (report, ledger record, bond fold, save, roster_changed handlers: see the roster action bead) and bring it under 33 ms. Log: pulse.log.
design:
DESIGN (extra, 2026-09-24; boundary calls by godot-architect; builds on ig-7sn.13's ADR, DECISIONS.md 2026-09-25 "Battle sim threading" (PROPOSED)). Scope: the repeat forecast only (95-105 ms of the settle pulse at P = 1, ~600 ms for verdant at P = 6). The handlers (ig-7sn.9), the save (ig-7sn.10) and expeditions_changed stay their beads'.

APPROACH: a "checking" phase. The forecast runs as two worker jobs (normal and stress runs, in parallel) after the settle.

CAN THE SETTLE SIMPLY WAIT (no saved state)? No, two ways:
- Forecast first, settle after: wrong. The settle's XP changes hero levels, and the repeat's snapshots must be built after it, or the forecast checks a different team than the one that runs.
- Settle first, forecast unsaved: a save during the forecast would write the finished battle with nothing marking it settled, and a reload settles it again (double rewards). So one saved marker is the minimum: phase "checking". Nothing else new is saved.

WHAT CHANGES (systems/game_session.gd; hub order card and battle view text):
1. The settle stays immediate: report, rewards, Ledger record, XP, as today.
2. _start_battle_repeat splits in two. At settle, if a repeat is due: check _loadout_spends_reserve (stop as today if short), spend the escrow now, draw the seed, build the snapshots, and set phase "checking", run_seed = the new seed (existing key), escrow. Then send the two jobs.
3. WHERE THE IN-PROGRESS FORECAST LIVES: only in GameSession memory, in ig-7sn.13's private job table (task ids, the snapshots, the battle Dictionary identity key). Never saved.
4. Landing (checked each pulse): safe -> create_run with the same snapshots and seed the check used; phase fighting; remaining_seconds = route duration. Unsafe -> refund the escrow; stop the order with unsafe_repeat, written onto that settle's report.
5. A "checking" order is skipped by _resolve_due_orders_in_memory (the double-settle guard). Its battle view shows the finished battle and "Checking the next run". Stop while checking ends the order at once (refund, reason requested); a result that lands after is dropped.
6. SAVE OR QUIT MID-FORECAST: the save writes phase checking, run_seed, escrow and the finished battle. A quit sets ig-7sn.13's cancel flag and waits (at most one chunk). On reload the first pulse sends a new check: snapshots rebuilt from the order's locked heroes, the same seed.
7. Offline settles (ig-7sn.12's round) enter checking too, so load never runs a forecast.

COST: the next leg starts when the check lands: one battle's wall time, since the two runs go in parallel. At P = 6: verdant ~0.3 s, frontier ~40 s (unmeasured; frontier's forecast is likely ~12 s even at P = 1). No frame cost.

BOUNDARIES: #1 a new phase value, no new key; acceptance below. #2 two text states. #3 none: settles and kills stay in today's code, on the main thread. #4 the forecast is still BattleSimulation.forecast's two runs, same seed and snapshots as the real repeat; the job equals the main-thread run by ig-7sn.13's byte test.
acceptance_criteria:
1. perf_baseline settle1/settle5: the settle pulse loses the forecast (95-105 ms at P = 1). Before and after with the same script.
2. The verdict is the one BattleSimulation.forecast gives on the main thread for the same snapshots and seed; the real repeat uses those snapshots and that seed.
3. Save round-trip through disk (boundary #1): save while checking, reload: the order is still checking, is not settled again (rewards, runs_completed, Ledger and report unchanged), and gets the same verdict. A legacy save with no checking phase loads as today.
4. Unsafe verdict: escrow refunded, order stopped as unsafe_repeat on that settle's report. Stop while checking: ends at once with the escrow refunded.
5. Quit while checking exits within 0.5 s; no task left running.
6. BUILT green; balance 8/8; the ig-7sn.13 determinism test green. Review: boundary #1 and #4 (Sol).
notes:
2026-09-24 rerun after Sol's ig-7sn.2 review (same commit 0df0e29, logs pulse1.log / pulse5.log / roster.log / battle_*.log; baseline.md updated). Supersedes the description's numbers: settle pulse 321 ms (1 battle), 422 ms (5). Likely cause from reading: _start_battle_repeat (game_session.gd ~2125) runs BattleSimulation.forecast, a whole battle, before create_run.
high1 2026-09-25: split measured (new perf_baseline measures settle1/settle5; run_measure.sh whitelists them; logs .agent-results/ig-7sn.6/settle1.log, settle5.log at 07e8013; one-off PROF instrumentation in .agent-results/ig-7sn.6-prof/ with game_session.gd restored to HEAD). Settle pulse 320 ms (1 battle) / 380-395 ms (5): roster_changed handlers 140-190 (ig-7sn.9), repeat forecast 95-105 (two whole sims: normal + stress; this bead), save 8-44 (ig-7sn.10), expeditions_changed handlers 6-10 (ig-7sn.11), credit xp 2, ledger record + bond fold 0.1, report 0, commit snapshot to_dict 1-4; the rest is the real flush reacting to real changes (handlers). No behaviour-free fix for the forecast found besides a faster sim (ig-7sn.7): the sim has no view-only work a forecast could skip. HOLD for director's pick among options (time-slice, thread, cache/skip, wait for 7sn.7).
Director 2026-09-24: option 4 now. Parked behind ig-7sn.7 (a faster sim shrinks the forecast) and ig-7sn.9 (the roster rebuild is 140-190 ms of the settle pulse). Then re-measure settle1/settle5. If the forecast is still over 33 ms, the planned fix is option 1 (time-slice the forecast in a 'checking' phase, same verdict, seed and snapshot; the repeat starts ~0.3 s later; one additive save field, so boundary #1 review). Declined: option 3 (cache or skip; it changes the safety rule, a designer call) and the unsafe-only trim (YAGNI). The settle measure (tests/perf/perf_baseline.gd, run_measure.sh) is committed with ig-7sn.7.
Director 2026-09-24: ig-1jw (combat 5-6x slower) makes the repeat forecast about 5-6x longer (~0.5 s). Time-slicing the forecast (option 1) is now required, not maybe.
Director 2026-09-24 ~23:45 local: UNPARKED. ig-7sn.7 landed (b52bad5); dep on ig-7sn.9 removed. At battle_pace 6 (ig-1jw) the repeat forecast grows ~6x (95-105 ms -> ~600 ms), so the time-slice is required and part of ig-1jw's export hold. Order: ig-36y -> ig-vl1.1 -> ig-1jw -> ig-7sn.12 -> this. The roster rebuild (ig-7sn.9) is pace-independent and stays its own bead.
STATUS (extra, 2026-09-25): done (design). Approach: phase 'checking' after an immediate settle; the forecast runs as two worker jobs (normal, stress). Where it lives: only in GameSession's unsaved job table (ig-7sn.13). Can the settle simply wait with no saved state? No: forecasting first checks the wrong team (the settle's XP changes levels), and an unsaved forecast lets a mid-forecast save plus reload settle the battle twice. Minimum saved state: the phase value 'checking' (run_seed and escrow are existing keys). Save or quit mid-forecast: saves phase checking + run_seed + escrow; quit cancels within one chunk; reload re-sends the check with the same seed. A checking order is skipped by _resolve_due_orders_in_memory (double-settle guard). Cost: next leg waits one battle's wall time (verdant ~0.3 s, frontier ~40 s at P = 6). FLAG: frontier's forecast is unmeasured and likely ~12 s even at P = 1 (settle measures covered verdant only). Suggest P1: it now gates ig-7sn.12 and the pace export. New follow-up: ig-7sn.14 (dispatch preview and until-stopped dispatch forecasts, same problem, depends on this).
Director 2026-09-25: P1 as extra suggested (frontier's forecast ~12 s even at P = 1). Order: after ig-7sn.13, before ig-7sn.12.
high1 2026-09-25 implemented, HOLD for director BUILT. Settle spends escrow + draws run_seed, phase 'checking'; tick_expeditions lands then sends checks (normal+stress legs as 2 WorkerThreadPool jobs); stale guard = generation (unsaved _battle_checks) + still checking + is_same(battle); safe -> create_run with the check's snapshots+seed; unsafe -> refund, 'unsafe_repeat' on the settle's report; stop while checking -> ends now with refund. _resolve_due_orders_in_memory and the tick due scan skip checking; load never sends checks. Evidence: gate 0/0, GUT 867/867; balance 8/8 identical (.agent-results/ig-7sn.6/balance_after.log); forecast split equals HEAD's forecast 64/64 (forecast_equal_probe); test_repeat_check 5/5 (disk save mid-check, unsafe, stop, quit); real-process quit mid-check exit 0.09 s (quit_checking_probe.log). Perf whole pulse: settle1 264-274 -> 195-204 ms; settle5 350-380 -> 269-280 ms. Note: perf_baseline.gd:229 'forecast' column is a side replay, now stale (rest goes negative). Sol APPROVE, no findings (.agent-results/logs/ig-7sn.6-sol.json).
close_reason: Landed 7f3d04f: repeat check runs as two pool jobs in a 'checking' phase; settle1 264-274 -> 195-204 ms, settle5 350-380 -> 269-280 ms. Director BUILT 867/867 gate 0/0, balance 8/8 identical, Sol APPROVE.

title: Victory banner: a big engraved banner on a win, and OK goes back to town
description:
WHY
Owner, 2026-09-24, after looking at the ig-1i2 text: "early-win text should be plastered and shoved in my face, it's too easy to miss right now, like it's engraved in a fancy banner and you can click ok to make it go away and return to town."

TODAY
ig-1i2 added a small status line in two places: battle_view.gd render_snapshot (a normal expedition that won with route time left) and the hub order card. Both are easy to miss.

WHAT (director defaults; design may adjust)
- When a normal expedition you are watching turns to Victory, a big banner covers the middle of the battle view: VICTORY, the ig-1i2 heading-home line with its live countdown, and an OK button.
- OK closes the banner and goes back to town, the same way the battle view's existing way back does. The order keeps running to its rewards.
- Opening the watch view on a battle that is already won shows the banner then too. View state only, never saved.
- The look: an engraved plate. A framed, gold-trimmed panel with big raised letters, built from Godot UI (StyleBox, font outline and shadow) and fonts already in the repo. No downloads.
- Practice and rescue keep their current flow. The hub order card keeps its text (you are already in town).

ACCEPTANCE
- GUT: a watched normal battle that wins shows the banner with the countdown line; OK returns to the hub; the order still pays out.
- A real window at 1920x1080 and 1280x720: the banner is readable and OK is clickable (the ig-ght lesson).
- Boundary #2 (scene <-> script): review mandatory.

NOT IN SCOPE
Banners for defeat or stranded, sound, a town popup for battles you are not watching.
design:
2026-09-24 extra (design): scope check of the director defaults. All defaults kept. Six tightenings:

1. WHEN IT SHOWS. The view has received a snapshot for this watched normal order with status Victory. That covers the early win (the owner's ask) and a late win, if its Victory snapshot reaches the view. Code fact: game_session.gd _advance_clocks_in_memory emits battle_changed every pulse (:1852), but a win with no route time left can complete the order in the same pulse (_resolve_due_orders_in_memory :1816). The view may then only see the order vanish, with no outcome. In that case keep today's "Battle ended · Return to hub for results" and show NO banner. The banner never claims VICTORY unless the view saw one.

2. TEXT. Plate title "VICTORY". One line under it: "Heading home · rewards in M:SS", ticking live. The title already says victory, so drop "Victory!" from the line. When route time is 0 or the order has completed while the banner is up, the line becomes "Rewards are in. See them in town." The banner stays until OK. Button label "OK" (the owner's word). The small status label under the plate keeps its ig-1i2 text.

3. OK. Call the existing _on_exit_button_pressed path (battle_view.gd:959): leave_requested, _release_live_binding (unpauses), SceneRouter.go_to(HUB). No second route home. OK takes focus when the banner opens, so Enter and Space work. Controller stays on hold.

4. IN YOUR FACE. A full-view dim backdrop (about 60% black, mouse_filter STOP) with the plate centred. Nothing under it takes clicks. A won battle has no commands left, and OK is the way out, per the owner.

5. LOOK, with no downloads and no new theme file:
   - Plate: StyleBoxFlat with a dark warm fill, a thick gold border, rounded corners and a drop shadow. Add an inset second border (a panel in a panel) for the engraved-frame edge.
   - Letters: large (at least 3x the HUD font), light-gold font_color, a dark font_outline and an offset font_shadow for the raised or engraved look.
   - Font: the theme default. Do NOT use addons/gut/fonts (e.g., LobsterTwo). GUT is a test addon, and the game shouldn't depend on it; exports may drop it later.
   - The Hexagon pack is 3D models only, so there's nothing to take from it here.
   - Size: the plate is about half the view wide and readable at 1280x720 and 1920x1080.

6. TESTS. Keep the director's acceptance, plus:
   (a) A banner test where the order vanishes with no Victory snapshot: no banner, "Battle ended" text.
   (b) The countdown line updates on the next battle_changed, then switches to the done line when the order completes.
   For any pushed click, use the bd memory "headless GUT click tests": GUT's output panel eats clicks. Pick the OK point with the _reachable/_hovered helpers in tests/unit/test_hub_controls.gd.

Unchanged: normal expeditions only. Practice, rescue and the hub card stay as they are. View state only, never saved. Not in scope: defeat or stranded banners, sound, a town popup. Boundary #2 review stays mandatory.
notes:
2026-09-24 director amendment to tightening 1: ALSO show the banner when a GameSession.expedition_reports entry for the watched order appears that is new since the view opened, with outcome 'victory' (game_session.gd:2061 writes StringName(outcome.status); :2044 'victory'). Why: at Verdant the fight (63-116 s, SYSTEMS el4 block) usually outlasts the route minimum (base 60 s), so the order completes in the same pulse as the win and the view never gets a Victory snapshot. With tightening 1 alone, the banner would almost never show in zone 1 and would read as a bug. The report is the record of the win, so the banner still never claims a win it didn't see. In that case the line is the done line ('Rewards are in. See them in town.'). Use the report's unique id to tell new from old: repeat orders keep one order_id across runs. Tests: (a) becomes 'vanish with no Victory snapshot and no new victory report -> no banner'; add (c) 'vanish with a new victory report -> banner with the done line'.
2026-09-24 extra (design): the director's report amendment is sound, and I checked it against the code. A tick with a due order runs _commit_profile_mutation(_advance_time_in_memory) (game_session.gd:1764). battle_changed for the order is flushed after _complete_order_in_memory has appended the report (:2064) and removed or repeated the order. So in that pulse, the view never sees the Victory snapshot, only the aftermath. Two build notes: (1) Check for a new victory report on EVERY battle_changed refresh, including the empty-snapshot path (_refresh_live_snapshot -> _mark_battle_ended, battle_view.gd:429). A single-run order, or a repeat that stopped (downed, completed, requested), is removed, so that path is the common one. (2) Count only reports for this view's order while it is a normal order (the snapshot kind). Rescue orders stay out. Report ids come from Item.new_instance_id, and the ring buffer trims from the front, so 'id not present at open' stays correct.
high1 build (uncommitted): combat/battle/battle_view.gd (+133/-1) and tests/unit/test_battle_controls.gd (FakeBattleController.expedition_reports + 7 tests). Banner is code-built over the HUD (last child, mouse STOP), no .tscn edit. _update_victory_banner() runs after every live refresh, both render and the empty-snapshot _mark_battle_ended path (extra's note a). Shows for a normal order on a Victory snapshot, or a victory report for this order whose id was not there at configure_live (note b; repeat orders reuse the order id, report ids tell runs apart). Countdown line while the win is live with route left, else 'Rewards are in. See them in town.'; stays until OK. OK = the Exit path, takes focus, exempt from _mark_battle_ended's disable; _unhandled_input returns while it shows. Evidence .agent-results/ig-rog/: gate.log exit 0; gut.log 836/836, orphans unchanged (1257); window.gd real window at 1920x1080 and 1280x720: real order won with 10 s route left, countdown banner shown (banner_*.png), click via Input.parse_input_event at OK hovers VictoryOk and the scene becomes res://hub/hub.tscn (after_ok_*.png). Sol review running.

Fix: OK's focus_next/previous and all four focus neighbours point at itself. (2) Low: WASD pan is polled in _process, so it still moved the camera under the banner. title: A melee hero can stop a float32 hair outside attack range against a still target and never swing
description: Found by high1 during ig-uu7.3 (2026-09-24); pre-existing, not caused by uu7.3. Vector2 is float32, attack_range is a GDScript float (64-bit). The move loop in combat/battle/battle_simulation.gd (~:568-580) stops when offset.length() <= desired_range and otherwise steps offset.length() - desired_range; float32 rounding can leave the hero at 1.6000001 from a 1.6 range. From there the step is below one ulp, so the hero never moves, and _in_range_target (:1445, distance_to > attack_range) never returns the target, so it never swings. Needs a target that stays still (a moving target breaks the tie, which is why play has not shown it). Fix idea: one shared tolerance used by both the arrival check and the in-range check, or aim the approach a hair inside range. Check the other resolve() for the same comparison (combat seam, CLAUDE.md boundary 4).
acceptance_criteria: A regression test with a stationary target placed so the approach lands just outside range: on HEAD the hero never swings; after the fix it swings. The arrival check and the in-range check use the same tolerance from one place. Both resolve() implementations agree. BUILT green.
notes:
2026-09-25 high1: fix = const REACH_TOLERANCE 0.0001 (battle_simulation.gd, by TICK_EPSILON) in move-loop arrival, _in_range_target, _update_carry. Probe: 940/1600 approach starts parked at 1.6000000238 and never swung (.agent-results/ig-9gf/probe.log). New tests/unit/test_reach.gd fails on HEAD, passes with fix. QuickResolve (math) and Arena (velocity stop 2.4 vs trigger 3.0) unaffected. BUILT: gate 0; GUT 810/813; fails = formation digests (3/4 keys), pre_skills checkpoint fixture (victory 73.4s -> stranded 71.7s), kite cornered (fixed by pinning the ranger; the enemy used to hang out of reach). Balance HEAD->fix: 1 loss (knights:1), new downings in both supplied mixed cases, big clear-time shifts (knights ~100s vs 138-180). Enemies were also stuck next to still heroes, so old balance was measured on a broken sim. Sent director options A land+retune later / B retune in 9gf (my pick) / C park. HOLD, pins not updated, Sol not run.
2026-09-24 director ruling (after the advisor check): A with an export hold. Land the fix alone, no export; the retune is ig-el4 (P1, design).
Widen the fix before landing. Per-consumer slack misses pairings: the protect stance (:2061) parks a GUARD knight at battle_guard_radius, then compares `> battle_guard_radius` bare. A knight parked a hair outside re-issues GUARD and returns every tick, so it never picks a target or covers. Also bare: carry validator :211, contact :484/:2140 (these only pair if an attack_range >= detection 12.0).
Root-cause shape (high1 owns the exact code): in _move_actors the step lands REACH_TOLERANCE inside any reach > 0 and never passes a point: step = minf(speed*tick, minf(len, maxf(len - desired_range + REACH_TOLERANCE, 0.0))). Arrival is len <= maxf(desired_range, REACH_TOLERANCE): bare for reaches, slack only for points. Revert the consumer slacks, so checks compare bare. Don't use bare arrival plus a +tol step: with desired_range 0 it overshoots the point and oscillates.
Proof: re-run the 1600-point probe (0 stuck), plus a guard-parking probe. Add a protect-stance regression test that fails with the fix reverted. Regen the pins the ig-gy0.4 way: a script under .agent-results/ig-9gf/, plus a fix-off run that reproduces the old digests and the old .expected.json. Update the comments at test_formation.gd:14 and test_battle_persistence.gd:100-105. Re-run the 8 balance cases on the final fix. Then BUILT, Sol, STATUS, HOLD.
Widened per ruling: _move_actors arrival len <= maxf(desired_range, REACH_TOLERANCE); step aims REACH_TOLERANCE inside a reach, never past a point; consumer slacks reverted (all checks bare). Probes on final fix: melee 0/1600 stuck (HEAD 940), Protect guard 0/1600 (HEAD 209 with the ward at (14,12); near origin HEAD shows 0 because float32 steps are fine there; my first per-consumer fix stuck 63). test_reach.gd: 2 tests, both fail on HEAD, pass with fix. Pins regenerated: test_formation all 4 digests (fix-off prints old 4: formation_fix_off.log); pre_skills expected.json via .agent-results/ig-9gf/regen_pre_skills_expected.gd (fix-off byte-identical to HEAD file; with fix: stranded 71.7s). Comments updated. BUILT: gate 0, GUT 814/814. Balance final (balance_final.log): starter_knights:1 AND :2 bare now lose (stranded 98.8/112.2), supplied knights win ~96-100s; mixed all win, supplied mixed:1 1 downing. -> ig-el4. Sol r1 running.
Sol r1 (.agent-results/logs/ig-9gf-sol-r1.json): source clean, no remaining hair-outside park path, pins/regen verified; only finding = GUT Float/Int warning in test_kite.gd:122 (landed uu7.3 test, JSON float kite_ready_tick) -> compared via int(). Final BUILT: gate 0, GUT 814/814, 0 warnings. STATUS done sent; HOLD.

Sol r1: source review clean, no other hair-outside parking path; its only finding (the pre-existing Float/Int warning at test_kite.gd:122) was fixed with an int() compare. title: A direct attack-move under Auto Battle is replaced by the squad AI on its first planning pass
description:
Found by Sol during the ig-axw review (2026-09-24, .agent-results/logs/ig-axw-sol.json, finding 1, High, pre-existing). Director confirmed by reading.

combat/battle/battle_simulation.gd, _choose_intentions: the direct-order continue (:469) excludes COMMAND_ATTACK_MOVE on purpose, and the clear skips direct orders. But with auto_battle on (the default), the actor then reaches _choose_squad_intention (:~2019), whose _set_auto_order (:2025-2029) overwrites order_kind, order_point and target, and sets direct_order false. So the player's Shift+A attack-move destination (SYSTEMS.md:34) is lost on the first pass. SYSTEMS.md:28 says a new direct movement/target order replaces the previous one; nothing lets the AI replace the player's order. With auto_battle off the order survives.

Expected: a direct attack-move keeps its destination. While it stands, the hero may fight enemies it meets (an ATTACK on an enemy near it, the squad AI's own target pick), but never gets a new destination. On arrival the order ends as a MOVE does (:549-551) and auto resumes. The same with auto_battle on and off.

Order: before ig-uu7.1 and ig-uu7.2. Their formation and cover rules go in the same squad call and assume 'no direct order' means auto.
acceptance_criteria: GUT, auto_battle on and off: a direct attack-move hero walks to its point, stopping to fight an enemy it meets on the way, then continues. The squad AI never changes its destination while the order stands. On arrival the order ends and auto resumes. Other direct orders are unchanged. The combat seam: forecast, live and offline share _tick. Sol review.
notes:
Director, 2026-09-24. Auto OFF is broken too. With auto_battle off, a direct attack-move survives but acts as a plain MOVE and never fights. A hero only swings at order_target_id (_in_range_target :1408), and no code gives an attack-move a target. COMMAND_ATTACK_MOVE appears only at :62, 75, 189, 205, 209, 469 and 549. So the fix has to cover both settings, in one place.

Suggested shape (high1 may improve on it):
(1) A direct ATTACK_MOVE gets its own branch in _choose_intentions, at the direct-order continue (:469). It keeps order_kind and order_point. It keeps a live target that is still in radius; otherwise it picks the nearest living enemy within BALANCE.battle_cohesion_wait_distance of the actor (_nearest_enemy_near_point, the radius stay_together already uses to look for a fight; no new balance key). It stores that in order_target_id, then continues, the same on both auto settings. The squad AI, the ig-uu7 rules (SYSTEMS § Hero AI on auto: 'direct order' comes first), the rescue auto branch and the supplies retreat all stop seeing it. The :469 exclusion then goes.
(2) _move_actors: an ATTACK_MOVE with a live target walks to the target and stops at attack_range, like ATTACK. With no target, it walks to order_point. TRAP: the arrival clear (:549-551) must fire only with no target, or the order ends the moment the hero reaches an enemy.
Hits then work for free, because _in_range_target reads order_target_id.
2026-09-24 extra (radius ruling, director asked): use the hero's contact range, max(battle_detection_range, its attack range), for both the pick and the keep check, not battle_cohesion_wait_distance (6.0). title: "Retreat when supplies run out" never retreats: _choose_intentions clears the order it just set
description:
Found by extra during the ig-uu7 design pass (2026-09-24). Director confirmed by reading.

title: Hero AI 3: back-row heroes hop toward the tank when a melee enemy closes in (one hop, then a cooldown)
description:
Parent: the hero AI epic. Owner: "ranged or vulnerable heroes should automatically try to make distance if enemies try to close the distance, but not get stuck in a infinite wild goose chase".

## Rule
- Who: back-row heroes (ranger, mage, cleric) on auto.
- Trigger: a living enemy whose order_target_id is this hero is within kite_trigger (PROVISIONAL 3.0: melee 1.6 plus a step) and the hero's kite cooldown is ready. Enemy ranged units stop at 8, so they never trigger it.
- Where: a point just behind the nearest living front-liner as seen from the threat, so the tank ends up between them. With no front-liner, straight away from the threat. At most kite_distance (PROVISIONAL 4.0) from the start. Clamped to bounds; if the clamp leaves under half of kite_distance (cornered), no hop: stand and fight.
- Budget: one hop, then kite_cooldown (PROVISIONAL 5 s) of standing and fighting. The hop ends early when the threat dies, is taunted away or retargets.
- Why toward the tank: heroes walk up to 5 u/s and every enemy walks 1.5 u/s. Plain running away would make melee enemies helpless and chase forever. Running to the tank ends the chase at the tank, which .2 then pulls off.
- Movement reuses the evade_point path in _move_actors. Saved state: optional effect_state kite_point ([x, y]) and kite_ready_tick (non-negative int).

## Acceptance (GUT)
- A melee enemy on a ranger: the ranger hops toward the knight and the knight pulls the enemy.
- A ranger cornered at the bounds does not hop.
- A 60 s fight: no back-row hero hops more than ceil(60 / kite_cooldown) times.
- A legacy battle snapshot without the two keys loads and advances.
- Then the epic's balance gate (eight ig-544 starter cases).
design:
FINAL DESIGN (2026-09-24). Rule text: docs/SYSTEMS.md § Hero AI on auto, Kiting. Numbers are in the table there. This field overrides the description where they differ.

CHANGES VS THE DESCRIPTION
- Who: back-row heroes whose attack_range is greater than battle_kite_trigger_range, so they can still attack from where they land. This leaves clerics out.
  Cleric answer: yes, the described rule loops for a cleric (melee range 1.6). It hops, walks back into melee to swing, waits out the cooldown, and hops again, whenever no knight pulls the threat. That is bounded but pointless. The range test is the smallest fix. Formation (.1) and cover (.2) still protect clerics.
  OPEN OWNER QUESTION: do clerics stay melee swingers that don't hop (default, my pick), or become stand-back healers at Mend range 6 (safer, less damage)? The second is a kit change and needs its own bead.
- Which front-liner: the hero's own squad's nearest living front-liner. That is the one .2 will cover with.
- Wrong-way guard: if the capped hop would end nearer the enemy than the hero is now (the tank is on the far side), hop straight away instead.
- Cornered: no hop, and the cooldown is NOT spent. The check runs again next tick at no extra cost. A hero standing next to its tank gets a hop under half length, so it stays put, which is the point.
- The hop ends on arrival (within battle_separation_radius of kite_point) or once no living enemy targets the hero.
- Evasion clears kite_point; kite_ready_tick stays spent.
- After a hop the stance's own return applies as usual. The cooldown bounds any back-and-forth, so the hop point needs no stance clamp.
- Movement is an auto MOVE to kite_point instead of the evade_point override. _move_actors already stops a MOVE at its point, so _move_actors needs no change.

WHERE (combat/battle/battle_simulation.gd)
- _choose_intentions: in the auto branch, after the rescue branch and before _choose_squad_intention (l.511). This is below evasion and direct orders and above the stances.
- Reuse .1's single pass. Add to it the nearest living enemy with order_target_id == actor.id; comparing ids needs no lookup.
- Hop in flight (kite_point present):
  - if no enemy targets the hero, or it has arrived: erase kite_point and fall through;
  - else: _set_auto_order(actor, COMMAND_MOVE, "", kite_point) and continue.
- New hop, when kite_point is absent, state.tick >= kite_ready_tick, and that enemy is within battle_kite_trigger_range:
  - F = the squad's nearest living front-liner to the hero.
  - p = F.position + (F.position - threat.position).normalized() * battle_formation_spacing.
  - end = hero + (p - hero).limit_length(battle_kite_distance).
  - If F is null, or end is nearer the threat than the hero is now: end = hero + (hero - threat).normalized() * battle_kite_distance.
  - end = _clamp_to_bounds(end). If |end - hero| < battle_kite_distance / 2: no hop.
  - Else: kite_point = [end.x, end.y]; kite_ready_tick = state.tick + ceili(battle_kite_cooldown_seconds / battle_tick_seconds); issue the MOVE.
- Evade branch (l.461-465): erase kite_point.
- create_run (l.114): erase kite_point and kite_ready_tick next to the last_*_tick resets. Tick restarts at 0 in a new run, so a carried kite_ready_tick would block hops.
- battle_actor.gd validate_dict, only when each key is present (the last_counter_tick pattern):
  - kite_point: an Array of two finite numbers;
  - kite_ready_tick: a non-negative integer;
  - FINDING, same pattern while you are there: evade_point has no validation today. Add it (two finite numbers).
- New balance.tres fields, all PROVISIONAL:
  - battle_kite_trigger_range 3.0
  - battle_kite_distance 4.0
  - battle_kite_cooldown_seconds 5.0

GOOSE CHASE, BOUNDED
- A 4 u hop takes about 1 s at 3.8+ u/s. A 1.5 u/s enemy then needs about 2.5 s to close again, which is free shots, and the hero fights about 1.5 s in reach before the next hop is ready.
- At most 12 hops a minute. The hop heads for the tank, so .2 usually ends the chase. With no tank, the chase drifts to the bounds, the hero is cornered, and it stands and fights.

ACCEPTANCE (GUT)
- A melee enemy on a ranger: the ranger hops, ends nearer its knight than it began, and the knight pulls the enemy.
- A ranger cornered at the bounds does not hop and its kite_ready_tick is unchanged.
- A 60 s fight: no back-row hero hops more than ceil(60 / battle_kite_cooldown_seconds) times.
- A cleric with a melee enemy on it never gets a kite_point.
- An evade during a hop clears kite_point and leaves kite_ready_tick as it was.
- A legacy battle snapshot without the keys loads and advances. A malformed kite_point, kite_ready_tick or evade_point is rejected at load.
- create_run with a saved-actor snapshot carrying kite_ready_tick 900: the hop is ready at tick 0.
- Then the epic's balance gate (the eight ig-544 starter cases).

COST
- No pass of its own: its fields ride .1's single pass. A hop in flight adds nothing.

title: Hero AI 4: knights cover their bond partner first, then heroes they share the most history with
description:
Parent: the hero AI epic. Owner: "maybe here we have room for the relationship mechanic where they will cover their friends or lovers first, then others".

## Rule
- Each hero's team snapshot (GameSession._team_snapshots) carries cover_order: teammate hero_ids with bond points above 0, most points first. The bond partner, when on the team, comes first by construction. Points come from the Bonds pair index (history/bonds.gd), read once per dispatch from hub.gd's kept index or one Bonds.index pass. Never per tick.
- The actor keeps it as an optional effect_state cover_order (Array of Strings), saved with the battle. A legacy snapshot loads it as [].
- .2's knight pick sorts threats by the victim's place in the knight's cover_order first (listed before unlisted), then .2's order.
- This snapshots derived data for one battle, like stats. It does not save bonds (DECISIONS.md "Bonds stay derived").

## Risky boundaries
#1 save round-trip (battle snapshots in the save) and the GameSession snapshot seam. Sol mandatory. Acceptance includes a real save and reload with a battle in flight, plus a legacy snapshot without the key.

## Acceptance (GUT)
- Two threatened back-row allies at equal HP: the knight covers its bond partner. With no bond, the lower-HP one.
design:
FINAL DESIGN (2026-09-24). Rule text: docs/SYSTEMS.md § Hero AI on auto, Bonds. This field overrides the description where they differ.

CHANGES VS THE DESCRIPTION
- Knights only, back row only. Only knights read cover_order, and only back-row allies can be victims (.2). So only a knight's snapshot gets it, and it lists back-row teammates only:
  - the knight's bond partner first, if the partner is a back-row teammate (a front-row partner is left out);
  - then the other back-row teammates the knight has bond points with (points > 0), most points first, ties broken by team order.
- The index read cannot come from hub.gd's kept index: GameSession must not reach into the hub (ARCHITECTURE rule 1). And one Bonds.index pass per launch is too dear for a repeat launch on the 0.25 s pulse. At the 10,000-record cap the all-pairs rebuild is 103-129 ms (SYSTEMS § Bonds, Bond read cost row), and _team_snapshots runs 2-3 times per launch (the forecasts plus the run).
  DIRECTOR DECISION, my pick: move the kept index from hub.gd to GameSession, the ledger's owner, and have the hub read it from there. Both then share one rebuild per ledger change. The fallback is a second ledger-keyed copy in GameSession, which pays the rebuild twice.
  Either way, skip the read when the team has no knight or no back-row hero.
- Snapshot key: a top-level cover_order on the team snapshot. _actor_from_team_snapshot copies it into actor.effect_state["cover_order"].
  Do not route it through snapshot.effect_state. Any snapshot with both max_hp and effect_state takes the BattleActor.from_dict path (battle_simulation.gd:841). _team_snapshots has neither key today, but adding one would silently change that path.
- Preemption: a knight already covering switches only to a threat on a victim strictly earlier in its cover_order (unlisted counts as last). This is stable, so it cannot ping-pong.
- Depends on ig-m6o.2.2.1 (the kept index; a dependency is set).

WHERE
- systems/game_session.gd _team_snapshots (l.1281): add "cover_order": Array[String] of hero instance_ids to each knight's snapshot. Take points from the kept Bonds index (history/bonds.gd index / bond_from).
- combat/battle/battle_simulation.gd:
  - _actor_from_team_snapshot (l.840), fresh-build path: copy snapshot cover_order into effect_state when it is an Array.
  - .2's pick and sticky check: sort and preempt by cover_order index.
  - Readers use effect_state.get("cover_order", []). No _default_effect_state entry.
- combat/battle/battle_actor.gd validate_dict: when cover_order is present, it must be an Array of Strings. A legacy battle has no key and reads as [].
- The battle is saved, bonds are not. This snapshots derived data for one battle, like stats, and does not save bonds (DECISIONS.md 2026-09-24 "Bonds stay derived").

RISKY BOUNDARIES
- #1, the save round-trip: battle actors in the save.
- The GameSession snapshot seam.
- Sol review is mandatory.

ACCEPTANCE (GUT)
- Two threatened back-row allies at equal HP, one of them the knight's partner: the knight covers the partner.
- The partner at higher HP than the other victim: still the partner.
- No bonds: the lower HP fraction.
- The knight is covering a threat on an unlisted victim, and a threat appears on its partner: it switches on the next tick. The reverse never switches.
- A team of knight, partner mage, ranger with 3 points and cleric with 0 points gives cover_order [mage, ranger]. A rogue partner is left out.
- A real save and reload through disk with a battle in flight that carries cover_order: the order is equal after the reload. A legacy battle without the key loads as [] and advances. A malformed cover_order is rejected.
- Perf: time the cover-order build for a 50-hero launch at the 10,000-record cap, best and worst of seven (CODING_RULES § Performance), and record it beside SYSTEMS § Performance budgets, Dispatched battles. A miss files a bead under ig-7sn.

Director decision 2026-09-24: the kept index moves to GameSession in ig-m6o.2.2.9 (which blocks this bead). _team_snapshots reads GameSession's index: no fresh Bonds.index per launch, and no second copy. Knight hits taunt under direct orders too, as designed (a trait of the hit). Clerics stay melee (director ruling; no hop).

Tests: test_cover 2, test_battle_persistence 2 (rules incl. a tie where only partner-first gives the answer; real SaveService.save + load_game with a battle in flight; legacy without the key loads as [] and advances; malformed rejected), test_bonds 1 perf. Evidence .agent-results/ig-uu7.4/: gate exit 0; GUT 841/841, orphans 1257 unchanged; balance gate identical to ig-el4/balance_final.log both without the key and with cover_order [] on every snapshot; mutants (partner-first off, rank ignored, always keep) each fail a test. Sol review running.
Sol (verifier high, .agent-results/logs/ig-uu7.4-sol.json): PASS, no findings. Suggest a bead under ig-7sn.

title: Hero AI 2: knights cover a back-row hero that an enemy is on (walk over, hit pulls aggro, Toss aims there)
description:
Parent: the hero AI epic. Owner: "tanks/front line heroes should be aware of backline units getting aggro, and should try to take aggro back (using skills or 'your suggestion')".

## Rule
- Threat: a living enemy whose order_target_id is a back-row ally, within battle_detection_range (12) of a knight.
- Each threat gets at most one knight. Knights on auto claim in spawn_index order. A knight picks: (.4 adds bond order first) lowest victim HP fraction, then nearest threat, then spawn_index. It gets an auto ATTACK order on that threat.
- Aggro pull (director pick for "your suggestion"): when a knight's hit (basic or weaponskill) lands on an enemy whose target is a back-row ally, that enemy gets a taunt status from the knight (PROVISIONAL 3 s). It then targets the knight and, being sticky, stays on it. Reuses the existing taunt status: no new mechanic.
- Gauntlet Toss (knight_gauntlet_toss): its AI also fires when the victim is back-row, not only lower HP fraction, and it aims at the knight's claimed threat first. Update its SYSTEMS.md skills row.
- Rogues do not cover.

## Acceptance (GUT)
- An enemy locked on a mage, a knight 8 units away: the knight walks over, hits, and the enemy's target is the knight right after that hit.
- Two knights, two threatened back-row allies: one knight each.
- A level-1 knight (no Toss) still pulls through the hit.
- Same seed twice gives the same result.
design:
FINAL DESIGN (2026-09-24). Rule text: docs/SYSTEMS.md § Hero AI on auto, Cover. The Gauntlet Toss row is already updated there. This field overrides the description where they differ.

CHANGES VS THE DESCRIPTION
- Threat zone follows the stance instead of a flat 12 from the knight:
  - Stay Together: within battle_cohesion_wait_distance (6) of the leader;
  - Defend: within battle_guard_radius (4) of the anchor;
  - Protect: within 4 of the guarded ally;
  - Advance: within battle_detection_range (12) of the knight.
  Answer to the director: cover respects the stance radii. It chooses only after the stance's regroup, anchor or guard check has had its chance to return, so cover never pulls a knight out of its stance and never fights the regroup.
- Only back-row allies in the knight's own squad count as victims.
- Sticky claim (fixes ping-pong): a knight keeps its previous threat while it is still a threat. It never picks a threat that any other living knight already targets: earlier knights this tick, later knights from last tick, because sticky knights keep what they hold.
- New-pick order: the victim's place in the knight's cover_order (.4; listed before unlisted), then the lowest victim HP fraction, then the nearest threat, then state.actors order.
- Aggro pull: EVERY direct knight hit, meaning anything through _damage (basics, weaponskills and ability hits such as Buckler Blow), not bleed or burn ticks. Two differences from the description: it is not limited to basics and weaponskills (one hook covers everything), and it also fires when the knight is under a direct order. Reason: it is a trait of the hit and moves nobody, so it takes no control from the player. Flagged to the director; restricting it to auto is one extra condition.
- Acceptance fix: enemy targets are chosen at the start of a tick, so the enemy switches on the tick AFTER the hit, not "right after the hit".

WHERE (combat/battle/battle_simulation.gd)
- _choose_squad_intention (l.1981), for an archetype "knight" ally: after the stance block computes its zone centre and `target`, and before l.2015, run the cover pick. If it finds a threat, that becomes `target`.
- Add a previous_target_id parameter (default ""). _choose_intentions already holds it in a local (l.478), taken before the order is cleared at l.479-481; this is ig-ls3's carry pattern.
- One pass over state.actors collects three things:
  (a) living back-row allies of the knight's squad, as a small id -> actor map;
  (b) living enemies inside the zone;
  (c) order_target_ids of other living allied knights.
  After the pass: threats = (b) whose order_target_id is in (a). Keep previous_target_id if it is in threats (.4 may preempt). Otherwise pick from threats not in (c).
- Aggro pull: at the end of _damage (l.1712), if attacker.faction == "ally", attacker.archetype == "knight", the target is still alive, and _actor_by_id(target.order_target_id) is a living back-row ally:
  _add_status(target, "knight_cover", "taunt", attacker.id, BALANCE.battle_cover_taunt_seconds, 1.0).
  _choose_enemy_intention already obeys _taunter, and enemies keep their target, so the pull lasts after the taunt ends.
- Gauntlet Toss: in _rule_aim "enemy_on_weaker_ally" (l.1315), first return the knight's own order target when it is within skill.range_units and its target is a back-row ally. Otherwise use the existing loop, now firing when the victim is back-row OR has a lower HP fraction. Only knight_gauntlet_toss.tres uses this rule, so change it in place. Update its doc comment at combat/abilities/ability_definition.gd:22.
- New balance.tres field: battle_cover_taunt_seconds = 3.0, PROVISIONAL (SYSTEMS table).

ACCEPTANCE (GUT; replaces the description's list)
- An enemy locked on a mage, a knight 8 units away (Advance). The knight walks over and hits. On the tick after that hit, the enemy targets the knight, and it still does after the 3 s taunt has ended.
- Two knights, two threatened back-row allies: one knight each, and neither claim changes over 10 s while both threats live.
- A level-1 knight (no Toss) still pulls through the hit.
- Defend: a threat on a back-row ally more than 4 from the anchor does not draw the knight out.
- A knight hit on an enemy targeting a rogue or another knight adds no taunt.
- Toss with a covered threat within 6: it aims at that threat.
- The same seed twice gives the same result.

COST
- One O(n) pass per knight per tick, plus one _actor_by_id lookup per knight hit, not per tick.
- Worst case: Frontier March, 50v30. Measure it with .1 (CODING_RULES § Performance).

Aggro pull at end of _damage: any direct knight hit on an enemy targeting a living back-row ally adds taunt knight_cover for battle_cover_taunt_seconds (3.0, balance.tres + balance_table.gd). title: Hero AI 1: the back row waits behind the front line until its squad is in contact
description:
Parent: the hero AI epic. Owner: "backline units should not race in front of frontline units during initial engagement".

## Rule
While no living enemy targets anyone in its squad, a back-row hero (ranger, mage, cleric) on auto never takes a step that ends closer to its reference point than the squad's nearest living front-liner (knight, rogue) is to that same point, plus one formation spacing (battle_formation_spacing, 1.8). Reference point: its attack target, or with no target the nearest living enemy. Steps that keep or grow that distance are always allowed (retreat, evasion, kiting).

Stateless on purpose: it turns off at contact and back on when the squad is free again, so the next wave's approach gets it too. No living front-liner in the squad: rule off (today's behaviour). No spawn-layout change: the rule alone keeps the back row behind.

## Acceptance (GUT, headless)
- Knight, knight, ranger, mage, cleric with the back row faster than the knights: before contact, no back-row hero is ever nearer the nearest enemy than the nearest knight, and the first enemy lock-on is a knight.
- Stay Together with a back-row leader (lowest spawn_index) still reaches contact: no stall.
- A squad with no front-liner moves exactly as today for a fixed seed (positions equal tick by tick).
- A direct move order on a back-row hero ignores the rule.
design:
FINAL DESIGN (2026-09-24). Rule text: docs/SYSTEMS.md § Hero AI on auto, Formation. This field overrides the description where they differ.

CHANGES VS THE DESCRIPTION
- Reference point: the attack target, else _assigned_objective_point. Not "the nearest living enemy": in a region, a camp off to the side would block a valid path.
- Contact test: the rule is off while any living enemy is within max(battle_detection_range, attack_range) of this hero. This replaces "no living enemy targets anyone in its squad", which needs an id lookup per enemy (O(n^2)). It matches the enemy detection range, so the first enemy to notice the squad finds the front-liner, 1.8 nearer. The max() keeps a ranger with basic_range (reach over 12) from losing shots.
- Advance and Stay Together only. Defend and Protect already hold the squad on one spot; their "move to the anchor" is centring, not a march.
- Runs after ig-axw (a dependency is set). Once that fix lands, the supplies retreat returns before the squad path, so this rule never sees a retreating hero.

WHERE (combat/battle/battle_simulation.gd)
- In _choose_squad_intention (l.1981), only at the final pick (l.2015-2018), for a back-row hero (ranger, mage, cleric) under Advance or Stay Together. The regroup, anchor and guard returns above it are untouched, so they are exempt by construction. Evasion, direct orders and rescue never reach this function.
- One pass over state.actors. If any living enemy is within contact range, stop: the rule is off. Otherwise collect this squad's living front-liners (knight, rogue) into a short list. .3 adds its fields to this same pass.
- ref = the target's position, else the objective. D_f = the distance from ref to the nearest front-liner in the list; cap = D_f + battle_formation_spacing.
  - If distance(actor, ref) > cap: _set_auto_order(actor, COMMAND_MOVE, "", ref + (actor.position - ref).normalized() * cap).
  - Else: _set_auto_order(actor, COMMAND_HOLD, "", actor.position).
- No _move_actors change: a MOVE stops exactly at its point. No new balance fields.

WHY IT CANNOT STALL
- Stay Together targets lie within 6 of a leader the hero stays within 4 of. That is always inside contact range, so the rule never touches a Stay Together target; it shapes only the march.
- A back-row leader holds until a front-liner is 1.8 ahead. Followers roam up to 4 ahead before they regroup, so every cycle gains about 2 units.
- A hero may pause while its front-liner is off covering (.2). It moves on when the front-liner does. It never holds with an enemy in contact range.

ACCEPTANCE (GUT, headless; replaces the description's list)
- Knight, knight, ranger, mage, cleric, with the back row faster, under Advance and again under Stay Together. Until the first enemy lock-on, a back-row hero never ends a tick nearer its ref than it began, unless it is still at least (nearest front-liner's distance + 1.8 - 0.001) from that ref. The first enemy lock-on is a knight.
- Stay Together with a back-row leader (spawn_index 0 is a mage) reaches its first lock-on before the timeout: no stall.
- A squad with no front-liner, and any squad under Defend or Protect: positions equal today's tick by tick for a fixed seed.
- A direct move order on a back-row hero ignores the rule.

COST
- One O(n) pass per back-row hero per tick (shared with .3), then work on a list no longer than the squad.
- Worst case: Frontier March, 50 heroes against 30. Measure best and worst of seven at that case (CODING_RULES § Performance) and compare with SYSTEMS § Performance budgets, Watched battle.
acceptance_criteria:
GUT, headless. This replaces the ACCEPTANCE list in the design field (director ruling 2026-09-24, option A; bullet 2 worded by high1 against the level spawn row).
- Knight, knight, ranger, mage, cleric, with the back row faster, under Advance and again under Stay Together. Until the first enemy lock-on:
  (1) no formation-ordered step (a MOVE point the rule sets) that comes closer goes inside the nearest front-liner's distance + 1.8 from the ref;
  (2) no back-row hero comes closer to its ref and ends the tick nearer than the nearest front-liner. The level spawn row may start one a hair ahead; the rule holds it there.
  The first enemy lock-on (every lock-on on that tick) is a knight.
  EXEMPT, per SYSTEMS § Hero AI on auto ('never walks closer'; the stance's regroup comes before formation; no _move_actors change): the Stay Together regroup walk, and the separation nudge on a holding hero.
- Stay Together with a back-row leader (spawn_index 0 is a mage) reaches its first lock-on before the timeout: no stall.
- A squad with no front-liner, and any squad under Defend or Protect: position digests equal the old code's over 400 ticks for a fixed seed.
- A direct move order on a back-row hero ignores the rule.
- Cost at Frontier March 50v30 is measured (best and worst of seven) and compared with § Performance budgets.
notes:
high1 STATUS partial (HOLD, needs a ruling). Code: combat/battle/battle_simulation.gd FRONT_ROW/BACK_ROW consts + _formation_order() called at the final pick of _choose_squad_intention for back-row under advance/stay_together (no hot-path allocation). Tests: tests/unit/test_formation.gd (+.uid) 5 tests: formation under advance+stay_together (ordered step >= D_f+1.8; end position never closer-and-ahead of the front line; every first lock-on a knight), back-row leader no stall, exact-bit position digests unchanged for no-front-liner advance/stay_together and full party defend/protect (recorded on old code), direct move ignores rule, cost print. Old code fails the main test. BUILT: gate 0, GUT 54 scripts 791/791, 0 SCRIPT ERROR. Cost frontier_march 50v30 one tick best 5.95 ms worst 6.03 ms, same as without the rule. Sol R1 FAIL (array literal in hot path; test gaps) fixed. Sol R2 FAIL: design acceptance says END of tick >= D_f+1.8-0.001; not met under stay_together: probe worst = holding cleric 1.05 inside the spacing (regroup walk brought it in, exempt per design WHERE; _apply_separation nudged it 0.12 more; separation runs on HOLD, :535). Advance meets the literal acceptance exactly (worst short 0.0000). Conflict inside the design (WHERE exempts regroup and says no _move_actors change vs acceptance). Options sent to director. Also open notes: escort (ref = moving cart) untested; a front-liner that never advances holds the back row (design accepts). Evidence .agent-results/ig-uu7.1/.
Director ruling 2026-09-24: option A. The design's acceptance ('never ends a tick nearer its ref... unless >= D_f+1.8-0.001') conflicted with its own exemptions: the regroup walk comes first by precedence, separation runs on HOLD at :535, and there is no _move_actors change. SYSTEMS says a back-row hero never WALKS closer, which the tests prove. Sol R1 said the acceptance must be read with the regroup exemption; Sol R2's FAIL was only against the literal wording. No code change. Not required now: an escort test, and a front-liner that never advances holds the back row (the design accepts pausing).
close_reason: The back row waits behind the front line until contact, per SYSTEMS § Hero AI on auto (Formation). Commit e39f5a4. Director BUILT green: 54 scripts, 791/791, gate 0/0, FP stable. Acceptance amended by director ruling A (the regroup walk and separation are exempt; bullet 2 worded for the level spawn row). Sol R2's FAIL was only against the old wording.

title: Smarter hero AI in battles: formation, knights cover the back row, bounded kiting, bonds pick who is covered
description:
Owner ask (2026-09-24), verbatim: "ranged or vulnerable heroes should automatically try to make distance if enemies try to close the distance, but not get stuck in a infinite wild goose chase / tanks/front line heroes should be aware of backline units getting aggro, and should try to take aggro back(using skills or "your suggestion" if backline is being targeted. but maybe here we have room for the relationship mechanic where they will cover their friends or lovers first, then others. / backline units should not race in front of frontline units during initial engagement"

## Why it happens today (combat/battle/battle_simulation.gd)
- Enemies lock onto the nearest hero within 12 and keep it until it dies or leaves the 18 leash (_choose_enemy_intention). Only a taunt switches them (_taunter).
- Heroes spawn in one row of five (_grid_offset, count = max(i+1, 5)), not front/back, and each walks at its own SPD speed (1.5-5 u/s). Fast back-row heroes arrive first and get locked on.
- Ally ranged range is 12.0 and enemy detection is 12.0, so a ranger that stops at its range already sits inside detection.
- Clerics use melee range 1.6 (_attack_range makes only ranger/mage ranged), so they walk into melee with the knights.
- A knight's only aggro tool is Gauntlet Toss: level 15, 15 s cooldown, range 6, and it fires only on an enemy already within 6 of the knight that hits a lower-HP-fraction ally (ai_rule enemy_on_weaker_ally). Knights never move to cover anyone.

Rows (SYSTEMS.md § Archetypes): front = knight, rogue. Back = ranger, mage, cleric. Tank = knight.

## Children, in order
.1 formation, .2 knights cover the back row, .3 back row kites (bounded), .4 bonds pick who is covered first.

## Shared constraints (every child)
- Allies on auto only. A direct order (direct_order) and telegraph evasion (evade_point) win over all of this. Enemy AI unchanged.
- Deterministic: ties by spawn_index, no new RNG draws, iterate in state.actors order.
- Cost: at most one extra O(n) scan per ally per tick (the tick is already O(n^2) through _apply_separation). No new per-tick Array/Dictionary allocation in the hot loop. Worst cases: fallen_citadel 30v30, frontier_march 50v30. Dispatched battles tick inside hub.gd's 0.25 s pulse on the main thread (DECISIONS.md "Performance: budgets at each scene's worst case" ADR).
- Saved battle snapshots: new per-actor state is an OPTIONAL effect_state key, validated only when present (the last_counter_tick pattern in combat/battle/battle_actor.gd). SIMULATION_VERSION stays 1. A legacy snapshot without the keys must load and advance. Risky boundary #1: Sol review mandatory.
- Docs: SYSTEMS.md carries the rules and numbers (new numbers marked PROVISIONAL), and the Gauntlet Toss row if its AI rule changes.
- Balance gate (the ig-544 pattern, SYSTEMS.md :166-176): after .3, and again after .4 if it moves anything, re-run the eight ig-544 starter cases on the same seeds. Any loss, any new downing in a supplied case, or a clear-time shift over 15% goes back to design.
notes:
2026-09-24 director: epic filed from the owner's ask. The extra design pass was dispatched (rules pressure test, numbers, SYSTEMS.md subsection, child design fields). high1 starts .1 after ig-m6o.2.2.1, in order .1 → .2 → .3 → .4, reading each child's design field first. Owner told: a knight's hit taunts (director pick), hops go toward the tank with a cooldown, partner first then most shared points, and no friend/lover tiers exist.
CHECKPOINT 2026-09-24 (design pass, session "game" docs-only). Nothing written yet: no SYSTEMS.md edit, no --design field set on any child. Code reads are done; all decisions below are final unless noted.

PRECEDENCE (all four): direct order > evade_point > kite (.3) > cover (.2) / formation (.1) > normal. None apply in rescue battles, to carriers, or to RETREAT orders. All hook into the auto-squad path after the rescue branch in _choose_intentions, so anything that continues earlier wins for free.

.1 FORMATION, changes vs director text:
- Reference point = attack target, else the squad objective point (_assigned_objective_point), NOT the nearest enemy (a region camp in another direction would block a valid path).
- Contact test, stateless, one fused O(n) pass: rule off while any living enemy is within battle_detection_range (12) of this back-row hero. Replaces "no enemy targets anyone in its squad" (needs id lookups, O(n^2)). Enemies lock the nearest ally, so the knight is still picked first.
- Caps only auto ATTACK approaches and objective MOVEs. Exempt: stay_together regroup, defend-anchor return, protect GUARD, evade, kite, retreat.
- Off while escort_active (the cart is the formation).
- Stay Together, back-row leader: followers may walk up to 4 ahead, leader may close to 1.8 behind the front-liner: progresses, no stall.
- Step clamp lives in _move_actors (min of existing step and the cap). No new numbers: battle_formation_spacing, battle_detection_range.

.2 COVER, changes:
- Threat radius respects stance: stay_together within 6 of leader; defend within 4 of anchor; protect within 4 of protected actor; advance within 12 of the knight. Cover picks its target AFTER the stance regroup/anchor/guard checks return (else cover vs regroup oscillates).
- Sticky claim fixes ping-pong: keep previous_target_id (the ig-ls3 carry pattern) while it is still a threat; re-pick only when invalid; skip threats already claimed by a knight earlier in state.actors order.
- Aggro pull: knight hit on an enemy targeting a back-row ally -> _add_status(enemy, "knight_cover", "taunt", knight.id, battle_cover_taunt_seconds, 1.0). Recommend ANY knight hit incl. direct orders (class trait, moves no one) = change vs "auto only", flag to director.
- Acceptance fix: enemy retargets on the NEXT tick (enemy intentions chosen at tick start), not "right after the hit".
- Toss: aim at the claimed threat if within 6 and still on a back-row ally, else existing loop with (lower HP fraction OR back-row victim). VERIFIED: enemy_on_weaker_ally is used only by knight_gauntlet_toss.tres, so change the rule in place (no new id); update its doc comment at combat/abilities/ability_definition.gd:22.
- SYSTEMS row :443 new text: "Range 6: taunt for 4 s, so that enemy targets the Knight | an enemy on a back-row ally or a lower-HP ally; the Knight's covered threat first".

.3 KITE, changes:
- Who: back-row on auto whose attack_range > battle_kite_trigger_range (can still attack after landing). Excludes clerics (melee 1.6) = the cleric fix.
- Fused into .1's O(n) pass (order_target_id == actor.id, no lookups).
- Hop ends on arrival or when no living enemy targets this hero. An evade clears kite_point; cooldown stays spent. kite_ready_tick = hop-start tick + cooldown ticks.
- create_run erases kite_point and kite_ready_tick (like the last_*_tick resets at battle_simulation.gd:114).
- Validate both only when present (battle_actor.gd last_counter_tick pattern).
- Goose chase bounded: 4 u hop ~1.1 s, enemy re-closes ~2.5 s, one hop per 5 s.
CLERIC ANSWER: yes .3 loops (hop, walk back to melee, cooldown, hop) when no knight pulls. Smallest fix: the attack_range > trigger condition. Owner question: "Clerics stay melee swingers that do not hop (pick), or become stand-back healers at Mend range 6?"

NUMBERS (all PROVISIONAL, Settled by: epic balance gate on the eight ig-544 starter cases + a played build):
- battle_kite_trigger_range 3.0 keep: ~0.9 s warning before a 1.5 u/s enemy reaches melee 1.6.
- battle_kite_distance 4.0 keep: one hop clears the trigger zone (3 + 4 - 1.65 > 3).
- battle_kite_cooldown_seconds 5.0 keep: <= 12 hops/min, ~2.4 s fighting per cycle.
- battle_cover_taunt_seconds 3.0 keep: = battle_basic_interval_max 3.0, holds until the knight's next swing at any SPD.

.4 BONDS, changes:
- cover_order = partner first (Bonds' own pick), then back-row teammates with points > 0, most first, ties spawn_index. Filter to back row at snapshot time.
- VERIFIED: _team_snapshots (game_session.gd:1281) has neither max_hp nor effect_state, so the from_dict path (battle_simulation.gd:841) is not hit today. Pick: a top-level snapshot key cover_order copied into actor effect_state in _actor_from_team_snapshot (snapshot.effect_state would flip to from_dict if max_hp is ever added).
- GameSession must not read hub.gd's kept index. One Bonds.index pass inside _team_snapshots covers every launch (callers :1129 :1155 :1159 :1394 :1790 :2089 :2095; a dispatch calls it 3x incl. forecasts). Measure per CODING_RULES Performance; over budget -> unsaved ledger-keyed cache in GameSession.
- Preempt only to a victim strictly higher in cover_order: stable.
- TODO dep: bd dep add ig-uu7.4 ig-m6o.2.2.1. Validate cover_order (Array of String) when present; legacy [].

COST: one fused O(n) pass per ally per tick; knight re-pick bounded lookups, sticky steady state 2. Worst case 50v30.

FINDINGS for director:
1. retreat_when_supplies_empty is DEAD: override at battle_simulation.gd:445-449 sets RETREAT, then :479-481 clears every non-direct order, then :511 squad intention overwrites. Dead with auto on AND off. No test covers it (only test_battle_hub sets it false). Needs a bug bead.
2. evade_point is not validated in battle_actor.gd validate_dict (gap, mention only).
3. create_run must reset the kite keys.
4. .2 acceptance next-tick fix.

LEFT TO DO: SYSTEMS.md subsection after stances/enemies paras (~:42-52, before "### Provisional shared combat numbers"); Toss row :443; bd update ig-uu7.1..4 --design-file; the .4 dep; STATUS to director.
2026-09-24 director: gate reading from ig-uu7.3 (design): a clear-time shift over 15% counts when the clear is slower, or faster with more downings. A faster clear with fewer downings is the feature working. Recorded in SYSTEMS (after-kiting baseline).
close_reason: All five parts landed: formation (.1), knight cover (.2), bounded kiting (.3), bond-first cover (.4), downing table (.5). Balance gate after .4: the 8 cases are unchanged from the ig-el4 baseline. The kiting and cover numbers stay PROVISIONAL in SYSTEMS until the owner plays them.

title: Window opens at 1920x1080, plus a window-size picker in the pause menu
description:
WHY
Owner, 2026-09-24: "please make the game window 1920x1080, and put in a resolution picker".

FACTS (director, checked)
- project.godot [display]: viewport 1280x720, stretch mode canvas_items, aspect keep (default). No display code exists anywhere.
- systems/settings.gd: a static ConfigFile store (user://settings.cfg), outside the save on purpose, not an autoload. Screen shake lives there.
- ui/pause_menu.gd shows Screen shake (%ScreenShake). The main scene is res://ui/main_menu.tscn. Autoloads: SceneRouter, SaveService, GameSession.

BEHAVIOR
1. The base stays 1280x720 with canvas_items, so the UI scales up and every layout and 720 test stays valid. Do NOT change viewport_width/height.
2. The window opens at 1920x1080: project.godot window/size/window_width_override=1920 and window_height_override=1080, so there is no resize flash.
3. The picker. Settings gains a "display" section with a "window_size" key: "1280x720", "1600x900", "1920x1080", "2560x1440", "3840x2160" or "fullscreen". The default is "1920x1080". A bad value falls back to the default, like screen_shake.
   - The pause menu shows a "Window size" OptionButton beside Screen shake. It lists only the 16:9 sizes that fit the current screen's usable area, plus "Fullscreen" (DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN).
   - Picking one applies at once (windowed mode, window_set_size, centered on the screen) and saves.
4. At startup, apply the saved choice once (SceneRouter._ready, or the main menu with a once-guard; implementer's pick). If the saved size doesn't fit the usable screen area, use the largest listed size that does. In headless, the DisplayServer calls should be harmless no-ops.
5. Nothing goes in the save. No new autoload.

ACCEPTANCE
- Tests (tests/unit, APPDATA redirected):
  - The settings round-trip works, and a bad value gives the default.
  - The size list is a pure static function of a given screen size: a 1920x1080 screen does not list 2560x1440, and a 3840x2160 screen lists all five.
  - "fullscreen" maps to the fullscreen mode.
- BUILT, with every existing layout and click test unchanged (the 2D space stays 1280x720).
- A windowed run with no "game" process running: screenshots at 1920x1080 of the hub and of the pause menu with the picker.
- A verifier pass is mandatory (Sol): boundary #2, the new %WindowSize node and its signal connection in pause_menu.tscn.

NON-GOALS
Render scale, vsync, choosing a monitor, non-16:9 sizes, a main-menu options screen.
notes:
Implemented (uncommitted): project.godot overrides 1920x1080; Settings display/window_size + window_sizes_for/effective_window_size/window_mode_for/window_sizes_here (subtracts title bar+borders)/apply_window_size (headless no-op); SceneRouter._ready applies once; pause_menu %WindowSize (VBox/WindowRow/WindowSize) + item_selected connection; tests/unit/test_window_size.gd (5). BUILT: gate 0, GUT 775/775, 0 SCRIPT ERROR (.agent-results/ig-qoz/gut-3.log). Windowed shots (no game process): hub_1920.png, pause_menu.png, pause_menu_picker_open.png; shots.log window 1920x1080 on a 2560x1440 usable screen, picker lists 1280/1600/1920+Fullscreen. Sol review running.
Sol round 1 FAIL (borderless after fullscreen; stale picker; '01280x720' accepted; test hook null) -> all fixed. Round 2 FAIL (fullscreen frame 0 lists too-big size; picker ticks effective not actual) -> fixed (_frame remembered while windowed; window_size_now). Round 3: A closed, B open (add_item auto-ticks first item) -> fixed (select(ticked) with -1), asserted in test. Final BUILT: gate 0 (gate-5.log), GUT 776/776 0 SCRIPT ERROR (gut-6.log). HOLD for director BUILT.

Sol ran 3 rounds; the seam (%WindowSize, item_selected, load_steps) was OK from round 1 and every finding was fixed. The last 4-line fix, select(ticked or -1) so add_item stops auto-ticking the first item, had no 4th Sol pass. It was accepted on a director read plus its test assert. title: Living-world 2.2: the line bank (several lines per fact, from Ledger facts)
description:
WHY
Owner, on the seeded Mara/Dunn save: "dunn only has 1 line". Each shared fact has exactly one greeting today (Bonds.greeting), so every meeting repeats it. Owner decision, 2026-09-24: "Line bank now, LLM test after". This slice is the authored bank.
ig-c2s (the LLM spike) waits on it. The spike needs the same fact inputs, and the bank is its baseline.
Design: GAME_SPEC.md § Scope boundaries (amended 2026-09-24: spoken lines from Ledger facts leave the dialogue item with this slice). SYSTEMS.md § Bonds and dreams, slice 1.

RULED
- Lines are authored text with slots for names and places, filled from Ledger facts. No runtime model, and nothing designed for one. One function that returns a line for a set of facts is the whole seam (owner, via the director).
- A line says only what its facts hold. No invented places, people or events.
- No saved state. How many times a pair has met is view state, reset on load.

BEHAVIOR
1. One function. New history/lines.gd, class_name Lines: Lines.line(facts: Dictionary, pick: int) -> String. It returns the pick-th candidate for those facts (wrapping), with its slots filled. It is a pure static function and reads no GameSession, so TownView may call it, like Ledger.zone_name.
2. The facts. hub.gd builds one facts dictionary for the partner's greeting, from the kept bond index and the speaker's dream:
   - kinds: the strongest shared fact's kind ("saved_by", "saved", "death" or "hard", as ig-m6o.2.1 defines them), plus "debt" while the speaker's open dream owes the listener.
   - slots: {name} the listener, {place} the fact's zone, {dead} the dead hero, {count} the hard fights in words. A slot is present only when its fact gives it.
   The candidates are every bank line under every listed kind.
3. The bank. A const table in history/lines.gd, keyed by kind. At least five lines each for "saved_by", "saved", "death", "hard" and "debt". Each line:
   - uses at least one slot, and only slots its kind always gives;
   - is spoken by the partner to the body, in plain words, under about 70 characters, so the Label3D stays on one or two lines.
   The current four greetings stay in the bank.
4. The pick. TownView gets the facts instead of one fixed line: show_partner(hero, facts). The partner's walker keeps a meeting count and shows Lines.line(facts, start + count) on each greeting.
   - start is a fixed hash of the two ids, so different pairs don't open on the same line.
   - With two or more candidates, two meetings in a row never show the same line.
   - The count resets on load and when the partner or the facts change.
5. Nothing else moves. The detail panel's bond line and dream lines are UI text, not speech. They stay in bonds.gd.

SAVE
None.

ACCEPTANCE (tests/unit, APPDATA redirected)
- The bank: at least five lines under each of the five kinds. Every line fills with no "{" left. Every line uses at least one slot, and only slots its kind always gives. "death" lines name the dead hero.
- Picks: two picks in a row for a pair differ, and pick wraps past the last candidate. A pair whose speaker owes the listener gets "debt" lines among its candidates; after the debt is paid or lost, it gets none.
- Town (headless): three approaches in a row show three different lines, and the first approach still shows one (ig-m6o.2.1's test keeps passing). Changing the partner resets the count.
- The owner's case: on the seeded Mara/Dunn save, Dunn has at least ten different lines for Mara ("saved" plus "debt").
- No saved state. No runtime model, new dependency or download.
- BUILT. Verifier pass mandatory: boundary #2 (show_partner's new signature between hub.gd and TownView; the new lines.gd and its .gd.uid pair).
- Close note: ig-c2s is unblocked. The spike uses Lines' facts dictionaries as its inputs and the bank as its baseline.

FILES
- history/lines.gd (new, with its .gd.uid)
- history/bonds.gd (greeting moves into the bank)
- hub/hub.gd (the facts)
- hub/town/town_view.gd, hub/town/town_walker.gd (facts and the meeting count)
- tests/unit/test_lines.gd (new), plus the town test

NON-GOALS
An LLM or any runtime model (ig-c2s). Lines for quirks, encounters or meals (their slices add kinds). Moods. Voiced audio. UI text through the bank. Replies or a dialogue tree. Saved line history.

1. THE FACTS DICTIONARY (hub.gd builds it in _refresh_partner, on roster_changed only)
{"kinds": Array[String], "slots": Dictionary, "start": int}
- kinds: the body's bond fact kind (bond["fact"]["kind"]), then "debt" when the partner's dream is open and owes the body:
  Bonds.dream(ledger, partner_id): state == "open" and owed == body id.
- slots, with keys and no braces, present only when the kind gives them:
  - "name": the body's display name;
  - "place": Ledger.zone_name(fact.zone);
  - "dead": the fact's dead hero, named through Ledger.known_names, falling back to "a hero now forgotten";
  - "count": the hard count in words.
- start: absi(("%s:%s" % [body_id, partner_id]).hash()). String.hash is stable across runs. It lives in the facts, so show_partner keeps one argument and TownView needs no ids; ig-c2s ignores it.
- The dream read costs about 25 ms at the cap, on roster change only. If ig-m6o.2.2.9 has landed, use its hub dream memo instead.

2. LINES (history/lines.gd, class_name Lines, with its .gd.uid)
- BANK: {kind: Array[String]}, a const table pasted from the notes' draft.
- NUMBER_WORDS moves here from bonds.gd; the greeting is its only user.
- line(facts, pick) -> String:
  - the candidates are BANK[kind] for each kind in facts.kinds, in that order;
  - return candidates[(facts.start + pick) % size].format(facts.slots);
  - "" when there are no candidates.
- Bonds.greeting is deleted. Its four lines are the first entry of each bank kind. Its asserts in test_bonds.gd (l.104-115) move to test_lines.gd as line(facts, 0) with start 0.

3. TOWN (the seam, boundary #2)
- TownView.show_partner(hero: Hero, facts: Dictionary) replaces show_partner(hero, line). _partner_line becomes _partner_facts. _attach_partner sets walker.facts.
- When a walker stops being the partner, TownView sets its facts to {}.
- TownWalker: `line` is replaced by `facts` plus a private meeting count. The existing `greetings` test counter stays as it is.
  - Setting facts different from the current ones (Dictionary ==) resets the count to 0.
  - _greet shows Lines.line(facts, count), then count += 1.
- No repeat across a reset: if the pick equals the last line this walker showed and there are 2 or more candidates, it shows the next pick instead. This keeps "two meetings in a row never show the same line" true when the facts change between meetings.
- A load recreates the walkers, so the count starts at 0.

Rebuild the seeded Mara/Dunn records inside tests/unit/test_lines.gd (or a shared helper in test_bonds.gd), copying the record list from .agent-results/ig-m6o.2.1/seed_save.gd. ig-m6o.2.2.9 also edits hub._refresh_partner, hub._bond_index and bonds.gd. Run the two one after the other, never in parallel. Either order works; whichever goes second rebases on the first.
