title: Town builder: place buildings, house heroes, assign work (Banished-style layer)
description:
WHY
The owner, 2026-09-23: "It can be anyone. I intend any hero to be able to be able to run any shop pretty much. I also want the player to be able to build their own town, manage work, have the heros have their own house, city management like the game banished". The town builder is no longer parked. It is the direction.

SPEC
- Design: GAME_SPEC.md § The town builder, and § Heroes eat, and can starve to death
- Numbers: SYSTEMS.md § Town builder (all PROVISIONAL)
- Boundaries: DECISIONS.md "2026-09-23: The town builder" (accepted 2026-09-23; items 11 and 12 fold in the owner's answers), ARCHITECTURE.md § The town is the interface, and rule 8's amendment (accepted 2026-09-23)

OWNER RULINGS, 2026-09-23 (all four questions answered)
1. Houses: a house is needed for a workplace job. Fighters and fodder need none. Hall keepers need none for now.
2. Food: "They eat and can starve to death." Chosen against our recommendation, knowingly. Starvation goes through kill_hero(); a warning ladder makes every death visible; the death clock stops at a last warning until the player looks; only housed heroes who are home eat; nothing happens while the game is closed.
3. Job skills: "I like the rimworld inspired multi passion idea." Eight professions (the five halls plus woodcutting, mining, farming). Every hero has two passions. A Rites passion is 1 in 4 (was 1 in 5). A saved calling becomes the first passion.
4. Offline: live play only.

SLICES
- .1 place a House and a Lumbermill on hexes, house a hero, put it to work, wood goes up (thin first playable)
- .2 the seven halls become placed buildings you can move, and each building type gets its own scene
- .3 stone, and buildings that take time to go up
- .4 hall upgrades also cost wood and stone (changes today's costs)
- .5 food, farms and starvation (warned, never offline)
- .6 heroes walk home and to work (replaces ig-wgj.5, covers ig-wgj.7)
- worker job skills: woodcutting, mining and farming earn XP and a skill bonus (after .1, ig-wgj.10 and the passions bead)

PAUSED IN ig-wgj (fixed-layout work that would be thrown away)
- ig-wgj.5 ambient life: waits for .6, which replaces it
- ig-wgj.6 level visuals: waits for .3
- ig-wgj.7 keepers at work: waits for .2

STILL VALID
The passions bead, then ig-wgj.10 (keeper bonuses), .11 (masterwork draughts), .12 (masterwork gates). None of them reads the layout.
notes:
2026-09-23: the owner ruled that heroes are the shopkeepers (GAME_SPEC § Heroes staff the buildings). Keeper professions are the labor this economy would read: more slots per building means more keepers, and production scales with keeper skill. Non-roster workers still need a Scope-boundaries ruling. Also blocked by ig-wgj.10, so professions exist before the economy is designed.
2026-09-23 game-designer, town lane sweep. Settled in the docs and beads:
- Stone and construction numbers (ig-6m2.3). Wood-only building costs; stone pays only for hall upgrades.
- Hall upgrade wood and stone costs (ig-6m2.4). The parts cost stays.
- The first of each producer is free, a restart rule (ig-6m2.1 addendum, else .3).
- Draughts do not cost food (ig-6m2.5 item 9).
- Walking is cosmetic (ig-6m2.6).
- ig-wgj.6's new tier mapping.
Non-roster workers: settled. GAME_SPEC says "Nobody is hired. The town still has no NPCs": every worker is a roster hero.
The stale needs-owner labels are removed from .1, .2, .3, .4, .6 and .7; the owner answered everything.
The ADR is ACCEPTED, so "PROPOSED" in the bodies is stale.

title: Walk the town as your embodied hero (saved body, protected from spending)
description:
WHY
Owner, 2026-09-23: "we see our heros walking around". GAME_SPEC § The town avatar (ruled 2026-08-13, pinned down 2026-09-23) says the player walks the town as one of their own roster heroes. That hero is swappable, and while embodied it cannot be spent. This bead adds the body and its save state. See ARCHITECTURE.md § The town is the interface and DECISIONS.md 2026-09-23.

BEHAVIOR
1. New hub/town/town_hero.gd: a CharacterBody3D built with heroes/hero_model.gd (from the loader bead).
   - WASD and arrow keys move it, relative to the camera.
   - Clips: Idle when still, Walking_A when moving.
   - A follow camera with zoom.
   - With no body, the town shows the fixed overview camera, as today.
2. Clicking a far building follows the owner's answer to the far-click question. Default: the body walks there, then the panel opens.
   - With no body, a click opens the panel at once.
   - A click never walks the body through a building. Straight line with a stop radius; no navmesh.
3. The hero detail panel gets a "Walk as this hero" button. The HUD gets a "Step out" button.
   - The choice is deliberate. There is no auto-pick.
4. GameSession gets:
   - embodied_hero_id: int, where -1 means none
   - embody_hero(id) -> bool: refused if the hero is busy (is_hero_busy) or not on the roster
   - step_out()
   It emits the existing roster_changed signal. No new signal unless one is needed.
5. Protection:
   - is_hero_protected() (game_session.gd:434) returns true for the body. That makes sacrifice refuse it.
   - Each dispatch entry point refuses a party that contains the body, with a message that names the hero:
     - dispatch_expedition (:526)
     - dispatch_force, via _preview_force_data (:600-622)
     - dispatch_rescue (:833)
     - recover_cache (:166)
   - Grep every is_hero_busy caller first. Any other path that reserves a hero gets the same check.
   - Do NOT fold the body into is_hero_busy(). The body can still be geared, enhanced and ranked up.
6. If the body leaves the roster by any path, the body resets to -1 and the town returns to the overview.

SAVE
- Additive key "embodied_hero_id" in GameSession.to_dict/from_dict (keys around game_session.gd:1824-1844).
- A missing key, a stale id or a busy hero loads as -1.
- Do not bump SAVE_VERSION unless an additive key forces it (P2-23 precedent).

ACCEPTANCE
- It survives save and reload: embody a hero, save through SaveService to disk, reload, and the same hero is the body. Prove it with a real disk round-trip, not to_dict alone.
- A save without the key loads with no body and no error.
- Tests:
  - each dispatch entry point refuses the body
  - sacrifice refuses the body
  - equip, enhance and rank-up on the body are allowed
  - embody_hero refuses a busy hero
  - the body resets when its hero leaves the roster
- BUILT: the import gate shows zero errors and zero warnings, and GUT is green.
- Screenshot evidence of walking and of the follow camera, in .agent-results/<id>/.
- Boundaries #1 (save) and #2 (scene<->script) make a verifier pass mandatory.

FILES
- new: hub/town/town_hero.gd (+ .uid)
- hub/town/town.tscn, hub/town/town_view.gd, hub/hub.gd, hub/hub_ui_builder.gd
- systems/game_session.gd
- tests/unit/test_town_hero.gd, tests/unit/test_game_session.gd (or the save test file that covers to_dict)

NON-GOALS
ambient heroes; NPCs; pathfinding or navmesh; jumping or combat in town; proximity-only interaction; gamepad input (controller work is on hold).
notes:
2026-09-23 staffing ruling (DECISIONS 2026-09-23 item 5): a stationed keeper CAN be the body, and its building keeps working. embody_hero must not refuse keepers; the station is not a busy state. ig-wgj.9 also edits is_hero_protected() and game_session.gd, so do not run the two at the same time.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-23 (uncommitted, nothing staged). STATUS: done pending the mandatory verifier.
Files: systems/game_session.gd; NEW hub/town/town_hero.gd(+.uid); hub/town/town_view.gd; hub/hub.gd; hub/hub_ui_builder.gd; NEW tests/unit/test_town_hero.gd(+.uid); tests/unit/test_save_service.gd. town.tscn was NOT touched: the body is built in code, like the battle's units.
SPEC ADAPTATION: the bead says embodied_hero_id: int, -1 = none. Hero ids are 32-hex String instance_ids, so it is a String with GameSession.NO_BODY = "" meaning none.
GameSession:
- embody_hero(id)->bool refuses a hero that is missing or away, sets last_action_error and emits roster_changed. step_out() also emits.
- is_embodied(). is_hero_protected() now includes the body; is_hero_busy() does not.
- A shared _body_refusal(team) refuses a party containing the body with '<name> is your body in town. Step out first.' It runs in _preview_force_data (covers dispatch_expedition, preview_force and dispatch_force), in dispatch_rescue and in recover_cache. recover_cache now sets last_action_error.
- Bulk sacrifice excludes the body with reason 'town body'. kill_hero resets the body.
- to_dict adds 'embodied_hero_id'. from_dict reads it last: missing, non-String, stale or away all load as NO_BODY. No SAVE_VERSION bump.
Town and hub:
- TownHero is a CharacterBody3D (layer 0, mask PICK_LAYER, floating) built with HeroModel at x0.75. No archetype draws the knight.
- Movement: WASD/arrows via Input.is_physical_key_pressed, camera-relative. Idle_A/Walking_A. Follow camera with wheel zoom 0.5-2.0.
- walk_to() walks a straight line. ponytail: a walk that stalls for 0.5 s still arrives, because there is no navmesh.
- TownView.embody(hero|null) swaps the body and restores the overview camera. A click with a body walks there, and building_selected fires on arrival (ARRIVE_RADIUS 2.8 covers a corner approach: 2.12 + 0.4).
- Hub: WalkAsHero button in SelectedHeroPanel (it closes the building). StepOut in the footer. The Hint shows WASD/Wheel when embodied.
- walk_enabled is false while a building or pause is open, so keys 1-7 still open panels at once and cancel a walk. Roster flag 'In town'; a state line for the body.
Not testable yet: 'stationed keepers must not be refused'. Hero has no station field yet (ig-wgj.5), and embody_hero only refuses busy heroes, so it holds by construction.
enhance_item acts on inventory items only, so there is no hero-bound enhance path to allow or refuse.
Evidence in .agent-results/ig-wgj.4/: import_gate.log (exit 0, 0 errors/warnings), gut_full.log (446/446), mutation.txt (9 of 9 mutants killed), stage.gd/.tscn/.log and screenshots 1-7.
Finding: test_save_service's test_an_incident_rebuilt_from_a_stranded_rescue_is_repaired_on_load failed once in about 8 full-file runs. It has no body in it and passed 3/3 alone and 3/3 in the full file. Likely a pre-existing flake; not chased.
REVIEW FIXES 2026-09-24 (ACCEPT-WITH-FIXES, uncommitted):
(1) Recovery:
- hub _on_recover_pressed refuses the body before the confirm dialog, via GameSession.body_refusal (renamed from _body_refusal, now public).
- _do_recover shows last_action_error on RECOVERY_INVALID_TEAM when it is set.
(2) Save tests:
- The round trip asserts NO_BODY after clearing and before reloading.
- The legacy test embodies a hero first, then loads a save with no key and gets NO_BODY.
(3) TownHero._input consumes arrow keys while controls are on, so the GUI can't move focus with them. Movement polls Input, which still sees them.
(4) _preset_status returns 'In town: <name>' for a team holding the body. It is not Ready, so recovery, dispatch and practice pickers skip it.
(5) embody_hero and step_out refuse while SaveService.load_blocked.
(6) TownView._unhandled_input ignores building clicks while walk_enabled is off and a body exists.
(7) The body is clamped to the 48 m ground (TownView.WALK_HALF_EXTENT 23.6, TownHero.bounds).
(Optional) Added a wheel-zoom test with a real pushed event.
KNOWN CEILING: with no navmesh, a walk that stalls against another building's wall opens the panel there, at the first wall, after 0.5 s (STUCK_SECONDS).
Sol round 2 (2 fixes), uncommitted:
1) embody_hero/step_out now go through _commit_profile_mutation via _set_body_in_memory, so a blocked load is refused and a failed save rolls back. step_out now returns bool; hub _on_step_out_pressed shows last_action_error. New test test_save_service.gd::test_a_failed_save_rolls_back_embody_and_step_out uses the TMP_PATH-dir seam. PREMISE NOTE: set_hero_favorite does NOT use _commit_profile_mutation; it mutates then autosaves like embody did. The pattern was taken from save_team_preset/_upsert_preset_in_memory.
2) TownView.walk_enabled renamed to input_enabled. It now drops every building click while off, with or without a body. The test was rewritten to cover both cases.
Mutants: embody_unchecked, step_out_unchecked, click_ignores_input_off and walks_behind_panels are all killed (.agent-results/ig-wgj.4/mutation_sol2.txt).

description:
WHY
Town heroes must reuse the battle's KayKit models and the same animation library (director, 2026-09-23). Today that code is private to combat/battle/battle_unit_view.gd:
- ALLY_LOOKS/ENEMY_LOOKS, CLIP_FILES, LOOPED_CLIPS
- the model and weapon part of _build_visual
- the static _shared_clips()
Reaching into it from hub/ couples the town to battle internals, and a copy under hub/ would drift. See ARCHITECTURE.md § The town is the interface and DECISIONS.md 2026-09-23.

BEHAVIOR
1. New heroes/hero_model.gd, static functions only. Its only state is the one static AnimationLibrary. It provides:
   - build(faction, archetype) -> Node3D: the model with its weapons on the handslot bones, and an AnimationPlayer (root_node "..") using the shared library
   - the looks and clip tables
   - the library builder, keeping today's loop flags and the Skeletons_Death root pin
2. Add the town clips that are already staged to the library: Walking_A, Idle_B, Interact, PickUp, Use_Item (Rig_Medium_General / Rig_Medium_MovementBasic).
3. battle_unit_view.gd calls the helper. Battle behavior is unchanged.
4. Harden the silent seams found in the ig-ixj review:
   - push_warning when an archetype falls back to the knight look
   - push_error when a weapon bone is not found on the skeleton
   - a test that asserts the source Skeletons_Death clip has the root position track before the pin removes it

ACCEPTANCE
- The existing battle unit view tests pass, changing only constant references that moved.
- New tests cover:
  - every archetype model loads, and every weapon slot has bone_idx >= 0
  - one shared library across calls
  - the walk and idle clips loop
  - a played clip moves a bone off its rest pose (use chest or spine; hips barely rotate in Hit_A)
- BUILT: the import gate shows zero errors and zero warnings, and GUT is green.
- The scene<->script seam (resource paths, clip names, bone names) makes a verifier pass mandatory.

FILES
- new: heroes/hero_model.gd (+ .uid), tests/unit/test_hero_model.gd
- combat/battle/battle_unit_view.gd, tests/unit/test_battle_unit_view.gd

CONSTRAINTS
- Do not start while any bead that touches combat/battle/battle_unit_view.gd is in progress. As of 2026-09-23 another worker owns combat/battle/*.
- The assets stay where they are, under combat/battle/models/kaykit/. Moving them churns .import/.uid files; a later move is optional.

NON-GOALS
clips from unstaged sets (that is the asset bead); moving asset files; changing how battles look.

title: Town-first UI: click a building to open its panel
description:
WHY
Owner, 2026-09-23: "i basically want our ui to be integrated into the town. ie the we can click on the blacksmith and upgrade from there, summon on the summon place, etc."
The 3D town already exists, but nobody has ever seen it. hub.tscn has five box buildings, each with a Label3D, under Buildings/. hub_ui_builder.gd:11-15 then adds an opaque full-screen ColorRect "Background", and the four tab views cover the screen.
This first slice makes the town visible and turns the buildings into the menu. It has no avatar, no art and no save change.
Spec: GAME_SPEC.md § The town hub (the mapping table); ARCHITECTURE.md § The town is the interface; DECISIONS.md 2026-09-23.

BEHAVIOR
1. Move the Buildings subtree into a new sub-scene, hub/town/town.tscn, instanced in hub.tscn as "Town".
   - Add two placeholder buildings in the same box + Label3D style: TownGate and Apothecary.
   - Every building gets a pickable collision body.
2. New hub/town/town_view.gd emits building_selected(building_id: StringName) on left click.
   - It never touches panels or GameSession.
3. hub.gd maps each building id to its panel, per the GAME_SPEC table:
   - Circle: summon + Circle upgrade
   - Forge: Armory (inventory, equip, salvage, enhance, convert) + Forge upgrade
   - Sanctum: sacrifice and rank-up, with the shared roster, + Sanctum upgrade
   - Training Hall: team presets + practice battle + upgrade
   - Reliquary: recovery + upgrade
   - Town Gate: the Expeditions view
   - Apothecary: supply crafting
   The Hall view's sections and its HALL UPGRADES list split up, so each building shows its own level and upgrade button.
4. No panel is open by default, so the 3D town is visible.
   - Remove the opaque Background.
   - The header currencies and footer status stay as a HUD.
5. Esc closes the open panel first. With no panel open, Esc toggles pause. (Today hub.gd:242-246 only toggles pause.)
6. Fallback: the nav row becomes a compact building list, one button per building, bound to number keys 1-7. Every panel stays reachable by keyboard, because controller support is still a target.
7. A click on a panel never falls through to a building behind it.

ACCEPTANCE
- Every action reachable today is reachable by clicking its building:
  - summon
  - equip, unequip, unequip all
  - salvage, enhance (bulk), convert
  - sacrifice, rank-up
  - save and delete preset
  - dispatch: single, combined and repeat, with battle settings and supply allocations
  - order cards, recent returns, stranded incidents
  - recover cache, start recovery window
  - practice battle
  - craft supplies
  - all 5 building upgrades
  - hero and item favorites
- The same actions are reachable through the building list and its number keys.
- With no panel open, a screenshot shows the 3D town. Evidence goes in .agent-results/<id>/.
- Every existing %UniqueName still resolves.
- The tests that pressed %TeamsTab/%ArmoryTab/%HallTab (tests/unit/test_hub_controls.gd:189-192 and :349) move to the new entry point and still prove the same behavior.
- BUILT: the import gate shows zero errors and zero warnings, and GUT is green (with the APPDATA prefix).
- No save change: GameSession.to_dict() on the same profile is identical before and after.
- Boundary #2 (the scene<->script seam: reparenting, a new sub-scene, input signals, %UniqueName) makes a verifier pass mandatory.

FILES
- hub/hub.tscn, hub/hub.gd, hub/hub_ui_builder.gd
- new: hub/town/town.tscn, hub/town/town_view.gd (+ .uid)
- tests/unit/test_hub_controls.gd
- any tests/unit file that reaches a moved control by absolute path. Grep for get_node paths first: P2-07d's Findings record a re-parent that turned a path-based test red.

NON-GOALS
avatar or walking; camera changes beyond keeping the town framed; art or models; building level visuals; ambient heroes; NPCs; levels for Gate/Apothecary; any GameSession change.

New hub/town/town.tscn (+TownGate, Apothecary; each building MeshInstance3D has Pick StaticBody3D+BoxShape3D) and town_view.gd (TownView, raycast in _unhandled_input, emits building_selected(id); id = building node name). hub.tscn instances it as %Town. hub.gd: BUILDING_PANELS map + _open(id) replaces VIEW_* tabs; Esc closes panel first, else toggles pause. title: Punchier squad battle hit and skill effects (first pass)
description:
Owner 2026-09-23: 'punchier effects for skills and attacks'. Now that units are KayKit models (ig-ixj), the existing effects (combat/battle/battle_vfx.gd: sparks _burst, _expanding_ring, _streak, crit label) read small and flat. First pass, polished later as we go. All values are PROVISIONAL feel numbers: put them as named constants at the top of battle_vfx.gd / battle_unit_view.gd so they can be tuned.

Build exactly these (director list, do not add others):
1. Hit flash: the struck model flashes white for ~0.08s on every landed hit, and stays brighter/longer on crit. Use ONE shared static overlay material (material_overlay) for the whole battle, not per-unit copies.
2. Camera shake: short trauma-style shake on crit and on every skill impact. Never on ordinary hits. It must follow the battle time scale and stop while paused. Put the camera offset on a child or on h_offset/v_offset so it doesn't fight the camera's own positioning in battle_view.gd.
3. Bigger impact bursts: melee hit sparks x2 count and bigger; crits get a second, larger ring. Arrow/magic impacts get a burst at the target, not just a streak.
4. Skill signatures, one per ability in combat/abilities/ (knight_rally, mage_burst, ranger_piercing_shot, rogue_flank_interrupt): a cast flash at the caster + a ground shockwave ring + a larger impact at the target(s). mage_burst is the showpiece: an expanding sphere and the strongest shake. Enemy skills get the same treatment in ENEMY_SKILL_COLOR.
5. Damage numbers pop: scale-in overshoot (~1.3x -> 1.0 over ~0.12s). Crits pop harder. Don't make the resting size any bigger. Readability is already tight (see ig-hpu).
6. Death: a dust puff when the body lands, at the end of the death clip.

Constraints: respect MAX_LIVE_EFFECTS and set_time_scale; shared static materials everywhere; no new autoload; battle_simulation.gd untouched (render-side only). Perf budget: the ig-ixj 60-unit benchmark (.agent-results/ig-ixj/benchmark.gd) render median must stay within +25% of the post-ig-ixj figure (~3.6 ms). Report before/after.

Acceptance: BUILT green (import gate zero errors/warnings + full GUT with APPDATA prefix); tests for the shared flash material (one instance across units), shake only on crit/skill, and time-scale/pause respect; a short sequence of screenshots in .agent-results/<id>/ showing a crit and each skill. Audio is NOT in scope (separate ask).
notes: 2026-09-24 first pass built (6 items only). Files: battle_vfx.gd, battle_unit_view.gd, battle_view.gd, test_battle_vfx.gd, test_battle_unit_view.gd. (1) hit flash: one static ShaderMaterial overlay (instance uniform flash strength), on for 0.08s / crit 0.16s brighter, removed after (extra pass only while flashing); hit-stop holds it. (2) camera shake: trauma from BattleVfx.shake_for (crit hit, every skill, mage/enemy-circle strongest; never ordinary hits), decays in view time, h/v_offset only, zero+held while paused. (3) sparks 14->28, bigger/faster; crits add two rings; projectile impact burst at target after flight. (4) skill signatures knight/ranger/mage/rogue + enemy circle/line + enemy knight/rogue in ENEMY_SKILL_COLOR (skill events now carry faction): cast flash + shockwave ring + big impact; mage = expanding sphere + double ring. (5) damage pop 1.3->1.0 TRANS_BACK 0.12s, crit 2.2 (was 1.8); resting size unchanged. (6) dust puff on body_landed signal at end of animated death clip; death event itself draws nothing now. All effect meshes share one ShaderMaterial (instance uniform tint), all specks one vertex-color material + cached speck meshes. All feel values PROVISIONAL constants. Perf 60-unit bench render median before 3.251/3.259 ms, after 3.313/3.334 (+2%). Mutation-checked flash-shared, shake-only-crit/skill, pause. BUILT gate 0/0, GUT 396/396 11714 asserts. Evidence .agent-results/ig-iml/ (fx_*.png, stage.gd, benchmark logs). Not committed.
close_reason: Six punch items shipped render-side, +2% render median; director re-ran gate + GUT 399/399. Committed.

title: [bug] Enemies face the wrong way when attacking in squad battle
description:
Owner report 2026-09-23 after ig-ixj: enemies face the wrong way when attacking. ig-ixj made the model yaw follow the sim facing exactly (atan2(fx, fy), facing_dot 1.00 in capture), so the model is now honest about whatever facing the sim holds. The ig-ixj review noted the sim aims at the target (battle_simulation.gd:844-845) while facing only turns during movement, so a standing attacker can face away from its target.

Diagnose first, with evidence: is it (a) stale sim facing while attacking, (b) skeleton models authored with the opposite forward axis to the hero models, or (c) something else. Check heroes too: owner named enemies, but confirm whether heroes attacking in place are also wrong.

Fix rules: attackers must visibly face their target during the attack. If the fix is in the sim (updating facing toward the target on attack), note that rogue flank (_is_behind, battle_simulation.gd:990) reads the TARGET's facing. Say in the report how the fix changes when flanks land, and add a test. If the fix is view-only, keep the sim untouched.

Acceptance: a test that fails on the old behavior (a stationary attacker whose facing pointed away now faces its target); a rendered screenshot in .agent-results/<id>/ of enemies mid-attack; BUILT green (import gate + full GUT with APPDATA prefix). A sim change = verifier pass mandatory.
notes:
2026-09-23 diag+fix. Cause (a) stale sim facing: facing only updated by movement (battle_simulation.gd ~487); stationary in-range attackers kept spawn facing (enemies DOWN, allies UP = both away). (b) ruled out: hero visor/skeleton eyes both at +z (0.26-0.34), capes -z. Heroes also affected. Probe before: enemy windups 17/46 away, ally 163/583 away. Fix: _offensive_actions faces target right after range check (+4 lines). After: enemy 0/48 away; ally 57/625 away, all either retargeted (windup target stale, cancelled at :546, facing new target) or out of range walking - no hit lands facing away. Flank change: rogue bonus needs target facing away; an attacking target now faces its own target, so rogue flanks only a target fighting someone else or idle/stunned. Existing rogue test now stuns the target (875 kept); new tests test_stationary_attackers_turn_to_face_their_targets + test_rogue_gets_no_rear_bonus_on_a_target_fighting_it fail on old sim (mutation checked). BUILT: gate exit 0, 0 err/warn; GUT 385/385, 11567 asserts. Evidence .agent-results/ig-oit/. Sim change -> verifier mandatory. Not committed.
2026-09-23 verifier-hard (Claude): ACCEPT-WITH-FIXES. To apply after ig-iml:
F1 (medium): rogue signature teleports behind the target at battle_simulation.gd:826-829 and hits at :832 without re-facing, so it strikes facing away (dot ~ -1). Fix: set facing toward the target after the teleport. Test it.
F2 (low-med): facing now changes inside the _offensive_actions loop, which also evaluates _is_behind (:994) and _rogue_flank_position (:1466). The result depends on actor order: allies come first, so an ally rogue sees last tick's enemy facing and an enemy rogue sees this tick's hero facing. Fix: turn attackers in a separate pass before any damage (a pre-loop at the top of _offensive_actions, keeping the telegraph exclusion). Test it with an enemy that retargets onto the rogue in the same tick.
F4 (low): manual casts (_manual_abilities :917 -> _use_ability) never turn the caster. Fix, and update the stale comment at battle_vfx.gd:108.
F3: the probe logs predate the saved facing_probe.gd (the AWAY lines are missing). Re-run the probe after the fixes and save the logs.
F5 (view, low, PLAUSIBLE): recoil and fling push back along the victim's own facing, not away from the attacker. Not in scope here.
2026-09-24 review fixes F1-F4 applied. F2: _offensive_actions now turns every in-range attacker in a pre-pass (same stun + enemy-telegraph exclusions) before any damage; in-loop turn removed; shared _in_range_target helper used by both passes. F1+F4: _use_ability success tail calls _face(actor, target.position if rogue else point) - covers manual and auto casts, rogue faces target after teleport. Knight self-cast (point == own position) leaves facing alone. battle_vfx.gd ranger comment updated. New tests: test_rogue_signature_faces_the_target_it_lands_behind, test_a_manual_cast_turns_the_caster_to_its_aim, test_rear_bonus_does_not_depend_on_which_side_the_tick_reaches_first (runs both actor orders); all 3 fail on the pre-review ig-oit sim (dot -1, dot 0, 875 vs 900 with allies first). F3: probe re-run, .agent-results/ig-oit/probe_after_review.log has AWAY lines: 56/601 ally windups away, every one in_range=false or order_is_windup_target=false (0 in-range current-target cases); enemy 0/48. Rogue swings from behind 10/27. BUILT: gate 0/0, GUT 399/399 11727 asserts. F5 not touched. Not committed.
close_reason: Attackers face targets via pre-pass; review fixes F1-F4 applied; director re-ran gate + GUT 399/399. Committed.

title: Squad battle units render as KayKit models with KayKit animations
description:
Squad battle units are still primitive capsules (combat/battle/battle_unit_view.gd:_build_visual, :282). Swap them for KayKit models driven by KayKit animations. Assets are staged by the director under combat/battle/models/kaykit/ (CC0; CREDITS.md row exists). Do not add or download other assets.

## Mapping (director decisions, do not redesign)
Allies (faction ally):
- knight -> characters/Knight.glb, weapon sword_1handed + shield (round or badge) in hand slots
- mage -> characters/Mage.glb, weapon staff
- ranger -> characters/Ranger.glb, weapon bow_withString
- rogue -> characters/Rogue.glb, dagger in each hand
- cleric -> characters/Mage.glb + wand (PROVISIONAL, no free cleric model; game-designer call later)
Enemies (faction enemy): knight -> Skeleton_Warrior (+Skeleton_Blade, Skeleton_Shield_Small_A), rogue -> Skeleton_Rogue (+Skeleton_Blade), mage -> Skeleton_Mage (+Skeleton_Staff), ranger -> Skeleton_Rogue (+Skeleton_Crossbow).
Use the model's own hand bone attachments (BoneAttachment3D on handslot.r / handslot.l or whatever the rig names them; read the rig, do not guess).

Clips (all Rig_Medium, one shared AnimationLibrary loaded once, static, not re-imported per unit):
- idle: Idle_A (skeleton enemies: Skeletons_Idle)
- moving: Running_A (skeleton enemies: Skeletons_Walking)
- attack/lunge: knight Melee_1H_Attack_Chop, rogue Melee_Dualwield_Attack_Stab, ranger Ranged_Bow_Release (skeleton ranger: Ranged_1H_Shoot), mage and cleric Ranged_Magic_Shoot
- hit (_react / recoil): Hit_A, critical Hit_B
- dead: Death_A then hold last frame (skeleton enemies: Skeletons_Death then hold)
- downed ally: Death_B then hold; revive back to idle
Clips must play in place. If a clip moves the root, pin it; report which ones did.

## Keep
HP bars, chip, selection/elite/telegraph rings, guard bubble, downed marker, lunge, recoil, hit-stop, set_time_scale (animation speed must follow _time_scale()). Public API of BattleUnitView unchanged: set_actor, hit_stop, set_time_scale, lunge, set_selected.
## Replace
Capsule body/head/legs and _add_archetype_silhouette primitives. Death pivot tilt (DEAD_TILT) and squash are replaced by the clips; delete constants that become unused (no warnings). Faction must stay readable (heroes vs skeletons is enough; keep rings).

## Acceptance
1. BUILT: tests/import_gate.ps1 exit 0, zero errors/warnings. GUT full suite green with the APPDATA prefix from CLAUDE.md. Update test_battle_unit_view.gd assertions that checked capsule/tilt internals to assert the new behavior (correct clip name playing per state), do not delete coverage.
2. Headless still works: models load under --headless without errors.
3. Perf: run .agent-results/ig-544/ui/benchmark_fallen_citadel.gd (50-unit) before and after; report both frame-time numbers. >2x slower = stop and report, do not optimize creatively.
4. A rendered screenshot of a live battle with all 4 ally archetypes and skeleton enemies, saved under .agent-results/<bead-id>/.
Non-goals: arena (combat/arena) and hub avatar stay on their current models. No new autoload. No gameplay/simulation changes (battle_simulation.gd untouched).
Engine: you get the engine alone; kill every Godot process you start and confirm Get-Process Godot* is empty before returning.
Boundary: scene<->script seam -> verifier pass mandatory after.
notes:
2026-09-23 checkpoint (implementer). STATUS done, uncommitted, verifier pass still owed.
Files: combat/battle/battle_unit_view.gd, tests/unit/test_battle_unit_view.gd, tests/unit/test_battle_vfx.gd (it referenced the removed DEAD_TILT and _squash_tween, so 4 asserts moved to clip names).
BUILT: import_gate.ps1 exit 0, 0 errors/warnings. GUT 381/381 (APPDATA redirected).
Rig facts, read from the GLBs: all 14 mapped clips exist. Bones handslot.r/handslot.l exist on every character. Character GLBs have no AnimationPlayer, so the view adds one with root_node '..'. Track paths are Rig_Medium/Skeleton3D:<bone>. Bow hand: in Ranged_Bow_Release the left hand is extended (z 0.79) and the right draws, so the bow goes in handslot.l. Ranged_1H_Shoot and Ranged_Magic_Shoot extend the right hand, so crossbow, staff and wand go in handslot.r. Knight shield is shield_round.
Root motion: only Skeletons_Death moves the root bone (0,0,0 to 0,0,-0.708). Pinned by dropping the root position track from every clip in the shared library.
Benchmark (.agent-results/ig-ixj/benchmark.gd, a copy of the ig-544 one so its log is untouched; 30v30 = 60 units, RTX 4090): before median 1.907/1.791/1.921 ms, p95 9.18/7.88/9.16, fps 362/366/352. After median 3.501/3.695 ms, p95 6.70/5.91, fps 253/253. Median about 1.9x, which is under the 2x stop but close. Mean frame about 1.4x, and p95 got better.
Screenshots: .agent-results/ig-ixj/battle_live.png and battle_wide.png (harness capture.gd).
Judgment calls to review: (1) Hit and skill flash and DEAD_COLOR were removed. They tinted capsule materials, and the spec did not list them under KEEP. Hit_A/Hit_B are now the hit read. (2) The root yaw was atan2(fx,-fy), which is mirrored on one axis; the symmetric capsule hid it. It is now atan2(fx,fy) so the model's +Z follows the sim facing (checked: dot=1.00 for every unit). (3) battle_view never calls lunge for projectile attacks, so ranger and mage attack clips are triggered in set_actor when attack_cooldown goes up (ponytail note in code). Cleric lunges, so it plays via lunge. (4) An enemy archetype with no mapping falls back to the knight row; the sim only spawns knight, ranger, mage and rogue. Nothing to stop on.
2026-09-23 review fixes (ACCEPT-WITH-FIXES), uncommitted.
(1) Telegraph line yaw is now atan2(x, y). New test_telegraph_line_points_along_its_aim covers facing (1,0) and (0.6,0.8). The old code gave dot 0.00 and 0.96; it now gives 1.
(2) The knight fallback now calls push_warning when the archetype is not in the table. The test _actor default now carries archetype knight.
(3) The weapon test asserts BoneAttachment3D.bone_idx > -1.
(4) The root-pin test first asserts that the source Skeletons_Death has the Rig_Medium/Skeleton3D:root position track.
(5) New test_clips_drive_the_skeleton: the chop moves the spine more than 0.1 rad from rest after 4 x 0.1 s advances. A single 0.4 s advance moved it only 0.01, so the steps are needed.
Mutation checks: the old telegraph formula fails (5); root_node '.' fails (5) with a spine delta of 0.0. Under GUT 9.7.1 root_node '.' also fails about 20 other tests through unexpected engine errors.
BUILT: import_gate exit 0, 0 errors/warnings. GUT 383/383, 11562 asserts.
Note: 13 fallback warnings in the GUT log come from test_battle_view* fixtures whose enemies have no archetype. They are not failures; I left them alone as out of scope.
close_reason: KayKit models+animations replace battle capsules; review fixes applied; director re-ran gate exit 0 and GUT 383/383. Readability follow-up ig-hpu.

title: Battle view: smooth live playback, punchier effects, smaller damage numbers
description:
Owner play-test 2026-09-23: movement looks choppy, battle feels too fast, hit-stop / lunge / wave-clear slow-mo not noticeable, damage numbers a bit big. HP bars OK.

ROOT CAUSE (director): live battles advance in 0.25s chunks (GameSession EXPEDITION_PULSE_SECONDS, systems/game_session.gd:21) and the view polls every 0.25s (BATTLE_PULSE_SECONDS, combat/battle/battle_view.gd:20). So 2-3 sim ticks land at once. Units then exponential-lerp (battle_unit_view.gd:201, rate 8/s): dash then stop, 4x a second. Every hit in the chunk fires on the same frame, so 0.06s hit-stop and lunges overlap and vanish.

FIX (view only, sim untouched, no save keys):
1. Live mode plays back one pulse behind: positions move linearly from the last snapshot to the new one over the pulse, no dash-and-stop. Practice mode (every frame) must stay correct.
2. VFX events play at their own tick time inside the pulse (offset = (event tick - first tick) * battle_tick_seconds), not all on one frame.
3. Punch tuning so each is visible: hit-stop, lunge distance, wave-clear slow-mo length/scale. Pick values, list old->new.
4. Damage numbers ~25-30% smaller (normal and crit); crit stays clearly bigger than normal.
Do NOT change battle pace/sim speed: owner re-judges pace after smoothing.

description: Found by verifier-hard reviewing ig-0gt (2026-09-23), inferred from code, not yet reproduced. title: Skills 2: the Cleric gets Mend and Grace (it has no battle ability today)
description:
Found by ig-8lj (2026-09-23). Cleric is the 5th summonable archetype (heroes/defs/cleric.tres, summon 1-in-5) but BattleSimulation.ABILITIES has no cleric entry, so it fights with basic attacks only. GAME_SPEC says Back/Heal.

DESIGNED 2026-09-23 under the skill system (ig-gy0). SYSTEMS.md § Skills, Cleric kit:
- Grace (passive): +20% to the Cleric's own heals and shields.
- Mend (ability, the Cleric's signature): 8 s cooldown, range 6, heal 3.0 x ATK to one ally. The AI uses it on the lowest-HP ally in range below heal_below (0.35), in the support pass, after revive and before items. Mend's 3.0 ATK is 48 HP at base ATK 16.
All PROVISIONAL.

BEHAVIOR
1. Two skill .tres files in the ig-gy0.1 data format. The Cleric's archetype default kit = Grace + Mend.
2. A heal primitive, if ig-gy0.1 did not add one. Healing never raises HP past max and never touches a downed ally (that is revive).
3. The heal shows through the existing view contract: last_skill_tick, and a VFX mapping in battle_vfx.gd.
4. Mend can be Manual like any signature.

ACCEPTANCE
- A test: a Cleric heals a hurt ally by 3.0 x ATK x 1.2 (Grace), capped at max HP; it does not heal above heal_below; its cooldown holds 8 s.
- The ig-544 golden cases without a Cleric are unchanged.
- A five-hero team with a Cleric: forecast still runs within 2x the ig-gy0.1 baseline.
- BUILT + GUT green. Verifier pass (boundary #4).

NON-GOALS
The rest of the Cleric kit (ig-gy0.2); a revive (Rekindle is a book skill).

title: Arena attack clips are stretched 3-4x to fit the balance windows; trim them instead
description:
Root cause of 'combat feels clunky' after the Mixamo swap (played 2026-09-05, play pass 4).

arena.gd:_play_animation() sets custom_speed = animation.length / target_duration, so every
attack plays the WHOLE Mixamo clip (stance -> windup -> swing -> return to stance) squeezed
into the balance window that was authored for capsules. Measured native lengths (headless,
2026-09-05) against the windows they are forced into:

  Attack_A  1.500 s -> 0.42 s  (3.6x)   light chain
  Attack_B  1.667 s -> 0.42 s  (4.0x)
  Attack_C  1.367 s -> 0.42 s  (3.3x)
  Attack_Heavy 1.000 s -> 0.92 s (1.1x) -- the one that reads fine, and the user agrees
  Standing Dodge Fwd/L/R ~1.0 s -> 0.38 s (2.6x); Backward 1.633 s -> 0.38 s (4.3x)
  Block (enemy parry) 1.400 s -> 0.20 s (7x, a twitch)
  Attack_A (enemy) 1.500 s -> 1.10 s (1.4x) -- but peak extension does not land at the
    0.55 s active onset SYSTEMS.md 'the t ~= 0.55 s alignment target' rules it should
  Hit_Chest (hero) plays at NATIVE 0.767 s but hit stun is 0.35 s, so Idle cuts it in half
  Block (hero) native 1.4 s, parry lasts ~0.65 s, cut mid-raise

The 0.06 s crossfade is a hard cut at 4x. The heavy is the proof: the one clip near native
speed is the one that feels right.

Fix, smallest that works: a per-clip trim table {clip: [start_s, end_s]} in arena.gd.
In _bind_animation_libraries set animation.length = end (Godot Animation has no trim API)
and in _play_animation seek(start) after play(). Stretch the TRIMMED swing segment into the
window, not the whole clip. The Mixamo attacks have ~0.5-0.7 s of actual swing, so light
attacks land near 1.3x instead of 4x. Give hero Hit_Chest a target_duration of
arena_enemy_hit_stun. Trim enemy Block to the shield raise (~0.3 s). Set the enemy Attack_A
trim so its peak lands at t = 0.55 s, which also closes the SYSTEMS.md alignment target.

The trim values need eyes on each clip in the editor (or a played guess, then tune). That
is the authored step; the code is ~20 lines. No AnimationTree, no new clips, no balance
changes. ig-e5u (AnimationTree, 8-way) stays separate and blocked on the backpedal asset.

Acceptance: import gate + GUT green; test_arena.gd's hit-stop resume test still passes
(seek after play must not break assigned_animation resume); a played light chain reads as
three swings, not three twitches; enemy contact reads as caused by the visible blade.
Boundary: none crossed (no save, no scene rename, no autoload). verifier optional.
notes:
2026-09-05 code landed, uncommitted, awaiting a played pass.
Director re-ran both gates on the final tree: import_gate.ps1 exit 0; GUT 204/204 passing.
Files: combat/arena/arena.gd (CLIP_TRIMS table, length trim in bind, seek-on-fresh-start in _play_animation, hero Hit_Chest fitted to arena_enemy_hit_stun), tests/unit/test_arena.gd (span helper, 1 new test).
Stretch now: lights ~1.1-1.7x (was 3.3-4x), dodges ~1.6x (was 2.6-4.3x), enemy Block 1x (was 7x), enemy Attack_A contact at 0.5395 s vs the 0.55 s target.

Finding: Block is a held guard pose with no raise motion at all. A real shield raise needs a new clip; out of scope.

Known ceiling: _play_animation decides 'fresh start' by assigned_animation changing. That is only correct because the state machine always plays Idle/locomotion for at least one frame between two uses of the same clip. If a future state ever chains the same clip back to back, the second play starts from the clip's frame 0 (stance) instead of the trim start. ponytail: fix then by also treating a finished clip as fresh.

Close when a played pass says the light chain reads as swings and enemy contact reads as caused by the blade. Trim values may then move.

title: Strong teams earn most in the easiest zone (the route floor)
description:
WHY
Found by extra (game-designer) in its ig-0og economy sweep on 2026-09-25.
- The route floor makes an easy zone pay best for a strong team.
- A route runs max(min x P, base x P / sqrt r) (hub/expedition/expedition_orders.gd:34-51), where r = team power / the zone's scaled power. A clear pays stone_reward x P (game_session.gd:2476), whatever r is.
- So at r >= 16, a Verdant route sits at its floor: 90 s routes plus 64 s stomps, about 6,000 stones an hour. A matched Sundered team (r = 1.25) makes about 2,700.
- Slots (ig-0og's pick) cap how many teams run, not what each one earns. A strong player farms the easiest zone.

LEAD (extra's, unmeasured): pay stones x min(1, 1/sqrt r), so an over-strong team earns what the route time saves.

This is design first (numbers are game-designer's). It lands after ig-0og's ruling, because the rate row and this factor multiply.
acceptance_criteria:
1. SYSTEMS § Summon Stones gets the rule and its numbers, PROVISIONAL until a run settles them: what a team earns per game hour at r = 1, 4 and 16 in Verdant, Ashfall and Sundered, before and after.
2. An over-strong team never earns more per hour in an easier zone than a matched team earns in its own zone (a table test over the three zones).
3. The balance gate's CASE lines are unchanged (stones don't touch the sim). The stage saves are remade if their Ledgers change.
4. BUILT green. Sol review for boundary #1 if a save key changes (none expected).

title: The gate sees no GDScript warnings
description:
WHY
CLAUDE.md:24 says BUILT needs zero errors AND zero warnings, but headless runs never print GDScript parser warnings. GDScript only sends them to an attached editor debugger. So the gate's WARNING grep only sees engine WARNING lines, and the warning rules are enforced by review alone. The tree may already hold warnings.
Proof (high1, during ig-rd9):
- An unused local var added to heroes/hero.gd left the gate at exit 0. Restored hash-equal.
- The same var in a standalone script: exit 0.
- --check-only printed no warnings either.
An example of what the gate misses: P2-19's integer-division trap (docs/TASKS.md:883), which the INTEGER_DIVISION warning flags.

LEAD (unverified)
Project Settings can set each GDScript warning's level to Error (debug/gdscript/warnings/<name> = 2). In a debug build (our editor binary), the parser should then fail the script with "(Warning treated as error.)". The gate (--quit + tests/gate_parse.gd) and GUT already catch that. Export builds skip the warning pass, so shipping is unaffected.
Check first: how many warnings the tree has today, per warning.
Other routes if the lead fails:
- an editor-mode parse;
- a lint step (gdtoolkit). That is a new dependency, so it needs the owner's OK to download.

Owner domain: godot-tester (gates). Engine lane.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A deliberate unused local var turns the gate red, in game code (heroes/hero.gd) and in a standalone script. The output names the file and line. Both are restored hash-equal.
2. Clean tree: gate exit 0 and GUT all passing.
3. The gate's comment lists which warnings are at Error. It says which ones stay at Warn, and why.
4. Warnings already in the tree are fixed in the same change. If there are more than about 20, they go to a follow-up bead, and their warnings stay at Warn until then.
5. The report gives the gate's wall time, before and after.
notes:

high1 2026-09-25: lead confirmed. project.godot [debug] sets 27 warnings to Error (the 26 the tree has 0 of + unused_variable); a script then fails with '(Warning treated as error.)' + file:line. Measured one warning at a time over 123 non-addon .gd: 112 sites in 11 types. Fixed unused_variable's 4 (hub.gd forge_level; hub.gd zone+zone_name; test_battle_controls ally; test_buildings status). 108 left in 10 types stay at Warn: .agent-results/ig-4k2/remaining_warnings.txt (static_called_on_instance 38, shadowed_global_identifier 16, confusable_local_declaration 14, shadowed_variable 12, integer_division 11, unused_parameter 6, shadowed_variable_base_class 5, incompatible_ternary 4, unassigned_variable 1, int_as_enum_without_cast 1). GUT 919/919, 67, 22391. Sol ACCEPT (.agent-results/logs/ig-4k2-sol.json), one Low: hub.gd:1859 removal drops definition_for's push_error for a preset with an unknown zone (save validation and dispatch still reject it). Re-ran ACC1 myself: an unused local at heroes/hero.gd:66 and tests/stages/stage_play.gd:36 -> gate exit 1, both named with '(Warning treated as error.)'; both restored hash-equal. title: Matched fights bite far less at higher ranks
description:
WHY
A matched fight bites far less at higher ranks. At m=1 (team power 85-103% of the zone's RP) a team ends F1 Verdant with 39-61% of its HP, but B30 Ashfall with 87-92%. Source: ig-vl1.6's baseline (.agent-results/ig-vl1.6/presence_baseline.log). The director re-derived each team's max HP from the hero defs and got the same numbers.

CAUSE
Damage = ATK x 100 / (100 + DEF) (combat/battle/battle_simulation.gd:1961, battle_damage_defense_scale 100). From F1 to B30 a hero's HP and DEF grow about x9 (level growth x rank multiplier). Enemy ATK grows only with the RP: x5.3 from Verdant (900) to Ashfall (4,800). A B30 Knight's DEF of 236 cuts each hit to 30%; an F1 Knight's 26 cuts it to 79%.

WHY IT MATTERS
- Permadeath: matched fights rarely down anyone from mid ranks on (KNOWN_ISSUES asks whether spending a life feels like something).
- Knights and Clerics lose value as ranks rise, because fights become damage races (B30 is clock-bound: ig-vl1.6).
- The Early fixture's 18 battles were all wins with no moment.

OPEN QUESTION (owner): is "easier as you grow" the intended curve, or a gap? Nothing changes until the owner answers.

LEVERS (if a gap): enemy ATK budget per zone (battle_enemy_atk_budget_multiplier), or DEF's scale (battle_damage_defense_scale). Either is a big balance change: it moves every zone's numbers, gy0.9's clear-time band, and the caster offset (re-set after it, like vl1.6's timing rule).

Found by extra (game-designer) in ig-vl1.6's baseline; filed by the director.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The owner's call (intended or gap) is recorded here, verbatim.
2. If a gap: design picks the lever and a target bite per rank band in SYSTEMS, marked PROVISIONAL until a sweep settles it. The engine change gets its own bead, with the balance gate as its check and the caster offset re-set after it.
3. If intended: SYSTEMS says so in one line with the why, and KNOWN_ISSUES' permadeath question gets the answer.

title: Import gate misses parse errors in standalone -s scripts (tests/balance, tests/stages, tests/*_check.gd)
description:
WHY
high1 found it on ig-vl1.3 (2026-09-25): a parse error in tests/balance/presence_check.gd passed tests/import_gate.ps1 with exit 0. The gate runs --headless --import, then --headless --quit, and greps the output (import_gate.ps1:30-37). Neither loads a script that nothing in the project references. So a broken harness only shows up when someone runs it by hand.
The scripts only reached by -s or load(), today:
- tests/balance/balance_gate.gd, presence_check.gd
- tests/stages/stage_bot.gd, stage_play.gd (stage_bot loads stage_play at runtime)
- tests/balance_table_check.gd, equipment_definition_check.gd, save_roundtrip_check.gd, summon_def_id_roundtrip_check.gd, summon_weight_check.gd, zone_definition_check.gd

WHAT (owner: godot-tester; tests/ only)
The gate also parses every standalone script under tests/ that GUT doesn't run, and fails on any parse error with the same patterns. Find them by glob, not a hand list, so new harnesses are covered. One engine process at a time; keep the stray and port-6005 checks. Either Godot's --check-only per script or one helper that load()s each; pick the cheaper one and say why.

ACC
1. A deliberate parse error in one of them (a scratch copy, then reverted) turns the gate red and names the file.
2. A clean tree stays green: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
3. Report the gate's wall time before and after.
4. BUILT green. No game code changes.
notes:
high1 2026-09-25 STATUS done. tests/import_gate.ps1: after --quit, globs every .gd under tests/ except tests/unit/test_*.gd (14 today: the 12 in the description + tests/unit/compare.gd + the helper) and runs tests/gate_parse.gd (new, + .uid) once with them after --; its output joins the SCRIPT ERROR|ERROR:|WARNING grep, and its exit (count of scripts that failed) also fails the gate. Stray/6005 checks unchanged; one engine process at a time. WHY load() not --check-only: --check-only compiles before the autoloads exist, so it falsely fails tests/stages/stage_play.gd (Identifier not found: GameSession); it is also N processes (0.3 s each) vs one. load() returns a Script even on a parse error, so the helper checks can_instantiate(). ACC1: a parse error appended to stage_play.gd (backup in scratch, restored hash-equal) -> gate exit 1, 'Failed to load script res://tests/stages/stage_play.gd ... Parse error' and 'gate_parse: 14 scripts, 1 failed'. ACC2: clean -> exit 0, 0 errors/warnings, 'gate_parse: 14 scripts, 0 failed'. ACC3: wall 4.2 s before (x3), 5.0-5.1 s after (x3). ACC4: GUT 919/919, 67 scripts, 22391 asserts. FINDING (not fixed, out of scope): the gate catches no GDScript warnings at all. An unused local in heroes/hero.gd (game code, restored) and in a standalone script both passed exit 0; --check-only prints none either. Headless runs don't emit parser warnings, so CLAUDE.md's 'zero warnings' only covers engine WARNING lines.
DIRECTOR 09:57 PDT: BUILT green. Gate exit 0 with 0 warn/err lines, and the log shows 'gate_parse: 14 scripts, 0 failed'. GUT 919/919, 67 scripts, 22391 asserts. FP d9c0bd16 at both ends and at commit. Diff reviewed: tests/ only. high1's negative controls (stage_play.gd, hero.gd) are restored; git shows both clean. Committed as e0a3167. No export (test-only). high1's finding (headless runs never print parser warnings) is filed as ig-4k2.
close_reason: The gate load()s every standalone .gd under tests/ in one helper process (tests/gate_parse.gd). A deliberate parse error turned it red; the clean tree is green. Wall time 4.2 s before, 5.0-5.1 s after. Committed as e0a3167.

title: View: draw Knight Charge's dash over 0.4 s (SYSTEMS § The v1 kits)
description:
WHY
ig-zht built Charge instantly in the sim: the Knight lands on the cast tick, and that is the owner's 'immune to cc while in motion'. SYSTEMS § The v1 kits says the watched view draws the dash over 0.4 s. Today battle_view.gd (render, ~:571) plays each tick back with the normal glide (a pulse split into tick steps), so a charge draws as a very short glide and may read as a teleport. The owner asked for a charge 'in a straight line towards a selected enemy'. Sol R2 on ig-zht rated the gap Low, because it's outside zht's ACC.

WHAT
View only. When a Charge lands, the view glides that Knight from its pre-charge spot to the landing spot over 0.4 s, then goes back to the normal glide. The cue is last_skill_id == knight_charge at last_skill_tick, which is already in the checkpoint effect_state. No sim change and no saved state. Pushed enemies keep today's push glide.
If the owner still sees a teleport after this lands, SYSTEMS' fallback (a timed dash with a real immunity window: saved state, boundary #1) becomes its own bead.

- Unwatched runs and forecasts are untouched, because the change is in the view only.
- The 'designed, not built (ig-<this bead>)' marker at SYSTEMS § The v1 kits comes off in the same commit.
