title: Stage saves part 3: remake Early and Mid, then build Late (after the town records and the gy0.9 balance pass)
description:
WHY
Split from ig-eek.1 by the director (2026-09-25), from extra's readiness sweep. Built where eek.1 sat (right after ig-vl1.3), Late would:
(1) hold no meetings or meals (ig-m6o.2.2.4, .5), so bond tuning couldn't tune those points or ig-m6o.2.2.10's dreams;
(2) evict routine battles at the cap instead of the tier-0 town records, so it shows the wrong eviction;
(3) cost about 3x the wall time. At pace 6 a 30-hero town writes about 10 battles an hour, so the cap takes about 1,000 h. With meetings and meals it's about 30 records an hour, so about 330 h, and meetings and meals cost no sim time;
(4) bake in who wins before vl1.4, vl1.5 and the gy0 combat beads (§ Stage saves: a big balance change makes it stale).
Mid is 20 h of game clock and cheap to remake, so it stays in ig-eek.1 for the owner's playtests. Late, the expensive one, is built once, here.

WHAT
With ig-eek's bot, on the HEAD after ig-gy0.9:
1. Remake Early and Mid (§ Stage saves' remake rule: a new Ledger record kind).
2. Then build Late.
Before each run, the director sees the projected wall time (ig-eek ACC 7). If Late projects over 8 h, it uses the F1 fallback pre-ruled in ig-eek's notes: a fixed 200 h game clock, with no eviction required.

ACC
- ig-eek's ACC items 3, 4, 5 and 6, for Early, Mid and Late (tests/fixtures/stages/early, mid and late; playtest/play-early.cmd, play-mid.cmd and play-late.cmd).
- Plus 8: no balance change.
- Plus 9: BUILT, with Sol on boundaries #1 and #3.
- The STATUS reports each stage's record counts by kind (battle, encounter, meal, died, ...). Late's STATUS also says how many records it evicted, and of which kind.

title: Flaky test: test_an_incident_rebuilt_from_a_stranded_rescue_is_repaired_on_load fails about 1 run in 10
description:
WHY
Found by high1 during ig-7sn.15 (2026-09-25). tests/unit/test_save_service.gd:606 fails 3 of 30 runs on HEAD's game_session.gd and 2 of 30 with ig-7sn.15's diff (.agent-results/ig-7sn.15/flake/h*.log and r*.log). The failure is always ":613 [0] expected to equal [1]: the failed rescue leaves one incident". A random red BUILT costs a full re-run on every bead.

LIKELY CAUSE
The test depends on luck. _strand_and_dispatch_rescue(true) pins the rescuers to 1 HP (ig-qjh) so the rescue fails. But the rescue's seed comes from _new_run_seed() (Crypto), and the loop gives it at most 300 one-second ticks. Since pace 6 (ig-1jw, 65f2956), HP is x6 and the bound is 1080 s. So some seeds end with no incident: the rescue wins, or the loop ends first. Confirm which before fixing.

FIX DIRECTION (godot-tester)
Make the test exact, not the game: force the rescue's outcome, or fix its seed, and bound the loop by the battle's own max_seconds. No change to production code unless the cause turns out to be a real bug. If it is, stop and report.

ACC
1. Name the cause, with the seed or outcome of a failing run.
2. The test passes 50 of 50 runs (same loop as .agent-results/ig-7sn.15/flake/).
3. It still checks what it checked before: one incident left, rebuilt from the rescue, repaired on load.
4. BUILT green.
notes:
STATUS (high1, 2026-09-25): done, uncommitted, HOLD. File: tests/unit/test_save_service.gd only (_strand_and_dispatch_rescue weak_rescuer branch).
CAUSE (ACC 1): not the loop or the 1080 s bound (failing runs end after 10-11 s of ticks). The rescue continues the stranding fight, so its enemies stand where that fight (Crypto seed) left them. In the 6 failing runs of 30 (.agent-results/ig-8f4/probe/r3,r6,r13,r19,r26,r29) they stood ~6 units from the downed hero, and the 1 HP rescuer carried the hero out unhit (moment 'carried' at tick 97-110): rescue result 'retreated' (all allies extracted, none downed), so the incident resolved and was removed. Passing runs: an enemy stood by the victim and downed the rescuer (~tick 43), result 'stranded'. ig-qjh's 1 HP pin can't stop a rescuer who is never hit. Not a game bug: SYSTEMS allows extraction without clearing enemies (Sol).
FIX: the weak rescuer starts downed (hp 0, LIFE_DOWNED, in downed_ever_ids; battle Dictionary replaced, per ig-7sn.15's writer rule), so the rescue ends 'stranded' on its first tick. Asserts unchanged.
ACC 2: 50/50 (.agent-results/ig-8f4/after50/). ACC 3: same asserts; GUT asserts 22005 = baseline. ACC 4: gate 0/0/0, GUT 897/897. Sol (.agent-results/logs/ig-8f4-sol.json): PASS, none.
2026-09-25 director: ACCEPTED and committed as d7c6c07.
- The cause is named, and it wasn't the director's guess (the crypto seed plus pace 6 against the loop). The rescue continues the stranding fight, so its enemies stand wherever that fight's Crypto seed left them. In 6 of 30 probe runs they stood ~6 units from the downed hero. The 1 HP rescuer carried the hero out unhit, the rescue "retreated", and no incident was left. Not a game bug: SYSTEMS allows extraction without clearing the enemies (Sol checked).
- Fix: the weak rescuer starts downed (hp 0, LIFE_DOWNED, in downed_ever_ids). The battle Dictionary is replaced, not edited (ig-7sn.15's writer rule). Only :607 passes weak_rescuer = true, so no other test changed.
- Checks: 50/50 focused passes (.agent-results/ig-8f4/after50, re-counted by the director). The asserts are unchanged (22005).
- Director BUILT: gate 0/0, GUT 897/897, 22005 asserts, 0 script errors, 0 GUT warnings, FP stable, Godot 0 at both ends.
- Sol: PASS, no findings.
- No export: this is a test-only change.
close_reason: Flaky test fixed at the cause: the weak rescuer starts downed, so the rescue always strands. d7c6c07, 50/50 passes, BUILT 897/897, Sol PASS.

title: Stage saves part 2: Mid, after ig-vl1.3 and the cost gate (Late moved to ig-eek.2)
description:
WHY
Split from ig-eek by the director (2026-09-25). Mid's and Late's Ledgers bake in who wins, and ig-zht and ig-vl1.3 both change that. So they are built after ig-vl1.3, with ig-eek's proven bot.

WHAT
Build the Mid and Late stages with ig-eek's bot, following ig-eek's design and ACC. Before each run, the director sees the projected wall time (ig-eek ACC 7). If Late projects over 8 h, Late uses the F1 fallback pre-ruled in ig-eek's notes: a fixed 200 h game clock, no eviction required.

ACC
ig-eek's ACC items 3, 4, 5 and 6 for Mid and Late (tests/fixtures/stages/mid and late; playtest/play-mid.cmd and play-late.cmd), plus 8 (no balance change) and 9 (BUILT; Sol on boundaries #1 and #3).
notes:
STATUS (extra, 2026-09-25): readiness sweep at a386397. One ordering finding for the director. The rest holds (it's ig-eek's ACC by reference; see ig-eek's sweep note).
FINDING: in the engine order, eek.1 runs before ig-m6o.2.2.4 (meetings) and .5 (shared meals). So Mid and Late would hold no meetings or meals.
- Bond tuning is these saves' first reader, and 2.4 and 2.5 add bond points from both. A Mid or Late without them can't tune those points, or 2.2.10's two dreams.
- Late's eviction would be the wrong kind. With 2.4's tiers, meetings and meals go first. A Late built before them evicts routine battles first.
- Late would cost about 3x more. At pace 6 a 30-hero town writes about 10 battles an hour, so the 10,000 cap takes about 1,000 h (§ Stage saves' "about 6x"). With 2.4 and 2.5's ~12 meetings and ~8 meals an hour, it's about 30 records an hour, so about 330 h. Meetings and meals cost no sim time, and sim cost follows battle-seconds, so Late's wall time drops to about a third. That makes F1's 200 h fallback less likely to be needed.
- F2's logic (balance moves bake into the Ledger) also covers vl1.4, vl1.5 and the gy0 combat beads, which all land after eek.1 today.
Options: (a) move eek.1 after m6o.2.2.5 [my pick: it fixes all four points]; (b) keep the order and add "a new Ledger record kind" to § Stage saves' rebuild triggers, so Mid and Late get built twice; (c) keep it, and accept that Mid and Late miss the town records until some other rebuild.
2026-09-25 director RULING on extra's FINDING: split, which is neither (a) nor (b).
- ig-eek.1 builds Mid only, where it sits now (after ig-vl1.3). The owner gets a mid-game save to play soon. Mid is 20 h of game clock, so it's cheap to remake.
- Late moves to the new ig-eek.2. It runs after ig-m6o.2.2.5 and ig-gy0.9, and in the order right after gy0.9. eek.2 remakes Early and Mid first, then builds Late once.
  - With the town records in, Late costs about a third of the wall time.
  - It evicts the right records (tier 0 first).
  - It lands after every combat bead in the order.
- § Stage saves' remake rule gains "a new Ledger record kind". The director updates the doc.
- This bead's ACC now covers Mid only: ig-eek's items 3, 4, 5 and 6 for Mid, plus 8 and 9.
Director 2026-09-25 ~08:50 (from ig-eek.3/.4/.5, SYSTEMS 8caff89):
- Doc vs code finding: stage_play.gd still checks Early against the old bounds (5-10 heroes, none above D, one team). Change them to SYSTEMS § Stage saves: 8-20 heroes, 1-2 teams, no rank check. Don't remake Early for this; its fixture already passes the new checks.
- Heads-up from design: Mid's row is still a desk guess. Early's best heroes (A and B at level 30-33) already pass Mid's "best team mostly C-B" at 2 h, so Mid will likely miss the same way. Each miss is filed as a progression finding, as in eek. Never tune the bot to meet a check.
- Ledger guesses are now Early about 80, Mid about 1,000. ig-0og (the pull rate) may move them.
STATUS (extra, readiness sweep on ecb82d2, 2026-09-25): READY after the fixes below. No engine runs.
REFS: tests/stages/stage_play.gd (Early-only, 445 lines), tests/stages/stage_bot.gd, tests/unit/test_stage_saves.gd, tests/unit/compare.gd, playtest/play-early.cmd, tests/fixtures/stages/README.md, SYSTEMS § Stage saves (8caff89).
1. stage_play.gd is hard-wired to Early. Mid needs: a --stage=early|mid arg (run() takes only --seed= now); the clock from the stage (EARLY_SECONDS 7200 at :14 and :50/:57, Mid 72000); OUT_DIR per stage (:20); the BOT print naming the stage (:46 prints stage=early). A stage arg is not a policy change, so Early needs no remake.
2. Stale Early lines in _report, fix while there: "heroes 5-10" (:319, SYSTEMS now 8-20), "none above D" (:320, dropped under eek.4), "one team" (:321, SYSTEMS now 1-2), and the INFO at :324 "SYSTEMS: about 20 at pace 6" (SYSTEMS now about 80 for Early, about 1,000 for Mid).
3. ig-eek ACC 5 "Mid has at least one bond" as a GUT assert breaks the "a miss is a finding, the save is kept" rule. Early had 0 moments in 18 battles, and bonds come only from battle moments until 2.4, so a Mid miss is likely. Fix: the GUT test pins the counts in Mid's run.log, as Early pins bond_index().size() == 0. ">= 1 bond" becomes a run-log CHECK; a miss files a finding.
   Also: test_stage_saves.gd:40's message "no bond yet: Early's Ledger has no meeting or meal" gives the wrong reason. Early's battles had no moments. Suggest "no bond yet: Early's 18 battles had no moment".
4. Mid check definitions, so the bot and the reviewer agree:
   - best team = the strongest 5-hero team by _team_power; pass = at least 3 of 5 at rank C or B (SYSTEMS "mostly C-B");
   - halls = every hall at level 2-3;
   - a death = a died record with cause != "sacrifice";
   - a rescue = a battle record with battle_kind "rescue";
   - a bond = bond_index().size() >= 1.
5. Early already cleared Ashfall (save.json cleared_zone_ids), so Mid's "Ashfall cleared" is met at 2 h. More evidence the Mid row is low, like Early's was. Expect design rulings like eek.3/.4/.5 after the first Mid run. Don't tune the bot to meet them.
6. The stop-dispatch guard (:57, _clock + maxf(_longest_order, 600) * 1.5 < EARLY_SECONDS) only knows orders already seen. A first send to Sundered or a force zone (Citadel RP 28,800, Frontier 48,000; the route scales by reference size over team size) can overrun the clock. Suggest the order's own estimate: ExpeditionOrders.force_duration_seconds (hub/expedition/expedition_orders.gd:34). Minor: the final request_stop ends the order anyway.
7. DIRECTOR'S CALL, casters. vl1.3 makes mage and cleric real (1% each in summon_archetype_weights). By Mid the bot pulls ~400, so ~8 casters. _feed (:153) and _staff (:136) take the weakest spares, and a caster is spare like anyone else, so casters mostly get fed or put to work.
   (a) keep the policy. My pick: a player feeds by power too, and vl1.3's caster_scale reaches the bot's _power on its own. No remake.
   (b) never feed or staff a caster. That's a policy change, so Early gets remade (about 5 s of wall time).
8. Small: playtest/play-mid.cmd is a copy of play-early.cmd with --stage=mid; the README table gets a mid row; food is fine (only housed heroes eat); cost is about 53 s wall (run.log mid_20h_projected_wall_s=53, linear from Early's stomp; a harder zone mix will cost more).
Director 2026-09-25 ~09:10: extra's readiness sweep is ACCEPTED, with the caster call ruled:
- Casters in the bot: (a) keep the policy. The bot feeds and staffs by power like a player, vl1.3's caster scale already reaches its power measure, and SYSTEMS says the bot is never changed to meet a check. No Early remake.
- One addition so we can see if that call matters: the run log prints "INFO casters pulled=N fed=M kept=K". If Mid feeds a caster, say so in STATUS, and it goes to design.
- ACC 5's "Mid has >= 1 bond" becomes a run-log CHECK (a miss is a finding, the save is kept). GUT pins the run log's counts, as test_stage_saves does for Early. Fix test_stage_saves.gd:40's message while there.
- The stop guard uses ExpeditionOrders.force_duration_seconds for a first send to a force zone.
DIRECTOR 09:58 PDT: GO to high1. Mid only: Late is ig-eek.2, so the description's Late parts don't apply here. The ~09:10 rulings were restated in the GO. A projected wall time under 10 min runs without waiting for me. Sol on boundaries #1 and #3, verdict at .agent-results/logs/ig-eek.1-sol*.json.
high1 2026-09-25: Mid run snowballs. seed 1: HOUR1 wall 3.8s roster 8; HOUR2 15.0s roster 23; HOUR3 38.4s roster 28; HOUR4 123.2s roster 78, 15 orders, ledger 729. No roster cap; the bot teams every 5 idle heroes, so stones -> pulls -> teams compounds; each game hour costs ~3x the last. Stopped at h4. STATUS sent with options (hold for ig-0og / bot team cap / wall-capped run / run anyway). stage_play.gd edits (--stage, SYSTEMS checks, casters INFO, force_duration stop guard, HOUR line) and the test_stage_saves:40 message are in the tree, not BUILT. HOLD.
DIRECTOR 10:16 PDT: HOLD. high1's Mid run snowballed (roster 78 and 15 teams by game hour 4), and it was stopped there. Ruling (a): wait for ig-0og's brake and rate. Not a bot cap, since the bot is never changed to meet a check. high1 is parking its WIP (stage_play.gd --stage=, SYSTEMS' Early checks, Mid checks, the INFO casters line, the stop guard, the HOUR line, test_stage_saves.gd:40) as .agent-results/ig-eek.1/wip-mid.patch. It re-applies when this bead resumes. The 53 s wall projection was wrong: it scaled linearly from Early, but the cost grows about 3x per game hour.

title: A rolled-back commit cancels every sim job: a refused battle command restarts the catch-up round and every repeat check
description:
WHY: _commit_profile_mutation undoes a refused or failed mutation with from_dict(snapshot), and from_dict starts with _cancel_battle_jobs (ig-7sn.13). So every rollback cancels every job that is out: the load's catch-up round (ig-7sn.12) and every 'checking' order's repeat check (ig-7sn.6). The next pulse sends them all again from scratch. It never loses data (the snapshot still owes / is still checking), but at battle_pace 6 a frontier check or catch-up takes ~40 s, so rollbacks can starve it.
How often: _issue_battle_command_in_memory returns false on any rejected command (BattleSimulation.issue_command not accepted), on ANY order, and the owner fires skills by hand. Also fallible: _append_battle_order_in_memory, _append_rescue_order_in_memory, _apply_bulk_plan_in_memory, and any failed save. ig-7sn.12 already refuses commands on a catching-up order before the commit, but a refused command on another order still restarts everything. Found by high1 (ig-7sn.12 STATUS), widened by the director.
WHAT: a rollback keeps the jobs that are still valid. The snapshot is the pre-mutation state, so a check that was current when the mutation began is still current after the rollback, by value. Candidate (root cause, one place): the rollback path skips the cancel, then re-points each still-current check's 'battle' to the restored order's battle Dictionary (every writer replaces that Dictionary, so identity before the mutation proves it unchanged). A load (a real from_dict) still cancels everything.
ACC sketch: a refused battle command on order A while order B is checking and order C is catching up: B's and C's jobs are not cancelled and land once, with the same result as with no refusal. A failed save rolls back the same way. A load still cancels every job. Quit still stops within 0.5 s. Review #1 (Sol).
design:
DESIGN (extra, 2026-09-25; checked against 858b45d). The description's candidate holds, and it is the whole fix: one place, the rollback. Plus one gap the candidate misses: a rollback of the landing commit itself.

WHY IT'S A CODE-VS-ADR GAP, NOT A NEW RULE: the threading ADR (2026-09-25, item 5) says jobs are cancelled "on quit and before load_game's from_dict". The code cancels at the top of from_dict (game_session.gd:2736). But _commit_profile_mutation's two rollbacks (:2557, :2581) call from_dict too, so every rollback cancels. The fix brings the code back to the ADR, and no amendment is needed.

WHY KEEPING JOBS IS SAFE
- A job holds only deep copies: the catch-up's state is built from order.battle.duplicate(true) (:147-151), and each forecast leg gets its own duplicated snapshots, squads, policies and escrow (:176-183). It never reads or writes the session (ADR item 1).
- Nothing sends a job inside a transaction. _submit_battle_job's only callers are in _send_battle_checks, whose only caller is tick_expeditions, after its commit (:2018-2019). So every job out when a rollback happens was sent for the pre-mutation state, and the rollback restores exactly that state by value.
- Landing already checks generation, phase and battle identity (ADR item 4; :213-259). After a rollback every order's battle is a new Dictionary with the same value, so the identity check needs re-pointing, as the description says.

THE FIX
1. Split from_dict. The public from_dict(data) is _cancel_battle_jobs() and then the body, unchanged for SaveService.load_game (save_service.gd:158) and every test. The body is the rest of today's from_dict, and it doesn't touch _battle_jobs or _battle_checks. ig-7sn.15's reuse table stays cleared by the body, as its design says: a miss just decodes once.
2. One rollback helper. The two rollback blocks in _commit_profile_mutation are the same eleven lines, so they become _roll_back(snapshot, kept), with one change in one place. It calls the body, not from_dict.
3. Keep the checks. At the top of _commit_profile_mutation, beside paused_snapshot:
   - checks_kept is _battle_checks with each entry shallow-duplicated. Entries hold job references, and landing erases entries rather than editing them, apart from this re-point.
   - current_ids are the order ids whose entry's "battle" is_same the order's battle at that moment.
   On rollback: _battle_checks = checks_kept, and each id in current_ids whose order still exists gets entry["battle"] = the restored order["battle"]. Entries that weren't current stay as they are and are dropped when they land, as today.
4. That also covers the landing commit. _land_battle_checks reaps finished jobs from _battle_jobs, then commits. If that commit's save fails, the landed entries come back from checks_kept. Their jobs are no longer in _battle_jobs, so the next land pass counts them as in and commits the same results again. No resend, and no second sim run.
5. A check the mutation ended stays ended. _end_battle_check_in_memory sets job.cancelled and erases the entry. The rollback brings back the order (still checking) and the entry with a cancelled job. That lands as cancelled, the entry is erased, and the next pulse sends a fresh check. So it's correct, just slow, and only on this rare path.

COST: two small loops over _battle_checks per transaction, at most one entry per order. Nothing is copied deeply.

BOUNDARIES
- #1: nothing is saved differently. The snapshot, ledger truncate and restored fields are as today, and a load still cancels everything.
- ADR item 5 is honoured: cancel on quit and on load only.
- #3: a rollback never removes a hero, as today.
- #2 and #4 are untouched.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A refused battle command on order A while order B is checking and order C is catching up:
   - B's and C's jobs are the same objects, not cancelled, and still in _battle_jobs;
   - _battle_check_generation doesn't move;
   - each lands once, and B's and C's to_dict after landing equal a control run with no refusal.
2. A failed save in an unrelated transaction (the injected write failure of tests/unit/test_save_refusal.gd) rolls back the same way: the same checks, the same result.
3. A failed save in the landing commit itself: the landed checks come back, and the next pulse lands them with the same results. No new job is submitted (the generation doesn't move), and the catch-up round still lands as one round.
4. A rolled-back mutation that had replaced B's battle Dictionary: B's check still lands after the rollback (the re-point, by value). A rolled-back mutation that ended B's check: B is checking again and gets a fresh check on the next pulse, and the cancelled job's result is never committed.
5. A load (SaveService.load_game, a real from_dict) still cancels every job and clears the checks. Quit still stops within 0.5 s.
6. The two rollback blocks are one helper, and no other from_dict caller changes.
7. BUILT green. Review: #1 (Sol).
notes:
Director 2026-09-25: engine order after ig-7sn.15 (both after ig-1jw, before ig-zht). Design: extra, if the candidate in the description needs more than the rollback path.
STATUS (extra, 2026-09-25): done (design + ACC; checked at 858b45d). The candidate holds, and it is the whole fix: split from_dict (the public one cancels, the rollback calls the body), dedupe the two rollback blocks into one helper, snapshot _battle_checks at commit start, and re-point the checks that were current. It's a code-vs-ADR gap, not a new rule: the threading ADR item 5 cancels only on quit and load. The candidate misses one case, now covered: a failed save in the landing commit itself restores the landed entries, so the same results land next pulse with no resend. No engine runs, no commits.
Director 2026-09-25 (from ig-7sn.14, 5334a79): _cancel_battle_jobs now also clears _preview_forecasts and emits preview_forecast_ready (deferred). So a refused battle command's rollback also drops every dispatch preview's forecast, and the hub goes back to "Checking...". The fix here should keep the preview entries too (they hold no saved state), beside the still-current checks.
Director 2026-09-25: design + ACC ACCEPTED, with one update for 5334a79 (ig-7sn.14 landed after the design's check). _submit_battle_job now has a third sender: _preview_forecast (game_session.gd:1392), the dispatch preview's forecast. Its entries live in _preview_forecasts, keyed by their exact inputs, and hold no session state. So the design's "nothing sends a job inside a transaction" still holds for _battle_checks, and the rule is simple: the rollback path doesn't touch _preview_forecasts at all. Only _cancel_battle_jobs (load, quit) clears it. An entry that an until-stopped dispatch consumed stays consumed after a rollback, so a seed is never reused. ACC 1 add: after the refused command, the preview entries and their jobs are the same objects, and preview_forecast_ready is not emitted. Engine order unchanged: after ig-7sn.15.
STATUS (extra, 2026-09-25): readiness sweep at a386397. The design and ACC hold. One line to carry from ig-7sn.15 (058fc74), plus refs.
1. 7sn.15 added `_battle_owed = owed_snapshot` to both rollback blocks (game_session.gd:2719, :2744), and from_dict's body clears `_battle_owed` (:2912). The one rollback helper (ACC 6) must restore it after calling the body, as both blocks do today. Keep these green unchanged: test_battle_session.gd:306 (test_a_rollback_keeps_the_owed_time_and_a_load_drops_it) and test_bonds.gd:731 (the kept index through a load and a rollback).
2. The repeat checks now land and go out from _pulse (:2131-2132), after its commit. tick_expeditions (:2053) and _process (:333) both reach it. ACC 3's "the next pulse lands them" holds.
Refs now: _send_battle_checks :162 (catch-up :167-173, legs :201-205), _land_battle_checks :210, _release_battle_jobs :233, _land_battle_checks_in_memory :257, _end_battle_check_in_memory :313, _commit_profile_mutation :2688 (rollback blocks :2711-2725 and :2737-2750), from_dict :2893 (_cancel_battle_jobs at :2894).
STATUS (high1, 2026-09-25): done, uncommitted. game_session.gd: from_dict = _cancel_battle_jobs + _read_profile (old body, unchanged); _rollback_kept() at commit start (checks copied, current ones recorded, plus owed/paused/ledger/checkpoint/command errors as before); _roll_back() is the one helper both branches call: _read_profile, restore kept (incl. _battle_owed after the body), restore checks, drop entries holding a cancelled job, re-point current checks at the restored battle. _preview_forecasts untouched by a rollback. No other from_dict caller changed. DEVIATION from design pt 5: an ended check is DROPPED on rollback, not landed as cancelled, because a job that finished before the cancel carries a whole result that would commit (ACC 4). A landing's own unsafe/error end cancels nothing (the entry is erased at :267 before _end_battle_check_in_memory reads it at :324), so ACC 3 holds for unsafe verdicts too. Tests: tests/unit/test_rollback_jobs.gd, 7 tests (ACC 1-5 + unsafe landing with a failed save); each rollback asserts to_dict() == before. Mutations: no re-point fails 5/7-ish (5/6 at the time), no cancelled drop fails 4b, from_dict in _roll_back fails 4/6. Kept green: test_battle_session:306, test_bonds:731, quit tests test_repeat_check:122, test_catch_up:169. BUILT: gate 0/0, GUT 904/904, 65 scripts, 22199 asserts. Sol R1 FAIL (unsafe landing + failed save; to_dict compare) -> R1.1 disputed with code refs + new test, #2 fixed; R2 PASS. Logs .agent-results/logs/ig-7sn.17-sol*.json. Godot reaped to 0.
2026-09-25 director: ACCEPTED and committed as 44708e5.
- DEVIATION from design point 5 accepted: a check the mutation ended is dropped on rollback, not landed as cancelled. A job that finished before the cancel still holds a whole result (cancelled=false in it), so the landing would commit it (ACC 4). Dropping it gives the design's intended end: the order is back to checking, and the pulse sends a fresh check.
- Director check of Sol's withdrawn R1 #1: _land_battle_checks_in_memory erases the entry (:267) before the unsafe or error branch calls _end_battle_check_in_memory, whose lookup (:324) then finds nothing and cancels no job. So a failed save in an unsafe landing brings back uncancelled jobs, and they land the same verdict (test at test_rollback_jobs.gd:116).
- Director BUILT: gate 0/0, GUT 904/904 (65 scripts, 22199 asserts; the baseline was 897/64/22005), 0 script errors, 0 GUT warnings, FP stable, Godot 0 at both ends.
- Sol R2: PASS. R1's two findings: one withdrawn, one fixed (exact to_dict restore).
- New GUT baseline: 904 tests, 65 scripts, 22199 asserts.
close_reason: A rollback keeps every sim job and re-points current checks; only quit and a load cancel. 44708e5, BUILT 904/904, Sol R2 PASS.

title: Settle pulse: 82-85 ms (1 order), 155-172 ms (5) at 48d3cc9, and the catch-up landing (320 ms)
description:
WHY: ig-7sn.6 (7f3d04f) took the repeat's forecast off the settle pulse: 264-274 -> 195-204 ms with 1 order, 350-380 -> 269-280 with 5 (.agent-results/ig-7sn.6-after/settle1.log, settle5.log). What is left, p50-ish: roster_changed handlers 132-137 / 176-190 ms (ig-7sn.9: hidden panels rebuild), the save 8 / 40-44 (ig-7sn.10), expeditions_changed handlers 6 (ig-7sn.11: walkers), the check's team snapshot 2, and about 40-50 ms nobody has split: the settle's own work (_settle_battle_order, _record_battle and the Ledger, rewards, _send_battle_checks). The dream read (34 ms when the hero detail shows during a settle; ig-7sn.11's design lists it and leaves it) belongs here too. Budget: SYSTEMS -> Performance budgets, no frame over 33 ms. ig-7sn.15's ACC 2 leaves a settle pulse out '(ig-7sn.6 owns that pulse)', but ig-7sn.6 only owned the forecast and is closed. This bead owns the rest.
WHAT: once ig-7sn.9 and ig-7sn.10 land, re-measure settle1 and settle5 with tests/perf/perf_baseline.gd (ig-7sn.12 drops its stale forecast column), split the rest, and bring a settle pulse under 33 ms, or report what is left and why.
NOT: moving a settle off the main thread. Settles and kills stay there (threading ADR; boundary #3).
design:
DESIGN (extra, 2026-09-25; 2026-09-24 performance ADR items 1-2; settles stay on the main thread).

TWO SAVES? No. A settle pays one save. _commit_profile_mutation saves once. Then _flush_deferred_notifications raises _save_deferred_depth around its emits, so roster_changed -> SaveService.save returns at once (is_save_deferred).
- But the settle measure counts it twice. _settle_parts' "roster_changed handlers" calls every connection directly, SaveService.save included, outside that deferral. So each SETTLE line's rest is low by one save, and also by the stale forecast column (the forecast is on workers since 7f3d04f).
- The real unsplit part: 1 order, -21.8 + 79.2 + 7.6 = about 65 ms. 5 orders, -28.6 + 79.8 + 39.7 = about 91 ms, which includes the other active battles' advances that ig-7sn.15 moves off the pulse frame. So it's more than the 40-50 ms the bead says.

WHAT THE REST HOLDS (from the code; the measure must confirm)
- Decodes (before ig-7sn.15). Every battle order is decoded in tick_expeditions' look-ahead, again in _advance_clocks_in_memory (returning orders), again in _resolve_due_orders_in_memory (to read a status), and the due order once more in _settle_battle_order.
- The settle's game work. snapshot_outcome, stranded capture and refund, _record_battle (moments duplicated), _record (Ledger.append, tier, Bonds.fold_in), credit_team_xp (grant_xp and instructor traits per hero, hero_by_id per id), roll_loot, _battle_stop_reason, _begin_battle_check, _append_report. Then the two expire passes, _evict_ledger (Bonds.fold_out), _land_battle_checks and _send_battle_checks.
- Handler costs that only happen on a real change, which the side measure (run before the pulse, on unchanged data) cannot see. Returning heroes get new town figures (TownWalker.create, add_child, a plan each). The hub's _bond_index sees a new ledger key (_say_new_bonds, _living_candidates, _dreams cleared). _refresh_recent_returns gains a row.
- The dream and history, when the detail shows a selected hero. Bonds.dream folds all 10,000 records and runs _save's moment loop on every battle record (34 ms). history_lines scans the whole ledger twice, in known_names and records_for_hero (12 ms). Both caches clear on any ledger change, so a settle always pays both.

MEASURE FIRST (tests/perf/perf_baseline.gd settle1 and settle5, after ig-7sn.9 and ig-7sn.10 land):
- (a) Fix the double count: the side "roster_changed handlers" part skips SaveService.save. Drop the forecast column if ig-7sn.12 hasn't.
- (b) Time each handler inside the real settle pulse. For the pulse, the script swaps each connection of roster_changed, expeditions_changed and battle_changed for a wrapper that times the original, then restores them. No game code changes.
- (c) Split the settle's game work on the side, rolled back after. Inside a deferred-notification scope, time each piece with the due order's real inputs, then restore with from_dict(snapshot) and a ledger truncate (as _commit_profile_mutation's rollback does). The pieces: _advance_clocks_in_memory; _resolve_due_orders_in_memory's decode loop; and inside _settle_battle_order its decode, snapshot_outcome, _record_battle (build vs _record), credit_team_xp, roll_loot, _begin_battle_check, _append_report. Then _evict_ledger, _land_battle_checks, _send_battle_checks, and the transaction's to_dict snapshot.
- (d) The same settles with the Forge open and one hero selected: dream, history_lines, known_names, and the roster list.

FIXES, in order, each only if (b)-(d) show it. Re-measure after each.
1. One decode is left. ig-7sn.15 (058fc74) took the look-ahead, the clocks pass and the resolve loop off decoding (_resolve_due_orders_in_memory reads the status off the dict). _settle_battle_order still decodes fresh (game_session.gd:2452): it takes the state from _battle_state(order) instead, identity-checked. Read-only use is safe, since a rollback or a new leg replaces the dict (extra's readiness sweep, accepted 2026-09-25).
2. Figures for returning heroes spread out. show_walkers creates at most N new figures a frame from a queue (PROVISIONAL N = 4); the rest appear on the next frames. The same queue as ig-7sn.11's plan cap, if that landed.
3. The dream skips what cannot move it. Bonds.dream skips a battle record whose team, rescued and rescuers all lack the hero. It checks that with Array.has before _save's moment loop. This is exact for records the game writes. A moment's hero and by are hero ids of actors in that fight (_add_moment; enemies are "enemy:<archetype>"). A battle never drops an actor. And team is every allied actor in the battle dict (_record_battle, _battle_ally_hero_ids). So the dead-actor bead from ig-7sn.10 fix 4 (not filed yet) must keep dead allies, or this skip breaks; whoever files it carries that line. A test proves it on data (below).
4. History reads from the newest end. history_lines walks the ledger newest-first with records_for_hero's filter inline, and stops where it stops today (max_lines, after the routine collapse). The lines come out the same. A hero with fewer than max_lines records still scans everything, as today. This beats ig-7sn.9's history cache (fix 3) on a settle, where that cache has just cleared. known_names (ledger.gd:110) gets the same treatment: history_lines calls it, and hub._bond_text calls it again on every detail refresh. Walk it newest-first too, or pass the names in once. Same output.
5. The settle's refresh gets its own frame. Only for the pulse's settle transaction: _pulse marks the commit, and _flush_deferred_notifications then leaves the pending signals for the next _process call, instead of emitting in the settle's frame. Same signals, same order, one frame later. Every other transaction still flushes at once. Boundary check: a hero killed in the settle is gone from roster before the refresh. For one frame the hub may still list them, so every action must refuse a hero no longer in roster (acceptance 5 checks it; not verified here). Sequencing, shared with ig-7sn.10: one heavy job per frame (the pulse, one battle advance, the periodic save, the settle's refresh). A later job waits for the next frame, and a waiting frame still calls _owe_battles(delta, false).
6. Then stop and report what's left. With five orders the save stays in the settle's frame, because save-or-rollback needs it there (ig-7sn.10's design). If ig-7sn.10 ends at 17-25 ms, a five-order settle likely still misses 33. The lever then is ig-7sn.10's dead-actor bead, not this one.

NOT: moving the settle or kill_hero off the main thread (threading ADR; boundary #3). Caching the dream across evictions: at the cap, each settle evicts a routine record that often names the hero, so a cache would refold on most settles anyway.

BOUNDARIES: #1: no saved key; fix 5 changes when signals fire, not what is saved. #2: fix 5's one-frame delay, and fix 2's queued figures; the hub's handlers and connections are unchanged. #3: kill_hero is still the only remover; fix 5 must not let a stale row act on a dead hero. #4: fix 1 reads the status the checkpoint holds; no sim change. Dream and history keep their outputs exactly (DECISIONS 2026-09-24 "Bonds stay derived", item 6: still read from records, one hero at a time).

Numbers and method: .agent-results/ig-7sn.2/baseline.md; rerun with tests/perf/perf_baseline.gd. Budget: SYSTEMS § Performance budgets (p99 8.3 ms, no frame over 33 ms). A fix cites before and after with the same script. Town row. 98 walker figures and 121 buildings, no battle: frames p50 3.6, p99 14.3, worst 20.8 ms (none over 33). With battles out, each expeditions_changed (every pulse) runs _refresh_walkers for 5.7 ms of its 6.5-7.3 ms. show_buildings with a forced graph rebuild is only 3.3 ms.
WHAT: find the town's p99 frame cost and the walker refresh cost; bring p99 to 8.3 ms. Logs: town.log, hub.log.
design:
DESIGN (extra, 2026-09-25; 2026-09-24 performance ADR items 1-2; threading ADR item 7).

SCOPE: hub/ and hub/town/ only: the town's frames and the hub's handlers on the pulse's signals. The pulse's own tick is not here. ig-7sn.15 (058fc74) already met the five-active target: the whole pulse is 7.48 ms p50 / 9.12 p99 at five active (fix3c/pulse5.log).

WHERE THE TIME GOES
- Town, no battle, 98 figures (town.log): frames p50 3.6, p99 14.3, worst 20.8 ms. Not split yet.
- Every pulse's expeditions_changed: 6.5-7.3 ms. _refresh_walkers is 5.7 of it (baseline row 2). _refresh_walkers loops the 100-hero roster: is_hero_busy (a typed array per order per hero), is_embodied, _partner_sign (bond_from with duplicate(true)), a sort, then show_walkers. It runs on every pulse, though the heroes in town only change when an order or an incident starts or ends.
- Five active, after ig-7sn.7 (ig-7sn.7/pulse5.log, p50): tick 36.6 (decode 4.5, advance 19.9, encode 1.5, other 10.7), plus rest 10.0 (the handlers). The whole pulse was about 46 ms (history: ig-7sn.15 brought it to 7.48 p50).

MEASURE FIRST (tests/perf/perf_baseline.gd):
- (a) The town measure records per frame: Performance.TIME_PROCESS, the viewport's measured render time (CPU and GPU), draw calls, and how many walker plans (_plan, _wander) ran and their time. TownView gets plain counters (plan_runs, plan_usec), like hub.dream_reads, and the script reads them every frame. GDScript can't wrap another script's method. Report the worst 1% of frames by cause.
- (b) The pulse5 measure times each expeditions_changed and battle_changed handler (_report_handlers), with 5 orders.
- (c) _refresh_walkers split: the busy/embodied checks, partner signs, the sort, show_walkers.

FIXES, in order. Re-measure after each.
1. Walkers refresh only when the heroes in town change. On expeditions_changed, a small guard compares a key (the busy hero ids: every order's and incident's hero_ids, which is all is_hero_busy reads) with the last one, and calls _refresh_walkers only when it changed. roster_changed keeps the full refresh (a death, a summon, a station, a home, a new bond). A death comes through roster_changed. A partial rescue shrinks an incident's hero_ids in place under the same id (game_session.gd:2543-2559); the hero-id key catches it by construction (extra's readiness sweep, accepted 2026-09-25). _show_partner stays on every pulse (it is cheap).
2. The town's p99, by what (a) finds. Each only if the measure points at it:
   - Plan spikes: at most N plans per frame from a queue (PROVISIONAL N = 4). A walker waiting for its plan lingers a frame longer.
   - Animation: a walker off screen pauses its animation (VisibleOnScreenNotifier3D, a native node) and resumes on screen.
   - Draw calls: visibility ranges on walker meshes far from the camera (native).
   If none of these is the cause, report the split and stop.

NOT FIXED HERE, AND WHY
- The dream read: 34 ms when the detail shows a selected hero and a settle adds a ledger record (_dreams clears on any ledger change). Once per leg end, only with the detail open. Folding the dream in (DECISIONS 2026-09-24 "Bonds stay derived from the Ledger", item 6: dreams stay derived, one hero at a time) has to handle eviction at the Ledger cap, so it gets its own bead if the owner wants the detail smooth through a settle. It is listed, not hidden.
- (History) At ig-7sn.7 the tick alone was 36.6 ms, over 33 before any handler ran. ig-7sn.15 has met the five-active target since.

HISTORY, met by ig-7sn.15 (fix3c: 7.48 ms p50 / 9.12 p99 at five active). THE FIVE-ACTIVE PULSE TARGET: what was left, and the answer on item 7
- After fix 1, the handlers are about 4 ms (10.0 less the walkers' 5.7 or more). The tick is still ~36.6. The whole pulse is ~40 ms. It still misses.
- What's left is tick_expeditions: all five battles advance in one frame (19.9), plus 4.5 ms of decode, plus 10.7 of other work. Returning orders are decoded twice a pulse just to read a status.
- The live pulse needs its own bead, but not a threading one. One battle alone fits a frame: frontier is 14 ms p50 / 19 p99 a pulse (ig-7sn.7/battle_frontier.log). The fix is to stop running all five in the same frame, on the main thread. Item 7 stands. Filed as its own bead under ig-7sn (see its design), after ig-7sn.6.
- Threading the live pulse (an item 7 amendment) only if one battle's own pulse later goes past ~25 ms, for example if walls pass their pathfinding budget (SYSTEMS: 2 ms added to a watched frontier pulse).

BOUNDARIES: #2: one guard function and a changed signal connection in hub.gd (in code, no .tscn change). Fix 2's nodes are added in code, if any. #1, #3, #4 untouched: no saved key, no roster removal, no sim change.

title: Periodic save with five battles out: 34-35 ms every 15 s
description:
WHY: Measured by ig-7sn.2 at 0df0e29 on the owner's PC (1920x1080, vsync off, 100 heroes, Ledger at 10,000). Numbers and method: .agent-results/ig-7sn.2/baseline.md; rerun with tests/perf/perf_baseline.gd. Budget: SYSTEMS § Performance budgets (p99 8.3 ms, no frame over 33 ms). A fix cites before and after with the same script. Hub row. The 15 s save is 3.5 ms with no battle out and 38.5 ms with five (save.json 52 KB -> 486 KB). Stages with five: to_dict 1.8, JSON.stringify 8.3, JSON.parse_string 10.5, _load_refusal 13.2 ms. The parse and refusal check the save before writing (save_service.gd: do not remove for speed); their cost grows with the battle state in save.json. ledger.jsonl is 4.39 MB and is appended, not rewritten.
WHAT: bring the save with five battles under 33 ms without dropping the refusal check. Log: roster.log.
design:
DESIGN (extra, 2026-09-25; 2026-09-24 performance ADR items 1, 2 and 6).

ITEM 6 STAYS: no thread touches the save. The case for keeping it is in the code, not a preference. A player action is a transaction that saves and rolls back if the save fails (game_session.gd _commit_profile_mutation: `var saved: bool = SaveService.save()`, then from_dict(snapshot) on failure). An async or threaded save would have to commit an action before knowing its save landed, which breaks save-or-rollback (boundary #1). So the save stays synchronous and gets cheaper. Every roster action pays this save too (roster_changed is connected to SaveService.save). So this bead also sets ig-7sn.9's five-order roster action.

WHERE THE TIME GOES (roster.log, 5 orders, p50): to_dict 2.0, JSON.stringify 8.1, JSON.parse_string 8.5, _load_refusal 10.5 (0.22 with no battles, so it is nearly all validate_snapshot + BattleActor.validate_dict), disk ~1-5. save.json is 486 KB against 52 KB with no battles. The battle checkpoints are the difference.
- Why they are big: a battle never drops an actor. spawn_index is state.actors.size() (battle_simulation.gd ~916), so every dead enemy of every cleared wave stays in the checkpoint.
- The format adds to it: JSON.stringify(payload, "\t") indents every line (6-8 tabs deep at an actor's keys, and every array element on its own line). sort_keys is on by default, so every actor's ~33 keys are sorted on every save.

MEASURE FIRST: the roster measure (5 orders) gains:
- (a) Per battle: bytes of its checkpoint, actors alive / downed / dead.
- (b) stringify and parse times for three forms on the same payload: today's ("\t", sorted), compact sorted (""), and compact unsorted ("", sort_keys false). Byte size of each.
- (c) _load_refusal split: heroes and the rest vs each battle's validate_snapshot.
- (d) The pulse5 frames: which frame the periodic save lands on, and that frame's time.
Numbers go in the bead and SYSTEMS § Performance budgets (Hub row).

FIXES, in order. Re-measure after each; stop once the target holds.
1. Compact text. save() writes JSON.stringify(payload, "", false): no indent, no key sort. One line. The parse and the refusal check still run on exactly the text written, so ig-6pm's promise holds. Load reads both forms, so old pretty saves load unchanged. The keys come out in to_dict's fixed order, so the text stays deterministic per build. The file is harder for a person to read; a pretty-printer is one command away.
2. The periodic save gets its own frame. Today it runs in the same _process call as the pulse (_pulse, then the save). Instead, the pulse sets a due flag, and the next _process call (a non-pulse frame; pulses are 0.25 s apart) runs the save and returns. On that frame the pulse accumulator still takes delta, and _owe_battles(delta, false) still runs first: each live battle is owed the frame's time, and none advances. Then the save, then return. It goes after the load_blocked return, so a blocked load never tries it. Below 4 fps every frame is a pulse's; there the due save runs at the start of the next frame, before its pulse (extra's readiness sweep, accepted 2026-09-25). Same save, one frame later. The checkpoint-failed retry path does the same. Transaction saves are untouched.
3. A cheaper validator, same verdicts. BattleActor.validate_dict and validate_snapshot read each field once into a typed local (faction, life, hp, max_hp and effects are read and str()'d over and over today). Constant lists are hoisted out of the per-actor loop (`in [LIFE_DOWNED, LIFE_DEAD]` builds an array per actor). Every refusal and its message stay exactly as they are.
4. Only if still over, stop and report. The next rung is the dead actors, and it is not this bead's: dropping or compacting dead enemies changes the sim's state and the checkpoint format (boundaries #1 and #4, spawn_index uniqueness, legacy checkpoints). File it as its own bead with the measured dead share.

NOT CHOSEN: a threaded or multi-frame save (breaks save-or-rollback, above). Skipping or sampling the refusal check (ig-6pm: do not remove for speed). Caching a checkpoint's validation between saves (a checkpoint is replaced at every commit, and the check must run on the text that is written).

TARGET: SaveService.save with five battles out, p99 under 33 ms (the bead's goal). Stretch, PROVISIONAL: p50 at or under 16 ms, so a five-order roster action fits in 33 ms beside ~17 ms of handlers (ig-7sn.9). Settled by: the measure after fix 3. If fixes 1-3 land at 17-25 ms, ig-7sn.9's five-order target waits on the dead-actor bead.

BOUNDARIES: #1: the save's text format changes (whitespace and key order only; the same keys and values, the same parse). The refusal check, the ledger order, the temp-file rename and the rollback are untouched. Acceptance needs a real save and reload through disk, plus a legacy pretty-printed save. #4: the validators' verdicts must not change (no sim change). #2, #3 untouched.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Measure first: the new split (per-battle bytes and alive/downed/dead counts; stringify and parse for the three text forms; _load_refusal split by battle; the pulse5 frame the periodic save lands on) runs at HEAD before any change, on the seeded perf save. Logged under .agent-results/ig-7sn.10/. Then the same script after each fix that lands.
2. Target, five battles out: SaveService.save whole p99 under 33 ms, and the frame that runs the periodic save under 33 ms (pulse5; today 44.5 ms, ig-7sn.15 fix3c/pulse5.log). No frame over 33 in pulse5 runs the periodic save. Report the save's p50 against the PROVISIONAL 16 ms stretch. If it misses, name the gap and file the dead-actor bead with the measured dead share (dead enemies only, per the director's line in the notes).
3. Save round-trip (boundary #1): a real save and reload through disk with five battles out. The reload is exact (==) against Compare.json_round_trip. Each battle, run on, stays within Compare.mismatch (1e-6) of the unsaved run. A save in today's form (JSON.stringify(payload, "\t", true, true)) loads to the same state. The refusal check still runs on the exact text written: a state with a NaN actor position is refused and writes no file (tests/unit/test_save_refusal.gd still passes).
4. Validator verdicts unchanged: a table test with one broken field per row, covering every refusal in BattleActor.validate_dict and validate_snapshot, gets the same message it gets at HEAD. Written and green before fix 3, and green after it.
5. The periodic save never shares a frame with _pulse or a battle advance. A test drives _process across a 15 s boundary with battles live, and sees _pulse, the save and each advance in different calls. On the save frame, each live battle's _battle_owed still grows by that frame's delta. A transaction's save still happens inside the transaction, and a failed save still rolls it back.
6. BUILT green. The balance gate's CASE lines are identical to the last saved baseline (in today's order, .agent-results/ig-vl1.5/balance_final.log). Review: #1 (Sol).

title: Roster action and building change: 137-195 ms, the 100-row roster list rebuild is 122-130 ms
description:
WHY: Measured by ig-7sn.2 at 0df0e29 on the owner's PC (1920x1080, vsync off, 100 heroes, Ledger at 10,000). Numbers and method: .agent-results/ig-7sn.2/baseline.md; rerun with tests/perf/perf_baseline.gd. Budget: SYSTEMS § Performance budgets (p99 8.3 ms, no frame over 33 ms). A fix cites before and after with the same script. Hub and Town rows. A roster action (set_hero_favorite) takes 166 ms with no battle out and 225 ms with five. roster_changed handlers: _refresh_roster 133 ms (hub/hub.gd: _refresh_hero_list rebuilds all 100 rows, each with a tooltip _hero_detail_text and a _partner_sign), _refresh_director_ui 13 / 31, _refresh_walkers 6.4, the save 4.4 / 40 (see the save bead). A building change (place_building) calls _notify_roster_changed and costs 137 ms. The dream read alone is 38-40 ms when the detail shows it.
WHAT: bring a roster action under 33 ms at 100 heroes. Logs: roster.log, town.log.
design:
DESIGN (extra, 2026-09-25; 2026-09-24 performance ADR items 1-2: measure first, cheapest fix first).

WHERE THE TIME GOES (roster.log, 0df0e29, 100 heroes, 0 / 5 orders): a roster action is 166 / 195 ms. Handlers: _refresh_roster 122 / 129, _refresh_director_ui 15 / 30 (its hero detail is 12, nearly all Ledger.history_lines over 10,000 records), _refresh_walkers 8.5 / 1.3, _refresh_partner 0.9, the save 4 / 35. The measure opens the hub with no building open. So today every roster action rebuilds panels nobody can see. A building change (137 ms) is the same handlers; you place a building with no panel open.

MEASURE FIRST: tests/perf/perf_baseline.gd's roster measure gains, before any change:
- (a) _refresh_roster split into: the per-row tooltip (_hero_detail_text), _partner_sign, is_hero_busy + is_hero_protected, add_item + metadata, _refresh_hero_option(TargetOption), _refresh_practice_options.
- (b) _refresh_director_ui split into its six calls.
- (c) The whole roster action and its handlers twice: no building open (as today), and the Forge open with one hero selected (the favorite toggle's real case).
Numbers go in the bead and SYSTEMS § Performance budgets (Hub row).

FIXES, in order. Re-measure after each and stop once the target holds.
1. Hidden panels don't rebuild (the root cause; fixes the building change and every roster action with the roster closed).
   - _refresh_roster returns at once while %SharedRosterPanel is hidden and marks itself stale. TargetOption (Sanctum) and the practice options (Training Hall) only show next to that panel, so one gate covers all three.
   - _refresh_director_ui's calls get the same gate, each on the panel it writes: _refresh_preset_lists on %TeamsView or %ExpeditionsView (PresetSelector and PresetDispatchList); _refresh_preset_editor and _refresh_practice_options on %TeamsView; _refresh_recovery_team_options on %ReliquarySection; _refresh_expeditions(true) on %ExpeditionsView; _refresh_hero_detail on %SelectedHeroPanel. The load-blocked lockout at its end stays ungated.
   - One small helper does it: a hidden panel records the refresh in a stale set and returns true.
   - The gate reads the panel's own visible flag, not is_visible_in_tree. Only _open sets those flags, so "hidden" and "_open will refresh it" always pair up.
   - _open, after setting visibility, runs the stale refreshes in a fixed order: roster first, then presets/practice, expeditions, and hero detail last (it reads the roster's selection). This follows the precedent: _open already refreshes the keeper, the placed panel and the lost caches.
   - Safe while stale: every reader of the roster's selection (_selected_hero, _selected_hero_ids: equip, rank up, sacrifice, favorite, walk-as-hero, the preset editor) sits in a panel that only shows with SharedRosterPanel. So a stale list is never read before _open rebuilds it.
   - The other roster_changed handlers are under 0.2 ms. Leave them. Not _refresh_equipped: it reads the roster selection (_selected_hero(), hub.gd:618), so with the roster gated it would read a stale list. Gate it on %SelectedHeroPanel (where %EquippedList lives), and _open runs it just before _refresh_hero_detail (extra's readiness sweep, accepted 2026-09-25).
2. No tooltip per row. _refresh_hero_list stops calling set_item_tooltip(_hero_detail_text) for all 100 rows. One gui_input connection on %RosterList (in code): on mouse motion, get_item_at_position(pos, true) → if that row's tooltip is empty, set it from _hero_detail_text. The row's text is unchanged. The tooltip waits about 0.5 s, so it is set before it shows.
3. Only if still over after 1-2, the history cache. _history_lines(hero) caches its lines per hero, next to _dreams. The cache clears where _dreams clears (_bond_index seeing a new ledger key). A hit also needs _roster_names() == the cached names, because a sacrifice changes names without a ledger record.
4. Only if still over, the per-row checks. Build the busy and protected id sets once per rebuild (from expedition_orders, stranded_incidents, team_presets), not per row (is_hero_busy builds a typed array per order per hero). Then look at bond_from's duplicate(true) per row.

NOT THIS BEAD: the save's 4 / 35 ms (ig-7sn.10: the roster action saves on roster_changed, so at 5 orders the whole action waits on it). _refresh_walkers' 8.5 ms (ig-7sn.11). The dream read's 34 ms after a ledger change (the settle pulse's handlers, ig-7sn.11).

title: Launch hitch: a 50-hero team snapshot is built 2-3 times per launch (about 60 ms on one frame)
description:
WHY

GameSession._team_snapshots costs 20-22 ms for a 50-hero team, and one launch or repeat run calls it 2-3 times (the forecasts, then the run). That is about 60 ms on one frame, over the 33 ms hitch line (SYSTEMS.md § Performance budgets). About 18 ms of each call is old cost (stats, kits). ig-uu7.4's cover orders add 2.2-2.5 ms.

FIX (lazy first)
- Build the team snapshot once per launch or repeat run, and give that same one to the forecasts and the run. First check that nothing between those calls can change the team (equip, rank-up, a roster change). If something can, the reuse must stop there.
- Only if one call is still over budget on its own: cut the per-hero stats cost.

ACCEPTANCE
- A 50-hero launch at the 10,000-record cap spends under 33 ms in team snapshots on its frame, measured the ig-uu7.4 way. Record it in the SYSTEMS Dispatched battles row.
- The 8 ig-544 cases are unchanged (.agent-results/ig-el4/balance_final.log), and the existing launch tests pass.
- This touches the GameSession snapshot seam (as ig-uu7.4 did), so review follows the usual rule.

QUEUE
After ig-7sn.3.

title: Early, mid and late game test saves for playtests and tuning
description:
WHY
Owner, 2026-09-24: "Kinda early in the game rn so let's hold off on the bond tuning, bc we're going to need to simulate early, mid and late game to play test correctly."
Bond tuning waits on this. So does any balance call that needs more than a fresh save.

WHAT (scope first: design says what each stage holds, tester says how to build it)
Three repeatable game states that look like a real player's game at three points:
- early: a few pulls, one team, low buildings
- mid: several teams, ranked heroes, gear, most halls, some history (fights, bonds, deaths)
- late: a big roster, high ranks, a full town, a long history
Each is built from a seed, so it comes out the same every time. Each goes through SaveService (boundary #1), loads in the game for a playtest, and can be read by tests for tuning (bonds first).

OPEN
- Fast-forward real play (a bot summons, builds and runs expeditions) or write the state directly? Fast-forward gives an honest Ledger history, which bond tuning needs. Writing it directly is quicker.
- What early, mid and late mean in numbers (goes in SYSTEMS).
- How the owner loads one without touching their real save: a separate slot or folder.

NOT
No balance changes while building it. Never written to the owner's real save folder.
design:
2026-09-24 extra (design), with a read-only godot-tester feasibility check (file:line verified by me).

WHAT EACH STAGE HOLDS: docs/SYSTEMS.md "## Stage saves — ig-eek" (new section, after the dream catalogue). Early 2 h, Mid 20 h, Late = the Ledger at its 10,000 cap after an eviction. The other columns are checks on the finished save, not inputs. PROVISIONAL.

METHOD: FAST-FORWARD. A headless bot plays through the public GameSession calls on the live clock. Why: bonds and dreams read the Ledger. A written Ledger would bake in the rate bond tuning has to measure (how often a battle isn't routine). Every action has a GameSession entry point:
- summon_hero :186 (after Summon.roll, hub/summon/summon.gd:19)
- sacrifice_hero / rank_up_hero :441 / :461
- equip_item :290
- place_building / upgrade_building :722 / :353
- station_hero :554, assign_home :767
- dispatch_expedition / dispatch_force :1020 / :1042
- rescue: start_rescue_window / dispatch_rescue / abandon_stranded :1346 / :1357 / :1413
- time: tick_expeditions :1720
Time must go through tick_expeditions, the live path. The offline path makes no wood, stone, food or construction (:1855). Big steps are safe: BattleSimulation.advance turns elapsed seconds into whole ticks and carries the remainder (battle_simulation.gd:135). Cost is small: the el4 grid ran 112 battles in about 32 s, mostly boot.
No cheating: no granted resources, no edited heroes. A bot stall is a progression finding (Ashfall's boss is already flagged, SYSTEMS § The three zones).

REPRODUCIBLE = KEEP THE FILES, not rebuild byte-identical. Design call: no code change.
- Battles are NOT seedable through the public API. GameSession._new_run_seed() uses Crypto (game_session.gd:2391), called by every dispatch path. Item ids use Crypto too (equipment/item.gd:25).
- seed(N) at start still fixes the summon and cache rolls (global randi/randf), so rebuilds stay close.
- Consumers read the kept files. Bond tuning recomputes from a fixed Ledger. Combat checks on a stage roster call BattleSimulation.create_run with explicit seeds, like the balance gates.
- If byte-identical rebuilds are ever needed, the fix is a seam that injects the run-seed source. That goes to the architect first; not now.
- Ledger "time" is wall clock (game_session.gd:2684), so a fast-forward stamps every record within minutes. Nothing reads record time today (only history/ledger.gd:20 writes it; bonds and history use seq). If a reader is ever added, the bot must pass game-clock time.

FILES (godot-tester owns the exact place): save.json + ledger.jsonl per stage as test fixtures, e.g. tests/fixtures/stages/<stage>/. Late is about 2.7 MB at the cap (SYSTEMS :764). Rebuild on purpose only: schema change, or a bot policy change. The bot saves with no order in flight, because a loaded save runs offline progress for the time since it was written (save_service.gd:169).

OWNER'S REAL SAVE: never touched.
- The bot runs with APPDATA pointed at a temp folder, same as the GUT command. Mandatory.
- The owner plays a stage through a launcher, e.g. playtest/play-mid.cmd: set APPDATA to a playtest folder next to it, copy that stage's files in if absent, start export/game.exe. No game code. It isolates everything, because save_service.gd:5-12, systems/settings.gd and ui/pause_menu.gd all write user:// only (no absolute path, no env read). Deleting the folder resets the stage.

BUILD ORDER: early first, then use it (check the bot, the checks and the launcher on a short run). Mid, then late.
ACCEPTANCE (proposed): each stage built by the bot under a redirected APPDATA and passing its SYSTEMS checks, or a filed finding naming the check it missed. A real load of each through SaveService (boundary #1, review mandatory). The launcher starts the export on each stage with the owner's real save folder untouched (compare its mtime before and after). One GUT test loads each fixture and reads its bonds.
acceptance_criteria:
(Every engine run has APPDATA redirected to a temp folder. Refs at HEAD 9687058. This turns the design's proposed acceptance into checks.)
1. The bot. godot-tester picks its path, for example tests/stages/stage_bot.gd. It is run by hand, never from tests/unit.
   - It plays only through public GameSession calls:
     - summon_hero, sacrifice_hero, rank_up_hero, equip_item;
     - place_building, upgrade_building, station_hero, assign_home;
     - preview_force, dispatch_force, request_stop_expedition;
     - start_rescue_window, dispatch_rescue, abandon_stranded;
     - tick_expeditions.
   - One exception: it lands jobs with GameSession._land_battle_checks() in a wait loop, like the GUT helpers (test_repeat_check.gd:180). That is the pulse's own landing step.
   - A grep of the bot finds no other underscore call on GameSession, no set(), no kill_hero, and no write to a Hero or GameSession field.
   - Time passes only through tick_expeditions, in one fixed step of at most 5 s. The step goes in the run log. Why the cap: a longer step delays each next leg by up to one step, and that lowers the records an hour that bond tuning reads.
   - A step starts only with no job out (GameSession._battle_jobs empty) and no order in "checking". A live repeat check lands within a second, so the bot adds no idle time a player wouldn't have.
   - Until-stopped dispatch goes preview_force, then land the preview, then dispatch_force with the same inputs (ig-7sn.14). Fixed-run dispatch needs no preview.
   - It plays SYSTEMS § Stage saves' fixed greedy order. It calls seed(N) once at the start, and N goes in the run log.
2. Deaths (boundary #3): every hero missing from the final roster has a death record or a sacrifice in the Ledger. The bot never removes a hero itself.
3. Each stage's save:
   - It is made at its SYSTEMS point: Early at 2 h of game clock, Mid at 20 h, Late once the Ledger holds 10,000 records and has evicted at least once.
   - Before it saves, request_stop_expedition is called on every order, and the orders come home. So there is no order in flight and no job out, and a later load runs no offline progress.
   - The run log lists each SYSTEMS check for the stage, with its value and pass or miss.
   - A miss files a bead under ig-eek that names the check (a progression finding). The save is still kept, per SYSTEMS.
   - The files are save.json plus ledger.jsonl per stage, in tests/fixtures/stages/<stage>/ (godot-tester may move them). A README line records HEAD, N, the step, the wall time and the game clock reached.
4. Boundary #1: copy each stage into a temp APPDATA and load it with the real SaveService.
   - load_game() returns true, with no warning and no load_blocked.
   - Roster size, building levels and Ledger count match the run log.
   - Save it again, reload, and to_dict is equal.
   - Sol reviews it.
5. A GUT test in tests/unit runs in the normal suite. It copies each fixture into user:// under the redirected APPDATA, loads it through SaveService, and reads bond_index():
   - Mid and Late have at least one bond;
   - Late's Ledger holds 10,000 records and ledger_next_seq is above 10,001, so it has evicted. (Seq 1 can survive, because eviction goes by tier, routine first.)

title: Bond index: fold appended records in instead of rebuilding every pair (ADR item 5 upgrade)
description:
WHY: ig-m6o.2.2.1 measured at the 10,000-record cap (7 runs, owner PC). The kept index in hub.gd rebuilds every pair on each ledger change: 103-129 ms with 5-hero teams, ~4.4 s with 50-hero teams (frontier_march). A record-writing roster change (settle, summon, rank-up) costs 251-351 ms end to end, against the 33 ms no-hitch line in SYSTEMS.md § Performance budgets. DECISIONS.md 2026-09-24 'Bonds stay derived' item 5 names the incremental fold as the upgrade path. Its considered-and-deferred 'the fold now: nothing needs it' is now contradicted by these numbers. The owner's save has 5 records today, so nobody feels it yet; the cost grows with the save.

WHAT: fold each appended record into the kept counts, and fold each evicted record out. At the cap every append evicts the oldest record, so a fold that falls back to a full rebuild on eviction gains nothing where it matters. A truncation (rollback) or a new array (load) still does a full rebuild. The counts stay unsaved view state in hub.gd beside the index. The ADR flagged eviction and the dream's order as the fiddly parts.
design:
DESIGN (2026-09-24). The ADR amendment (DECISIONS.md "Bonds stay derived", items 3 and 5) is already written. This field adds to the description and its acceptance.

1. WHERE THE INDEX LIVES
- GameSession holds it as unsaved fields: _bond_state, _bond_ledger (the array it mirrors, or null), _bond_seq, and bond_builds (for tests).
- bond_index() -> Dictionary returns _bond_state["pairs"], the dict Bonds.bond_from reads today. Callers never mutate it.
- If the ledger array is not the mirrored one, or ledger_next_seq != _bond_seq, it first rebuilds with Bonds.index and counts bond_builds.
- The hub and ig-uu7.4's _team_snapshots both read bond_index(). hub.gd drops _bonds, _bonds_ledger, _bonds_seq and bond_builds.
- The rules stay in Bonds (pure static). GameSession only holds the state and calls Bonds. ARCHITECTURE rule 1 holds.

2. THE FOLD (history/bonds.gd)
State: {pairs, counts, dead, battles}.
- pairs: {hero: {other: tally}}, the same shape as today.
- counts: {hero: {other: [4 slots in FACTS order]}}. Each slot is [count, seq, wording, dead, zone]. seq is the seq of the latest record with that fact. Today the slot holds the record's array index, which eviction shifts. zone is that record's zone.
- dead: {order: [dead hero ids, in died-record order]}.
- battles: {order: battle record} for the battles present, so a later died record can find its battle.

_tally(other, slots, balance) stops reading the ledger:
- fact.seq and fact.zone come from the best slot;
- last_seq is the highest slot seq;
- the tie rule (>= on seq, later kind in FACTS order wins) is unchanged.

fold_in(state, record, balance):
- A battle: register battles[order]. Count exactly what index() counts today, with `at` replaced by the record's seq, and store its zone. Deaths come from dead[order], which is normally empty because a hero dies after the battle that stranded it.
- A died record with battle_order: append its hero to dead[order]. If battles holds that battle B, then for each ordered pair (h, o) of B's team where both differ from this hero:
  - skip the pair if an earlier id in dead[order] is neither h nor o (it already counted B: the first qualifying death, once per record);
  - otherwise count the death slot with dead = this hero.
  A slot's seq, wording, dead and zone move only when B's seq is greater than the slot's seq: the latest battle wins, as in the rebuild.
- Anything else: nothing.
- Then retally every pair it touched.

fold_out(state, record, balance) -> bool:
- A battle B: take out exactly what fold_in put in, deaths recomputed from dead[order], then erase battles[order]. In each touched slot, count -= 1:
  - at 0, the slot empties;
  - still above 0 with slot seq == B.seq: return false, because the previous latest record is unknown.
  A pair whose counts are all 0 is erased. Then retally the rest.
- A died record whose battle is still in battles: return false. Otherwise remove its id from dead[order], erasing an empty entry.
- Anything else: true.
- Under today's tiers, false never happens:
  - every scoring record is a non-routine battle (a routine victory has no moments, so no downing, no stranding and no death);
  - tier 1 evicts oldest first;
  - died records (tier 4) go only after every battle.
  So an evicted scoring record is always the oldest in each of its slots. The false path exists for a future tier change (meals and encounters, ADR item 7).

index(ledger, balance) = a fresh state with every record folded in, oldest first. The rebuild and the fold share one set of rules. The old upfront dead_by_order pass becomes dead[order] filling as records arrive; a battle folded in after its death still picks that death up, so both orders give the same answer.

3. HOOKS AND INVALIDATION (systems/game_session.gd)
- Ledger.evict returns the records it removed, in eviction order. _evict_ledger passes each to fold_out. Callers that ignore the return are unchanged.
- _record: check in_step (mirrored array and _bond_seq == ledger_next_seq) BEFORE the append. After the append, if in_step: fold_in(ledger.back()) and _bond_seq = ledger_next_seq.
- _evict_ledger: for each evicted record, while in step, call fold_out. If it returns false, set _bond_ledger = null so the next bond_index() rebuilds.
- A load and a rollback need no hook; the key handles both:
  - _read_ledger always builds a new array, so a load (and the from_dict inside a rollback) leaves the mirrored array behind;
  - the rollback then restores the same array with its old ledger_next_seq. A rolled-back append leaves ledger_next_seq below _bond_seq, so the next ask rebuilds. A rollback with no append leaves them equal and keeps the index.
- Eviction runs before the deferred notifications flush (ADR item 3), so no reader sees the list between an append and its eviction.
- Nothing is saved: no to_dict/from_dict key, no SaveService change.

4. THE DREAM'S ORDER
- The dream stays out of the fold (ADR items 2 and 6).
- Why the order matters: a dream is an oldest-first state machine. Evicting the record that opened, paid or lost a debt changes how every later record reads, so the next save can open a different debt. No exact take-out exists short of re-reading that hero.
- What changes: the hub memoises dreams. _dreams is {hero_id: dream}, hub view state, emptied whenever the hub sees the ledger key change (section 5).
  - Every dream read goes through one hub helper that calls _bond_index() first, so the key check always runs before the memo is read. No handler order can see a stale dream.
  - The detail panel reads the selected hero's dream once per ledger change, however many times it refreshes. How many times it refreshes is ig-7sn.3's job (cut 2026-09-24): this bead owns what one refresh costs, not how many there are.
  - ig-m6o.2.2.2's speaker dream costs one read per ledger change.
  - A quiet roster change reads none.
- Upgrade path, only if a measurement asks for it:
  - on append, a forward step is exact;
  - on eviction, a routine battle only moves the fights count, and any other record naming the hero re-reads that hero.

5. HOW THE HUB LEARNS THE INDEX CHANGED
No new signal:
- Every append arrives with roster_changed (settle, summon, rank-up, death), which already runs _refresh_partner and _refresh_walkers.
- _bond_index() stays the hub's one entry point. It returns GameSession.bond_index(), and compares the ledger key (array identity plus ledger_next_seq) with the hub's last look:
  - same array, new seq: say new bonds, then empty _dreams;
  - a new array (the first look, or a load): say nothing, empty _dreams.
- _say_new_bonds can no longer diff the old index, because the fold changes it in place. The hub keeps _partners ({hero_id: partner_id} for the living) from its last look and compares the new partners with it. The wording is unchanged.

6. FILES
- history/bonds.gd
- history/ledger.gd (evict's return)
- systems/game_session.gd
- hub/hub.gd
- tests/unit/test_bonds.gd (bond_builds moves to GameSession), plus test_ledger.gd if it pins evict.

7. ACCEPTANCE (adds to the description's)
- Property test: seeded random ledgers appended one record at a time under a small cap (about 20). They mix hard fights, saves, rescues, strandings with later deaths, routine victories, summons and rank-ups. After every append and every eviction, the folded pairs equal Bonds.index(ledger)'s pairs. Include one load and one rollback mid-run.
  Equal means every non-empty tally matches; a hero with no pairs may be absent or {}.
- The new index() equals the pre-change index() on test_bonds' fixtures and on one seeded 2,000-record ledger. Capture the old output before the rewrite.
- A constructed eviction fold_out cannot take out (a died record evicted while its battle stays, using a test tier list) makes the next bond_index() rebuild, and the result is still equal.
- Invalidation counts:
  - an append folds and rebuilds nothing (bond_builds unchanged);
  - a load rebuilds once;
  - a rolled-back mutation that appended rebuilds once;
  - a rolled-back mutation with no append rebuilds nothing.
- The hub still says "X and Y grew close." once, on the append that forms the bond, and says nothing on the first look or after a load.
- The memo: two detail refreshes with no ledger change between them read the selected hero's dream once. An append between them reads it again. Call _refresh_hero_detail twice in the test, so it holds whether or not ig-7sn.3 has landed.
- Printed at the cap, best/worst of seven:
  - a record-writing roster change against a quiet one; expect them within one fold plus at most two dream reads;
  - the per-record fold with 5-hero and with 50-hero teams (milliseconds);
  - the rebuild after a load with 50-hero teams (still seconds; load only).
  Record them on the Bond read cost row and under § Performance budgets, Load (no target yet, measured and recorded).
- BUILT. Sol review: confirm nothing new reaches to_dict, and that fold == rebuild holds by construction.

ORDER: ig-m6o.2.2.2 also edits hub._refresh_partner and bonds.gd (greeting). Run the two one after the other, never in parallel (the director's order: this bead first). ig-7sn.3 also edits hub.gd (the roster_changed connects and the order cards) and the SYSTEMS Bond read cost row. It shares no behaviour with this bead, so either order works; whichever lands second rebases. If ig-7sn.3 lands first, the "quiet roster change" baseline above already has one detail refresh, not two.
acceptance_criteria: 1) GUT: the folded index equals a full rebuild after appends below the cap, appends at the cap with eviction, a rollback, and a load (reuse the test_bonds fixtures). 2) Printed at the cap, best/worst of 7: a record-writing roster change costs about a quiet one, and with 50-hero teams the per-record cost is milliseconds, not seconds. 3) Nothing saved: no to_dict/from_dict key, no SaveService change. 4) DECISIONS.md item 5 gets a dated amendment line saying these numbers pulled the fold forward.
