title: Ground blood for flesh bodies: a pool under a downed hero or dead creature, capped and fading
description:
WHY
Owner ruling, 2026-09-24: "blood for creatures/our heroes". Flesh bodies leave blood on the ground when they go down or die. Today, heroes are the only flesh, and in battle they go down (downed) but never die in the view: only enemies die there. So today this shows under downed heroes, and it will show under a dead flesh enemy with no new code once one exists.

BEHAVIOR
1. When. In the view's snapshot diff, a flesh actor going from alive to downed, or from alive to dead, leaves a blood pool where it fell (Low or Full). The body type comes from .1's lookup. A skeleton never bleeds.
   - The death event today is enemies only (battle_vfx.gd:201). Add the downed transition the same way (an ally, alive before, downed after), or read it in the unit view, which already knows "downed" (battle_unit_view.gd:413). Pick whichever keeps it in one place.
2. The pool. A flat dark red disc on the ground, built in code (a flat mesh with an unshaded material, or a Decal with a GradientTexture2D made in code). No new assets. It grows over a short time, then stays.
3. Caps. A pool fades and frees after a PROVISIONAL time, sooner on Low. A live-pool cap (PROVISIONAL, Low's smaller than Full's): past it, the oldest pool fades early. Pool the nodes if the measurement shows creation or cleanup over budget.
4. A revived or carried hero leaves its pool behind; the pool fades as normal. No blood trail.
5. Off: nothing, as today.

ACCEPTANCE (tests/unit, APPDATA redirected)
- A hero going down on Full leaves one pool at its position. A skeleton dying leaves none. On Off, nothing spawns.
- The live-pool cap holds, and the oldest pool is the one that fades early. Pools free after their time.
- Rebuilding the view from a snapshot shows no pools (nothing is saved, the same view-only rule as the lost limb).
- Boundary #4, Off vs Full: the same outcome.
- Cost: frontier_march with 50 heroes going down in a short window, Full, windowed: p50, p99, the worst frame, and the peak pool count.
- A screenshot of a downed hero in a pool, gore Full. Throwaway APPDATA.
- BUILT. Verifier pass: boundary #4.

FILES
combat/battle/battle_vfx.gd and/or combat/battle/battle_unit_view.gd, tests/unit.

NON-GOALS
Blood trails. Blood on walls or units. Saving pools. Hero limbs. Skeletons.

title: Gore worst case, everything at once: measure and set the Low and Full caps
description:
WHY
Each slice measured its own worst case, but effects stack: one area skill can dust, dismember, gib and collapse 30 skeletons at once, while up to 50 heroes bleed and go down. This slice measures everything together and sets the Low and Full caps, so Full holds the watched-battle budget and Low holds it with room to spare.

WORK
1. Two seeded worst cases, windowed, throwaway APPDATA, each with gore Full, then Low, then Off, and the heavy and crit chances forced high. Include heroes going down, so ground blood (.7) is in the count:
   - fallen_citadel: 30 heroes against a 30-enemy wave, then the boss and 10 adds;
   - frontier_march: 50 heroes against 30 objective enemies.
2. Report p50, p99 and the worst frame over the fight, the peak live parts, pools and effects, and the difference from the ig-7sn.2 baseline.
3. Set the caps (live parts, pools, fade times, specks and droplets) in their PROVISIONAL rows, so Full meets the watched-battle budget in SYSTEMS § Performance budgets and Low has headroom. Pool nodes if creation or cleanup is the cost.
4. Record the numbers in SYSTEMS § Performance budgets.

ACCEPTANCE
- The numbers in .agent-results/<this id>/ and in SYSTEMS.
- Full fits the budget at the worst case, or its caps come down until it does.
- BUILT.

NON-GOALS
New effects.

title: Dismemberment: a heavy hit knocks a part off, and the skeleton fights on
description:
WHY
"dismemberment ... as enemies get hit". A heavy hit knocks a part off a living skeleton, and it keeps fighting.

BEFORE BUILD (game-designer)
- The chance that a heavy or critical hit takes a part (PROVISIONAL). "Heavy" is today's: hp lost >= RECOIL_HP_FRACTION (0.25) of max HP.
- Which parts can go: arms, the head or skull, the jaw, the hat. Legs? A legless skeleton that still walks reads wrong, so the default is no legs.
- The most parts one enemy can lose.

BEHAVIOR
1. On a critical or heavy hit that doesn't kill a bones body (Low or Full), roll the view RNG against the chance. On a success, detach one allowed part with .3's helper, pushed along the hit direction.
2. It fights on. The sim is untouched, so it moves, attacks and dies as before; only the part is gone. Losing the weapon arm drops the weapon, and the attack animation still plays.
3. When it dies, the rest collapses as in .3. A lost part stays lost.
4. Low: the same, under Low's smaller cap on loose parts.

KNOWN ISSUE (add to KNOWN_ISSUES § Deliberate shortcuts when this lands; game-designer owns the wording)
"A lost limb is view-only. Reloading mid-battle, or leaving the battle view and coming back, rebuilds each enemy whole from the snapshot. Keeping it would mean saving view state or making the sim own it, and neither is worth it for looks." The director and extra agree on this.

ACCEPTANCE (tests/unit, APPDATA redirected)
- A forced heavy hit (the chance set to 1 in the test) hides one allowed part and spawns one loose body. A leg is never picked. The per-enemy limit holds.
- The enemy's actions and the outcome don't change (boundary #4, Off vs Full).
- Rebuilding the view from the same snapshot shows the enemy whole (the known issue, pinned by a test).
- Cost: the worst wave with every hit heavy, windowed, on top of .3's numbers.
- BUILT. Verifier pass: boundary #4.

FILES
combat/battle/battle_unit_view.gd, the gore helper, tests/unit, docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md.

NON-GOALS
A lost limb changing stats or behaviour (that would be the sim). Keeping lost limbs across a reload. Flesh bodies: heroes keep their limbs, because the sim carries, rescues and revives a downed hero, so a lost arm would need a saved injury (boundary #1). "Limbs only on true death" is a later owner ask.

title: Gibbing: a killing crit or skill blasts the skeleton apart along the hit
description:
WHY
"gibbletting". A killing crit or a killing skill blasts the skeleton apart instead of collapsing it.

BEHAVIOR
1. A bones body killed by a critical hit or a skill (Full): every part detaches at once with a strong push along the hit direction, spread in a cone, plus a burst of bone dust and splinters. For a burst skill, the push points away from its center.
2. Which kills count: in the same diff, the death's actor also took a critical "hit", or was hit by a "skill".
3. Low: a kill that would gib collapses instead (.3), with the extra dust.
4. The force and the spread are PROVISIONAL feel numbers (game-designer).

ACCEPTANCE (tests/unit, APPDATA redirected)
- On Full, a crit kill gibs: every part is loose, pushed away from the attacker (the parts' average velocity points along the direction). A plain kill collapses. On Low, a crit kill collapses.
- Boundary #4, Off vs Full.
- Cost: one burst skill killing 30 (fallen_citadel), Full, windowed.
- BUILT. Verifier pass: boundary #4.

FILES
The gore helper, combat/battle/battle_vfx.gd, tests/unit.

NON-GOALS
Flesh bodies (heroes and creatures bleed instead, .1 and .7). Parts breaking into smaller pieces.

title: Skeletons collapse into loose physics bones on death
description:
WHY
"physics for the bodies too". Today a dead skeleton plays Skeletons_Death, gets flung back a little (_pose_dead), and stays as a dimmed corpse. With gore on, it falls apart into loose bones instead.

DESIGN CHOICE (scoping)
Loose part bodies, not a ragdoll. A ragdoll (PhysicalBoneSimulator3D) keeps the joints together and needs colliders set up per bone for every model. Loose parts give one mechanism for this slice, dismemberment (.4) and gibbing (.5): "detach this part with this push". And a skeleton falling apart is the better look.

BEHAVIOR
1. One part-detach helper in the view (in combat/battle/: a small gore helper beside battle_vfx.gd, or inside battle_unit_view.gd). Given a unit, a part and an impulse, it:
   - bakes the part's current pose. The parts are skinned, so a raw copy pops into the bind pose. Try MeshInstance3D.bake_mesh_from_current_skeleton_pose first, and check it exists in 4.7.1. If baking spikes a 30-death frame, cache one baked mesh per model and part and place it at its bone's transform.
   - hides the source part and spawns a RigidBody3D with that mesh and a simple box or capsule shape, on the loose-parts layer from .2 (ground only).
   - matches part names by suffix, since they differ by model: the head is Head or Skull; the hat is Helmet, Hood or Hat; Cloak or Cape.
2. Death. When a bones body dies (Low or Full; every enemy today), it collapses: after a short buckle, every part detaches with a small push along the killing hit's direction (the "hit" event's direction from .1). Held weapons (the handslot attachments) drop too.
3. body_landed still fires once per death, when the parts first touch the ground. battle_view.gd:530 listens for it (the landing dust and shake).
4. Caps. Loose parts sleep, then fade and free after a PROVISIONAL time. A live-part cap (PROVISIONAL, Low's smaller than Full's): past it, the oldest parts fade early. Pool the part bodies if the measurement shows their creation or cleanup is over budget.
5. Off: today's death exactly (the clip, the fling, the dimmed corpse).

ACCEPTANCE (tests/unit, APPDATA redirected)
- Off gives today's death: the same nodes, and body_landed fires as today.
- Full: a dead enemy's parts are hidden and the same number of loose bodies exist. They sleep and free within the cap and time. body_landed fires once.
- Boundary #4: .1's Off-vs-Full outcome check, extended to deaths.
- Cost, on top of the ig-7sn.2 baseline: 30 enemies killed in one frame (fallen_citadel's wave, one area skill), windowed. Report p50, p99 and the worst frame over the next 3 seconds, and the peak part count. It must fit the watched-battle budget, or Full's cap comes down.
- A screenshot of a collapse, gore Full. Throwaway APPDATA.
- BUILT. Verifier pass mandatory: boundary #4, and boundary #2 (the body_landed wiring).

FILES
combat/battle/battle_unit_view.gd, combat/battle/battle_vfx.gd or a new gore helper in combat/battle/, heroes/hero_model.gd if the part lookup belongs there, tests/unit.

NON-GOALS
Limbs lost before death (.4). Gibbing (.5). Flesh bodies: heroes and creatures bleed (.1, .7) and keep their limbs.

title: Gore setting (Off/Low/Full) and hit effects by body type: bone dust or blood spray (view only)
description:
WHY
The first visible gore, and the off switch every later slice needs. The director's first order put the setting last. It comes first here, so no physics slice ever ships without a way to turn it off.
Owner ruling, 2026-09-24: "bones for skellys, blood for creatures/our heroes". So the hit effect depends on the body type.

BEHAVIOR
1. The setting. systems/settings.gd gains a "gore" key in its "combat" section: "off", "low" or "full", default "full". A bad value falls back to the default, like screen_shake does. ui/pause_menu.gd shows it beside Screen shake. It stays out of the save; the Settings header says why (not boundary #1, not an autoload).
   - Off: today's effects, nothing added.
   - Low and Full: the body-type hit effect below. Low spawns half the specks or droplets. Later slices give Low smaller caps too.
2. The body type, decided in the view. heroes/hero_model.gd gains one small static lookup from (faction, archetype) to "bones" or "flesh": a look whose model is a Skeleton_* is bones, everything else is flesh (every hero today). The unit view keeps it. The sim never sees it.
3. Hit direction, derived in the view. BattleVfx.events_between already diffs two snapshots. For a "hit" on actor T in the same diff:
   - a basic_attack whose target_id is T: from the attacker's position to T (the event carries both);
   - a skill that hit T: from its center to T for a burst, along its facing for a line;
   - otherwise: backward from T's facing, which is what _pose_dead's fling uses today.
   Add it to the "hit" event as "direction" (a flat Vector3). No sim change and no new snapshot field.
4. The hit effect picks by body type (Low or Full). A critical or heavy hit throws more; "heavy" is today's: hp lost >= RECOIL_HP_FRACTION of max HP.
   - Bones: bone-coloured dust and a few splinters, thrown along the direction instead of straight up.
   - Flesh: a blood spray (dark red droplets) along the direction.
   - Reuse _burst and the shared materials. Build the speck, splinter and droplet meshes in code (a small box, prism or sphere), like today's specks. No new assets.
   - It stays under MAX_LIVE_EFFECTS (40). The counts and the blood colour are PROVISIONAL feel numbers beside ig-iml's, game-designer's to tune.
5. Its own RNG. Any randomness uses a view RandomNumberGenerator, never the sim's.

ACCEPTANCE (tests/unit, APPDATA redirected)
- Settings: the key round-trips through settings.cfg, and a bad value reads "full". Nothing new in any to_dict or from_dict, and no SaveService change.
- Body type: every enemy look reads bones and every hero look reads flesh.
- Direction: for a seeded diff with a basic attack, a burst skill, a line skill and a hit with no attacker, each "hit" event's direction follows the rule above.
- Off spawns exactly what today spawns for the same events (count the children). Full: a hit on a skeleton spawns dust; a hit on a hero spawns blood.
- Boundary #4: the same seeded battle, run twice with the view attached, gore Off then Full, gives the same BattleOutcome. If the view can't run with the sim headless, the verifier checks instead that no gore code writes battle state or draws from the sim's RNG.
- Cost: time the worst hit burst (one area skill hitting fallen_citadel's 30-enemy wave), best and worst of seven, printed (CODING_RULES § Performance).
- Screenshots in .agent-results/<this id>/: dust on a skeleton crit and blood on a hero hit, gore Full. Throwaway APPDATA.
- BUILT. Verifier pass: boundary #4 (view only, its own RNG) and boundary #2 (the pause-menu option).

FILES
systems/settings.gd, ui/pause_menu.gd (and its .tscn if the option is a node), heroes/hero_model.gd (the body-type lookup), combat/battle/battle_vfx.gd, combat/battle/battle_unit_view.gd (keeps the body type), tests/unit (settings, body type, the vfx direction).

NON-GOALS
Ground blood (.7). Loose parts or physics (.3). Hero limbs. The action arena.
design:
DESIGN (extra, 2026-09-25; checked against 7a758ae). The body's BEHAVIOR stands, except item 3, which ig-36y made simpler.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE THE BODY: ig-36y (e10861c, real knockback) already writes the hit direction.
- The sim now stores effect_state.hit_from on every direct hit: the unit vector the hit sends the target, away from the attacker (battle_simulation.gd:1890-1895).
- Area and telegraph hits set it through _push_all: along the line for a line, out from the center for a circle or around_caster (:1140-1167, :1621-1630). That covers enemy telegraphs on heroes too.
- It is a view cue, and the sim never reads it. Old saves have none. The unit view already reads it for recoil and the death fling, with -facing when it's missing (battle_unit_view.gd:193-195).
- So body item 3 and readiness notes 1-2 are superseded: no pass after the loop, and no copy of the skill test. The direction is read straight from the snapshot. Still no sim change and no new field.

PLAN
1. The setting. Copy Settings.window_size, not screen_shake. Add GORE_KEY = "gore" in SECTION "combat", GORE_LEVELS = ["off", "low", "full"], default "full". Settings.gore() returns anything else as "full", and set_gore() is next to it. The config is already cached in memory (Settings._config), so reading it on every hit costs nothing. The pause menu gets a %Gore OptionButton beside %ScreenShake: a node in ui/pause_menu.tscn with a unique name, filled and wired in pause_menu.gd like %WindowSize (boundary #2).
2. Body type. HeroModel.body_type(faction, archetype) returns "bones" if look(faction, archetype)[0].begins_with("Skeleton_"), else "flesh". look() falls back to the knight for an unknown archetype, so bosses read bones.
3. The hit event carries the rest. In BattleVfx.events_between, the "hit" event gains three keys:
   - "body": body_type(faction, archetype).
   - "direction": the actor's hit_from as Vector3(x, 0, y), normalized, or -facing when hit_from is missing. Same rule as the unit view.
   - "heavy": hp lost >= max_hp * BattleUnitView.RECOIL_HP_FRACTION. Today's heavy test, read from the snapshot's max_hp.
   The event carries the body, so battle_unit_view.gd needs no change. Neither does battle_view.gd, which has high1's WIP.
4. The spray. In spawn's "hit" branch, after today's sparks, only when Settings.gore() != "off":
   - Bones: bone-coloured dust (a new BONE_COLOR const) plus a few splinters (a thin PrismMesh).
   - Flesh: dark red droplets (a small SphereMesh).
   - Each one is a _burst aimed along "direction" with a narrow spread. _burst gains three parameters, direction, spread and mesh, whose defaults are today's values (UP, 180, the speck), so every existing call is unchanged.
   - Count: base, doubled for a critical or heavy hit, halved on Low (at least 1).
   - The particles go under the hit's own effect node. That adds no node to BattleVfx, so the MAX_LIVE_EFFECTS (40) cap and the reaper work as they do today.
   - PROVISIONAL: the counts, the spread, and the bone and blood colours are consts beside HIT_SPARK_COUNT. They are game-designer's to tune.
5. RNG. CPUParticles3D and the global randf draw from the engine's global generator. The sim draws only from its own RandomNumberGenerator, which it restores from state.rng_state. So gore can't shift a battle, and no new RNG is needed. Boundary #4 is a read (readiness note 5).

KNOWN LIMIT (ponytail): a bleed or burn tick goes straight to _take_damage (battle_simulation.gd:1278). It bumps last_hit_tick but leaves hit_from alone, so its spray follows the last direct hit. That's fine for a spray. Add a DoT cue only if the owner notices.

COST: SYSTEMS' watched-battle row says effects already reach the 40 cap, and a frame that spawns one peaks at 15-19 ms. Gore adds particle nodes inside those effects, so measure it in that row, not only as one burst.

BOUNDARIES: #4, view only, with no sim read or write and not the sim's RNG. #2, the new pause-menu node. #1: out of the save, since Settings is settings.cfg. #3 untouched.

FILES: systems/settings.gd, ui/pause_menu.gd, ui/pause_menu.tscn, heroes/hero_model.gd, combat/battle/battle_vfx.gd, and tests/unit (test_window_size.gd's pattern for the setting, test_hero_model.gd, test_battle_vfx.gd), plus the perf row in tests/perf/perf_baseline.gd. Not battle_unit_view.gd, and not battle_view.gd.

AMENDED (director, 2026-09-25, from extra's readiness sweep on a07f3a6): the refs moved (hit_from :1626/:1640/:1985, erased :133; the unit view's read :198-199; the global-generator rule game_session.gd:488); the note has the list. _burst gained a trailing delay parameter (ig-n7b), and :272 passes it positionally, so the new direction, spread and mesh parameters go after delay, with today's values as defaults. Gore sprays only when damage > 0.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Setting: "gore" round-trips through settings.cfg for off, low and full. A missing key, a bad string or a non-string reads "full". Nothing new in any to_dict or from_dict, and no SaveService change. The pause menu's %Gore shows the stored value and writes it back.
2. Body type: every ENEMY_LOOKS archetype reads "bones", every ALLY_LOOKS archetype reads "flesh", and an unknown enemy archetype reads "bones".
3. Direction: in a seeded diff, a hit on an actor with hit_from gives a direction equal to that vector, normalized, on the flat plane. A hit on an actor without it (an old save) gives -facing. "heavy" is true exactly when hp lost >= 25% of max_hp.
4. Spawn: with gore off, the same events give exactly today's children under each effect node (count and class). With full, a skeleton hit with damage > 0 adds bone dust and splinters, and a hero hit with damage > 0 adds droplets. A hit with no damage adds nothing. Each burst's direction is the event's direction, and none of them adds a child to BattleVfx itself. Low's amount is half of full's, and at least 1. A crit or heavy hit throws double. Every gore burst's delay + lifetime ends inside its hit effect's lifetime (0.7 s, or 0.85 s on a crit), and the hit effect's lifetime is today's. No gore code or test calls seed() or randomize() on the global generator.
5. Boundary #4: the same seeded battle, run twice with the view attached, gore off then full, gives the same BattleOutcome. If the view can't run headless with the sim, the verifier checks that no gore code reads or writes battle state or touches the sim's RNG.
6. Cost: the worst burst is one diff with 30 hits (fallen_citadel's wave), timed best and worst of seven. Then perf_baseline's two watched-battle rows (battle_citadel, battle_frontier), each run four times in one session, alternating gore off, full, off, full. For each row, both full runs have frames over 33 no more than the worse off run's + 1, and p99 no more than the worse off run's p99 + 1 ms (PROVISIONAL, settled by this run). title: Spike: physics engine for loose bones (Jolt or Godot Physics) and its ADR
description:
WHY
Loose bones need rigid bodies. project.godot sets no physics engine, so 4.7.1's default runs today. Choosing Jolt changes one project setting that every physics user shares. Godot resolves that at runtime, so a green gate alone proves little. This spike picks the engine with numbers and writes the ADR. Engine lane.

QUESTIONS TO SETTLE
1. Which engine runs today? Print it at runtime (the "physics/3d/physics_engine" setting and the server actually in use). Don't assume the default.
2. Jolt or Godot Physics for loose bones? Measure both in a throwaway scene that isn't committed: 30 skeletons x 10 parts = 300 small bodies dropped at once on a ground plane, settling and sleeping. Report p50, p99 and the worst frame over the first 3 seconds, and when all of them sleep.
3. What else changes if the engine changes:
   - combat/arena/arena.gd: %HeroCapsule and %EnemyCapsule are CharacterBody3D with move_and_slide; %AttackHitbox and %EnemyAttackHitbox are Area3D. Test: tests/unit/test_arena.gd.
   - hub/town/town_hero.gd: the body is a CharacterBody3D (MOTION_MODE_FLOATING, move_and_slide at l.112). Test: tests/unit/test_town_hero.gd. The director's list missed this one.
   - hub/town/town_view.gd:665: the click pick is direct_space_state.intersect_ray. Test: tests/unit/test_town_walkers.gd:434.
   Run both gates with the engine switched, plus a windowed walk of the town body and a windowed arena fight.
4. The physics thread (physics/3d/run_on_separate_thread): measure it too. It isn't free here: the town pick at town_view.gd:665 queries the space from input, and with a separate physics thread Godot only allows that during the physics step. Name the fix (move the pick into the physics step). Switch the thread on only if it measurably wins (threading ADR, item 3).

OUTPUT
- An ADR in DECISIONS.md (godot-architect): which engine, the numbers, what it changes, and what was rejected. If it's Jolt, one line in project.godot, and both gates green with it.
- The collision layer loose parts use: they hit the ground only (a static plane in the battle scene), never units, never the town's pick layers.

ACCEPTANCE
- The measurement in .agent-results/<this id>/: both engines, the 300-body drop, the hardware noted.
- BUILT with the chosen engine. Windowed check: the town body walks and collides as before, and the arena's hitboxes still land.
- Verifier pass mandatory: boundary #2 (the project setting and the physics nodes).

FILES
project.godot (only if the engine changes), docs/DECISIONS.md.

NON-GOALS
Any gore code. Hero ragdolls.
design:
DESIGN = THE SPIKE'S PLAN (extra, 2026-09-25; checked against HEAD 9687058). It keeps the ACC. It adds where the spike lives, a decision rule so the numbers pick the engine, and today's refs.

WHAT'S THERE (checked)
- project.godot has no physics key at all: no engine, no thread setting, no layer names.
- Four physics users. Only the town pick queries the space:
  - arena.gd moves capsules with move_and_slide inside _physics_process (:209, :217, :243, :811). Its layers are 1 and 2 (arena.tscn :78, :96-97, :108, :122).
  - town_hero.gd moves with move_and_slide in _physics_process (:125, :134). It's MOTION_MODE_FLOATING (:55), on layer 0 with mask PICK_LAYER (:57-58).
  - town_view.gd's _pick (:671) calls direct_space_state.intersect_ray (:677). It runs from _unhandled_input (:169, via :184 and building_at :663→:664). Ten test call sites call building_at directly: test_hub_controls 4, test_town_builder 3, test_town_camera 1, test_town_food 1, test_town_walkers 1. ground_point (:653) is plane math, with no physics.
  - The town layers are PICK_LAYER 2 (layer 2) and WALKER_PICK_LAYER 4 (layer 3) (town_view.gd:43, :46).
- The battle scene has no physics. battle_view.tscn's Ground is a MeshInstance3D with no collider, and SceneRouter loads it as its own scene (scene_router.gd:8), so it's a separate world from the town and the arena.

1. WHERE THE SPIKE LIVES: its own throwaway project, outside the repo.
- Why not inside the repo: .agent-results/ is gitignored but still inside the Godot project, and Godot scans it (it already holds .gd copies, for example .agent-results/ig-6l4/baseline/tests/unit/test_arena.gd). A spike .tscn there would be imported and gated. A second project also lets the engine switch be one line in a file nobody else reads. The repo's project.godot is never edited to measure.
- So: a folder in the temp dir with its own project.godot. vsync is off there (display/window/vsync/vsync_mode = 0), and the window is 1920x1080. Afterwards, its source is kept in .agent-results/ig-c9y.2/spike/ with a .gdignore beside it, so the repo never imports it. The logs go in .agent-results/ig-c9y.2/.
- Same binary: tools/godot/Godot_v4.7.1-stable_win64_console.exe. Still one Godot at a time on the machine, for clean numbers and by the lane rule.

2. QUESTION 1: WHICH ENGINE RUNS TODAY
- The first run of the spike project has no physics key, the same condition as the repo (checked by grep at HEAD; the log records that grep). It prints:
  - ProjectSettings.get_setting("physics/3d/physics_engine");
  - PhysicsServer3D.get_class(), the server actually running;
  - the setting's hint_string from ProjectSettings.get_property_list(), which gives the exact engine names this build accepts (use those names in step 3, not a guess).
- It runs windowed, the way the game runs.
- No run against the repo is needed for this. If one is made anyway, it's -s with APPDATA redirected: the autoloads load in -s mode, and SaveService would read the owner's save.

3. THE DROP (both engines; the same scene, only the engine line changes)
- Ground: a StaticBody3D with a WorldBoundaryShape3D, on layer 5.
- 30 skeletons × 10 parts, all spawned in one physics frame at 1.0 m, at 30 spots spread over a 20 × 20 m field (a battle's size).
  - Parts are primitives sized like KayKit skeleton bones: a skull sphere (r 0.12), a ribcage box, a pelvis box, and 7 capsules (arms, legs, spine).
  - Each is a RigidBody3D with a MeshInstance3D, mass 1, default damping, can_sleep on.
- Layers are the ADR's rule: each part is on layer 4 with mask = layer 5 only. Parts don't collide with each other, which is the description's "ground only".
- Per frame, from the drop for 3 s: the frame time (Time.get_ticks_usec between _process calls) and Performance.TIME_PHYSICS_PROCESS. Also the time until every part reports sleeping (cap 10 s).
- Three runs per setup. Report the median of each number: p50, p99, the worst frame, and the time to sleep.
- The setups:
  - A, Godot Physics;
  - B, Jolt;
  - C, the winner of A/B with physics/3d/run_on_separate_thread on;
  - D, the winner with parts colliding with each other (mask 4 + 5), for the record only, so ig-c9y.3 knows the price if its look wants piles.
- The log also notes the hardware (the owner's PC) and the build.

4. THE DECISION RULE (so the numbers decide, not taste)
- The budget is SYSTEMS § Performance budgets: p99 ≤ 8.3 ms, and no frame over 33 ms.
- If both engines pass, keep what runs today. That's no switch, and no risk to the arena, town body and pick.
- If only one passes, it wins.
- If neither passes, the lower p99 wins, and the miss goes to ig-c9y.6, the caps (fewer live parts, a faster fade). The engine choice doesn't absorb it.
- The physics thread stays off unless the winner misses the budget without it and passes with it. Why: the pick at town_view.gd:677 would have to move into the physics step, and building_at (:663) would then answer a physics frame late. That touches its two production call sites and the ten test call sites listed above.

5. IF THE ENGINE CHANGES (only then)
- One line in project.godot: [physics] 3d/physics_engine = the name step 2 printed.
- Jolt defaults to check against our users:
  - physics/jolt_physics_3d/simulation/areas_detect_static_bodies is off by default. EnemyAttackHitbox's default mask (layer 1) does cover ArenaBounds, a StaticBody3D (arena.tscn:57). But its handler drops every body except the hero capsule (arena.gd, _on_enemy_attack_hitbox_body_entered), and AttackHitbox only watches layer 2 (the enemy capsule). So the setting can stay off.
  - Jolt's collision margins can change how close the town body stops at a box. The windowed walk checks that, after ig-6m2.8.2's new boxes.
- BUILT with the line in place, then the director's windowed checks (the ACC): the town body walks and collides, and the arena's hitboxes land.
- If nothing changes, the repo diff is DECISIONS.md only, and BUILT is just a re-run.

6. THE ADR (godot-architect writes it; the spike supplies the numbers)
- The engine, and the numbers for A-D.
- The decision rule's outcome.
- What changes, or "nothing" when today's engine stays.
- What was rejected, and why.
- The thread: on or off, with its number.
- The layers:
  - layer 4 = loose parts, with mask = layer 5 only;
  - layer 5 = the battle ground collider, which ig-c9y.3 adds to battle_view.tscn;
  - layers 1-3 stay the arena's and the town's. No layer_names line is needed.

ORDER: after ig-6m2.8.2, so the windowed walk tests the final hall boxes. The measuring can run before it, because it doesn't touch the repo. Only a project.godot switch waits. Engine lane.

BOUNDARIES: #2 only if project.godot changes (the setting plus the three physics users). #1, #3 and #4 are untouched, because the sim never sees physics.

NON-GOALS (unchanged): gore code, hero ragdolls, the live-part cap and fade (ig-c9y.3 and .6).

title: Fix now: an order card updates only for its own battle, and hero detail refreshes once
description:
WHY
Line refs refreshed 2026-09-24 (extra) against hub.gd and game_session.gd as committed at 2c3dc93.

Sol audit finding 2:
- _on_battle_changed(_order_id) (hub.gd:2256) ignores the id and runs _update_order_cards() (:2543) over every card.
- Each card update does a linear _order_by_id (:2682) and copies that battle's snapshot (GameSession.get_battle_snapshot).
- A quiet pulse (tick_expeditions, game_session.gd:1712): _advance_clocks_in_memory emits battle_changed once per battle order (:1844), then expeditions_changed (:1759). That runs _on_expeditions_changed (hub.gd:2249) → _refresh_expeditions(false) (:2462) → every card again (:2474).
- So N orders cost N×N + N card updates every 0.25 s.

Sol audit finding 7:
- roster_changed refreshes the selected hero's detail twice: once directly (connect at hub.gd:156), then again through _refresh_director_ui (connect at :158, call at :1807).
- SYSTEMS.md:690 (the Bond read cost row) measured each refresh at ~34 ms, ~25 of it the dream read.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWNS (cut 2026-09-24)
- How many cards update (items 1 and 2).
- How many times the detail refreshes per roster change (item 3).
- NOT what one refresh costs. ig-m6o.2.2.9 owns the dream read: its memo reads the dream once per ledger change, however many refreshes there are. After 2.2.9 the second refresh drops to ~9 ms: the ledger scans in _bond_text (Ledger.known_names) and _history_lines, plus the label.

BEHAVIOR
1. battle_changed(order_id) updates only that order's card.
   - Split _update_order_cards' loop body into a one-card update.
   - _on_battle_changed finds the card by its "order_id" meta. No card means nothing to do.
2. expeditions_changed still updates every card, once. Coalesce further only if ig-7sn.2 shows it matters.
3. The selected hero's detail refreshes once per roster change.

title: Performance baseline: Sol's measure list, windowed, against the budgets, before gore's collapse
description:
WHY
Nothing is measured yet. Sol's audit (.agent-results/perf-audit/sol-code-audit-2026-09-24.md) ranked the risks by reading only. This bead measures them, in the audit's order, against SYSTEMS § Performance budgets (ig-7sn.1). It runs before gore's collapse slice (ig-c9y.3), so gore's cost lands on a known floor.

SETUP
- Windowed, with the _console binary. Turn vsync off (DisplayServer.window_set_vsync_mode(DisplayServer.VSYNC_DISABLED) and Engine.max_fps = 0), or every frame reads 16.7 ms. Note the CPU, GPU and window size.
- Run while the owner isn't playing. One Godot at a time; reap it after.
- A throwaway APPDATA, seeded by a script. Start from .agent-results/ig-m6o.2.1/seeded_appdata and grow it: 100 heroes, the Ledger at its 10,000-record cap, and a full town. For measure 1, dispatch through GameSession's own API so the orders are real: all five zones at their hero caps (5+5+5+30+50 = 95 heroes). Never the owner's save.
- The seed and perf scripts go in tests/perf/, outside -gdir=res://tests/unit, so the gate doesn't run them. Timing probes stay in the perf script or a throwaway change. Nothing permanent goes into game code without a reason.
- Frames: skip 5 s of warm-up, then record 30 s. Report p50, p99, the worst frame, and the count of frames over 33 ms.

MEASURE LIST (Sol's, in order)
1. The 0.25 s pulse (game_session.gd:1712), split into phases: the due-order preview (each battle decoded and advanced once), the real advance (_advance_clocks_in_memory decodes, advances and encodes each battle again), state conversion, and order resolution. At 1 dispatched battle and at all five. This is the top risk.
2. The hub's battle_changed and expeditions_changed handlers: time and snapshot-copy count as the order count grows (1, 3, 5, 10 orders). Expect about N×N card updates: hub.gd:2179 updates every card for each order's signal. If ig-7sn.3 has landed, measure after it too.
3. The watched battle: frame time and event spikes, split into the sim, the snapshot render, the unit views, and VFX nodes and particles. Use the real worst case, not the 11 units the audit assumed: fallen_citadel (30 heroes, 30-enemy waves, a boss with 10 adds) and frontier_march (50 heroes, 30 objective enemies).
4. A roster action's latency, split into the signal handlers, the 10,000-record Ledger readers (history, bond, dream, known names), save serialization and validation, and the disk flush. Record the save's size in bytes. Also time the periodic save that runs every 15 s while orders run.
5. The full town: every walker out (16 wanderers plus keepers, workers and the body). Report the frame time, plus the single frame of one building change (the occupancy scan and walker replanning, town_view.gd:375).
6. The load: offline catch-up of all five dispatched battles after a long close (game_session.gd:1762, audit finding 3).

OUTPUT
- .agent-results/<this id>/baseline.md: each measurement against its budget, and the top 5 hotspots by time.
- The Measured column of SYSTEMS § Performance budgets.
- One child bead of ig-7sn per budget miss, carrying its number.

ACCEPTANCE
- Every row of the measure list has a number, or a stated reason it couldn't be taken.
- The seed and perf scripts are committed in tests/perf/ and can run again for later slices.
- BUILT stays green: the scripts don't break the gate.
- The owner's APPDATA is untouched: the run log shows the throwaway path.

NON-GOALS
Fixing anything. Children do that (and ig-7sn.3). No threads.

title: Gore and body physics: bones for skeletons, blood for heroes and creatures
description:
WHY
Owner, 2026-09-24: "i also want to add in gibbletting, dismemberment, and gore effects as enemies get hit by attacks, skills, etc. i also want physics for the bodies too"
Owner ruling, 2026-09-24: "bones for skellys, blood for creatures/our heroes"

BODY TYPES (decided in the view, from the look)
Every look has a body type. The skeleton looks are "bones"; everything else, heroes included, is "flesh". The view decides it from the look in heroes/hero_model.gd (ENEMY_LOOKS picks a Skeleton_* model; heroes use Knight, Mage, Rogue, Ranger). The sim never knows. So a future creature enemy bleeds with no new code.
- Bones: bone dust and splinters on a hit, loose physics parts on death, dismemberment, gibbing.
- Flesh: blood spray along the hit direction, and blood on the ground when downed or killed. Flesh keeps its limbs: no dismemberment, gibbing or loose-body physics.
- Heroes are flesh. They bleed but stay whole. Why (director's default): the sim carries, rescues and revives downed heroes, so a lost arm would need a saved injury, and that crosses boundary #1. The director is offering the owner "limbs only on true death" as a later ask.
- In battle today, heroes go down (downed) and never die in the view; only enemies die there. So ground blood shows under downed heroes now, and under dead flesh enemies once one exists.

WHAT BONES MEANS HERE
Every skeleton model is already split into part meshes: arms, legs, body, head or skull, jaw, eyes, and a hat, hood, helmet, cloak or cape. Checked in the .glb files: Skeleton_Warrior, Skeleton_Rogue, Skeleton_Mage and Skeleton_Minion all split this way. So a loose part is a hidden mesh plus a physics copy. No mesh cutting, no new assets, no downloads.
One catch: the parts are skinned to a 23-bone rig (only the Warrior's Helmet isn't). A loose copy must bake the part's current pose, or it pops into the bind pose.

THE SETTING
Gore: Off, Low or Full (.1). Off shows today's effects. It is also the performance knob. Blood and bones both follow it.

HARD RULES (every slice)
- Looks only. The sim never reads gore. Boundary #4 holds: both resolve() paths give the same outcome with gore Off or Full.
- Gore never draws from the sim's RNG. It uses its own view RNG, so turning gore on can't shift a battle.
- Hit direction comes from the view's own snapshot diff (.1). No sim change.
- Capped: loose parts and ground blood fade and free. Pool the nodes if a measurement shows their creation or cleanup is over budget. Sol audit finding 5: every hit already creates and frees nodes (battle_vfx.gd:206).
- Each slice measures its own worst case against SYSTEMS § Performance budgets (CODING_RULES § Performance), on top of the perf baseline (ig-7sn.2).
- No saved state. Nothing gore makes survives a reload.
- Assets only from what is already in the repo. Blood and splinter meshes and materials are built in code. No downloads.
- The battle view only. The action arena is out of scope.

WORST CASE (bigger than 5 + 1)
verdant_outskirts, ashfall_reaches and sundered_vault send 5 enemies a wave, then a boss. fallen_citadel sends 30 a wave, then a boss with 10 adds, against up to 30 heroes. frontier_march fields up to 50 heroes and up to 30 objective enemies. So one area skill can kill up to 30 skeletons in one frame, and up to 50 heroes can bleed at once. Caps are sized for that.

SLICES
.1 The Gore setting, and hit effects by body type: bone dust or blood spray.
.7 Ground blood for flesh: under a downed hero or a dead flesh enemy. After .1.
.2 Spike: the physics engine for loose bones, and its ADR.
.3 Death: skeletons collapse into loose bones. After .1, .2 and the perf baseline.
.4 Dismemberment: a heavy hit knocks a part off a skeleton, and it fights on.
.5 Gibbing: a killing crit or skill blasts a skeleton apart along the hit.
.6 The worst case, everything at once: set the Low and Full caps. After .4, .5 and .7.
The director's queue sets the build order; bd deps mark only true needs.
notes:
2026-09-24 extra: owner ruling folded in ('bones for skellys, blood for creatures/our heroes'). Body type per look, decided in the view. .1 picks bone dust or blood spray; new .7 is ground blood (after .1, before .6). Heroes bleed but keep their limbs (director default, boundary #1).
2026-09-24 owner: 'Gore: only skellies rn'. Dismemberment stays skeleton-only for now; heroes and flesh creatures bleed but keep their limbs, as designed here. The owner wants a hero/NPC body-part damage system later (too much damage takes a limb off, town potions and healing magic put it back): its own epic, ig-82z, after this one.

title: Living-world 2.8: split the rest of step 2 (knowledge, gossip, moods, joy)
description:
WHY

These are too open to spec before slices .1 to .7 land and show what the town feels like. This bead is the split, not the build.

TO SPLIT (tech-lead, with godot-architect and game-designer)
- Knowledge, gossip and recall (Direction v2 A2 item 1): per-hero knowledge that points into the Ledger (DECISIONS.md 2026-09-24 "Bonds stay derived", items 8-12). Gossip needs contact: meals, work, travel, bedside visits. Bounded topics per exchange; tellers bend stories; detail fades while confidence rises; ten people repeating one source are still one source; belief is played through encounters. Witnessed details land here (GAME_SPEC § 10 ruling). Needs its own save amendment (boundary #1).
- Trust, commitments and grievances that outlive their records (they live in knowledge).
- Dreams revised by new knowledge (GAME_SPEC § 5).
- Moods, routines and habits, only while the game is open. Diaries that describe only what their writer knows. Writing these tickets takes morale and the rest of dialogue off GAME_SPEC § Scope boundaries.
- Place imprints.
- Profession dreams (A2 item 2): woodcutting "Give us a road home", smithing "This shield brings you back", rites "Let them remember whom they buried". Check which proofs need step 5 or 6 first.
- Joy: nicknames, petty hobbies, festivals out of residents' histories, and soup factions if ig-m6o.2.2.5 left them.

ACCEPTANCE
Child beads with WHY / BEHAVIOR / ACCEPTANCE under ig-m6o.2.2, any ADR the knowledge save needs, and GAME_SPEC § Scope boundaries updated for what leaves the list.

NOT HERE
Anything step 3 or later owns: bonds in combat, techniques, institutions, Essence.

title: Living-world 2.7: the dream catalogue
description:

Design: GAME_SPEC.md § Direction § 5. DECISIONS.md 2026-09-24 "Bonds stay derived" (item 6: dreams stay derived).

BEFORE BUILD (game-designer)
- Three to five more dreams that today's records can prove: battle, summoned, ranked_up and died, plus encounter and meal once they land. Each with § 5's parts and the owner's reason.
- A fixed rule for which dream a hero holds when several could open (e.g. the first formative event, oldest first).

- Profession dreams (Direction v2, A2 item 2) are not here. Their proofs need later pieces: a road, the paired sequence, departed testimony. ig-m6o.2.2.8 re-scopes them.

RULED
- Derived from records (ADR item 6). No saved dream field.
- One dream at a time per hero, as now. When it is fulfilled or lost, the next formative event opens the next one.
- "New knowledge can revise it" waits for knowledge (ig-m6o.2.2.8).

BEHAVIOR
1. Bonds.dream reads the catalogue: each entry opens on its formative event, tracks its milestones and ends fulfilled or lost.
2. The detail panel shows the dream and its milestones, as it does for the life debt.
3. The line bank gets a kind per dream, so a partner can speak about the listener's or speaker's dream.

None.

Profession dreams. Dreams revised by knowledge. Founding a dream's institution (step 5). Essence or rank rewards for a dream (step 4).

(2) life_debt keeps the existing 'debt' line kind. The three new kinds read only the speaker's (partner's) dream; lines about the listener's own dream are left for a follow-up if wanted. title: Living-world 2.6: friends, rivals and collaborators (directed, layered relationships)
description:
WHY
ig-m6o.2's scope: "Bonds: friend, rival, collaborator, grown from recorded encounters, meals and shared battles", and "adjoining workshops invent techniques (only as a bond label in this step)". Direction v2 widens it: relationships are directed and layered (familiarity, affection, situational trust, respect, grievances, commitments, shared techniques), and roles overlap. Today one undirected number makes one "partner".
Design: GAME_SPEC.md § Direction § 5. DECISIONS.md 2026-09-24 "Bonds stay derived" (derived, one pass, kept index).

BEFORE BUILD (game-designer)
- The first layers. Suggest familiarity, affection, respect and grievance. Trust and commitments wait for knowledge (ig-m6o.2.2.8); shared techniques are step 3.
- Which facts feed which layer, and in which direction. For example: being saved raises the saved hero's affection toward the saver; meals and meetings raise familiarity both ways.
- The roles: friend, rival and collaborator, with their rules and thresholds (PROVISIONAL). Collaborator comes from working at adjoining workplaces.
- What "partner" (the ♥ sign, ig-m6o.2.2.1) means now: suggest the strongest affection at or over a threshold.

RULED
- Still derived (the ADR). The index gains directed layers per ordered pair. No saved relationship state.
- Roles change no number (step 3 owns combat effects).
- The rebuild stays within the ADR budget.

BEHAVIOR
1. The index keeps, per ordered pair (A toward B), each layer's value from the facts, and the roles that follow.
2. The detail panel shows a hero's roles: "Friend: Mara. Rival: Wren. Works well with: Tamsin." Only roles at or over their thresholds.
3. The ♥ sign follows the partner rule the designer sets.
4. The line bank gets kinds for the new roles, used by meetings and greetings.

SAVE
None.

ACCEPTANCE (tests/unit, APPDATA redirected)
- Each layer from its facts, direction included: A toward B differs from B toward A where the facts differ.
- Each role at and one step under its threshold. Roles overlap (a rival can also be a collaborator).
- The partner rule. Update ig-m6o.2.2.1's equivalence test to the designer's rule.
- Rebuild cost at the cap, within the ADR budget.
- No saved state. BUILT. Verifier pass mandatory: boundary #2.

FILES
history/bonds.gd, history/lines.gd, hub/hub.gd, balance rows, tests/unit/test_bonds.gd, docs/SYSTEMS.md, docs/GAME_SPEC.md.

NON-GOALS
Trust, commitments and grievances that outlive their records (knowledge, ig-m6o.2.2.8). Bond effects in combat (step 3). Real techniques (step 3). A relationship screen.
design:
DESIGN (extra as game-designer, 2026-09-25; checked against HEAD 3fd43c1). Built on ig-m6o.2.2.4 and .5 (meetings and meals: the slots, the tier-0 eviction and the fold pattern), so it runs after them. Rules: DECISIONS 2026-09-24 "Bonds stay derived" (derived, one pass, kept index, fold). All numbers PROVISIONAL.

PICKS (director's call)
1. Three layers now: affection, respect and teamwork. Each feeds exactly one role, and a layer ships only with the role that reads it.
   - Familiarity waits. It would be the tally's own counts (hard fights, meetings, meals), and no role or line reads it yet.
   - Grievance waits for knowledge (ig-m6o.2.2.8). Every good source for one lives outside a single record. "You fed my friend to the Door" needs the griever's bond with the dead at the time of the sacrifice. "You left me out there" needs to know who could have come. A fold can't take either out exactly when older records leave. The bead's non-goals already hold grievances that outlive their records for knowledge.
2. Affection is directed where the facts are. Being saved or rescued counts in full toward the saver. Doing the saving counts less. So a saver can be someone's partner without that hero being the saver's.
3. Rivals come from kills. In hard fights side by side, each has outdone the other at least 3 times. Kills are already in every battle record ("kills", game_session.gd:3072). So rivals are peers who keep trading the lead, and it needs no new record.
4. Collaborators come from coworker meetings (ig-m6o.2.2.4's "why": "coworkers"). That's the record of "working at adjoining workplaces". Amend 2.4 (unbuilt): why is "coworkers" when the stations qualify, else "neighbours". Work goes first because it's the rarer tie, and neighbours already share meals (2.5). With 2.4's current order, two neighbours who also work side by side could never become collaborators.
5. The partner (♥) is the strongest affection at or over bond_threshold: today's rule, read from the new affection.

1. THE LAYERS (history/bonds.gd; per ordered pair, A toward B)
| Layer | Direction | From (points each) |
|---|---|---|
| affection | directed | hard fight 1, death witnessed 5, meeting 1, meal 1 (both ways); saved by B 3, rescued by B 5 (toward the saver, the existing rows); saved B 1, rescued B 2 (toward the one saved, new rows) |
| respect | directed | a hard fight side by side where B had more kills than A: +1 toward B. A tie scores nothing |
| teamwork | both ways | a meeting whose why is "coworkers": +1 |
- Slots: FACTS gains four, after 2.4's "meetings" and 2.5's "meals":
  - "outdone": A's slot toward B counts the fights where B outkilled A;
  - "cowork";
  - "saving" and "rescuing", the given side of a save or rescue.
  The existing "saves" and "rescues" slots keep only the received side (wording "saved_by").
- Why the split: today one slot holds both directions, and only the latest record's wording survives (_count, bonds.gd:138 and :214-216). So a count can't say which way it went, and affection can't be directed without it.
- bond_line still says "N saves" and "N rescues" for both sides together, as today.
- The tally keeps "points" as the affection, so every reader of points (bond_from, _living_candidates, ig-uu7.4's cover order) follows the new rule without an edit. It gains "respect" and "teamwork".
- Scoring:
  - respect is scored in _score's existing non-routine loop (bonds.gd:117-124), with kills from the record (absent means 0). Routine victories still return early, so the hottest line at the cap is unchanged;
  - teamwork is scored in 2.4's encounter branch.
- The fold stays exact:
  - every new slot uses _count and _uncount, and _unscore mirrors the split;
  - outdone, saving and rescuing evict with their battle (oldest first in the battle tier);
  - cowork evicts with its encounter (oldest first in tier 0).
  That's the same argument as the hard and meeting slots.

2. THE ROLES (a read, not stored: static func roles(pairs, hero_id, living, balance) -> Dictionary)
| Role | Rule | Row |
|---|---|---|
| Friend | affection A toward B at or over bond_threshold | bond_threshold 8 (existing) |
| Rival | respect both ways at or over rival_threshold: A toward B and B toward A | rival_threshold 3 |
| Works well with | teamwork at or over collaborator_threshold | collaborator_threshold 4 |
- Friend and "works well with" are read from A's own entries. Rival reads B's entry toward A too, so roles() takes the whole index.
- Roles overlap: a rival can be a friend and a collaborator at once.
- Living heroes only, like bond_from.
- It returns {friends: [ids], rivals: [ids], collaborators: [ids]}, each strongest first: affection, the respect sum, or teamwork, then last_seq, then id (_ahead's order).
- The partner is friends[0]. bond_from keeps returning exactly that, so no caller of it changes.
- Roles change no number (the bead's rule). ig-uu7.4 reads affection, which it already did as points.

3. THE PANEL (hub/hub.gd, built in code)
- The "Closest to Mara: …" line stays: the partner's facts, from bond_line.
- One new line under it, only when a role is held: "Friends: Mara, Dunn. Rival: Wren. Works well with: Tamsin."
  - Up to 3 names per role, strongest first, singular when one. "(away)" after a busy hero, as bond_line does.
  - A role with nobody is left out.
- The partner shows in "Closest to" and first among Friends, on purpose. The line is the whole list; the ♥ is the one.
- New-role notices: none in this slice. The panel shows roles. Add a notice when the owner can't tell that rivals formed.

4. THE LINES (history/lines.gd)
- Two new kinds, {name} only, 5 lines each (the longest is 66 characters with a 14-letter name):
  - "rival": "Still counting, {name}? I had one more than you last time." / "Next fight, {name}. Loser buys the soup." / "You got lucky out there, {name}. It won't happen twice." / "Keep up, {name}. I won't wait for you." / "Not bad, {name}. Not as good as me, but not bad."
  - "collaborator": "Hand me that, {name}. We're faster together." / "Good work today, {name}. Same again tomorrow?" / "{name}! I had an idea for the work. Tell me if it's mad." / "We make a good team, {name}. Everyone says so." / "Leave the rest, {name}. We'll finish it together."
- Meetings (2.4's play_meeting): the kind is "rival" if the pair are rivals, else "collaborator" if they work well together, else "met".
- Greetings:
  - greeting_facts gains roles: Array[String] = [], appended after the bond and dream kinds and before 2.2.3's quirk kinds;
  - hub._refresh_partner passes ["rival"] when the partner is also the body's rival, and ["collaborator"] when they work well together;
  - the default keeps every caller unchanged.
- test_lines' SLOTS gains both kinds with ["name"].

5. BALANCE ROWS (balance_table.gd, balance.tres; SYSTEMS § Bonds and dreams; all PROVISIONAL)
- bond_points_saving 1: the saver's affection toward the one it saved. Less than bond_points_saved 3, because being saved is what makes a debt.
- bond_points_rescuing 2: the rescuer's toward the rescued. Less than bond_points_rescued 5.
- rival_threshold 3: three fights each way. At about one hard fight in several (uncounted, the section's first PROVISIONAL), that's a long rivalry, not one lucky night.
- collaborator_threshold 4: four coworker meetings. A coworker pair in a 30-hero town meets about 0.27 times an hour, so that's about 15 live hours; in a small town, about 4.
What this changes:
- A hero who saves B twice used to reach 8 toward B (2 × (3 + 1)). Now it's 2 × (1 + 1) = 4, while B toward the saver stays 8. So B's partner is the saver, and the saver's partner is someone else, or nobody.
- The hub's notice already says it one way: "Bea grew close to Cal." (hub.gd:807).
- Slice 1's reference reader in test_bonds (_slice1_bond, used by _assert_same_answers) moves to the new rule. That's the bead's "update the equivalence test".

6. COST
- One more compare per team pair in a hard fight, and one more slot per pair. The fold's per-record cost barely moves.
- roles() is read per selected hero or partner, from the kept index. It isn't per frame and isn't in the pulse.
- The ACC prints the rebuild and one fold-in at the cap, worst of seven, with 50 heroes in 5-hero teams (test_bonds' existing setup).

DOCS (after acceptance: SYSTEMS rows and roles as "designed, not built"; the lines that describe today's partner rule change with the code)
- SYSTEMS § Bonds and dreams: a "Layers and roles" subsection with the two tables and the four rows.
- GAME_SPEC § 5: one sentence, "the first layers are affection, respect and teamwork, and the first roles are friend, rival and works-well-with", with a pointer.

BOUNDARIES
- #2: the panel line, greeting_facts' new parameter and play_meeting's kind. Sol reviews it.
- #1: no saved state (the ADR).
- #3: untouched.
- #4: only through ig-uu7.4's cover order, which reads affection. Its digests don't move (the gate has no records).

NON-GOALS (the bead's, plus): familiarity and grievance (above); role notices; relationships with the dead; roles in combat.

ORDER: after ig-m6o.2.2.4 and .5 (slots, tier and coworker meetings), and after ig-m6o.2.2.3 (greeting_facts' quirk parameter). The same files as those, so never side by side.

title: Living-world 2.4: neighbours meet (encounter records from saved state)
description:
WHY
ig-m6o.2's scope: "Neighbourhood encounters: heroes who live or work near each other meet, and the meeting is recorded." Signature moment: neighbours become friends and rivals. Today bonds form only in battle, so heroes who never fight together never grow close, and the town's walkers pass each other without a word.
Design: DECISIONS.md 2026-09-24 "Bonds stay derived" (items 5 and 7). ig-m6o.2 finding (b): walking is cosmetic (ig-6m2.6), so a record must come from saved state, never from where figures meet.

BEFORE BUILD (game-designer)
- Who counts as neighbours (Houses within N hexes) and as coworkers (the same workplace, or adjoining ones).
- How often a pair meets: a chance per live minute, and a cap per pair per hour.
- The encounter's bond points: a PROVISIONAL row, small, so meetings alone take much longer to make a bond than hard fights.
- The volume check: records per hour for a 30-hero town, added to SYSTEMS § The Ledger's records-per-hour estimate, against the 10,000 cap.

RULED (ADR items 5 and 7)
- GameSession decides an encounter on the live tick from saved state: homes, stations, and who is in town and not busy. Never in the offline catch-up. Never from walker positions.
- One record per meeting: {seq, time, kind: "encounter", heroes: [a, b], place, why}. place is a House or workplace id. why is "neighbours" or "coworkers". GameSession is its one writer (Ledger ADR item 5 gains the kind).
- Encounters are evicted first: a new tier ahead of routine battles (ADR item 7, which amends the Ledger ADR's item 8). This slice changes Ledger.tier() and TIER_BY_KIND (today an unknown kind falls to tier 1 and routine battles are tier 0), and SYSTEMS § The Ledger's eviction order.
- The bond index counts encounter points. After this slice the ledger changes on the live tick, so a rebuild must stay within one 60 FPS frame (16.7 ms) at the cap, measured as the worst of seven runs. If ig-m6o.2.2.1's measurement is over that, this slice first switches the index to the incremental fold (ADR item 5).
- Walkers show a meeting; they never cause one.

BEHAVIOR
1. The rule. On the live tick, each eligible pair (neighbours or coworkers, both in town and not busy) may meet, at the designer's rate and within the pair cap. A meeting writes one encounter record.
2. Bonds. The bond reader adds the encounter row's points to the pair, once per record. The detail line counts meetings ("3 chats").
3. The town. When an encounter is recorded and both heroes are shown, the two walkers walk to each other, face, play the Interact clip, and one says a line from the bank (a new "encounter" kind with {name} and {place}). If either is not shown (the wanderer cap, the body), nothing plays; the record stands.

SAVE
Records only, through the existing Ledger side file. No new save key.

ACCEPTANCE (tests/unit, APPDATA redirected)
- Encounters happen only between neighbours or coworkers who are both in town and not busy; never in the catch-up; never above the pair cap.
- The record's shape, and its eviction tier (evicted before any routine battle).
- A real save and reload keeps the records (the side file), and a legacy save without them loads.
- Bond points add up; a pair can bond from meetings alone at the designer's pace.
- Rebuild cost at the cap with encounters in the ledger: the worst of seven runs, printed, within 16.7 ms (or the fold lands first).
- Town (headless): a recorded encounter between two shown walkers plays the meeting once.
- BUILT. Verifier pass mandatory: boundary #1 (new record kind through the side file) and boundary #2 (the walkers).

FILES
systems/game_session.gd (the live-tick rule, the writer), history/ledger.gd (tier), history/bonds.gd, history/lines.gd, hub/hub.gd, hub/town/town_view.gd, hub/town/town_walker.gd, balance_table.gd and balance.tres (rows), tests/unit, docs/SYSTEMS.md, docs/DECISIONS.md (the Ledger ADR's item 5 and 8 lines).

NON-GOALS
Rivals and other roles (ig-m6o.2.2.6). Gossip in a meeting (ig-m6o.2.2.8). Meetings in the offline catch-up. Records from walker positions. New animation clips.
design:
DESIGN (extra, 2026-09-25; checked against HEAD 48d3cc9, which has the same code as 9687058). Rules: DECISIONS 2026-09-24 "Bonds stay derived", items 3, 5 and 7, and the Ledger ADR, items 5 and 8. The numbers are game-designer's, below, all PROVISIONAL.

WHAT'S ALREADY THERE (so two of the bead's worries are settled)
- The fold has landed (ig-m6o.2.2.9). GameSession._record folds each append into the kept index (game_session.gd:3029-3041), and _evict_ledger folds each eviction out (:3043-3048). So the bead's "rebuild within 16.7 ms, or switch to the fold first" is already met. What's left is making the fold exact for encounters (section 4).
- Every encounter lands in a periodic save without a new trigger. Neighbours are housed and home, so food_eaters() is non-empty. Coworkers are home keepers or workers, so _working_keepers() or _workers_home() is non-empty. Either one already opens the periodic-save gate (:351), and it saves every 15 s. There's no save on quit, so an encounter from the last few seconds can be lost. Alone, they matter little (ADR item 7).
- The record's hero list key is "heroes", not "team". So Ledger.records_for_hero (ledger.gd:72) skips encounters, and the History list stays battles, summons and deaths. Meetings show as a count in the bond line instead.

1. WHO MEETS (GameSession, from saved state only)
- In town means on the roster and not is_hero_busy (:1092). The body counts: it's in town. A pair is eligible when both are in town and either:
  - neighbours: both are housed, in the same House or in Houses at most encounter_neighbour_hexes apart (TownRules.ring_distance of the hex difference; the hexes come from town_buildings); or
  - coworkers: both are stationed (a hall or a workplace), at the same building or at buildings at most encounter_coworker_hexes apart. The halls stand in a row (town_rules.gd:27-35), so neighbouring keepers are coworkers.
- why is "neighbours" when the homes qualify, else "coworkers". place is that why's building for a, where a is the pair's lower instance_id: a's House, or a's station.

2. WHEN (the live tick only)
- In _advance_clocks_in_memory (:2173). tick_expeditions calls it on both live branches: bare (:2090), or inside a commit through _advance_time_in_memory (:2088, :2142). The offline catch-up (_advance_orders_in_memory) never calls it, like wood and stone (:2193).
- Inside a commit, a rollback drops the record and its signal but keeps the unsaved cooldown. That only makes the pair wait longer.
- New unsaved GameSession fields:
  - _encounter_clock, the live seconds since the last roll;
  - _encounter_cooldowns, pair key → seconds left;
  - _encounter_rng, a RandomNumberGenerator, randomized at startup (tests set its seed).
  from_dict clears all three.
- The clock adds delta. For each whole 60 s in it:
  - every cooldown drops by 60 s, and one at 0 is erased;
  - one roll: with encounter_chance_per_minute, one eligible pair off cooldown is picked uniformly from the pairs sorted by key;
  - it gets one record and a cooldown of encounter_pair_cooldown_minutes.
  So one big tick is the same as sixty small ones, and it caps a pair at one meeting per cooldown.
- Why a town-level chance and not a chance per pair: volume stays bounded whatever the roster size (at most 60 × chance an hour). A pair per-pair chance would grow with the square of the town.
- A reload resets the clock and the cooldowns, since they're unsaved. That loses at most one minute's roll, and lets a pair meet again sooner after a reload. The cap holds within a session, and there's no new save key.
- The record: _record("encounter", {"heroes": [a, b], "place": id, "why": "neighbours" | "coworkers"}). Ledger.append adds seq and time. GameSession is its one writer.

3. EVICTION (history/ledger.gd; ADR item 7)
- TIER_BY_KIND = {"encounter": 0, "battle": 2, "ranked_up": 3, "summoned": 4, "died": 5}. A routine battle is 1, and an unknown kind is 2 (with the other battles, as today).
- evict()'s loop reads TIER_BY_KIND.size() + 1, so it covers 0..5 unchanged. "meal" waits for its own slice.
- _ledger_tiers is never saved, so a load recomputes it.

4. BONDS (history/bonds.gd)
- FACTS gains "meetings" at the end (index 4), so the existing slot indexes don't move. _slots makes 5 slots.
- _fold: "encounter" → both directions of the pair count +1, and the record becomes the slot's latest, with wording "met".
- fold_out: "encounter" → both directions count −1 through _uncount (bonds.gd:305). Evict takes the first record of the lowest tier (ledger.gd:37-39), so encounters go oldest first. The evicted one is a slot's latest only when its count reaches 0, and then the slot clears. So it's exact, and _uncount's false (a rebuild) stays a safety net. fold_out's comment (:67-70) gains encounters.
- _tally:
  - points gain balance.bond_points_encounter × meetings;
  - the tally gains "meetings";
  - the fact dict gains "place";
  - "met" is the strongest fact only when the pair has no battle fact, so a fight you shared beats a chat. (_tally's tie rule, :329, would otherwise let a newer chat beat a hard fight, since both are worth 1.)
- bond_line adds "N chats" ("Closest to Mara: 2 hard fights, 3 chats.").
- Knights: ig-uu7.4's cover order reads bond points (game_session.gd:1575-1610), so meetings count there too. My pick is to keep one rule for bonds. It's snapshot-time only, and the gate's digests don't move (its fights have no encounters).

5. LINES (history/lines.gd)
- One new kind, "met", with {name} and {place}. It serves both:
  - the partner's greeting when a bond's strongest fact is a meeting;
  - the line said in a town meeting.
- static func place_name(id) -> String: "the " + (id if TownRules.is_hall(id) else TownRules.type_of(id)).capitalize(), for example "the Summoning Circle" or "the House". It's pure, like Ledger.zone_name.
- greeting_facts: for kind "met", place = place_name(fact["place"]).
- The 5 lines (the worst case, a 14-letter name and the Summoning Circle, is at most 67 characters):
  "{name}! I was hoping I'd catch you by {place}." / "Same time tomorrow at {place}, {name}?" / "Busy day at {place}, {name}?" / "I like our talks at {place}, {name}." / "Sit a while, {name}. Work at {place} can wait."
- test_lines' SLOTS gains "met": ["name", "place"].

6. THE SIGNAL AND THE HUB (no roster_changed)
- GameSession gains signal social_recorded(records: Array[Dictionary]), once per tick with every record the tick's social rule wrote. It's deferred like battle_changed (_notify_battle_changed :380), and a rolled-back commit drops it along with its records. ig-m6o.2.2.5's meals use the same signal, so it's named for both.
- Encounters never emit roster_changed. A record-writing roster change costs 99-189 ms (SYSTEMS § Bonds and dreams, the Bond read cost row), and that would be a hitch every few minutes.
- hub.gd, on social_recorded (once per tick, however many records):
  a) it asks _bond_index(). That's the existing look: it says "Mara and Dunn grew close." if this meeting made a bond, and it forgets the dream memo;
  b) if a bond appeared or ended, or the body's partner changed, it runs _refresh_roster once. That's rare: once per new bond;
  c) otherwise, if the selected hero is in any record, it refreshes the detail panel's bond line only;
  d) it tells the town to play each meeting.
- TownView.play_meeting(a_id, b_id, facts):
  - it plays only when both have walkers and neither is the body or already meeting;
  - b holds where it stands, and a is led to b over the walk graph (_lead);
  - within TownWalker.MEET_DISTANCE, a greets with facts through the existing _greet path (one line, Interact), and b faces a and plays Interact;
  - then both resume;
  - it's dropped after MEETING_SECONDS = 30 if a can't get there (a presentation constant, not balance).
  The partner's greeting to the body is unchanged. A walker that's meeting skips it until it's done.
- facts = {kinds: ["met"], slots: {name: b's name, place: place_name(place)}, start: hash of the record's seq}.
- Walkers show a meeting; they never cause one. play_meeting reads no GameSession.

7. BALANCE ROWS (balance_table.gd, balance.tres; SYSTEMS § Bonds and dreams, all PROVISIONAL)
- encounter_chance_per_minute 0.2 (so at most 12 an hour);
- encounter_pair_cooldown_minutes 60;
- encounter_neighbour_hexes 2 (the same House counts);
- encounter_coworker_hexes 1 (the same building, or adjoining);
- bond_points_encounter 1.
The pace this gives:
- In a 30-hero town with about 45 eligible pairs at a time, a given pair meets about 12 / 45 ≈ 0.27 times an hour. Eight meetings reach bond_threshold 8, so that's about 30 live hours.
- A pair on the same team bonds from hard fights in a few hours. So meetings alone are much slower, as the bead asks.
- A two-hero town is capped at one meeting an hour, so about 8 hours.

8. VOLUME (SYSTEMS § The Ledger, records-per-hour estimate)
- Encounters add at most 12 an hour. At battle_pace 6 the battles give about 10 (SYSTEMS :368), so the total is about 22.
- Encounters are evicted first, so at the cap they give way before any battle. The cap's 10,000 then holds every non-encounter record for about 1,000 hours, as before.
- The ig-eek stage saves' Ledger column grows by up to 12 an hour of town time (a note on that section).

DOCS (after acceptance; I'll write them on the director's word)
- SYSTEMS § Bonds and dreams: the five rows and the pace note. § The Ledger: the eviction order line, and the volume.
- DECISIONS (godot-architect): the Ledger ADR's item 5 gains "encounter", written by GameSession. Item 8's amendment line names the tier change as done.

BOUNDARIES
- #1: records only, through the existing side file, with no new save key. Test a disk round-trip that keeps them, and a legacy save without them. Sol reviews it.
- #2: a new GameSession signal, the hub's handler, and TownView.play_meeting. No .tscn change. Sol reviews it.
- #3: untouched.
- #4: only through uu7.4's cover order, at snapshot time. The digests don't move.

ORDER: it edits game_session.gd, hub.gd, lines.gd and bonds.gd, so run it after ig-m6o.2.2.7 and ig-m6o.2.2.3 (they share lines.gd and test_lines.gd), and off the ig-gy0.7 and ig-6m2.7 lanes (they share game_session.gd and hub.gd).
