title: Living-world 2.5: shared meals (the meal record)
description:
WHY
ig-m6o.2's scope: "Meals become social events: housemates who eat together, soup factions. The Ledger's meal kind is written here." Today eating is a steady rate with no meal times (SYSTEMS § Food and starvation), and each hero lives alone (house_capacity 1), so there are no housemates (ig-m6o.2 finding (a)).
Design: DECISIONS.md 2026-09-24 "Bonds stay derived" (item 7). The Ledger ADR, item 5 ("meal is reserved for step 2. Eating ticks are not events").

BEFORE BUILD (game-designer)
- Finding (a): who eats together. Suggested default: heroes who are home at a meal time and whose Houses are within N hexes share one meal. Other options: everyone home at one table, or a meal building (town builder scope, so not here).
- Meal times: every N minutes of live play.
- The shared meal's bond points (PROVISIONAL, small).
- Soup factions: in this slice or in the joy work (ig-m6o.2.2.8).
- The volume check, as for encounters.

RULED (ADR item 7)
- GameSession settles a shared meal on the live tick, from saved state: food_eaters() (housed and home) and their Houses. Never in the offline catch-up.
- One record per meal: {seq, time, kind: "meal", diners: [ids], place}. Two or more diners, or no record. GameSession is its one writer.
- The food rules don't change. A shared meal eats no extra food, and the food clock stays the rate in SYSTEMS § Food and starvation.
- Meals are evicted first, in the same tier as encounters (ADR item 7; ig-m6o.2.2.4 changes Ledger.tier()).

BEHAVIOR
1. The rule. At each meal time, the designer's groups of eaters who are home share a meal. Each group of two or more writes one meal record.
2. Bonds. Every pair of diners gets the meal row's points, once per record.
3. The town. When a meal is recorded, the shown diners walk to the meal's place, stand around it with the eating clip, and one says a line from the bank (a new "meal" kind). Cosmetic only; the record stands either way.

SAVE
Records only, through the existing side file. No new save key.

ACCEPTANCE (tests/unit, APPDATA redirected)
- Meals happen only on the live tick, only for eaters who are home, only in groups of two or more; never in the catch-up.
- Food is unchanged: the same run with and without shared meals ends with the same food.
- Record shape and eviction tier. A real save and reload keeps the records; a legacy save loads.
- Bond points add up per pair.
- Rebuild cost at the cap with meals and encounters in the ledger, within the ADR budget.
- Town (headless): the diners gather.
- BUILT. Verifier pass mandatory: boundary #1 and boundary #2.

FILES
systems/game_session.gd, hub/town/town_rules.gd (the grouping, as a pure rule), history/ledger.gd, history/bonds.gd, history/lines.gd, hub/hub.gd, hub/town/town_view.gd, hub/town/town_walker.gd, balance rows, tests/unit, docs/SYSTEMS.md, docs/DECISIONS.md.

NON-GOALS
Recipes, dishes and provisions (Rift potlucks, a later step). A new building. Houses for more than one hero. Starvation changes. Gossip at the table (ig-m6o.2.2.8).
design:
DESIGN (extra, 2026-09-25; checked against HEAD 48d3cc9). Rules: DECISIONS 2026-09-24 "Bonds stay derived", item 7, and the Ledger ADR, item 5. It builds on ig-m6o.2.2.4 (the tier change, the fold pattern, the social_recorded signal), so it runs after it. The numbers are game-designer's, below, all PROVISIONAL.

PICKS (director's call)
- Finding (a), who eats together: neighbours at small tables. Eaters whose Houses are within meal_house_hexes of a host's House sit at the host's table, up to meal_table_size. Why:
  - "everyone at one table" gives a 30-hero town 435 pairs a meal, so everyone bonds with everyone and the partner means nothing;
  - small fixed tables make the signature moment: the same neighbours eat together meal after meal and become friends.
  Houses hold one hero (house_capacity 1), so "housemates" are the heroes next door. The rule works unchanged if Houses ever hold more (distance 0).
- Soup factions: not here, in ig-m6o.2.2.8 (joy). A faction needs a taste per hero, and there's no such saved state yet. This slice records who ate with whom, and a faction rule can read that later.

1. THE TABLES (hub/town/town_rules.gd, a pure rule, as the bead asks)
   static func meal_tables(eaters: Array[Array], buildings: Array[Dictionary], reach: int, size: int) -> Array[Dictionary]
   - eaters is [[id, home_id], ...]; each House's hex comes from buildings ("q", "r"). An eater whose home isn't in buildings is skipped.
   - Eaters are sorted by their House's hex (q, then r), then id.
   - Each eater not yet seated, in that order, hosts a table at its House. It seats up to size - 1 unseated eaters whose Houses are within reach (ring_distance of the hex difference), nearest first, then by hex, then by id.
   - It returns {place: host's House id, diners: sorted ids} for each table of 2 or more. A table of one is no meal.
   - No RNG. The same town gives the same tables, so tablemates stay tablemates until someone moves house, leaves on an order, or comes home.

2. WHEN (GameSession, the live tick only)
- In _advance_clocks_in_memory (:2173), beside 2.4's encounter roll, so the same two live branches reach it (:2090 bare, :2088 in a commit) and the offline catch-up never does.
- An unsaved _meal_clock (live seconds), cleared by from_dict. Each time it passes meal_interval_minutes, one meal time. A long tick that passes several gives one meal time, not a burst.
- At a meal time:
  - no meal while the food store is empty (town_resources["food"] <= 0). It reads food and never changes it;
  - eaters = food_eaters() (housed and not busy, :1076), the body included;
  - one _record("meal", {"diners": ids, "place": house_id}) per table from meal_tables. GameSession is the one writer.
- Food is unchanged: the meal eats nothing extra and the food clock stays SYSTEMS § Food and starvation's rate (:2205).
- A reload restarts the meal clock, so the first meal comes meal_interval_minutes into each session. PROVISIONAL: if the owner's sessions often end before a meal, shorten the interval. Why not the wall clock ("on the hour"): a real hour boundary during the test suite would drop a meal record into unrelated ledger tests. The live clock keeps tests exact.
- Every meal lands in a periodic save: its diners are food_eaters, which already opens the save gate (:351).

3. EVICTION (history/ledger.gd)
- TIER_BY_KIND gains "meal": 0, beside 2.4's "encounter": 0 (ADR item 7: the same tier). The loop still covers 0..5.

4. BONDS (history/bonds.gd)
- FACTS gains "meals" after 2.4's "meetings" (index 5). _slots makes 6.
- _fold: "meal" → every ordered pair of diners counts +1 (a table of 4 is 12 slots), the record is each slot's latest, wording "meal".
- fold_out: "meal" → _uncount every ordered pair. Tier 0 goes oldest first, and meals and encounters use different slots, so the evicted meal is the oldest in each of its slots. Exact, as for encounters.
- _tally: points gain balance.bond_points_meal × meals; the tally gains "meals"; the fact carries "place". A battle fact still beats "meal" and "met". Between those two, _tally's tie rule (the later record) picks.
- bond_line adds "N meals" ("Closest to Mara: 3 chats, 5 meals.").
- The Knight cover order (ig-uu7.4) counts meal points too, as 2.4 does for meetings.

5. LINES (history/lines.gd)
- A new kind "meal", {name} only (the House is always "the House", so {place} adds nothing). 5 lines, the longest 59 characters with a 14-letter name:
  "Pass the bread, {name}. And leave me the crust." / "Good soup, {name}. Don't tell the cook I said so." / "Food tastes better with company. Sit by me, {name}." / "{name}, you've got crumbs on your chin. Other side." / "Save me a seat at the next meal, {name}."
- It serves the partner's greeting when the bond's fact is "meal", and the line said at a table.
- test_lines' SLOTS gains "meal": ["name"].

6. THE HUB AND THE TOWN (no roster_changed)
- The tick's meal records go out in 2.4's social_recorded(records), once per tick. The hub's handler is 2.4's: one _bond_index() (new-bond notices say "(+N more)" when a table makes several), a roster refresh only if a partner changed, the detail panel only if the selected hero dined.
- TownView.play_meal(diner_ids, place_id, facts):
  - it seats only shown walkers that aren't the body and aren't already in a meeting or meal. Fewer than 2, and nothing plays;
  - the table's centre is free_point(work_spot(place_id)): the free hex nearest the House's door, the street in front of it (town_view.gd:575, :590). Each diner is led (_lead) to a spot on a ring (MEAL_RING = 1.5 m, inside the hex's 3 m inner radius, HEX_SIZE 3.46 m) around that centre, so all stay on the one free hex;
  - each faces the ring's centre and lingers (linger_at) with Sit_Floor_Idle for MEAL_SECONDS = 20. That clip is already loaded (hero_model.gd:41, the Sanctum's work clip), so no new clip;
  - the first seated diner says one "meal" line to the next, through _greet's line path;
  - then all resume. A diner that isn't seated within 30 s is dropped from it (presentation constants, not balance).
  The body at a table isn't moved. The partner's greeting to the body pauses for a walker at a table, as for meetings.
- Walkers show a meal; they never cause one.

7. BALANCE ROWS (balance_table.gd, balance.tres; SYSTEMS § Bonds and dreams, all PROVISIONAL)
- meal_interval_minutes 60;
- meal_house_hexes 2 (the same as encounter_neighbour_hexes);
- meal_table_size 4;
- bond_points_meal 1.
The pace this gives:
- Tablemates who stay home bond from meals alone in 8 live hours (8 meals × 1 point, bond_threshold 8). Neighbours at one table are also encounter pairs, so it's nearer 7 hours. Hard fights take a few hours. So a shared table is the slow, steady way to a friend.
- Three tablemates tie on meals. Their encounters and fights break it, then the partner tie rule does.

8. VOLUME (SYSTEMS § The Ledger)
- A 30-hero town seats about 8 tables a meal, so about 8 records an hour. With 2.4's encounters (at most 12) and battles at pace 6 (about 10), that's about 30 an hour.
- Meals and encounters go first at the cap, so battles, summons and deaths keep their room.

9. COST
- A meal time writes up to about 8 records in one tick, each folded in and evicted at the cap. The ACC measures that whole tick, worst of seven.
- A rebuild runs only on a load or a rolled-back append. The ACC prints its time at the cap with meals and encounters in the ledger (a table's 12 slots make a meal dearer to fold than a battle).

DOCS (after acceptance; I'll write them on the director's word)
- SYSTEMS § Bonds and dreams: the four rows and the pace note. § The Ledger: meals in the eviction line and the volume. § Food and starvation: one line, "shared meals eat nothing; see § Bonds and dreams".
- DECISIONS (godot-architect): the Ledger ADR's item 5, "meal" is no longer reserved: GameSession writes it, one per table.

BOUNDARIES
- #1: records only, through the side file, with no new save key. Round-trip and legacy tests. Sol reviews it.
- #2: play_meal and the hub handler. No .tscn change. Sol reviews it.
- #3: untouched. A meal never touches starvation or kill_hero.
- #4: only through ig-uu7.4's cover order, at snapshot time. The digests don't move.

NON-GOALS (the bead's, plus): soup factions (ig-m6o.2.2.8); dreams on meal records (ig-m6o.2.2.10, SYSTEMS :986); a meal-time clock of day.

ORDER: after ig-m6o.2.2.4 (the tier, FACTS index 4, the signal and the hub handler). The same files as 2.4, so never side by side with it, ig-m6o.2.2.3 or ig-m6o.2.2.7.
notes:
STATUS (extra, 2026-09-25): done. Design and ACC set (refs at HEAD 48d3cc9). No engine runs, no commits, no doc edits. Director's calls: (1) finding (a): neighbours at small fixed tables (Houses within 2 hexes, up to 4 a table, a pure TownRules.meal_tables with no RNG), not everyone at one table (435 pairs a meal would make every hero bond with every other); (2) soup factions go to ig-m6o.2.2.8 (they need a per-hero taste that isn't saved state yet); (3) an unsaved live meal clock (every 60 live minutes; a reload restarts it), not the wall clock, so no real hour boundary can drop a meal into unrelated ledger tests; (4) no meal while food is 0 (reads food, never changes it); (5) meals share ig-m6o.2.2.4's social_recorded signal and hub handler, so it runs after 2.4. Four balance rows, PROVISIONAL, written to SYSTEMS only on your word.
Director 2026-09-25 ~04:10 local: design + ACC ACCEPTED, picks (1)-(5). Same doc rule as ig-m6o.2.2.4: the four rows and the pace note go into SYSTEMS now, marked as designed and not yet built. § The Ledger's lines, the § Food and starvation line and the DECISIONS line change in the same commit as the code. Engine order: after ig-m6o.2.2.4 (dep exists).

title: Living-world 2.3: quirks, shown and spoken
description:
WHY
ig-m6o.2's scope: "Passions exist (ig-wgj.13). Add quirks". The pillar is affection and everyday amusement. Passions say what a hero loves to do; quirks give a hero something small to be known for. They also give the line bank a second axis, so the same fact sounds different from two heroes.
Design: GAME_SPEC.md § Direction § 5 (People). ig-wgj.13 and heroes/hero.gd passions_for (the precedent).

BEFORE BUILD (game-designer)
- The quirk list. Suggest 12-16 small, harmless habits.
- How many per hero (ig-m6o.2's open "number of quirks"). Suggest 1 or 2.
- Two or three bank lines per quirk, using the ig-m6o.2.2.2 slots.
Record them in SYSTEMS.md (new § Quirks, PROVISIONAL) and GAME_SPEC.md § 5.

RULED (the passions precedent, ig-wgj.13)
- Rolled from instance_id by a hash, like Hero.passions_for, and saved as an additive Hero key, "quirks". A later change to the list never rewrites existing heroes. No SAVE_VERSION bump.
- A save without the key derives quirks from instance_id silently (legacy). A present but invalid key re-derives with a push_warning (passions' rule).
- Quirks change no number: no stats, XP, production, food or combat. Flavour and lines only, in this step.

BEHAVIOR
1. Hero.quirks, set when a hero is created, like passions.
2. The hero detail panel shows "Quirks: <a>, <b>." under the passions line.
3. The line bank takes the speaker's quirks as facts: each quirk adds its lines under its own kind ("quirk:<id>"). A partner's greeting draws from its fact kinds and its quirk kinds together.

SAVE
Crosses boundary #1: an additive Hero key.

ACCEPTANCE (tests/unit, APPDATA redirected)
- Rolls are stable for an instance_id and spread over the list (a quick count over 1,000 ids).
- Save round-trip through a real disk reload keeps quirks. A legacy save without the key derives them. An invalid key re-derives with a warning.
- The detail panel shows them. A greeting's candidates include the speaker's quirk lines.
- Quirks move no number: the diff touches no stat, XP, production or combat code.
- BUILT. Verifier pass mandatory: boundary #1 (the Hero key) and boundary #2 (the detail panel).

FILES
heroes/hero.gd, history/lines.gd, hub/hub.gd, tests/unit (new quirk tests), docs/SYSTEMS.md, docs/GAME_SPEC.md.

NON-GOALS
Quirks with effects (a later step, if ever). Nicknames and hobbies (ig-m6o.2.2.8, joy). Quirks that change or are learned. Moods.
design:
DESIGN (extra, 2026-09-25; checked against HEAD 9687058). The precedent is passions: Hero.passions_for (hero.gd:73), _read_professions (:454), _valid_passions (:491), and their tests in test_hero_professions.gd. The line bank is history/lines.gd (ig-m6o.2.2.2), and its tests are in test_lines.gd.

PICKS (director's call)
- One quirk per hero, not two. Why:
  - one habit is what a hero is "known for";
  - a partner's pool stays 5 bond lines plus 3 quirk lines, so the bond is still the main voice. With two quirks, quirk lines would outnumber bond lines 6 to 5.
  The key is still an Array ("quirks": [id]), so a second quirk later needs no new key, only the size check.
- 14 quirks, 3 lines each. The lines use {name} (the listener) or no slot at all. A quirk line's fact is the speaker's own habit, so it names no place, person or event (lines.gd's rule).

1. THE LIST (heroes/hero.gd)
   const QUIRKS: Dictionary[StringName, String] = { id: label }, in this order, append only. The roll indexes QUIRKS.keys(), and an id removed later re-derives every hero that had it, with a warning.
   hums: Hums while working · counts_steps: Counts every step · collects_pebbles: Pockets pretty pebbles · names_weapon: Names their weapon · early_riser: Up before dawn · whittles: Whittles little figures · bad_puns: Makes terrible puns · sweet_tooth: Has a sweet tooth · lucky_charm: Carries a lucky charm · hates_wet_boots: Hates wet boots · sketches: Sketches everyone · tidies: Can't leave a mess · cloud_names: Names the clouds · afraid_of_moths: Afraid of moths

2. THE ROLL AND THE SAVE (hero.gd, following passions)
- var quirks: Array[StringName]. _init sets it right after passions (:68): quirks = quirks_for(instance_id).
- static func quirks_for(id) -> Array[StringName]: return [QUIRKS.keys()[("%s#quirk" % id).md5_buffer().decode_u32(0) % QUIRKS.size()]]. It draws nothing from the global RNG.
  - Why md5 and not passions' String.hash() with a salt: String.hash() is djb2 (h × 33 + c), so hash(id + salt) is a linear function of hash(id). Its parity copies the parity of hash(id), and the first passion is hash(id) mod 8. With 14 quirks, each first passion would only ever get 7 of the 14. I checked this in Python over 1,000 random ids: djb2 with a salt gives 7 quirks per first passion, md5 gives all 14. ACC 1's last check catches it. md5 is a fixed standard, so the roll is stable across engine versions.
- to_dict writes "quirks" as strings, next to "passions" (:368).
- from_dict, a new _read_quirks beside _read_professions:
  - absent: derive, silently (legacy);
  - present and valid (an Array of exactly one known id): keep it;
  - anything else: re-derive, with push_warning("Invalid hero quirks …; re-derived.").
- It's an additive key: no SAVE_VERSION bump. A later change to the list never rewrites a hero that has a valid saved quirk.

3. THE PANEL (hub/hub.gd, built in code)
- _profession_text (:884) gains one line under the passions: "Passions: …\nQuirk: Hums while working\nSkills: …". test_hub_controls.gd:534 checks with contains, so it keeps passing.
- No .tscn change.

4. THE LINES (history/lines.gd)
- BANK gains one kind per quirk, "quirk:<id>", 3 lines each (below). The BANK comment gains: "quirk:<id> {name}, or no slot".
- greeting_facts gains a last parameter, quirks: Array[StringName] = []. It appends "quirk:%s" for each, after the bond and dream kinds. The default keeps every existing caller and test unchanged.
- hub._refresh_partner (:712) passes GameSession.hero_by_id(_partner_id).quirks. The partner is living by construction, because bond_from reads `living`. Lines still reads no GameSession.
- A hero with no bond still says nothing, as today. The bead gives quirk lines only to the partner's greeting.

THE LINES (spoken by the quirky hero to the body; the longest is 64 characters with a 14-letter name, under test_lines' 72)
- hums: "Sorry, was I humming again, {name}?" / "Can't get this tune out of my head. Hum it with me?" / "Work goes quicker with a tune. Mine are just off-key."
- counts_steps: "Hush, {name}, I'm counting. ...And now I've lost it." / "Every road has a number. I like knowing it." / "Guess how many steps it is to the edge of town. I know."
- collects_pebbles: "Look at this one, {name}. Perfectly round." / "My pockets are heavy again. Worth it." / "Found a good pebble today. You can have it."
- names_weapon: "Don't laugh, {name}. A weapon with a name fights harder." / "I'm thinking up a better name for it. Any ideas?" / "Say hello to it properly this time, {name}."
- early_riser: "Up before dawn again, {name}. Best part of the day." / "You missed a fine sunrise. Again." / "Next time I'll wake you for the sunrise. You'll thank me."
- whittles: "Hold still, {name}. I'm carving you." / "Made you a little figure. The nose came out wrong." / "Wood talks, if you're patient with the knife."
- bad_puns: "Why do skeletons stay in? No body to go out with." / "{name}, I've got a new one. You're going to hate it." / "Stop groaning. That one was good."
- sweet_tooth: "You wouldn't have anything sweet on you, {name}?" / "Honey cakes. That's all I can think about." / "Everything's better after something sweet."
- lucky_charm: "Touched my charm twice today. Can't be too careful." / "Want to hold it for luck, {name}? Gently." / "It's never let me down. Not once."
- hates_wet_boots: "Wet boots again, {name}. Nothing worse. Nothing." / "If there's a puddle, my boots will find it." / "Dry socks. That's the whole secret to a good day."
- sketches: "Hold that pose, {name}. Almost done." / "I'm drawing you. I made you a little taller." / "Another page full. Want to see?"
- tidies: "Your collar's crooked, {name}. There. Better." / "Everything in its place. Is that so strange?" / "Hold still. You've got something on your sleeve."
- cloud_names: "See that one, {name}? I call it the Duke." / "The clouds are good company today." / "That cloud looks just like you, {name}. Mostly."
- afraid_of_moths: "Is that a moth? Tell me that's not a moth." / "I'll face a skeleton any day. Moths, no." / "Keep that lantern away from me, {name}. You know why."

5. WHAT MOVES IN test_lines.gd

title: Spike: measure a small local LLM for NPC lines (after the line bank)
description:
WHY
Owner, 2026-09-24: "i was wondering how feasible it is to run a tiny llm for npc dialogue? something like LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct or Qwen3-1.7B quantized of course". The owner decided the same day: "Line bank now, LLM test after". The authored line bank (a slice of ig-m6o.2.2) ships first. This spike measures whether a local model adds enough over the bank to be worth its cost.

KNOWN (director, 2026-09-24, checked on the web)
- NobodyWho (github.com/nobodywho-ooo/nobodywho): a Rust + llama.cpp GDExtension for Godot 4.x, in the Asset Library. It runs any GGUF model, supports GBNF grammar-constrained output, and streams.
- LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct Q4_K_M: 731 MB (huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct-GGUF). The LFM Open License v1.0 is based on Apache 2.0, but allows commercial use only while annual revenue is under US$10M.
- Qwen3-1.7B Q4_K_M: about 1.1 GB (bartowski/Qwen_Qwen3-1.7B-GGUF). Apache 2.0.
- Today's export is about 130 MB (game.exe 109 MB + game.pck 20 MB).

QUESTIONS THE SPIKE ANSWERS (numbers from the owner's PC)
1. Does NobodyWho load under Godot 4.7.1 on Windows? How much does it add to the export (plugin plus model)?
2. Model load time and RAM, for both models.
3. Seconds per line on CPU, and on GPU if the plugin's Vulkan path works. Measure with the game running, including the frame-time hit while a line generates.
4. Quality: 50 lines per model, generated from real Ledger facts (the same fact inputs the line bank uses). Count the lines that name a person or place that isn't in the facts, the lines out of tone, and the lines worse than the bank's.
5. Do a GBNF grammar and a name/place check make the output safe to show, with the line bank as the fallback?

RULES
- Get the owner's approval before any download. Name each file, its source and its size: the plugin release and the two GGUFs.
- Work on a throwaway branch or worktree. Nothing merges from the spike. No autoload (hard cap of 3). No save changes. It uses the engine lane: one Godot at a time.
- Output: a short report in .agent-results/<this id>/ with the numbers, the 50-line samples and a recommendation. Any adoption path starts with a godot-architect ADR, since this is a new native dependency.

WAITS FOR: the line-bank slice of ig-m6o.2.2. It supplies the fact inputs and the baseline to compare against.
notes: ig-m6o.2.2.2: the greeting facts builder is Lines.greeting_facts(bond, dream, body_id, names) in history/lines.gd (pure static, reads only its arguments). Reuse it; ignore facts.start.

title: Town look 1: pan and zoom the overview over the whole map, green grass, Lumbermill label
description:
WHY
Slice 1 of ig-6m2.8. Read the parent first. The overview camera can't leave the centre of a 217-hex map, the grass reads lime-yellow, and the Lumbermill hides its label. All three are view code.

BEHAVIOR
1. Two methods on TownView do the moving; input only calls them, so tests drive them directly.
   - pan_overview(offset: Vector3) moves the overview camera by offset on the ground (x and z only).
   - zoom_overview(steps: int) moves it along its own view direction; positive steps zoom in.
   - Both act on get_viewport().get_camera_3d(), and only while body == null (then that is hub.tscn's Camera3D, which embody already saves and restores). hub.tscn stays the one place that sets the start framing and the 30° pitch. No new camera node.
2. Clamp, after every move.
   - The focus is where the camera's view direction meets the ground (y = 0 in town space). It stays within the map extent of the town origin: town_map_radius × TownRules.HEX_SIZE × √3 (48 m today). If a move takes it past, shift the camera back so the focus sits on that circle.
   - The camera's height stays within OVERVIEW_HEIGHT_MIN 4.5 m and OVERVIEW_HEIGHT_MAX 27 m (today it sits at 9 m). A zoom step that would leave that range stops at the bound.
3. Input, in TownView, only while body == null and input_enabled (no panel, no pause menu), and in placing mode too, so the player can place far out.
   - W A S D and the arrow keys pan, camera-relative (W is away from the camera), at OVERVIEW_PAN_SPEED 20 m/s × (height / 9). Read keys the way TownHero._key_direction does; reuse TownHero.MOVE_KEYS.
   - Right-mouse drag grabs the ground: the ground point under the cursor stays under it (pan by ground_point(before) − ground_point(now)). Nothing in the hub uses the right button today.
   - The mouse wheel calls zoom_overview(±1). Each step is OVERVIEW_ZOOM_STEP 10% of the current distance to the focus.
   - These come through _unhandled_input or _process, so a click or wheel on a panel never reaches them.
4. Grass. HexGround gets a material_override: a duplicate of the tile mesh's own material with albedo_color = GRASS_TINT (start Color(0.72, 0.85, 0.62)), which multiplies the shared atlas texture on the ground only. Tune it by screenshot toward a natural green.
5. Lumbermill label. lumbermill.tscn's Label goes from y 4.4 to 5.6, above the crane (the model's top is 5.11 m at ×3).
6. Constants. OVERVIEW_HEIGHT_MIN, OVERVIEW_HEIGHT_MAX, OVERVIEW_PAN_SPEED, OVERVIEW_ZOOM_STEP and GRASS_TINT are presentation constants in town_view.gd, not SYSTEMS rows. Tune them by screenshot.

SAVE
None. No key, no load path. The camera starts at hub.tscn's framing every time the hub opens.

ACCEPTANCE (tests/unit, APPDATA redirected)
- pan_overview far past the edge in each of four directions: the focus ends within 48 m (+0.01) of the origin.
- zoom_overview(+100) and (−100): the height ends at 4.5 and 27 m, and the camera keeps its pitch.
- With a body, and with input_enabled false: a pushed right-drag motion and a wheel event leave the camera where it was.
- With body == null and input enabled: a pushed wheel event changes the height; a pushed right-drag moves the focus.
- Embody, then step out: the overview camera is back where it was before the embody.
- HexGround has a material_override whose albedo_color is GRASS_TINT, and the House model's material is unchanged.
- building_at still names a building after a pan and at both zoom bounds (PICK_DISTANCE 200 m covers the far bound).
- test_town_builder.gd and test_town_hero.gd stay green.
- Screenshots in .agent-results/ig-6m2.8.1/: the start view, both zoom bounds, the focus at a map edge, and the Lumbermill label. Reuse .agent-results/ig-6m2.2/capture.gd's pattern (windowed, APPDATA redirected, never the owner's save).
- BUILT. Verifier pass: normal (view only; the lumbermill.tscn label is a position change, not a seam change).

FILES
- hub/town/town_view.gd (the two methods, input, the clamp, the tint, constants)
- hub/town/buildings/lumbermill.tscn (the Label's y)
- new tests/unit/test_town_camera.gd

NON-GOALS
Everything in the parent's NON-GOALS. Edge-of-screen pan. A pitch that changes with zoom. The embodied hero's walk bounds: WALK_HALF_EXTENT keeps it in a 48 m square (about ring 4 of 8), so it can't walk to buildings placed farther out. A walk that can't reach still arrives after STUCK_SECONDS. That is a separate bead if wanted.

title: Ledger budget test is flaky: its empty baseline swings 0.8-3.5 ms, wider than the 2 ms margin
description:
WHY
test_ledger_file.gd test_a_full_ledger_adds_at_most_2_ms_to_a_commit_or_a_periodic_save failed once in the director's BUILT (2026-09-24, wgj.11 tree): on the idle save, the empty case took 0.838 ms and the mixed cap 3.240, a 2.402 gap against a 2.0 limit. It passed on a re-run.
About 20 runs today show the pattern:
- The empty baseline is the test's first timing. It swings from 0.8 to 3.5 ms.
- The eventful cap is also a full ledger, but it holds steady at 0.7 to 1.0.
So the baseline is mostly warm-up noise, and the test passes because that noise pads it. Against a clean baseline, the mixed cap's idle and periodic saves cost 1.2 to 3.2 ms. The 2 ms budget in SYSTEMS § The Ledger may really be broken for a mixed ledger.

FIX
1. godot-tester: make the test honest. Warm up before the empty timing by running one _timings() and throwing it away, so the baseline is clean.
2. Then check whether the mixed cap still breaks 2 ms. If it does, find why a save with nothing new costs about 2 ms more with a mixed full ledger than with an eventful one. The test's own comment says eventful is the eviction's worst case. Fix that, or take the budget to the game-designer.

ACCEPTANCE
With the warmed baseline, the test passes 10 runs in a row, and BUILT is green.
The data is in the LEDGER BUDGET lines of .agent-results/*gut*.log.
notes:
2026-09-24 investigation (read-only, no engine). The premise is wrong: mixed does not cost more than empty. Eventful is the odd one out.

DATA. All 29 LEDGER BUDGET lines in .agent-results/**/*.log, 03:20 (m6o.9) to 08:14.
- Periodic and idle saves are about 2.2-3.3 ms for EMPTY and MIXED alike (27 of 29 runs). Mixed minus empty is -0.5 to +0.9 ms.
- EVENTFUL sits at about 0.7-1.0 ms. Commit is about 0.8 in all three cases.
- The pattern predates ig-6pm (c1bdebb, 07:14), so the parse and validate step is not the cause.
- Each case is bimodal: about 0.7 (fast) or about 2.7 (slow), a step with nothing in between. A slope would mean work that grows with history; a step means a wait.
- The failures are the baseline catching one fast sample (best of 7) while the full case catches none: wgj11 (empty 1.455 / 1.497), the director's run (0.838 against 3.240), and one mixed flip the other way (ig-6m2.2, 0.880).

CODE. Nothing on a save with nothing new scales with the ledger:
- save_service.gd:53: the rewrite check is O(1) (is_same).
- save_service.gd:258: _append_ledger returns before any file I/O when nothing is new.
- to_dict (game_session.gd:2304) and validate_saved_state carry only ledger_next_seq.
- Eviction and _ledger_tiers run in _record and after a commit (game_session.gd:2531-2533, 2188), never inside save().

WHY EVENTFUL IS FAST. tests/unit/test_ledger_file.gd:281: the periodic sample records a routine battle.
- In the eventful ledger it is the only tier-0 record, so Ledger.evict (ledger.gd:36) evicts it the moment it is recorded.
- So eventful's "periodic save" appends nothing. It is a second idle save, and eventful never saves twice in a row with an append.
- Empty and mixed keep the record, so their periodic save is a second append to ledger.jsonl about 1 ms after the commit's append.
- The slow step shows up exactly there: that save and the one after it. The next commit is fast again.

SO:
- The +2 ms does not come from routine records or ledger size. It is an OS file-I/O wait after back-to-back appends. The exact mechanism is unproven read-only. Lead suspect: an on-close or on-open scan of the just-written side file.
- In play, saves are seconds apart (periodic every 15 s).
- The 2 ms budget (growth with history) holds.
- SYSTEMS.md:581-582 is wrong: "0.2 ms to a periodic save ... worst case is a ledger with no routine battles" measured no append at all.
- The test comment at test_ledger_file.gd:252 is wrong for the same reason.

FIX (test only):
1. test_ledger_file.gd:281: record a battle that survives eviction in every case, e.g. _battle(0, [{"tick": 1, "what": "downed", "hero": "hero:a", "by": "enemy:rogue"}]). Then all three cases do the same I/O. It also makes eventful the real worst eviction scan (find(0) misses the whole list, then find(1) takes index 0).
2. Let each timed step start with the disk quiet, the way play does: OS.delay_msec(20) before each of the three `started = Time.get_ticks_usec()` lines, outside the timed window. That adds about 1.3 s to the suite.
   - Expected, if the wait is an after-effect: all nine numbers drop to about 0.7-1.0.
   - If they stay at about 2.7, the wait is part of the append itself. Then take the budget to game-designer: a fixed per-append I/O cost at any size (about 2 ms, well under a 16.6 ms frame) is not growth with history.
3. The warm-up _timings() is harmless, but on its own it won't stop the flake. The baseline is not warm-up noise: it sits in the same slow mode as mixed.
Director, 2026-09-24: extra's diagnosis is accepted. Build plan (test only; it needs the engine, so it goes in the next free window):
(1) At test_ledger_file.gd:281, record a battle that survives eviction, so all three cases do the same append.
(2) Add OS.delay_msec(20) before each timed op, outside the timed window.
(3) Fix the :252 comment.
Then run the file 10 times and paste the LEDGER BUDGET lines. If the numbers stay bimodal after (1) and (2), switch best-of-7 to the median of 7 (a bimodal wait makes the minimum fragile). Once the data is in, extra corrects SYSTEMS.md:581-582 with the measured numbers.
Director, 2026-09-24, correction: drop the median fallback. The m6o.9 logs (.agent-results/ig-m6o.9/gut_ledger2.log) already ran the median, and it flaked the other way (eventful commit 10.3 ms against an empty 0.87). If the 10 runs stay bimodal after fix 1+2, take it to game-designer for a ruling on what the 2 ms budget counts (a fixed ~2 ms per append at any size). Don't change the statistic.
close_reason: Fixed by the director from extra's diagnosis, committed e076895. 10 of 10 runs pass, with all nine timings between 0.77 and 1.27 ms. BUILT green: gate 0/0, GUT 682/682. Extra is correcting SYSTEMS.md:581-582 with these numbers.

title: Town builder 5b: starvation, warned and never offline
description:
WHY
Slice 2 of ig-6m2.5. Read the parent first. The owner ruled that heroes can starve to death. This slice makes that fair: every death is warned, the next victim is named ahead of time, and nobody dies while the player is not looking. It crosses boundaries #1 (save) and #3 (permadeath).

BEHAVIOR
1. The clock. It is pure, in TownRules, and GameSession calls it only from _advance_clocks_in_memory. Each tick:
   - Every workplace's production (wood, stone, food) is multiplied by starving_work_multiplier while starving.
   - Demand not met (food would go below 0): food = 0, and town_starving_seconds += delta, up to the next stop point (item 2).
   - food ≥ food_low_warning_minutes × the current eating per minute: town_starving_seconds = 0 and town_starve_acked = false.
   - In between: the clock holds.
   - Starving means town_starving_seconds > 0 (SYSTEMS § Food and starvation). So work doesn't flicker between half and full speed.
2. Deaths are due at fixed points. Death n (from 1) is due at starve_first_death_minutes + (n − 1) × starve_next_death_minutes of starving: 20, 30, 40 minutes.
   - n is derived, not saved: n − 1 = how many due points the clock has already reached (a death happens as the clock reaches its point).
   - The stop point is due_n − starve_last_warning_minutes (15, 25, 35). Unless acked, the clock never passes it. Any delta is capped there, so a long tick or a hitch can't skip a warning.
3. acknowledge_starvation(). It does something only while the clock sits at a stop point, and is a no-op otherwise. It sets town_starve_acked through _commit_profile_mutation. Once acked, the clock runs to due_n.
4. The death. When the clock reaches due_n:
   - victim = TownRules.starvation_victim(eaters), using slice 1's eater read. It is pure and returns an instance_id or "". Order: lowest rank, then lowest level, then newest in the roster (the last in roster order).
   - GameSession unequips every equipped item to inventory through unequip_item, then calls kill_hero(hero, &"", balance, "starvation"). Nothing is equipped by then, so no Lost Cache.
   - town_starve_acked = false. The status line says "<name> starved."
   - No other code removes a hero (rule 8). If the victim is the body, kill_hero already clears the body.
5. The ladder. It is built in code in hub_ui_builder.gd, like the recovery-clock warning, so hub.tscn does not change. It refreshes on the tick signals.
   - "Food low": food < food_low_warning_minutes × eating per minute, while anyone eats.
   - "Starving": work at half speed, plus who dies next and when ("Mira starves in 12:30 unless the town is fed").
   - "Last warning": stopped at a stop point. It says who and when, and has a button that calls acknowledge_starvation().
6. Numbers. Add food_low_warning_minutes 10, starving_work_multiplier 0.5, starve_first_death_minutes 20, starve_next_death_minutes 10 and starve_last_warning_minutes 5 to balance_table.gd and balance.tres. Keep other people's uncommitted work intact.

SAVE (boundary #1)
- town_starving_seconds and town_starve_acked are additive keys: no SAVE_VERSION bump.
- town_starving_seconds: missing → 0. Not finite, or < 0 → 0, with a warning. Past the next stop point while not acked → the stop point, so a save can't skip a warning.
- town_starve_acked: missing, or not a bool → false. True while the clock is not at a stop point → false. It only ever means "this warning was seen".
- ig-6pm: these are repairs, never refusals (no validate_saved_state rule). Every value written is one the load keeps as it is.

ACCEPTANCE (tests/unit, APPDATA redirected)
- The clock:
  - food 0 with demand unmet: the clock advances by delta;
  - a farm that makes less than the town eats still starves (food ticks above 0 but never reaches the food-low line);
  - food above the line resets the clock;
  - in between, the clock holds.
- Starving halves wood, stone and food production. After the reset, full speed.
- Ladder:
  - the clock stops at 15:00, and stays there over any number of ticks and one huge delta;
  - an ack starts it again, and the death comes at 20:00;
  - the next stop is at 25:00, and after another ack the death comes at 30:00.
- AFK: an offline catch-up of any length moves neither food nor the clock. Hours of live ticks with no ack kill nobody past the first stop.
- Victim:
  - order is rank, then level, then newest;
  - away, busy and unhoused heroes are never picked.
- The death:
  - the victim's gear is in inventory, and there is no Lost Cache;
  - the Ledger holds a 'died' record with cause "starvation";
  - a victim who is the body leaves no body behind.
- grep: roster.erase appears only in kill_hero.
- Save:
  - a real disk save and reload stopped at a last warning keeps food, the clock and acked false, and the clock is still stopped;
  - a save and reload after the ack keeps acked true;
  - repairs: clock -1 → 0; a clock past the stop with acked false → the stop; acked true below the stop → false; no keys → 0 and false.
- A screenshot of each ladder state, in .agent-results/ig-6m2.5.2/.
- BUILT. Verifier pass mandatory: boundaries #1 and #3.

FILES
- hub/town/town_rules.gd (the clock step, the victim)
- systems/game_session.gd, balance_table.gd, balance.tres
- hub/hub_ui_builder.gd (the ladder line and its button; keep the uncommitted work already in it)
- hub/hub.gd (refresh, the ack, the status line)
- tests/unit/test_town_food.gd; tests/save_roundtrip_check.gd if the disk case lives there

NON-GOALS
Everything in the parent's NON-GOALS.
notes:
Director 2026-09-24, at GO: the acked repair on load is 'acked true with the clock BELOW the stop point -> false' (the acceptance wording). Behaviour item 3's 'not at a stop point' would reset a save made after an ack, while the clock runs from the stop toward the death, and pull the clock back to the stop.
Implementer (sub-session), 2026-09-24. Uncommitted, ready for director review. BUILT: import gate exit 0; GUT 713/713, 17183 asserts, 0 [Failed]/SCRIPT ERROR (.agent-results/6m252-gate.log, 6m252-gut.log). Godot reaped, count 0. Sol review (.agent-results/logs/ig-6m2.5.2-sol-1.json, brief .agent-results/ig-6m2.5.2/sol-brief-1.md): PASS WITH FINDINGS, no code defect; 3 minor test gaps, all fixed: (1) the status-said-once check now changes the status and asserts it stays; (2) the ack is a pushed click after the layout settles (GUT's own panel layer is hidden for that one click) plus a click-through check on the row; (3) the failed-save rollback equips the victim and compares the whole to_dict before/after. Mutants: 20/20 earlier, plus 3 new (status re-said, row STOP, button IGNORE), all caught. grep roster.erase: only in kill_hero. Screenshots of all 4 ladder states in .agent-results/ig-6m2.5.2/. Deviation: tests live in a new file tests/unit/test_town_starvation.gd (+.uid), not test_town_food.gd. Headless note: the row reports a stale 917px-tall rect until a frame runs; after one frame it is correct, and the screenshots are right.
close_reason: Landed 34b818b. Director BUILT green: gate exit 0 with 0 warnings/0 errors, GUT 713/713 (17183 asserts), 0 SCRIPT ERROR, tree fingerprint unchanged, Godot count 0. Sol (#1, #3): PASS WITH FINDINGS, no implementation defect; its 3 test gaps fixed (status said once, a real pushed click plus a row click-through check, a full to_dict rollback compare with an equipped victim).    - eaten = food_per_housed_hero_minute × eaters × minutes.
   GameSession calls it only from _advance_clocks_in_memory, never from the offline catch-up.

description:

   - Pick: a StaticBody3D on layer 2 with a 4.5 × 3 × 4.5 box;

6. HUD and panel.

SAVE (boundary #1)

title: Town builder 3b: buildings take live-play time to go up
description:
WHY
Slice 2 of ig-6m2.3. Read the parent first. A new House or workplace takes live-play time to go up, and you can see it happen: scaffolding, then three stages, then its own model. Until it is finished it does nothing.

BEHAVIOR
1. Placing. place_building sets build_remaining on the new building's dict, from TownRules.build_seconds(type, balance):
   - house_build_seconds for a House;
   - workplace_build_seconds for every workplace type (TownRules.worker_slots(type) > 0). That covers the Lumbermill and the Mine, and the Farm too, whichever of this slice and ig-6m2.5.1 lands first.
   Halls are never placed, so they are never under construction.
2. The clock.
   - _advance_clocks_in_memory takes delta off every build_remaining. At 0 the key is erased, and the building is finished.
   - The offline catch-up (_advance_orders_in_memory) does not touch it.
   - The live tick already emits roster_changed, so the town and the panels refresh without a new signal.
3. Under construction = the key is present.
   - station_hero and assign_home refuse with a reason, e.g. "House 3 is still being built (0:42 left)."
   - Its hex is taken. Placing there is refused, as today.
   - move_building works and keeps build_remaining (it only changes q and r).
   - It counts as having one for the free rule. TownRules already counts any building of the type.
   - A Lumbermill or Mine under construction can have no workers, so it makes nothing.
4. The look.
   - TownView.show_buildings shows a building under construction as its type's scene, with the Model hidden and a Stage model in its place.
   - The stage follows how much is done: building_scaffolding for the first quarter of the build time, then building_stage_A, _B and _C. When it finishes, the Model shows again. Stage = floor(done fraction × 4), clamped to 0..3.
   - Hexagon models are ×3.0, as ig-wgj.3 set.
   - Label, Pick and WorkSpot don't change.
   - show_buildings runs on every tick (roster_changed), so it swaps the stage node only when the stage changes. Otherwise it does nothing.
5. Panel. A building under construction shows "Under construction: 0:42 left" in its placed panel, and Assign is disabled.
6. Numbers. Add house_build_seconds 60 and workplace_build_seconds 120 to balance_table.gd and balance.tres. Keep other people's uncommitted work intact.

SAVE (boundary #1)
- build_remaining is an additive key on a building dict, in seconds. No SAVE_VERSION bump.
- to_dict writes it only while it is > 0. A missing key means finished, so every older building loads finished.
- Today _read_town_building builds a new dict holding only id, type, q and r. It must carry build_remaining too:
  - a finite number > 0 is kept, clamped to that type's build seconds (a lower tuned time never leaves a longer wait);
  - a missing key, 0 or less, or a non-number means finished: drop the key, and warn on a bad value;
  - on a hall, it is ignored.
- ig-6pm: keep this a repair, not a refusal (no validate_saved_state rule), so a written save always loads. build_remaining is maxf(finite − delta, 0), so it stays finite.

ACCEPTANCE (tests/unit, APPDATA redirected)
- A placed House has build_remaining 60, and every workplace type in TownRules.TYPES has 120. A hall has none.
- The live tick moves it 1 s per s, and it finishes (key gone) at 0. An offline catch-up of any length moves it 0.
- Under construction, assign_home and station_hero refuse with the reason and change no state. After it finishes, both work.
- Moving a building under construction leaves build_remaining unchanged.
- Free rule: while the free Lumbermill is under construction, a second one costs full price. The preview equals the result.
- Save:
  - a half-built House (build_remaining 30) survives a real disk save and reload with 30;
  - an ig-6m2.3.1-era save loads every building finished;
  - bad values on a House (−1, "x", 1e9) load as finished, finished and 60.
- The look:
  - at 0 %, 25 %, 50 % and 75 % done, the stage node is scaffolding, stage_A, stage_B and stage_C;
  - at 100 % the Model shows and the stage node is gone;
  - a tick that doesn't cross a quarter keeps the same stage node.
- Screenshots of the four stages and the finished House, in .agent-results/ig-6m2.3.2/.
- BUILT. Verifier pass mandatory: boundary #1 (build_remaining, the legacy save) and #2 (the stage node in the building scenes).

FILES
- systems/game_session.gd, hub/town/town_rules.gd, balance_table.gd, balance.tres
- hub/town/town_view.gd (the stage node)
- hub/hub.gd (the placed panel)
- new hub/town/models/hexagon/building_scaffolding.gltf + .bin and building_stage_A.gltf + .bin (parent § Assets)
- tests/unit: test_town_builder.gd, or a new test_town_construction.gd

NON-GOALS
Builders or hauling (it just takes time). Cancelling, refunding or rushing. Construction for halls or upgrades. Build time for moving. Everything in the parent's NON-GOALS.

Refresh the town's build stages on expeditions_changed too. (2) The periodic save gate (game_session.gd ~l.114) must also fire while any building has build_remaining, or a crash rolls back build progress. One test, like test_town_stone's periodic-save test. (3) FILES lists only building_stage_A, but item 4 needs stage_B and stage_C too, from the local KayKit Temp folder.

title: The body cannot walk to buildings near the map edge (fixed 23.6 m walk bounds)
description:
Found by extra while scoping ig-6m2.6 (2026-09-24). hub/town/town_view.gd:37 WALK_HALF_EXTENT = 23.6 sets the player body's bounds (town_view.gd:120-121) as a fixed square. The hex map (town_map_radius 8) reaches about 30 m, at hex (5,0) for example. Since ig-6m2.2 any building can move to any free hex, so a building placed near the edge is out of the body's reach, and so is a partner standing out there.

Fix: derive the bounds from the map geometry (TownRules map hexes and the hex size) instead of a constant, so every placeable hex is reachable. Keep it the simplest rule that works (a bounding rect of the map plus one hex is fine; corners past the hex map are harmless ground).

Acceptance: a test that the body can reach the centre of the farthest map hex in each direction; test_town_hero's edge test updated to the derived bound; BUILT green. Scene seam (#2) is not touched unless the fix moves nodes.

title: Town walkers 2: wanderers, the partner as a walker, click a walker
description:
WHY
Slice 2 of ig-6m2.6. Read the parent first. The rest of the town comes alive: heroes in town with no job wander and use the halls. The bond partner becomes an ordinary walker, so nothing stands at a fixed spot a building can swallow (the ig-6m2.2 note on the parent). A click on a walker opens that hero. This is what ig-wgj.5 asked for, rebuilt on slice 1's hex walk graph.

BEHAVIOR
1. Wanderers. Every in-town hero with no station gets a figure, up to the cap.
   - It walks to a free hex that touches a building (the streets, not the empty map edge), picked by its own RNG. It lingers LINGER_SECONDS, then picks again.
   - If that hex is an approach hex of a hall, it faces the hall and plays Interact (it is using the stall). Elsewhere it plays Idle_B.
   - A wanderer with a House ends one trip in HOME_EVERY at its door (Idle_A).
   - First show: each wanderer starts at a street hex from its own RNG. Later joiners come in at the TownGate, as in slice 1.
   - A wanderer who gets stationed re-plans from where it stands. It does not re-enter at the gate.
2. Cap. AMBIENT_HERO_CAP, a constant in town_view.gd, counts wanderers only. Keepers, workers and the partner always show.
   - hub.gd passes the in-town heroes in pick order: keepers and workers, the partner, then favorites, then higher rank, then lower instance_id. The same heroes appear each visit.
   - FPS: measure at caps 8, 12 and 16 in a windowed run, with APPDATA pointed at a throwaway folder holding a seeded save with enough heroes. Never the owner's real APPDATA.
   - Set the cap to the highest value that holds 60 FPS. Mark it PROVISIONAL in the code comment, and put the numbers in these notes.
3. The partner is its own walker. hub.gd stops leaving the partner out. show_partner hands the line and the body to the partner's walker.
   - The greeting keeps what ig-m6o.2.1 built: MEET_DISTANCE, REARM_DISTANCE, LINE_SECONDS, Interact once, the line above its head. The greeting pauses the walk, and the walk resumes after it.
   - A partner that starts inside REARM_DISTANCE of the body starts disarmed, so a load never fires the greeting at once.
   - Drop PARTNER_SPAWN_OFFSET, PARTNER_DOOR_OFFSET and the fixed placement in show_partner. The partner works, rests or wanders by its role, like everyone else. One figure per hero.
   - Fold town_partner.gd into town_walker.gd, or keep it as a greeter the walker owns: implementer's choice.
4. Click a walker. Each figure gets a pick shape on a new WALKER_PICK_LAYER. The body stays on no layer.
   - One ray over both pick layers; the nearest hit wins.
   - A walker hit emits a new hero_selected(hero_id), and hub.gd opens that hero's detail. A building hit still emits building_selected.
   - With a body embodied, a walker click opens the detail at once, with no walk.
   - This changes ig-wgj.7 item 4 ("clicking a keeper emits building_selected for its building"). A keeper stands in front of its building, which is still one click away. Director: confirm, or keepers and workers open their building and only wanderers open the hero.
5. Numbers: LINGER_SECONDS, HOME_EVERY and AMBIENT_HERO_CAP stay in the view scripts (parent § Rules).

ACCEPTANCE (extend tests/unit/test_town_walkers.gd; change tests/unit/test_bonds.gd)
- Wanderers use only free ground: 60 s of simulated wandering, sampled every 0.25 m, never inside a grown box. At a hall's approach hex a wanderer faces the hall and plays Interact.
- Cap and order: with more unemployed heroes in town than the cap, the shown set matches the pick order. Keepers, workers and the partner show beyond the cap. The set updates after a dispatch, a return, a summon and a kill_hero.
- Partner:
  - exactly one figure for the partner hero;
  - it greets once when the walking body comes within MEET_DISTANCE, pauses and resumes, and re-arms past REARM_DISTANCE;
  - it starts disarmed inside REARM_DISTANCE;
  - the ig-6m2.2 case: move the Sanctum off (1, 0) and a House onto it, and the partner is never inside a box;

- Click: a click on a walker emits hero_selected with its id and opens its detail. A click on a building still names the building. A walker in front of its building wins the click. Pick click points as the bd memory headless-gut-click-tests says (GUT's output panel eats clicks).
- Nothing saved and the global RNG untouched, as in slice 1, now with wanderers.
- The FPS numbers and the chosen cap in these notes. A screenshot of the town with wanderers in .agent-results/ig-6m2.6.2/.
- BUILT. Verifier pass mandatory: boundary #2 (the new signal, the pick layer, the hub wiring).

FILES

- hub/town/town_walker.gd: wandering, the greeting

Heroes talking to or reacting to each other. Wanderers reacting to the body (only the partner greets). Everything in the parent's NON-GOALS.

title: Town walkers 1: keepers and workers walk House to work and back
description:
WHY
Slice 1 of ig-6m2.6. Read the parent first: it holds the shared rules and the walkable-area ruling. The town looks like it works. Every keeper and worker in town is drawn at its building, walking to it from its House and back. This is ig-wgj.7's scope, rebuilt on the builder's per-scene WorkSpot.

BEHAVIOR
1. Walk graph. TownView builds the AStar2D and updates it in show_buildings (parent § The walkable area). It exposes two reads over the current occupancy, both testable without frames:
   - route(from, to), where each end is a building's WorkSpot (reached through its approach hexes) or a free-ground point;
   - free_point(near).
   The six axial directions may live in TownRules as a constant (hex math only).
2. Figures. New TownWalker (hub/town/town_walker.gd): a Node3D holding the HeroModel, with the archetype picked as TownHero.create does and the same MODEL_SCALE. No physics body. It follows its route at WALK_SPEED playing Walking_A, faces where it walks, and plays its activity clip on arrival.
3. show_walkers(heroes: Array[Hero]). hub.gd passes every in-town hero with a station (keepers and workers), except the bond partner, which keeps its TownPartner figure until slice 2.
   - A refresh keeps an existing figure and its walk. It re-plans only a hero whose station or House changed.
   - It frees the figures of heroes no longer in the list.
   - expeditions_changed fires on every 0.25 s pulse, so a refresh that changes nothing must do nothing.
4. The loop, per figure:
   - A House and a route both ways: walk from the House door to the work spot, work WORK_SECONDS, walk back, rest at the door HOME_SECONDS (Idle_A, facing out), repeat.
   - No House (hall keepers may have none), or no route: stand at the work spot and work. No route = no free approach hex, or the free ground is cut in two. No error, no warning.
   - The work clip comes from a station → clip table in town_walker.gd. A station missing from the table plays Working_A, so a later workplace (the Mine, the Farm) never breaks a figure; those slices add their own row. 6. A place or a move re-plans every figure from where it stands: first to the centre of the hex it is on, then on. A worker whose building moved walks to the new spot. Anyone on a hex that just got a building, other than at that building's own WorkSpot, moves to free_point(where it stood). title: A save can write a state its own loader refuses (the save path skips validate_saved_state)
description:
Found by high1 during ig-wgj.10 (2026-09-24). A test fixture with a bad stranded incident committed through _commit_profile_mutation and saved fine, then load_game refused the same file ('squad_id must match squad membership'). So the write side never runs the loader's validation. In play this only matters if a bug ever makes in-memory state invalid, but then the next save writes a file the game will not load, and the player is locked out of the save (boundary #1).

Question for godot-architect first: should SaveService (or _commit_profile_mutation) run validate_saved_state on the dict before writing, and on failure refuse the save so the existing rollback undoes the action? That turns 'a bug locks the save' into 'a bug refuses one action'. Weigh the cost of a full validation on every save.

Related, lower: Sol (ig-wgj.10 round 1) noted validate_saved_state does not check hero profession_xp. Hero.from_dict loads a bad value as 0 with push_error by design, so a bad XP number is zeroed rather than refused. Rule whether that stays.

Acceptance, if the answer is yes: a test that corrupts in-memory state, runs a real action, and shows the save refused, the action rolled back and the file on disk still loadable (APPDATA redirected). BUILT green. Verifier pass on boundary #1.
notes:
ARCHITECT RULING (2026-09-24): yes, check before writing. Put it in SaveService.save(), not in _commit_profile_mutation. No boundary moves, so no ADR.

WHERE, AND WHY THERE
- save() is the one door every writer uses: _commit_profile_mutation (every action, plus tick_expeditions when something falls due), the 15 s periodic save and its retry (game_session.gd ~95-120), the roster_changed signal save (_ready), and load_game's legacy-migration save. A check in _commit_profile_mutation would miss the last three.
- The rules stay in GameSession.validate_saved_state. SaveService already calls it on load (save_service.gd:130-131), so on save it only calls the same thing. The invariant "SaveService never writes a file its own load refuses" is file integrity, which is SaveService's job (ARCHITECTURE rule 4). It is not a game rule, and the autoload rule holds.
- Quit: nothing extra. The game does not save on quit (main_menu.gd:26 just quits, and nothing handles WM_CLOSE), so the per-action and periodic saves are the only writers. A quit save added later gets the guard for free.

THE EXACT RULE (save_service.gd save())
1. Build payload as today, with version and saved_at_unix set. Then text = JSON.stringify(payload, "\t").
2. Before the ledger write, check what load will read: parsed = JSON.parse_string(text). Not a Dictionary → refuse. Otherwise GameSession.repair_rescue_timestamps(parsed), then GameSession.validate_saved_state(parsed, SAVE_VERSION); a non-empty result → refuse. Put parse → repair → validate in one small helper that load_game (130-134) uses too, so the two can never drift.
3. Refuse = _write_failed("Save refused: this game state would not load (<reason>). Your last save is safe; restart to return to it.") and return false. It runs before the ledger write, so a refusal touches no file and needs no _undo_ledger.
4. Write the same text to TMP_PATH (no second stringify).
5. Check the round trip, not the in-memory dict. The loader reads JSON text: numbers come back as floats, StringName comes back as String, and keys come back as strings. A NaN or inf may not survive stringify at all. The in-memory dict is a different object from what load sees, so checking it could refuse good states or pass bad ones.
6. Comment the check with ig-6pm and "do not remove for speed", so a later pass does not strip it.

WHAT THE PLAYER SEES
- An action: it does nothing, and last_action_error shows the message (the existing rollback, game_session.gd ~2149-2171).
- Periodic: _checkpoint_save_failed stops the world clocks, as a disk-full failure does today, and the battle views show checkpoint_error. It retries every 15 s and keeps failing until restart.
- Next main-menu visit: _load_notice shows it too (already set by _write_failed).
- Restarting loads the last good save; progress since then is lost. That is the right cost for a bug, and far better than a locked save.
- The rollback restores the pre-action snapshot. If memory went bad in an earlier signal or periodic save rather than inside this action, every later save is refused too. That is expected: the file stays good.
- No auto-repair. Silently "fixing" state hides the bug and could drop heroes (permadeath, boundary #3).

COST (acceptable; measure, don't gate)
- save() already stringifies the whole payload and writes, flushes and renames two files. The check adds one parse plus one linear walk over the same data: the same order as the stringify, and below the disk work.
- Saves happen per player action, when an order or cache falls due, and every 15 s at most. Never per frame. The 0.25 s pulse already runs BattleState.from_dict twice per order, which costs more.
- Acceptance prints save() time with and without the check on a large profile, best of seven (test_ledger.gd style). Report it in this bead. If the check costs more than the write itself, raise it with the director; don't drop the check.

REJECTED
- Check only in _commit_profile_mutation: it misses the periodic, signal and migration saves.
- Check the in-memory dict: that is not what load reads (see rule 5).
- Debug-only assert: the lock-out happens in the player's build.
- Keep a save.bak and write anyway: it still writes a file the game refuses, and needs a restore UI. Revisit only if a refusal ever shows up in play.

profession_xp: STAYS as is (zeroed with push_error, not refused)
- validate_saved_state refuses what breaks integrity: ids, cross-references, duplication, permadeath and battle checkpoints.
- Soft per-hero numbers (xp at hero.gd:527, passions, profession_xp) are repaired on load with an error log. Refusing the whole save over one bad XP number would lock the player out to protect a few minutes of one hero's hall progress. That is the failure this bead exists to remove.
- It stays consistent with the new rule, because the write check refuses only what load refuses. A soft-repaired field never blocks a save.

TESTS (APPDATA redirected; restore SAVE_PATH and LEDGER_PATH like test_battle_persistence.gd:113-121)
1. Action refused: put the ig-wgj.10 bad stranded incident in memory (squad_id vs membership), then run a real action through _commit_profile_mutation (e.g. a favorite toggle). Check: it returns false, last_action_error names the reason, the action is rolled back, save.json is byte-identical, and load_game on it succeeds.
2. Ledger untouched: in the same case, ledger.jsonl keeps its length and there is no orphan line.
3. Periodic: bad state plus an active order, then drive past PERIODIC_SAVE_SECONDS. _checkpoint_save_failed is set, checkpoint_error carries the reason, and the file is unchanged.
4. Signal save: bad state, then emit roster_changed. The file is unchanged.
5. Non-finite: set a saved float (e.g. recovery_clock_seconds) to NAN in memory and save. It is refused, and the file is unchanged.
6. Legacy migration still loads and re-saves (the existing v2 tests stay green).
7. Cost print (above).
8. BUILT + full GUT, with the determinism golden unchanged.
- Any existing test that commits deliberately invalid state and expects the save to land relied on this bug. Fix the test, not the check.
- Review: boundary #1 → Sol read-only (Claude verifier-hard if Codex wrote it).
2026-09-24 director: ruling accepted as written (the check goes in SaveService.save on the round-tripped text, through a helper shared with load_game, before the ledger write; profession_xp stays zeroed with an error). Queued for high1 right after ig-wgj.12 and ahead of ig-ls3 (P2 before P3). The implementer fixes any test that relied on saving invalid state, not the check.
2026-09-24 BUILD (high): check in SaveService.save() on the round-tripped text (stringify once, parse, _load_refusal = repair_rescue_timestamps + validate_saved_state, shared with load_game), before the ledger write, writes the checked text, exact refusal message, comment ig-6pm + do-not-remove-for-speed. load_game parses itself (version check sits between parse and validate), so the shared part is repair+validate. BUILT: gate exit 0; GUT 649/649 (643 + 6 new), asserts 16340, golden test_pre_skills_checkpoint unchanged. Timing, 300 heroes + 2000 items + 1 battle order, save.json ~423 KB, save() best of 7: before 9.05 ms (HEAD save_service.gd, same test), after 19.62 ms; the check alone 10.26 ms. Tests that relied on the bug (fixed the test, not the check): test_battle_hub.gd 2 incident fixtures -> GameSession._incident_snapshot; test_expedition.gd + test_loot.gd _make_zone zone_id test_zone -> verdant_outskirts; test_keeper_bonuses.gd live-tick test _come_home before the catch-up save, panel test expeditions_changed instead of roster_changed; test_save_service.gd settlement test sets phase returning with status victory. New tests/unit/test_save_refusal.gd (bead tests 1-5, 7). Sol (verifier high, log .agent-results/logs/ig-6pm-sol-1.json, wrapper state incomplete_contract but full verdict): changes needed, 2 medium test gaps, no code bug, no writer bypasses the check. Both fixed: missing vs empty file told apart and LEDGER_TMP_PATH checked; ledger test now does a good save after the refusal and reloads with the same seqs. Not committed.
close_reason: Built by high1 on extra's ruling. Director BUILT: gate exit 0, GUT 649/649, reap 0, tree unchanged across the run; every Save refused line comes from test_save_refusal.gd. Sol round 1 (two medium test gaps) fixed. Timing: 9.05 -> 19.62 ms per save on a 423 KB profile, best of 7.

description:

It also waits for the owner gate in ig-m6o.2.1.

Start only if the owner says the slice's partner is someone worth knowing. If not, game-designer re-plans ig-m6o.2 first. Before any code, tech-lead splits this bead, and godot-architect settles the ADR on derived versus stored bonds (use the slice's measured read cost) and architecture note 9 (testimony versus the Ledger).

SPLIT (tech-lead, 2026-09-24)
Eight children, in order. This bead closes when all of them close.

The owner's two asks are .1 and .2. .3 to .7 carry needs-design: game-designer's numbers and catalogues come first, and each body lists them under BEFORE BUILD.

ADR (godot-architect role, 2026-09-24, PROPOSED): DECISIONS.md "Bonds stay derived from the Ledger, read in one pass for every pair; knowledge and testimony are per-hero state that points into it". Bonds and dreams stay derived. One pass reads every pair, and its holder keeps it until the ledger changes. Meals and encounters are live-tick records from saved state, evicted first. title: Summon and rank-up ignore a failed save (a locked save gives a free summon re-roll)
description:
From Sol's review of ig-m6o.9 (point 2; .agent-results/logs/ig-m6o.9-sol.json). Rescoped 2026-09-24 after extra traced every death path.

THE BUG
Two hub actions change the profile outside _commit_profile_mutation. They save only through the roster_changed signal, which is connected to SaveService.save (systems/game_session.gd:84) and ignores its return:
- GameSession.summon_hero, from hub/hub.gd (about line 1053)
- GameSession.rank_up_hero, from hub/hub.gd (about line 1111)
When that save fails (full disk, lock, permissions), memory runs ahead of disk with no rollback and no error. Summon is the bad one. hub.gd rolls the hero with the global randi() (Summon.roll) before any commit and shows 'Summoned X'. Quitting then undoes the pull and refunds the stones: a free re-roll by locking the save file.

NOT A BUG (the first version of this bead was wrong)
Every death already runs inside _commit_profile_mutation, so a failed save rolls it back and memory and disk agree. The director checked each path:
- abandon: :1189
- live expiry and failed rescue: the live tick, :1507
- offline catch-up: :1520
- legacy QuickResolve: _complete_order_in_memory, under both ticks
- sacrifice: _apply_bulk_plan_in_memory
The original claim came from grepping the direct kill_hero call sites without tracing the wrappers.

FIX
Route summon_hero and rank_up_hero through _commit_profile_mutation, so a failed save rolls back and reports the reason, like every other profile action.

ACCEPTANCE
- For summon and rank-up, a forced save failure leaves memory and disk agreeing and shows the reason. Prove it with a real disk reload (boundary #1).
- A summon's result is revealed only after its commit lands. No reveal or animation may come before it (the re-roll hole).
- One forced-failure GUT test per death path (abandon, live expiry, failed rescue, offline catch-up) asserts the hero is alive on disk after a reload. This locks in the guarantee above (boundary #3).
- BUILT + GUT green. Sol reviews (boundaries #1 and #3).

NOTES
- extra's design draft (2026-09-24, in the director's session) recommends an immediate pause plus a persistent 'can't save' banner on the first failed commit. Today the live tick retries silently for up to 15 s, until the periodic save fails and shows the error. That's not needed for this bug; build it only if the owner ever hits it.
- At close, game-designer records in KNOWN_ISSUES: quitting while saves fail resumes from the last save, up to 15 s back (PERIODIC_SAVE_SECONDS), the same as a crash.
notes: 2026-09-24 high: summon_hero and rank_up_hero now go through _commit_profile_mutation (_summon_in_memory/_rank_up_in_memory). rank_up_hero also refuses a Hero not on the roster (Sol finding 2: a stale object after a rollback). hub.gd reveals the pull only on true; a failed pull shows only last_action_error. Tests in test_ledger.gd: summon and rank-up through the hub buttons with a forced save failure and a real reload (both the append and the whole-rewrite ledger paths), plus abandon, live expiry, failed rescue and offline catch-up, each with a control step. BUILT: gate exit 0; GUT 599/599 (.agent-results/ig-8hj/gut_full2.log). Sol: FAIL (2 findings) -> fixed/argued -> PASS WITH NITS (.agent-results/logs/ig-8hj-sol*.json). Open: a failed rewrite leaves an orphan summoned line in ledger.jsonl until the next save; load drops it, so there is no re-roll (Sol agrees). Pre-existing nit: summon_hero accepts a Hero already on the roster. Uncommitted.
close_reason: Summon and rank-up run through _commit_profile_mutation; a failed save rolls back and shows the reason, and the hub reveals a pull only after its commit lands. Tests reload from disk: summon and rank-up (also on the whole-rewrite ledger path) and the four death paths. Director BUILT: gate exit 0, GUT 599/599 (15782 asserts), reap 0.
