title: Living-world 2: People at home (quirks, dreams, shared meals, encounters, Bonds)
description:
WHY
New feeling: affection and everyday amusement. Heroes are people at home before they are units.
Spec: GAME_SPEC.md § Direction, pillar "A Home Worth Returning To" and step 2.

OPENS WITH A THIN SLICE, THEN AN OWNER GATE (director, 2026-09-24)
- Slice 1 is a thin vertical slice: ONE dream, ONE bond, ONE visible moment. For example, two housemates who shared meals and a battle become friends, and the player sees it happen in town. It is built on the Ledger.
- Then the owner plays it. The full scope below starts only if the owner says "someone worth knowing" lands. If it does not, game-designer re-plans .2 before anything else is built.
- Why: the whole direction rests on this feeling. It is cheap to test now and expensive to discover late.

SCOPE, after the gate (tech-lead splits it)
- Passions exist (ig-wgj.13). Add quirks and one dream per hero (a want with milestones).
- Meals become social events: housemates who eat together, soup factions. The Ledger's `meal` kind is written here.
- Neighbourhood encounters: heroes who live or work near each other meet, and the meeting is recorded.
- Bonds: friend, rival, collaborator, grown from recorded encounters, meals and shared battles. Bonds are derived from the Ledger plus a small saved bond state if derivation proves too slow. That choice needs an ADR.
- Joy: nicknames, petty hobbies, festivals that come out of residents' histories.
- Signature moments this step delivers: neighbours become friends and rivals; adjoining workshops invent techniques (only as a bond label in this step; real techniques come in step 3).

READS / WRITES THE LEDGER
Writes meal and encounter records, and bond-change records if bonds are events. Reads shared battles.

DEPENDS
Step 1 (the Ledger). ig-6m2.5.1 (food and eating, for meals; starvation, .5.2, is not needed). ig-6m2.6, both slices (.6.1 keepers and workers, .6.2 wanderers and the partner walker, to show encounters). These live on ig-m6o.2.2 as bd deps; the slice ig-m6o.2.1 needs none of them.

OPEN (game-designer)
- The dream catalogue and its milestone shapes.
- The number of quirks.
- Bond thresholds (PROVISIONAL).
- Whether bonds are derived or stored (ADR).

NOT HERE
Bonds changing combat (step 3). Founding a dream's institution (step 5).
notes:
2026-09-24 DIRECTION v2 (final; GAME_SPEC § Direction). Adds to the body above; where it says SUPERSEDES, v2 wins.
The thin slice and the owner gate still come first.

V2 STEP 2 LIST: spatial routines, directed relationships, knowledge, gossip, recall, moods, dreams and place imprints.
- Relationships are directed and layered: familiarity, affection, situational trust, respect, grievances, commitments, shared techniques. Roles overlap (friend, rival, partner, mentor, debtor, enemy). This widens the body's "Bonds: friend, rival, collaborator".
- A dream names its owner, formative events, desired change, beneficiaries, acceptable methods, observable milestones and the owner's reason. New knowledge can revise it (GAME_SPEC § 5).
- Moods drive routines, private goals produce actions, repeated choices become habits, all only while the game is open. Diaries describe only what their writers know and infer.
- Pulled in from step 1: witnessed details land here, with their first reader (GAME_SPEC § 10 PROVISIONAL).
- Scope boundaries: moods and dialogue (stated reasons, requests, diaries) leave GAME_SPEC § Scope boundaries only when this step's ticket is written.

A2 ITEMS ON THIS STEP (GAME_SPEC § Kept in full):
1. How gossip works [r1]. Gossip needs contact: meals, work, travel, bedside visits. Each exchange carries a bounded number of topics, picked by relevance, emotional intensity and the listener's interests. Couriers reach other districts faster; a popular tavern reaches more listeners. The screen shows who knows which claim, and through whom. Tellers bend a story to their motives (an eyewitness omits their shame, a boaster exaggerates, a partisan swaps the culprit). Detail fades with each retelling while confidence can rise. Ten people repeating one source are still one source. Memory keeps the gist and the feeling longer than the wording; varied retellings and reenactments strengthen recall more than repetition. Forgetting a betrayal does not restore trust. Belief is played through encounters: a hero shows a disputed claim and a concrete objection the player can test ("That cannot be her technique"). Bring the witness, the item or the person.
2. Profession dreams [r4]. Woodcutting, "Give us a road home": a raised connection between home and work; proof is the named residents making the once-dangerous journey. Smithing, "This shield brings you back": forge a response to an observed failure; proof is the paired sequence working and both coming home. Rites, "Let them remember whom they buried": gather witnesses, a place's imprint and departed testimony; proof is the account established and the rite held. Their schools and Essence payoffs are step 5 (ig-m6o.5); departed testimony is step 6.

ARCHITECTURE NOTE 9 (director, v2 Appendix B): testimony against the Ledger. godot-architect owns the split; game-designer owns the volume numbers.
- The Ledger holds settled facts. If every retelling became a record, the 10,000 cap and the records-per-hour estimate would break.
- Keep knowledge and testimony as per-hero state that points into the Ledger.
- Only consequential statements become records: a Herald's covenant, a confession, a public accusation.
- The ig-m6o.9 side file keeps the write cost flat either way.
- Settle it before the full scope after the gate is split. The thin slice (one dream, one bond, one moment) should not need gossip.
2026-09-24 director ruling (GAME_SPEC § 10, folded 2026-09-24): the § 10 PROVISIONAL is settled. Each step-1 piece lands with its first reader, so witnessed details land here with knowledge. The earlier "(GAME_SPEC § 10 PROVISIONAL)" pointer in these notes now means that ruling.
2026-09-24 re-check after the 6m2 splits (bodies only, no new scope): meals need ig-6m2.5.1 only; encounters need both ig-6m2.6 slices; the bd deps sit on ig-m6o.2.2. Two findings for game-designer, NOT ruled: (a) house_capacity is 1 (SYSTEMS: 'each hero has its own house'), so there are no housemates. 'Housemates who eat together' and the slice example need another group, e.g. neighbours, or everyone home at a meal. (b) Walking is cosmetic (ig-6m2.6, game-designer 2026-09-23), so encounter records must come from saved state (Houses and workplaces near each other), never from where walker figures happen to meet. Otherwise a Ledger record would depend on render timing and differ between sessions.

title: Living-world 3: People in combat (bonded chains, informed refusals, rescue motives, recognition)
description:
WHY
New feeling: trust in a particular squad. Relationships change what the squad can do.
Spec: GAME_SPEC.md § Direction, pillar "People Inside the Fight" and step 3; ruling 3 (Defiance).

SCOPE (tech-lead splits it)
- Finish the skill foundation (the ig-gy0 epic) first. This step builds on it and does not redo it.
- Personal chains across bonded heroes: one commits, and another counters the retaliation. An apprentice answers the missing beat in a grieving survivor's old combo.
- Rescue motives: a bonded hero breaks pursuit, lifts a friend, and casts while carrying.
- Recognition: a veteran recognises a killing pattern it has seen before. The Ledger holds the downed-by moments that make "seen before" true.
- Informed refusals (ruling 3):
  - A hero can refuse or break a mid-fight order.
  - The refusal ALWAYS shows its reason on screen: a bond, a fear or a promise, read from the hero's state and history.
  - It can be right (it saves someone) or tragically wrong.
  - It is never random noise.
  - This amends "per-ability/item Auto or Manual preferences remain authoritative" (GAME_SPEC § Combat model).
- Joy: squad sports, skill exhibitions, apprentices parodying a nemesis's pose.

COMBAT SEAM
Refusal rules live in the one simulation and draw only from its seeded RNG. The forecast must predict refusals exactly as a real run would (boundary #4). A refusal is a moment in the battle record.

DEPENDS
Step 2 (bonds). The ig-gy0 epic (skills).

OPEN (game-designer)
- Refusal frequency and triggers (PROVISIONAL).
- How the player can see a refusal coming.
- Whether a refusal can be overridden, and what that costs.
notes:
2026-09-24 game-designer, OPEN (add to the design): do refusals fire in unwatched repeat runs? A refusal that gets a hero killed while nobody watched reads as a bug, not drama. It also threatens the forecast's safe verdict unless it is fully deterministic in the one simulation. Leaning: refusals fire in watched battles only, or the forecast counts them exactly.
2026-09-24 director clarification: refusals live inside BattleSimulation and draw only seeded RNG, so the forecast stays honest either way. The unwatched-runs question is FEEL (a death nobody saw reads as a bug), not determinism. This supersedes the forecast worry in the note above.
2026-09-24 DIRECTION v2 (final; GAME_SPEC § Direction). Adds to the body above; where it says SUPERSEDES, v2 wins.
V2 STEP 3 LIST: skill eligibility, commitments, reservations, shared technique triggers, Concordance, carrying, recognition and the piloted lens.
- The six personal rules (GAME_SPEC § 6): Trust, Missing beat, Recognition, Commitment, Parliament, Legend. Parliament needs step 6's souls and Legend needs step 4's belief. This step builds the eligibility rule they plug into, not those powers.
- Commitment: a hero rejects an action before spending its cooldown and pursues a stated alternative. Same ruling 3; the body's refusal rules still hold.
- Private techniques [r8]: one can emerge when a deepest commitment is threatened. It fires at the hero's next legal action, respecting cooldowns and the ability lock, and may protect the person you ordered attacked. Witnessing grants knowledge; teaching needs its owner's agreement.
- Rescue [r9]: a persistent objective, reevaluated at each step (separate, reach, lift through the existing carry, extract), never queued blindly. Carrying allows compatible spells and moves; skills that need free hands mean setting the person down. Casting cannot bypass the lift channel.

CONCORDANCE (§ 4; architecture note 6): the sacrifice x3 stays, but it gates on a technique two distinct heroes have practised together, not the same def_id. Kinship can help; rivals can qualify. SYSTEMS § Dupes and resonance carries the Amended line. Open for game-designer: what triggers resonance once the x3 leaves def_id (ig-m6o.4 OPEN).

A2 ITEM ON THIS STEP:
- Offers and responses [r8]. Before a relevant command, a hero states their condition ("I'll cross if Mira covers me"), and the ribbon joins the people and actions involved. Show who waits at whose door, who leaves a seat open, who accepts help. Another hero can visibly contest the piloted hero's reading of the field with a concrete objection; switching lens shows the difference without briefing either hero. Needs step 2's knowledge.

FLAG (sequencing, for the director): v2's Recognition rule is "nemeses predict familiar openings from experience". Across battles that needs a persistent enemy id, and architecture note 1 puts that in the nemesis step (ig-m6o.7). Within one battle it does not. Decide at scoping: either step 3's recognition is within one battle (plus heroes recognising patterns from the Ledger, as the body says), or enemy ids move up to this step.

POINTERS: Held the Bridge's legend skill (ig-m6o.4) and the battlefield band (ig-m6o.5) ride on this step's eligibility rules.
2026-09-24 director ruling (answers the FLAG above; GAME_SPEC § 10): step 3's Recognition works within one battle only. A nemesis or veteran can predict openings it saw earlier in the same fight. Recognition across battles needs persistent enemy ids, and it lands with ig-m6o.7 (architecture note 1). Heroes recognising patterns from the Ledger's downed-by moments (the body's Recognition line) is not affected: heroes already have stable ids. Don't add enemy ids at this step.

title: Town look + camera: pan/zoom over the hex map, grass tint, real hall models
description:
WHY
From the ig-6m2.1 screenshot (.agent-results/ig-6m2.1/town.png). The town is now a 217-hex map (town_map_radius 8, 48 m to the farthest hex centre), but the overview camera is fixed at the centre and cannot pan, so most of the map is out of reach. The grass tiles read lime-yellow. The seven halls are still grey 3 m boxes next to real House and Lumbermill models. The Lumbermill's crane hides its own label.
View only: no save key, no number in SYSTEMS, no rule change. Every model already sits in hub/town/models/hexagon/ (staged by ig-wgj.3 from the owner-approved KayKit Medieval Hexagon Pack). Nothing is downloaded.

SPLIT (2026-09-24). Two slices, one implementer pass each, in either order. The parent closes when both close.
- ig-6m2.8.1, camera and ground: overview pan and zoom clamped to the map, the grass tint, the Lumbermill label. town_view.gd plus one line of lumbermill.tscn.
- ig-6m2.8.2, hall models: each hall scene's grey box becomes its KayKit model, with its click box, label and WorkSpot fitted to it. Boundary #2 (scene↔script seam).

RULED (do not reopen)
- The hall models are wgj.6's final (level 5) models, and the Town Gate and Apothecary get the fixed ones wgj.6 item 2 asks for. So the models are chosen once: ig-wgj.6 then adds only the lower tiers (destroyed, and the ×0.75 / ×0.9 steps) on top of each scene's base scale. The Reliquary castle sits at about ×2 (the director, on ig-wgj.6).

SEQUENCING
Both slices edit files other town beads edit: town_view.gd (ig-6m2.3.2, ig-6m2.6.1, ig-wgj.6) and the hall scenes (ig-wgj.6). Don't run them at the same time as those. ig-wgj.6 waits on .8.2.

NON-GOALS
Relighting; a day/night cycle; a new camera node or scene; edge-of-screen pan; saving where the camera is; any download or new model; level tiers (ig-wgj.6); props (ig-wgj.6 item 4); the embodied hero's walk bounds (see ig-6m2.8.1 NON-GOALS).

title: Skills 10: balance pass, clear times back in the pre-skill band
description:
WHY
The v1 kits are a large buff (combos alone take sustained damage to about 1.4-1.6x basic swings). Enemy skills offset part of it. This pass puts clear time back where the pre-skill baseline measured it.
Spec: SYSTEMS.md § Skills ("What the kits cost the balance").

SCOPE
- game-designer retunes skill multipliers only: not the six stats, not zone power, not rewards.
- Target: five mixed F-rank level-1 heroes clear Verdant in 72.5-79.0 s over seeds 1 and 2 (the band restated 2026-09-24 after the facing fixes; SYSTEMS.md § Provisional shared combat numbers), and three starter Knights win Verdant bare on seeds 1-4 (today seed 2 times out).
- Class + general check (owner ruling: class plus a shared pool): a C-rank level-30 team of all five classes with full class kits runs Sundered with and without all six general skills each. With them, clear time may fall by at most 10%. Report any change in the forecast safe verdict to the director: general skills add survival, and safe means no downings, so more orders can qualify for unlimited repeats.
- Also check: the forecast safe rate on starter teams does not jump.
- Update SYSTEMS.md § Skills with measured numbers; remove the PROVISIONAL markers the measurements settle.

ACCEPTANCE
Measured clear times in the notes with the log path; BUILT + GUT green.
design:
DESIGN (extra as game-designer, 2026-09-25; checked against HEAD 3fd43c1). Pace 6. Baseline: .agent-results/ig-1jw/balance_final.log.

FINDING 1, the gate measures a kit nobody plays (a premise fix for the director)
- The balance gate script (.agent-results/ig-9gf/balance_gate.gd, whose output format balance_final.log matches) builds hero snapshots with no "level" and no "skills" key (its _starter_snapshots).
- With neither key, BattleSimulation gives the hero set_default_kit (battle_simulation.gd:1010-1011). That's the passive and the level-1 abilities only: default_kit reads kinds "passive" and "ability" (:1521-1527), so no weaponskill.
- A real order builds snapshots in _team_snapshots with "level" and "skills": Hero.bar_for(hero) (game_session.gd:1568). So a real level-1 hero also swings its starter weaponskill (Iron Cut and the rest; ability_definition.gd:102, unlock_level 1). After ig-zht, a real level-1 Knight also has Charge and Ground Slam.
- Enemies do get their weaponskills (enemy_kit reads known_kit(archetype, 1), :1532). So the gate's heroes are short a skill that their enemies have.
- What it means:
  - The el4 band (62.9–78.6 s) and the P = 6 numbers (316–356 s mixed, 555–602 s Knights) measure a default kit.
  - The owner played real kits when they said "too fast" and asked for 5–6x slower.
  - So the bead's "back in the pre-skill band" can't be checked with today's gate. The owner's 5–6x is a ratio between two real-kit runs.
- The pass therefore starts by giving the gate real kits. Everything below is measured that way.

FINDING 2, the bead's premise is mostly stale
- The kits (ig-gy0.2) and the enemy skills (ig-gy0.4, closed 4e44335, 09-24 05:44) landed before ig-9gf (68d0d49, 17:51) and ig-el4 (3330400, 19:46). el4's retune ("HP brings the mixed clear time back to the band the owner has been playing") was done with the kits in, and the owner then played it.
- So there's no known "large unmeasured buff" to take back. The pass is a measurement with real kits, plus the checks the bead names. It retunes only where a check misses, by the rules below.

1. THE GATE, GIVEN REAL KITS (measurement script, not repo code)
- A new .agent-results/ig-gy0.9/balance_gate.gd, a copy of ig-9gf's with one change: each snapshot gains "level": 1 and "skills": Hero.bar_for(hero, BALANCE). That's the same shape as _team_snapshots, so the sim reads the bar the way a real order does.
- The same eight cases (mixed = knight, ranger, mage, rogue, knight; starter_knights = 3 Knights; bare and suggested). Seeds 1–4, not 1–2: the bead asks for Knights on 1–4, and mixed gets the same seeds for free.
- Run twice at the bead's HEAD: pace 1 and pace 6. The pace-1 run passes pace = 1 to BattleSimulation.create_run (its last parameter, battle_simulation.gd:101 and :113; every ×P reads the battle's own pace). balance.tres is never edited, and nothing else sees P = 1.
- Also run ig-9gf's default-kit gate at the same HEAD at P = 6, so the drift since balance_final.log (ig-zht, ig-vl1.3-.5, ig-85w and the rest land before this bead) is separated from the kit change.
- Logs: .agent-results/ig-gy0.9/gate_default_p6.log, gate_real_p1.log, gate_real_p6.log.

2. THE CHECKS (targets at P = 6)
a) Pace ratio, mixed, per case: real-kit P6 time / real-kit P1 time on the same seed is 4.7–6x. 4.7 is the floor the director accepted at ig-1jw; 6 is the owner's top.
b) Mixed band: every real-kit P6 mixed case wins, with no supplied case gaining a downing over the default-kit P6 run.
c) Knights: all 8 Knights runs (bare and suggested, seeds 1–4) win with real kits at P6, under the 1,080 s bound.
d) General skills (the owner's class-plus-pool ruling):
   - a C-rank level-30 team, one of each archetype (knight, ranger, mage, rogue, cleric);
   - each hero knows every skill of its archetype, level and book-only alike (book-only ones through learned_skills);
   - run at sundered_vault, seeds 1–4, real kits, P6, without and with all six general skills in every hero's learned_skills;
   - pass: the median clear time with them is at most 10% under the median without them;
   - report: each seed's forecast verdict (BattleSimulation.forecast) with and without. Any change in safe goes to the director, as the bead says.
e) Starter safe rate: the eight cases' forecast verdicts, real kits at P6, without and with the two tier-1 general skills (Catch Breath, Field Dressing) on every hero. A level-1 Training Hall can teach those to a starter team, so this is the check that means something. Pass: at most one case flips to safe. Every flip goes to the director.
f) The dodge margin (the director's pick from ig-gy0.4, ruled in this pass):
   - Slip (combat/abilities/rogue_slip.tres) and Dust Roll (general_tumble.tres, :19) go from a 1.0 s dodge status to 1.2 s;
   - SYSTEMS § Counters' "if it resolves within 1 s" becomes 1.2 s;
   - the dodge stays in real seconds at any pace (§ Battle pace);
   - why: the AI answers after skill_reaction_delay_seconds (0.2 s), and Crushing Blow's telegraph is 1.2 s, so the blow lands exactly as a 1.0 s dodge ends. The tick expires statuses before it resolves telegraphs, so a tie means a hit. 1.2 s gives 0.2 s of margin with no change to the tick order and no golden moved by the order.

3. RETUNE RULES (only for a check that misses; skill numbers only: not the six stats, not zone power, not rewards, not battle_pace)
- a) misses: P is the lever, not skills. A skill multiplier moves P1 and P6 alike, so it barely moves the ratio. Report it to the director, with the unscaled share. That's ig-1jw's rule: try P = 7 only on the director's word.
- b) or c) misses (a loss, or a new supplied downing):
  - the log names the case and the wave, and prints the damage each hero skill dealt;
  - game-designer then proposes one change, the smallest that fixes it: one skill number, a step of 0.05 on a multiplier or 5% on a heal or guard;
  - the director rules it before any .tres edit.
  - Stop rule: after 3 proposals on the same miss, stop and rethink (the repo's stop rule).
- d) misses (more than 10% faster): the pool deals no damage by rule, so the speed comes from staying up. Cut Catch Breath's heal (20% of max HP) and Field Dressing's (1.5 ATK) together, in 5% steps, until the check passes. Each step re-runs d) and e).
- e) misses: the same heal cut as d), then re-run.
- f) is a fixed change, not a tune.

4. SYSTEMS (game-designer, in the same commit as the .tres changes)
- § What the kits cost the balance: the measured numbers (a–e, with the log paths). Replace the PROVISIONAL at :897 with the measured result. The one kit-feel risk, the owner playing it, stays as its own PROVISIONAL.
- § Provisional shared combat numbers: one "Restated" note. The el4 band is a default-kit measurement, and the real-kit P1 and P6 numbers now stand beside it as the reference.
- § Battle pace: the real-kit ratio, beside its "Measured at P = 6" line.
- § Counters: 1.2 s.
- ig-gy0.9's own body names targets from before el4 (72.5–79.0 s, "today seed 2 times out"). That text is history. This design's checks replace it.

WHAT MOVES IN THE REPO
- At most: rogue_slip.tres and general_tumble.tres (f, always); skill .tres numbers a ruled retune names; SYSTEMS.md; and any GUT test pinned to Slip's or Dust Roll's 1.0 s.
- Digests: a retune or the dodge change can move the formation and pinned digests. That's a re-baseline in the same commit, named in the STATUS.
- The gate stays a measurement script in .agent-results/ig-gy0.9/. It isn't added to tests/unit: a full P6 run of 16 cases, twice, is minutes.

BOUNDARIES

- #1, #2 and #3 are untouched.

title: Skills 8: skill books and Training Hall teaching
description:
WHY
The owner ruled skills are also learned from skill books and the Training Hall.
Spec: GAME_SPEC.md § Skills ("Learning"). SYSTEMS.md § Skills (Learning, drop and teach rows). DECISIONS.md "2026-09-23: Skills" items 3, 11.

BEHAVIOR
1. Books: an extra roll in Expedition.roll_loot's settlement (hub/expedition/expedition.gd) at skill_book_drop_chance per clear (a ZoneDefinition value). It never replaces a stone, part or Essence reward. skill_book_general_share (0.5) of drops are general books, one general skill picked uniformly. The rest are class books for a class book-only skill, class weighted by the roster's archetypes. GameSession.skill_books {skill_id: count}, additive key.
2. Using a book: a GameSession mutator teaches it, adds it to learned_skills, spends the book. A class book needs a hero of its class. A general book needs any hero at or above the skill's tier minimum level (1 / 10 / 20), whatever the hall level. Refused if the hero already knows it. Never another class's skill (owner ruling 2026-09-23).
3. Training Hall teaching, class: a class skill with unlock_level <= hero.level + training_hall_teach_levels_per_level * hall level, for training_hall_teach_parts_per_unlock_level * unlock_level F parts. Never a class book-only skill.
4. Training Hall teaching, general: a general skill whose tier <= hall level and whose minimum level <= hero.level, for training_hall_general_parts[tier] F parts (20 / 40 / 80).
Both add to learned_skills.
5. UI: books in the inventory with a Teach button; a Teach tab in the Training Hall panel with Class and General lists.

ACCEPTANCE
- Spine test: summon stones, parts and Essence from a fixed-seed clear are identical with and without the book roll; compute_essence_yield of a hero is identical before and after it learns skills.
- Disk round-trip of skill_books and learned_skills (boundary #1).
- Tests for every refusal (wrong class, already known, hall too low, hero below a general tier's minimum level, not enough parts, a class book-only skill at the hall, another class's skill).
- About half the book drops over a fixed-seed sample of clears are general.
- BUILT + GUT green. Verifier pass (boundary #1).

NOTE
Touches GameSession save keys and hub panels. Never beside the town lane's save work.
design:
DESIGN (extra, 2026-09-25; checked against 858b45d. game_session.gd and hub.gd refs are HEAD's: high1's uncommitted WIP shifts them). Rules: GAME_SPEC § Skills, "Learning skills"; SYSTEMS § Skills (the rows at :590-594, the tier table at :695-701, the book and class-weight text at :703-714, the level-0 amendment at :677-679); DECISIONS 2026-09-23 Skills, items 3 and 11. The notes' two rulings are folded in: one level helper, and Field Dressing's "ready with a valid target".

FINDINGS (director's call)
- Book drop chance exists for three zones, but there are five. SYSTEMS :590 gives Verdant / Ashfall / Sundered only. Fallen Citadel and Frontier March came later, so a new ZoneDefinition field would default them to 0: no books from the two hardest zones. My pick: 0.08 and 0.10, continuing the +0.02 steps, PROVISIONAL, and game-designer adds them to the row.
- The UI: the bead asks for books in the inventory with a Teach button, plus a Teach tab in the Training Hall. My pick: one learning surface, the hero's SkillPanel (hub/skill_panel.gd). It already lists the locked class skills (:66-73), so they gain a Teach button. The inventory shows book counts only. Why: every book and every lesson needs a hero, so hero-first skips a picker. It's one place to test, and it doesn't touch hub.tscn. The Training Hall panel already shows SelectedHeroPanel (hub.gd:14), whose Skills button (:245) opens it. If you want the bead's layout as written, say so; the mutators below don't change.
- Learning while away: set_skill_bar allows a busy hero (game_session.gd:1129-1147), and equip refuses one. My pick is to allow it, like the bar: the dispatch snapshot is fixed (ADR item 4), so a battle in flight is unchanged.

1. ONE LEVEL HELPER (director ruling, 2026-09-24)
- Hero.skill_level(level: int) -> int: return maxi(level, 1).
- It replaces the three maxi(level, 1) calls: battle_simulation.gd:991, hero.gd:380 and skill_panel.gd:66. It is used by every new check: the general tier minimums, the hall's reach, and the book's minimum level.

2. DATA
- balance_table.gd and balance.tres, the SYSTEMS rows:
  - training_hall_teach_levels_per_level 5;
  - training_hall_teach_parts_per_unlock_level 3;
  - skill_book_general_share 0.5;
  - training_hall_general_parts [20, 40, 80];
  - general_tier_min_levels [1, 10, 20] (the tier table's minimums, as a row, rule 9).
- ZoneDefinition gets `@export var skill_book_drop_chance: float = 0.0`, set in the five zone .tres files: 0.02, 0.04, 0.06, then the finding's 0.08 and 0.10. tests/zone_definition_check.gd checks it's in [0, 1].
- The pool is read from BattleSimulation.ABILITIES. A general book is any archetype "general" skill (six today, tiers 1-3). A class book is that class's one book_only skill (five today: knight_anvilheart, ranger_hunters_focus, mage_hanging_star, rogue_deathmark, cleric_hearthcall).

3. THE DROP (hub/expedition/expedition.gd, game_session.gd)
- Expedition.roll_book(zone, balance, loot_seed, archetypes: Array[String]) -> String returns a skill id, or "".
- It uses its own RandomNumberGenerator, seeded from ("%d:book" % loot_seed).hash(). roll_loot's seed and sequence are untouched, so the item a seed drops is the same with or without books (the spine test).
- Rolls: first the drop chance; then general (skill_book_general_share); a general book picks uniformly from the pool; a class book picks its archetype uniformly from the distinct archetypes on the roster (SYSTEMS' 2026-09-24 amendment: each counts once), then that class's book_only skill.
- It's called in _settle_battle_order on a victory, right after roll_loot (:2325), with the run_seed and the roster's distinct def_ids. A hit does skill_books[id] += 1.
- The report gains an optional "book": id key. Reports are saved whole (:2718, :2823-2825), so it's additive and old reports lack it. The report text says "and a skill book: <name>".
- Legacy_v2 orders (Expedition._resolve, :100) get no book: they only resolve saves from before ig-544.

4. SAVE: GameSession.skill_books
- A Dictionary[String, int]. to_dict writes "skill_books".
- from_dict clears it, then keeps only ids that are a general skill or a book_only skill with a count that is a positive integer. Anything else is dropped with a push_warning (the ADR item 3 pattern). A save without the key loads {}.
- validate_saved_state needs no change: it has no key whitelist.
- Hero.learned_skills already saves and validates: its own class or general, known ids, no duplicates (hero.gd:371, :417-422). No hero save change.

5. THE MUTATORS (GameSession, through _commit_profile_mutation, refusing on load_blocked like set_skill_bar)
- Both share one refusal helper, _learn_refusal(hero, skill), for: not on the roster; unknown skill; another class's skill; already known (Hero.known_skills).
- use_skill_book(hero, skill_id):
  - refused with no book;
  - a class book needs a hero of that class (the shared check);
  - a general book needs Hero.skill_level(level) >= general_tier_min_levels[tier - 1], whatever the hall level.
  - On success: learned_skills.append, skill_books[id] -= 1, and the key is erased at 0.
- teach_skill(hero, skill_id), at the Training Hall, level L = building_levels[2]:
  - refused for a book_only skill;
  - class: refused when unlock_level > skill_level + teach_levels_per_level × L; costs teach_parts_per_unlock_level × unlock_level F parts;
  - general: refused when tier > L, or the hero is below the tier's minimum; costs training_hall_general_parts[tier - 1] F parts;
  - refused when parts[0] is short, with the cost in the message.
  - On success: parts[0] -= cost, and learned_skills.append.
- The Training Hall keeper adds nothing to reach: SYSTEMS :5352 gives Drill expedition XP only.
- bar_for already appends a new known skill as auto at the end, so the bar needs no change.

6. FIELD DRESSING (combat/battle/battle_simulation.gd, the notes' ig-gy0.2 nit 5)
- _class_heal_ready(actor) (:1479-1484) becomes _class_heal_ready(state, actor). A class heal counts only if it is auto, off cooldown, and _rule_aim(state, actor, heal, null, "heal") returns an ally.
- The only caller is _rule_aim's ai_no_ready_heal guard (:1424). The heal has no ai_no_ready_heal, so there's no loop.
- No hero knows Field Dressing until this bead, so the balance digests don't move.

7. THE PANEL (hub/skill_panel.gd, built in code as today)
- Locked class rows (:66-73) gain a "Teach · N F parts" button. When teach_skill would refuse, it's disabled, with the reason as its tooltip.
- A class book row for the class's book_only skill, when it isn't known: "Use book (k)", enabled with k > 0.
- A General section: each general skill not known, with its tier, a Teach button and a Use book button, each disabled with the refusal as its tooltip.
- Every button calls the mutator and shows last_action_error in _error, as _commit does. It refreshes through the hub's selected-hero refresh (hub.gd:649-653), as today.
- _refresh_inventory (hub.gd:486) gains one "Skill books: Tumble ×1, Deathmark ×2" label, built in code, when there are any.

BOUNDARIES
- #1: skill_books is a new additive profile key, and the report gains an optional key. learned_skills is unchanged in shape. A disk round-trip plus a legacy save missing both. Sol reviews it.
- #4: the Field Dressing guard is in the sim, so both resolve paths get it (quick_resolve is legacy only). Digests are unchanged, because no current hero has the skill.
- #2: the SkillPanel is built in code, so there are no .tscn edits; plus the inventory label.
- #3: untouched. Death erases learned skills, because they live on the Hero.

ORDER: it edits game_session.gd, hub.gd and battle_simulation.gd, so it runs alone in those, after high1's WIP lands. "Never beside the town lane's save work" (the bead) still holds.
notes:
From the ig-gy0.2 review (nit 5, 2026-09-24): Field Dressing's 'a class heal is ready' check counts a heal on Auto and off cooldown even when it has no valid target, so Field Dressing can hold while nobody heals. Harmless until this bead grants general skills. Before granting them, make 'ready' mean 'ready with a valid target'.
Director ruling 2026-09-24 (from the ig-gy0.2 renames): heroes start at level 0, and EVERY level check reads 0 as 1: skill unlocks (already max(level, 1) at battle_simulation.gd:864), the general tier minimums and hall reach (hero.level + 5 x hall level). Put them all behind one helper, not scattered max() calls.
STATUS (extra, 2026-09-25): design and ACC done, checked against 858b45d. Both rulings in the notes are folded in: the Hero.skill_level helper replaces the three maxi(level, 1) calls, and Field Dressing's 'ready' now needs a heal target. Three FINDINGS for the director: (1) SYSTEMS gives a book drop chance for 3 zones, but there are 5. Fallen Citadel and Frontier March would drop no books. My pick: 0.08 and 0.10, PROVISIONAL, for game-designer to add. (2) UI: my pick puts all learning in the hero's SkillPanel (Teach on the locked rows, a book row, a General section), with the inventory showing counts only. The bead asks for a Teach button in the inventory plus a Training Hall tab. The mutators are the same either way. (3) Learning while away is allowed, like set_skill_bar, because the snapshot is fixed at dispatch. Hero save needs no change: learned_skills already validates (hero.gd:417-422). The new save work is GameSession.skill_books plus an optional 'book' key on reports.
Director 2026-09-25: design + ACC ACCEPTED. Rulings on extra's three calls (the UI one is told to the owner; they can overrule):
1. Book chances for the two late zones: 0.08 (fallen_citadel) and 0.10 (frontier_march), PROVISIONAL. game-designer adds them to the SYSTEMS row (extra, wearing that hat).
2. UI: extra's pick. All learning is on the hero's SkillPanel (Teach on locked rows, a book row, a General section), reached from the Training Hall's SelectedHeroPanel as well. The inventory shows book counts only.
3. Learning while away is allowed, like set_skill_bar.
One add, from ig-1jw (lands first): pace 6 pays loot as P rolls per clear so earnings per hour hold. A skill book is loot, so roll_book follows the same rule: P rolls per victory (P from the battle's saved pace key, missing = 1), each with its own seed ("%d:book:%d" % [loot_seed, i]). Otherwise books per hour fall 6x. The spine test still holds, since roll_loot is untouched. ACC 2 add: a pace-6 victory rolls the book 6 times, and a legacy battle without pace rolls once.
STATUS (extra, 2026-09-25, as game-designer): the SYSTEMS skill_book_drop_chance row now lists 0.08 (Fallen Citadel) and 0.10 (Frontier March), under the section's PROVISIONAL. It also says 'per loot roll, so P rolls a victory', which is the director's pace-6 ruling. Uncommitted, for the director.

title: Skills 7: take control of one hero in a watched battle (click + number keys)
description:
WHY
The owner: "players can also take control basically play an mmo character." Thin first version: one hero, watched battles, click and number keys.
Spec: GAME_SPEC.md § Skills ("Take control of one hero"). DECISIONS.md "2026-09-23: Skills" item 9 (amends the 2026-09-22 "not piloting one hero" line).

BEHAVIOR
1. In a watched battle, select one allied hero and press Take Control (button + hotkey). One piloted hero at a time. Press again or pick another to switch.
2. While piloted, the simulation skips that actor's skill choice and target choice. It auto-attacks its current target. Its chains still run when the player fires a trigger.
3. Right-click ground moves; right-click an enemy targets and attacks (today's commands).
4. A hotbar for the piloted hero: its skills in bar order; keys 1-0 fire the first ten; every skill is clickable (the bar scrolls; no limit). Area skills take a ground click. Cooldowns show on the bar.
5. New command use_skill {actor_id, skill_id, target_id or point}, validated like today's commands (life, range, cooldown, ability lock, silence).
6. Piloted is view state, like tactical pause: cleared on leaving the view and on reload, never saved in the checkpoint, never set in an unwatched run or a forecast.

ACCEPTANCE
- Tests: a piloted actor makes no automatic skill or target choice; use_skill is refused out of range, on cooldown, inside the ability lock and while silenced; a checkpoint saved while piloting has no piloted flag; closing the view returns the hero to AI.
- A played check by the director: take a Knight, stun a Crushing Blow by hand.
- Editable text fields still suppress battle hotkeys.
- BUILT + GUT green. Verifier pass (boundaries #2, #4).

NON-GOALS
WASD, tab-targeting, camera follow, bar pages, rebinding (ig-gy0.8). Owner ruling 2026-09-23: click + number keys first.
design:
DESIGN (extra, 2026-09-25; checked against 7a758ae). Rules: DECISIONS 2026-09-23 Skills item 9; SYSTEMS § Hero AI on auto, the "A piloted hero is not on auto" block; the director's 09-24 ruling that Off skills can be fired by hand. This note is where each rule goes in the code. It comes after ig-gy0.5, because it calls _start_chain.

FINDINGS
- Keys 1-0 are taken. project.godot binds them to rts_squad_1..rts_squad_0, and battle_view.gd:282 selects a squad with them (test_battle_controls.gd pins it). The bead says 1-0 fire the hotbar. My pick: while a hero is piloted, the same actions fire hotbar slots 1-10, and they select squads again once piloting ends. This means no new actions, and ig-gy0.8's rebinding covers both. Director's call.
- Open, and my pick is "skip": the piloted hero's auto items (the order's auto_heal and auto_revive policies). SYSTEMS doesn't say. "Not on auto" reads as skip. The item commands still work, and the other heroes still use the supplies. If you agree, the SYSTEMS block gains that line (game-designer).

1. WHERE "PILOTED" LIVES (view state, not saved, the same as the tactical pause)
   - GameSession gets _piloted_battle_actors: Dictionary[String, String], order id to actor id. It has no save key.
   - set_battle_piloted(order_id, actor_id) sets it, and "" clears it. It follows set_battle_paused: it refuses an unknown order and notifies battle_changed.
   - It's cleared, snapshotted and restored in the same places as _paused_battle_orders: the preview sandbox (~2539-2586), the reset (~2752), and load. The view's _exit_tree clears it beside set_battle_paused(false).
   - BattleState gains piloted_id: String = "". It's not in to_dict or from_dict, the same as BattleState.zone.
   - Every live advance sets state.piloted_id from the table just before BattleSimulation.advance. Today those are the look-ahead (game_session.gd:1985) and _advance_clocks_in_memory (:2106). ig-7sn.15 may move them, so use one helper that sets it and advances, and have every live site call it.
   - Forecasts, sim jobs and unwatched runs build their own state, so theirs stays "". A reused state (ig-7sn.15's table) is set again on each advance.

2. WHAT THE SIM SKIPS FOR actor.id == state.piloted_id (each is one guard)
   - _choose_intentions: after the earlier returns (the rescue carry, the supplies retreat), skip the rest: the automatic-target handling and every ig-uu7 rule. It moves only on its direct order. When its target dies it gets no new one.
   - The counter claim pass (~1644): skip, so the claim passes to the next hero.
   - _support_actions: skip. No revive or heal band, and no auto item (the open pick above).
   - _offensive_actions: skip _auto_cast(["buff", "attack"]). ig-gy0.5's _chain_step still runs, so a chain the player started goes on, and nothing cuts in because the cut-ins were all skipped.
   - At the swing, the order is: effect_state.next_swing_skill if set, else the chain's weaponskill step, else a plain basic. Never _pick_weaponskill.
   - To everyone else it stays an ordinary squadmate: formation reference, threat ownership, cover taunt. No change there.

3. THE COMMAND: use_skill {actor_ids: [one], skill_id, target_id or point}
   - Parsed like COMMAND_ABILITY: exactly one living ally. The skill must be in its skills, in any mode (Off fires by hand). A passive is refused.
   - Ability:
     - The aim is target_id if given, else point for a ground area, else the actor itself for a self-centred skill.
     - _use_skill's checks move into _skill_refusal(state, actor, skill, target, point) -> String, returning "" or the first reason. The checks and their order stay the same: life, cooldown, lock, stun or silence, range, target, root. _use_skill calls it, so every verdict is unchanged.
     - A refusal becomes the command's error. On success, it fires with an RNG seeded from state.rng_state and written back, as _manual_abilities does. Then _start_chain(by_hand = true).
   - Weaponskill:
     - Refused when silenced, or with no living enemy target.
     - Otherwise it sets effect_state.next_swing_skill, replacing any earlier one. That's one slot for the next swing only, not a queue. The swing clears it.
     - Optional and validated when present: a weaponskill id in the actor's skills. It's erased when a snapshot is carried into the next leg, beside the chain keys.
   - The sim accepts use_skill for any living ally. Only the view limits it to the piloted hero, so the sim needs no pilot check at command time.

4. THE VIEW (battle_view.gd, built in code like today's command buttons)
   - A "Take Control" button, plus a hotkey: a new action rts_pilot, PROVISIONAL key T, rebindable in gy0.8. It pilots the one selected ally. Pressing it again ends piloting, and picking another ally and pressing it switches.
   - A hotbar for the piloted hero: its skills in bar order from the actor snapshot. The first ten are labelled 1-0. A cooldown shows from skill_cooldowns, and a weaponskill shows the swing timer. It scrolls, with no limit.
   - Firing: a unit skill aims at the current target, or waits for a click on a unit. A ground area sets a command mode that waits for a ground click, like attack-move.
   - Right-click to move or attack stays today's commands.
   - Keys keep today's editable-focus guard (_has_editable_focus).

BOUNDARIES
- #4: forecasts and unwatched runs never pilot, so both resolve paths are unchanged. With piloted_id "" every guard is off, and the balance digests are unchanged.
- #1: the pilot flag is never in a checkpoint. next_swing_skill is an optional saved key, absent in every legacy checkpoint.
- #2: the new button, hotbar and action, and the number keys' mode switch.
- #3 untouched.

ORDER: after ig-gy0.5. It edits battle_view.gd, which holds high1's uncommitted WIP, plus battle_simulation.gd, battle_actor.gd, game_session.gd and project.godot, so it runs alone in those files.
notes:
2026-09-24 extra (design pass). The rule is in SYSTEMS.md § Hero AI on auto, the "A piloted hero is not on auto (ig-gy0.6)" block after the precedence paragraph.
- A piloted hero runs none of ig-uu7's rules: no evasion, hop, stance move, cover or formation. It claims no telegraph, so the claim passes to the next hero; that's what lets the director stun a Crushing Blow by hand.
- It moves only on orders. After a target order it closes in, as the order does today. After a move order it holds. When its target dies it picks no new one.
- Earlier returns (the rescue carry, the supplies retreat) still win, as over any direct order.
- To the others it is an ordinary squadmate: it counts as the front-liner for formation and hop points, its target keeps other Knights off that threat, and its hits still give the cover taunt.
- Its chains run with no cut-ins. A hand-fired non-trigger leaves the chain running.
- Tests this implies:
  - piloted: no walk-out from a telegraph, and no claim, so the next hero with a counter claims it;
  - piloted: no hop, and no new target after a kill;
  - a back-row ally still forms up behind a piloted Knight;
  - a second Knight won't take the piloted Knight's threat.
- Open, director's call: can the hotbar fire an Off skill? GAME_SPEC § Skills says Off is "Never used", but BEHAVIOR 4 says every skill is clickable. My pick: yes. Off stops the AI, not the player's hand; the player turned it off for the AI. If you agree, GAME_SPEC's Off line gains "by the AI".
2026-09-24 director ruling (extra records it): Off skills can be fired by hand. Off stops the AI, not the player's hand, so the hotbar fires every skill whatever its mode. GAME_SPEC § Skills' Off line now reads 'Never used by the AI. You can still fire it by hand.' The owner can overrule. Test: use_skill fires an Off skill for a piloted hero, and the AI still never picks it.
STATUS (extra, 2026-09-25): done (design + ACC; checked at 7a758ae). Two director calls. (1) Keys 1-0 are already rts_squad_1..0 (battle_view.gd:282, pinned by test_battle_controls). My pick: while piloting, the same actions fire hotbar slots 1-10, and squads come back when piloting ends. (2) The piloted hero's auto items. My pick: skip ('not on auto'), and SYSTEMS gains a line. Design: the pilot lives in GameSession._piloted_battle_actors, unsaved like _paused_battle_orders. BattleState.piloted_id is unsaved and set before every live advance (one helper, since ig-7sn.15 may move the sites). There are 4 skip guards in the sim. use_skill reuses _use_skill's checks via _skill_refusal (same verdicts). A weaponskill press sets one optional next_swing_skill key. After ig-gy0.5. No engine runs, no commits.
Director 2026-09-25: design + ACC ACCEPTED. Rulings on extra's two calls (told to the owner; they can overrule):
1. Keys: extra's pick. While a hero is piloted, rts_squad_1..0 fire hotbar slots 1-10. With no pilot they select squads, as today. No new actions; ig-gy0.8's rebinding covers both.
2. Auto items: skip. A piloted hero uses no auto_heal or auto_revive item. The item commands still work, and the other heroes still use the supplies. Extra adds this line to SYSTEMS' "A piloted hero is not on auto" block.
Checked: ig-7sn.15 keeps the live pulse on the main thread and reuses BattleState from its table, so "set piloted_id before every live advance, through one helper" covers it. Engine order unchanged: after ig-gy0.5.
STATUS (extra, 2026-09-25): docs for the two rulings, uncommitted for the director. docs/SYSTEMS.md 'A piloted hero is not on auto' gains the no-auto-item line. docs/GAME_SPEC.md 'Take control of one hero' gains 'The keys fire the bar only while you control a hero; otherwise they select squads.'

title: Skills 6: chains, a trigger skill and what follows, programmed by the player
description:
WHY
The owner: "players should be able to program skill order too, as in theres one trigger skill and the player can choose what skills come after it."
Spec: GAME_SPEC.md § Skills ("Chains"). SYSTEMS.md § Skills (chain rows). DECISIONS.md "2026-09-23: Skills" items 3, 6.

BEHAVIOR
1. Hero.skill_chains: [{trigger, then: [ids]}], at most skill_chain_max_steps after the trigger. One chain per trigger skill. Validated on load (known skills only).
2. In battle: when a trigger fires (AI or player), the actor's chain state starts. The picker's "continue a chain" step fires the next skill as soon as it is ready. A step that cannot fire within skill_chain_step_timeout_seconds is skipped. Counters, revives and heals cut in (the picker order, DECISIONS.md 2026-09-23 item 7; director ruling 2026-09-24); the chain resumes after. The chain ends if its target dies or it runs out. Chain state is saved in the checkpoint.
3. A chain is an AI preference. It is not a command queue: a direct order still replaces a direct order.
4. The skill panel gains a chain editor: pick a trigger, then add, remove and reorder the skills after it.

ACCEPTANCE
- Tests: trigger -> steps fire in order; a step on cooldown past the timeout is skipped; a counter cuts in and the chain resumes; target death ends it; a Manual skill inside a chain fires as part of the chain (director ruling 2026-09-23: programming it counts as firing it by hand); an Off skill inside a chain is skipped.
- Disk round-trip of skill_chains, and of a checkpoint mid-chain (boundary #1).
- BUILT + GUT green. Verifier pass (boundaries #1, #4).

NOTE
Touches heroes/hero.gd save keys. Never beside ig-wgj.13, ig-6m2.x save work or ig-gy0.7.
design:
DESIGN (extra, 2026-09-25; checked against 7a758ae). Rules: SYSTEMS § Skills "Chains (ig-gy0.5)"; DECISIONS 2026-09-23 Skills items 3-7. This note is where each rule goes in the code.

WHAT'S THERE
- Hero.skill_chains is saved, and the load checks it: known skills, a non-empty "then" (hero.gd:422-428).
- The team snapshot carries "chains" (game_session.gd:1493). But _actor_from_team_snapshot reads only "skills" (battle_simulation.gd:976). BattleActor has no chains field, so nothing in the sim reads a chain yet.
- Findings:
  - balance.tres and balance_table.gd have NEITHER chain row. skill_chain_step_timeout_seconds is missing too, not only the max-steps row the gy0.3 note named.
  - The load accepts the passive as a trigger or step, and it accepts two chains with the same trigger. SYSTEMS forbids both.
  - GAME_SPEC's cut-in sentence now names heal. The 2026-09-24 finding is settled.

1. BALANCE. Add skill_chain_step_timeout_seconds = 3.0 and skill_chain_max_steps = 8 to balance_table.gd and balance.tres, as SYSTEMS has them. Both stay under the section's PROVISIONAL. One helper turns the timeout into ticks: ceili(seconds / battle_tick_seconds - TICK_EPSILON), which is 30.

2. HERO (boundary #1, no new key). _read_skills gets three load rules:
   - A chain whose trigger or step is the passive is dropped.
   - A second chain on the same trigger is dropped.
   - A chain over the cap is cut to it.
   Each gets its own push_warning. GameSession.set_skill_chains(hero, chains) is a transaction copied from set_skill_bar. It refuses the same things as the load, and it refuses an over-long chain instead of cutting it. It is fixed at dispatch like the bar (ADR item 4), so an edit applies from the next leg.

3. ACTOR (boundary #1, the checkpoint).
   - BattleActor.chains holds [{trigger, then}], read from the snapshot's "chains". A step whose skill isn't in the actor's skills is kept, and skipped when reached.
   - to_dict writes "chains" only when there are some, so no pinned checkpoint changes. validate_dict checks it only when present: an array of {trigger: String, then: Array of String}, every id a known non-passive skill.
   - Chain state is the four optional effect_state keys SYSTEMS names: chain_trigger, chain_step, chain_deadline_tick, chain_target. The rule is all four or none. chain_trigger must name one of the actor's chains, and chain_step must be under that chain's "then" size.
   - Not in the tick-bound check (battle_simulation.gd:384): a deadline is ahead of the tick by design.
   - A snapshot carried into the next leg erases the four keys (beside hit_from, :121-127), because ticks restart at 0.
   - SIMULATION_VERSION stays 1.

4. START (_start_chain(state, actor, skill, by_hand)).
   - It starts a chain when the actor has a chain for this skill, and either none is running or by_hand.
   - It sets chain_step 0, chain_deadline_tick = tick + timeout ticks, and chain_target = order_target_id.
   - Called with by_hand false from _spend_ability, which every ability passes through: picker, counter, heal band. It's also called from _use_weaponskill after the weaponskill lands.
   - Called with by_hand true from _manual_abilities after its cast lands. ig-gy0.6's number keys will call the same thing.
   - A step never starts a chain. The chain is still running while its step fires, and it advances only after.

5. STEP (the chain band, DECISIONS item 7: counter, revive, heal, CHAIN, buff, attack). Counters and the support pass run earlier in the tick, so they cut in with no new code. A cut-in takes the ability lock, the step waits, and the deadline runs.
   - In _offensive_actions, just before _auto_cast(["buff", "attack"]), _chain_step returns FIRED, WAITING or NONE. FIRED: continue. WAITING: skip that _auto_cast, but still swing. NONE: today's path.
   - _chain_step goes through these, in order:
     1. End the chain if the actor isn't alive. If chain_target is set, also end it when that actor is dead or gone, or when the actor's order_target_id is no longer it. An empty chain_target adopts the first target the hero gets.
     2. If tick > chain_deadline_tick, skip the step: next step, and a new deadline from this tick. So a chain that skips every step lasts 8 × 3.0 s at most, as SYSTEMS says.
     3. An Off step, or a skill the actor lacks, is skipped at once, in the same loop.
     4. An ability step goes through _use_skill, which is the hand-fire check (cooldown, lock, stun, silence, range, target). Manual mode fires, and the "AI uses it when" cell is ignored. The aim:
        - an enemy skill aims at chain_target;
        - self-centred aims at self;
        - a heal or shield aims at the lowest-HP living ally in range;
        - a ground area aims at the target's position.
        On success, advance the step and return FIRED; otherwise return WAITING.
     5. A weaponskill step: at the swing, the swing uses it instead of _pick_weaponskill if its target is chain_target, then advances. The combo bonus applies as usual.
   - The step after the last ends the chain, and it erases the four keys. The chain also ends on a replacing hand trigger (4) or when the hero is downed (1).
   - Enemies have no chains (ADR item 7), so nothing is spent on them.

6. EDITOR (hub/skill_panel.gd, which is built in code, so no .tscn).
   - Under the bar: a Chains section, one block per chain, with a trigger OptionButton of the hero's known non-passive skills. Its step rows have a skill OptionButton, Up, Down and Remove, like the bar rows. Then "Add step" (disabled at the cap) and "New chain" (disabled when every skill already triggers one).
   - Every change goes through GameSession.set_skill_chains, and its error shows in _error.
   - Node names follow the bar: Chain_<trigger>, Step_<i>.

BOUNDARIES
- #1: the hero key already exists, with the new load rules, plus the actor's "chains" and four chain keys, all optional. A legacy checkpoint and a legacy hero load as no chain.
- #4: both resolve paths run the same sim. With no chains, every battle is today's, so the balance digests are unchanged. A seeded chain battle is deterministic.
- #2: the panel's new rows, in code.
- #3 untouched.

ORDER: it edits hero.gd and game_session.gd, so never beside ig-wgj.13, ig-6m2.x or ig-gy0.7 (the bead's note). It also edits battle_simulation.gd, so don't run it beside ig-zht (Charge) or high1's uncommitted combat/battle work. ig-gy0.6 comes after it, and calls _start_chain(by_hand).

title: Town jobs are professions: woodcutting earns XP and a skill bonus (mining, farming as they land)
description:
WHY
The owner ruled (2026-09-23) that the new town jobs are professions too, under the multi-passion system. A worker should get better at its job, and a hero with a woodcutting passion should be the one you want at the Lumbermill.
Design: GAME_SPEC.md § The town builder ("Job skills"). Numbers: SYSTEMS.md § Keepers and professions ("Workers"). All PROVISIONAL.

BEHAVIOR
1. A worker at a placed workplace earns XP in that workplace's profession (Lumbermill -> woodcutting; Mine and Farm once they exist), on the live tick only, only while home, x passion_xp_multiplier for a passion. Same XP scale as keepers.
2. Output: base_rate * (1 + worker_skill_bonus_per_level * skill). worker_skill_bonus_per_level = 0.10 in balance.tres.
3. The workplace panel shows each worker's skill and whether it has the passion. The assign list sorts passion heroes first.
4. The town script maps workplace type -> profession. No new save keys: profession_xp already holds any profession id.

ACCEPTANCE
- Tests: a home Lumbermill worker earns woodcutting XP (x4 with the passion); an away worker earns none; an offline catch-up grants none; a skill-5 worker makes x1.5 wood.
- A real disk round-trip keeps woodcutting XP.
- BUILT + GUT green. Verifier pass (boundary #1).

NON-GOALS
Masterwork for the town jobs (none: GAME_SPEC.md says skill bonus only); mining and farming buildings (ig-6m2.3.1 adds the Mine, ig-6m2.5.1 the Farm). Whichever lands second adds the map row: if a slice has landed, this bead maps its type; if this bead lands first, that slice adds its one row.
design:
DESIGN (extra, 2026-09-25; checked against 858b45d. game_session.gd and hub.gd refs are HEAD's: high1's uncommitted WIP shifts them). Rules: GAME_SPEC § The town builder, "Job skills"; SYSTEMS § Keepers and professions, "Workers" and "Starving and skill". The Mine (ig-6m2.3.1) and the Farm (ig-6m2.5.1) have both landed, so this bead maps all three types, and the NON-GOALS "whichever lands second" clause is settled.

WHAT'S THERE
- The professions already exist: Hero.ALL_PROFESSIONS (hero.gd:23) holds woodcutting, mining and farming, passions roll over all eight, and Hero.from_dict keeps profession_xp for any of them (:468). No save work.
- Hero.PROFESSIONS (:26) is halls only, and station validation reads it. Leave it alone.
- XP: _working_keepers (game_session.gd:843) feeds Hero.add_profession_xp on the live tick (:2148-2149). The offline catch-up (_advance_orders_in_memory :2078) never calls it.
- Output counts heads: _workers_home(type) -> int (:1002) goes into TownRules.wood_made / stone_made / food_made (town_rules.gd:175-187) and starve_step (:217).

1. THE MAP (hub/town/town_rules.gd)
   const JOB_PROFESSIONS: Dictionary[StringName, StringName] = {LUMBERMILL: &"woodcutting", MINE: &"mining", FARM: &"farming"}
   static func worker_work(hero: Hero, type: StringName, balance: BalanceTable) -> float:
       return 1.0 + balance.worker_skill_bonus_per_level * Hero.profession_skill(hero, JOB_PROFESSIONS[type], balance)
   worker_work is the one copy of the SYSTEMS formula. The live tick and the panel both sum it.

2. OUTPUT: heads become work
- _workers_home(type) -> int becomes _work_home(type) -> float: the sum of worker_work over that type's workers who aren't busy. Every home worker adds at least 1.0, so the periodic-save gate (:316, `... > 0`) reads the same.
- The first parameter of wood_made, stone_made, food_made and starve_step becomes `work: float` (it was workers_home / farm_workers: int). The formulas are unchanged. Tests that pass ints still work (int → float converts).
- Starving stays a multiply after it (work_multiplier), so the SYSTEMS order base × (1 + 0.10 × skill) × 0.5 holds.
- The call sites all switch to _work_home: the live tick (:2121, :2122, :2130) and the starve-death look-ahead (:2007-2008). The look-ahead must pass the same farm work as the live tick, or it decides a death the tick doesn't bring.

3. XP
- _working_keepers also returns [worker, JOB_PROFESSIONS[type]] for each hero whose station is a placed workplace (TownRules.type_of(hero.station) in JOB_PROFESSIONS) and who isn't busy. Its doc line becomes "every home keeper and worker".
- Nothing else changes. add_profession_xp already applies the ×4 passion rate, and the offline catch-up already skips it.
- A workplace under construction has no workers (station_hero refuses at :765), so it earns nothing.

4. THE PANEL (hub.gd)
- _refresh_placed_panel (:1141-1170): each worker's name gains its skill here and a passion mark: "Ada (Woodcutting 3, passion)", or "Ada (Woodcutting 3) · Away". The "Makes … a minute" figure sums TownRules.worker_work over the home workers instead of counting heads, so it shows what the tick pays. A House is unchanged.
- _on_placed_assign_pressed (:1182-1195): for a workplace, the rows gain the same "— Woodcutting 3 · passion" text as the keeper picker (:1300-1305). Passion heroes come first, then the rest, each in roster order (a stable sort). A House's picker is unchanged.
- It already refreshes on the live tick (test_town_builder.gd:470), so a skill-up shows without a new hook.

5. BALANCE: worker_skill_bonus_per_level = 0.10 in balance_table.gd and balance.tres. It's under the existing SYSTEMS PROVISIONAL at :5371. No other number.

WHAT MOVES
- The panel-text tests that pin "Workers n/m: A, B" gain the skill text: test_town_builder.gd:589, test_town_food.gd:181, test_town_stone.gd:137 and :139. At skill 0 the rates stay 1.0, 0.5 and 1.0 a minute.

ORDER: it edits game_session.gd and hub.gd, which both hold high1's uncommitted WIP, so it waits for that to land. It doesn't touch town_view.gd or the building scenes, so it can go beside ig-6m2.8.2.

BOUNDARIES
- #1: no new key. profession_xp already round-trips every ALL_PROFESSIONS id. A disk round-trip test covers the new ids.
- #2: the panel label and picker text only; no node changes.
- #3: starvation's victim and clock rules are untouched; only the food made changes.
- #4 untouched.
notes:
2026-09-23 game-designer: nothing open.
- Starving (ig-6m2.5) multiplies the final rate after the skill bonus: base * (1 + 0.10*skill) * 0.5.
- A workplace under construction (ig-6m2.3) earns no XP; it has no workers.
- The needs-owner label is removed: the passions ruling (ig-wgj.13) landed.
STATUS (extra, 2026-09-25): design and ACC done, checked against 858b45d. The Mine and the Farm have both landed, so this maps all three jobs (woodcutting, mining, farming). No save work: the professions and their XP keys already exist (hero.gd:23, :468). The one catch I found: the starve-death look-ahead (game_session.gd:2007-2008) counts farmers separately from the live tick, so both must use the same new work sum, or a skilled farmer's food would be left out of the death check (ACC 3). It waits for high1's WIP in game_session.gd and hub.gd to land. No doc edit is needed: SYSTEMS already has the formula and the starving order.
Director 2026-09-25: design + ACC ACCEPTED. The starve look-ahead catch (ACC 3) is the key part. high1's WIP noted in the design has landed (ig-7sn.14, 5334a79), so re-check the game_session.gd and hub.gd line refs at build time. Engine order unchanged.

title: Town builder 6: heroes walk home and to work (replaces ambient wandering)
description:
WHY
The town should look like it works. Heroes in town walk from their House to their job, work there, and walk back. Heroes with no job wander. This covers ig-wgj.7 (keepers stand and work) and replaces ig-wgj.5 (ambient wandering, written for the fixed layout).
Design: GAME_SPEC.md § The town hub ("The town looks alive") and § The town builder. ARCHITECTURE.md § The town is the interface ("Ambient heroes are views onto the roster", "Presentation numbers stay in the view scripts"). DECISIONS.md 2026-09-23 "The town is the interface" (rejected: saving ambient hero positions).

SPLIT (tech-lead, 2026-09-24)
Two slices, in order, one implementer pass each. This parent closes when both close. ig-m6o.2.2 waits on it.
- ig-6m2.6.1, the town works: the hex walk graph, the walker figure, keepers and workers walking House → work spot → House, heroes coming and going, the work clips.
- ig-6m2.6.2, the town lives: heroes with no job wander, the bond partner becomes an ordinary walker (no fixed spot), a click on a walker opens that hero, the wanderer cap with an FPS measurement.

RULES BOTH SLICES KEEP (already ruled)
- Walking is cosmetic (game-designer, 2026-09-23, notes). Production, profession XP and eating never wait for a walk. They follow the saved state (home, station, busy) exactly as ig-6m2.1, .5 and .7 do.
- Nothing is saved: no to_dict/from_dict key, no SaveService change, no GameSession field. Positions and activities are derived and reset on every load.
- TownView never reads GameSession. hub.gd decides who is in town and hands TownView the Hero objects. The view reads hero.station and hero.home, as show_partner already reads hero.home.
- Terms: "in town" = on the roster, not is_hero_busy(), and not the body. "House" = hero.home (GAME_SPEC's "home" means in town).
- Work spots are the WorkSpot Marker3D in each building scene (ig-6m2.2). A House's WorkSpot is its door.
- The work clips come from Rig_Medium_Tools and Rig_Medium_Simulation, staged by ig-wgj.3.
- Presentation numbers are constants in the view scripts, not balance.tres rows (ARCHITECTURE § The town is the interface; rule 9): walk speed, how long a hero works, rests or lingers, the wanderer cap, the clip table.
- Cosmetic randomness uses each walker's own RandomNumberGenerator, seeded from its hero's instance_id. Never the global randi()/randf(): summoning in hub.gd draws from the global RNG, so a view that drew from it would change what the player pulls.

THE WALKABLE AREA (tech-lead ruling, 2026-09-24)
Buildings fill whole hexes, one per hex (TownRules.hex_refusal). A hex is 6 m across the flats, and the biggest building box is 4.5 m. So a hex with no building is open ground, and the walkable area is the hex grid itself.
- TownView keeps an AStar2D (built into Godot) over TownRules.map_hexes: one point per hex centre, joined to its six neighbours. A hex with a building is disabled. show_buildings updates the graph when the set of occupied hexes changes, which is exactly a place or a move.
- A route = start → the centres of the free hexes on the path → end. A segment between two adjacent hex centres stays inside those two hexes, so it never crosses a building (the nearest box edge stays over 1.5 m away).
- A walker enters and leaves a building only through its approach hexes: the building's two neighbours nearest its WorkSpot (with today's markers, the two +z hexes). The last leg, approach-hex centre → WorkSpot, stays clear of the box: the spot sits at local z 2.5 (halls) or 2.8 (House, Lumbermill), and the boxes end at 1.5 and 2.25.
- Free ground = the centre of a map hex with no building. free_point(near) = the free hex centre nearest near. Ties go to the earlier hex in map_hexes order.
- REJECTED: a NavigationRegion3D baked at runtime (an async bake and a new seam, for a grid we already have); steering around boxes with collision (walkers wedge in gaps, and nothing proves they never cut through).

NON-GOALS (both slices)
Schedules, day/night, sleeping animations. Anything saved. Navmesh. Walkers avoiding each other or the body (they may overlap). Walking out to the gate when dispatched (a sent hero just leaves). Summons walking out of the Summoning Circle (they come in through the gate). Pathing for the body's click walk (it stays straight, with its stuck timer). Dialogue beyond the partner's line. Townsfolk who are not on the roster.

FOUND WHILE SCOPING (in neither slice; file separately if wanted)
The body's walk bounds are a fixed square (TownView.WALK_HALF_EXTENT = 23.6 m), but the map has radius 8 (hex (5, 0) is 30 m out). The body cannot reach a building placed that far out: a click on it still opens through the stuck timer, but the body stops at the edge, and a partner standing out there can't be met.
notes:
2026-09-23 game-designer: walking is cosmetic.
- Production, profession XP and eating never wait for a hero to reach its building or its house.

- The needs-owner label is removed.

That is inside hex (1, 0), the Sanctum's default hex, 0.5 m outside the Sanctum's box. Buildings can move now, and nothing checks that spot, so a House moved onto (1, 0) would swallow the partner. When the partner becomes its ambient hero here, place it by the same free-ground rule as everyone else and drop the fixed spot.
2026-09-24 (6m2.8 scoping): ig-6m2.8.2 moves every hall's WorkSpot from z 2.5 to 2.8 and grows its Pick box from 3 m to 4.5 m, like the House and Lumbermill. The rule in the Rules section (spot outside the box grown by 0.3 m) still holds; only the numbers in that line go stale once .8.2 lands. .8.2 re-runs .6.1's route test if .6.1 is in.

title: Town builder 3: stone, and buildings that take time to go up
description:
WHY
Banished's pull is that building costs material and time. This slice adds the second resource, stone, which pays for hall upgrades (ig-6m2.4). It also makes new buildings take live-play time to go up.
Design: GAME_SPEC.md § The town builder. Numbers and rules: SYSTEMS.md § Town builder, "Stone and construction" and "The first of each producer is free" (game-designer ruling 2026-09-23, see the notes; deadlock check 2026-09-24).

RULED (do not reopen)
- One resource, one job. Houses and workplaces cost wood only. Stone pays only for hall upgrades. There is no town_start_stone. This overrides the first scope line, "houses and workplaces cost wood and stone": a stone House needs a Mine, whose workers need Houses, so a fresh town would deadlock.
- The first of each producer is free, and so is the first House (deadlock check, 2026-09-24): from 40 wood, a free Lumbermill plus two more at 20 left 0 wood and no House, with no way back.
- One meaning per model. building_scaffolding and building_stage_A/B/C mean construction only. building_destroyed means a level-0 hall. ig-wgj.6 already carries its new mapping, and this scoping leaves it unchanged.
- Live play only. Stone and build time move in _advance_clocks_in_memory, never in the offline catch-up.
- Halls are never under construction. Hall upgrades stay instant.

SPLIT (tech-lead, 2026-09-24)
Two slices, in order, one implementer pass each. Both touch the save, so both get a boundary #1 review. The parent closes when both close.
- ig-6m2.3.1, Mine and stone: the Mine, stone as a saved resource, the free first House. It unblocks ig-6m2.4, which needs stone but not construction.
- ig-6m2.3.2, construction time: build_remaining, the stage models, and a building under construction does nothing.

ASSETS (no download)
building_mine_blue, building_scaffolding and building_stage_A are in the owner-approved KayKit Medieval Hexagon Pack 1.0 FREE (ig-wgj.3 notes). It is already unzipped at C:\Users\Joony\AppData\Local\Temp\kaykit\town\KayKit_Medieval_Hexagon_Pack_1.0_FREE\Assets\gltf\buildings\ (blue\ and neutral\).
- Copy each .gltf and its .bin flat into hub/town/models/hexagon/.
- They use the hexagons_medieval.png that is already staged.
- If that Temp folder is gone, stop and ask the director: fetching it again is a download.

NON-GOALS
builder jobs (construction just takes time); hauling; food and the Farm (ig-6m2.5); mining XP and skill (ig-6m2.7); hall upgrade costs (ig-6m2.4); demolishing, cancelling or refunding a building; stone costs on anything but hall upgrades; a price or build time for moving.
notes:
2026-09-23 game-designer RULING: the numbers and design calls are set (SYSTEMS.md § Town builder, "Stone and construction"). The tech-lead can finish the body from this.

NUMBERS (balance.tres, PROVISIONAL)
- mine_wood_cost 20
- mine_worker_slots 2
- stone_per_worker_minute 0.5
- house_build_seconds 60
- workplace_build_seconds 120 (Lumbermill, Mine, Farm)

CALLS
1. One resource, one job. Houses and workplaces cost WOOD ONLY. Stone pays only for hall upgrades (ig-6m2.4).
   - This overrides this bead's scope line "houses and workplaces cost wood and stone".
   - Why: a House that costs stone needs a Mine first, and the Mine's workers need Houses, so a fresh town would deadlock without start stone.
   - There is no town_start_stone.
2. The Mine is building_mine_blue from the approved pack, already on disk. Stage it with building_scaffolding and building_stage_A. Those two are not staged yet; stage_B, stage_C and destroyed already are. No new download.
3. The first of each producer is free (SYSTEMS § "The first of each producer is free"). If ig-6m2.1 did not already carry it, it lands here, for the Lumbermill, the Mine and the Farm type key.
4. Construction:
   - A new building shows scaffolding, then stage_A, stage_B and stage_C, a quarter of its build time each, then its own model.
   - Until finished it does nothing. assign_home and station_hero refuse it with a reason, and so do their previews.
   - Its hex is taken. move_building works on it and keeps its progress.
   - It counts as "having one" for the free rule.
5. Saved as the additive key build_remaining (seconds) on the building dict. A missing key means finished, so every ig-6m2.1/.2 building loads finished.
6. Build time moves only in _advance_clocks_in_memory. The offline catch-up moves it 0.
7. The halls are never under construction. Hall upgrades stay instant.
8. One meaning per model: scaffolding and stage_A/B/C mean construction only; destroyed means a level-0 hall. ig-wgj.6 has its new mapping.

ACCEPTANCE ADDS
- A half-built building survives a real disk save and reload with its build_remaining.
- An old save loads with every building finished.
- A building under construction refuses a resident and a worker.
- Build time moves on the live tick at 1 s per s, and 0 across an offline catch-up of any length.
- Free rule: with none, 0; with one under construction, full price; preview equals result.
- A Mine worker makes stone at the table rate only while home.
The needs-owner label is removed.
