title: Town builder 4: hall upgrades also cost wood and stone
description:
WHY
The town has to feed the hero game, or it is a side game. The link is the halls: upgrading the Circle, Forge, Training Hall, Sanctum or Reliquary now also costs wood and stone, on top of today's parts.
Design: GAME_SPEC.md § The town builder ("What the town makes, and what it pays for"). Numbers: SYSTEMS.md § Town builder, "Hall upgrades cost wood and stone" (game-designer ruling 2026-09-23, see the notes; PROVISIONAL until played).

RULED (do not reopen)
- Going from level n to n+1 costs 20·(n+1) wood and 10·(n+1) stone, on top of the unchanged 10·(n+2) rank-n parts. n is the current level. A hall costs 300 wood and 150 stone in total.
- The parts cost stays. It is calibrated against the spine (264 clears to max one hall).
- Levels already reached stay. Nothing is refunded or charged again.
- This applies only to the five halls with levels. The Apothecary and the Town Gate have none.
- Upgrades stay instant: halls are never under construction.
- This changes today's game on purpose: a player with no Mine cannot upgrade a hall.

BEHAVIOR
1. The plan. _building_upgrade_plan also takes the town's wood and stone, and returns wood_cost and stone_cost next to part_rank and part_cost. Both are computed there, next to the parts formula, from two new rows. No other file derives a cost.
2. It is valid only when parts, wood and stone are all enough. The error names every resource that is short, and only those: "Need 30 D parts (have 12) and 20 stone (have 0)."
3. upgrade_building spends all three, or nothing.
4. preview_building_upgrade passes GameSession.town_resources. upgrade_building builds the same plan, so the preview equals the result.
5. Hub.
   - The level row reads "Forge — Lv 1 · Next 30 D parts · 40 wood · 20 stone". MAX is unchanged.
   - _upgrade_building takes the preview before it upgrades. Its success line reads the costs from that plan, and its refusal line shows the plan's error.
   - hub.gd stops working out 10·(level+2) itself. Today it does, in both of those lines.
6. Numbers. Add hall_upgrade_wood_per_level 20 and hall_upgrade_stone_per_level 10 to balance_table.gd and balance.tres. Keep other people's uncommitted work in both files intact.

SAVE (boundary #1)
- No new key. Wood and stone already save in town_resources (ig-6m2.1 and ig-6m2.3.1), and building_levels doesn't change.
- An existing save with hall levels loads unchanged.
- ig-6pm: nothing new to repair or refuse.

ACCEPTANCE (tests/unit, APPDATA redirected)
- At each n from 0 to 4:
  - wood_cost and stone_cost match the table (20/40/60/80/100 and 10/20/30/40/50);
  - part_rank and part_cost are identical to before this bead.
- Level 5 shows no cost and is refused as capped, as today.
- Short of any one resource:
  - the upgrade is refused;
  - parts, wood and stone are all unchanged, even the ones that were enough;
  - the error names exactly the short ones.
- The preview equals the result for all five halls.
- A real disk save after an upgrade reloads with the new level and the lower wood and stone. An old save with levels loads unchanged.
- Existing upgrade tests (test_buildings.gd, test_bulk_operations.gd, tests/save_roundtrip_check.gd) give the town enough wood and stone first. Their parts assertions don't change.
- BUILT. Verifier pass mandatory: boundary #1.

FILES
- systems/game_session.gd (_building_upgrade_plan, preview_building_upgrade, upgrade_building)
- balance_table.gd, balance.tres
- hub/hub.gd (_building_level_text, _upgrade_building)
- tests/unit/test_buildings.gd, tests/unit/test_bulk_operations.gd, tests/save_roundtrip_check.gd

NON-GOALS
Costs for the Apothecary or the Town Gate. New levels. Upgrade build time. Refunds. Any change to the parts cost. Moving upgrade_building onto _commit_profile_mutation: today it mutates and notifies directly, so a refused save does not roll it back. That is older than this bead; file it separately if wanted.
notes:
2026-09-23 game-designer RULING: the numbers are set (SYSTEMS.md § Town builder, "Hall upgrades cost wood and stone").
- Costs:
  - hall_upgrade_wood_per_level 20: level n -> n+1 costs 20*(n+1) wood
  - hall_upgrade_stone_per_level 10: it also costs 10*(n+1) stone
  - n is the current level, the same n as _building_upgrade_plan's parts formula
  - Totals per hall: 300 wood and 150 stone
- The parts cost STAYS unchanged (10*(n+2) parts of rank n). It is calibrated against the spine (264 clears per hall), and the town adds a gate, not a replacement.
- It applies to Circle, Forge, Training Hall, Sanctum and Reliquary. The Apothecary and the Town Gate have no levels.
- Levels already reached stay. Nothing is refunded or charged again.
- The preview shows parts, wood and stone. A refusal names every resource that is short. A refused upgrade spends nothing, not even the resources it could afford.
- Acceptance adds:
  - a test at each n (0..4) that the wood and stone match the table
  - the parts cost is identical to before this bead
  - a level-5 hall shows no cost and is refused as capped, as today
  - an existing save with hall levels loads unchanged
- The needs-owner label is removed; nothing here waits on the owner.
2026-09-24 tech-lead: now depends on ig-6m2.3.1 (Mine and stone) instead of the whole ig-6m2.3. Hall upgrades need stone, not construction time (halls never build and upgrades stay instant), so they don't wait for ig-6m2.3.2.
Director, 2026-09-24: this bead also takes extra's finding. upgrade_building (game_session.gd:338) changes parts and building_levels directly. It skips _commit_profile_mutation, so it ignores load_blocked, and a failed or refused save (ig-6pm) does not take the upgrade back. Every other mutator goes through the commit path. Since this bead rewrites that function to spend wood and stone anyway, route it through _commit_profile_mutation. Test it the way test_a_failed_save_takes_the_building_back does: a failed save takes the upgrade and all three costs back, and load_blocked refuses. The save path is touched, so this is a boundary #1 review.
Director 2026-09-24, at GO: (1) The director note above overrides NON-GOALS' last item: upgrade_building DOES move onto _commit_profile_mutation in this bead. (2) Carry-in nit from ig-6m2.3.2: in hub.gd _refresh_placed_panel, the 'Under construction: %s left' string holds a raw line break; write \n like the Workers line above it.
Checkpoint 2026-09-24: implemented. _building_upgrade_plan takes resources, returns wood_cost/stone_cost, error names only short ones ("Need X (have Y) and Z."). upgrade_building on _commit_profile_mutation via _upgrade_building_in_memory (own load_blocked guard dropped: equivalent mutant, commit path refuses with the same reason). preview marks invalid when load_blocked (mirrors preview_place_building). Hub row + success line read the plan; refusal shows last_action_error as 'Cannot upgrade X. <error>'. Balance rows hall_upgrade_wood_per_level 20 / stone 10. New tests/unit/test_hall_upgrades.gd (8); test_buildings/test_bulk_operations/save_roundtrip_check updated. BUILT green: gate 0, GUT 740/740, save_roundtrip_check PASS. 13 mutants all killed (.agent-results/ig-6m2.4/). Sol review running: .agent-results/logs/ig-6m2.4-sol-1.json. Carry-in nit (raw newline in Under construction string) fixed.
Sol (ig-6m2.4-sol-1.json): PASS WITH NITS. Nit 1 (blocked+short: upgrade said 'Need...' while preview said blocked) was caused by dropping the guard; guard restored before the plan, test extended (blocked wins over short), mutant now killed. Nit 2 (preview uses balance.tres, upgrade_building takes a caller BalanceTable) left: pre-existing signature the bead says to keep; every caller passes matching values. Re-run BUILT: gate 0, GUT 740/740, save_roundtrip_check PASS. Not committed.
close_reason: Hall upgrades cost wood and stone via the commit path. Director BUILT: gate 0/0, GUT 740/740 (48 scripts), save_roundtrip_check PASS, FP stable. Sol PASS WITH NITS; nit 1 fixed, nit 2 (balance param) ruled leave as is.

title: Masterwork draughts: only a born master alchemist brews them
description:
WHY
Owner, 2026-09-23: "only the ones with calling can make masterwork(the final tier) equips/food/etc". On 2026-09-23 the owner ruled that masterwork draughts get built now, after ig-wgj.10. The Apothecary's output is draughts, and today they come in one tier, so its masterwork tier has to be added.
Design: GAME_SPEC.md § Heroes staff the buildings. Numbers: SYSTEMS.md § Keepers and professions (the draught table). Boundaries: DECISIONS.md "2026-09-23: Masterwork draughts are two more supply kinds, not a tier on the old ones". Read it first: it rules the save shape, the one kind list and the battle rule.

BEHAVIOR (numbers PROVISIONAL)

   Replace every hand-written ["healing", "revival"] list with one constant on BattleState.

SAVE

- Tests:
  - brewing is refused without a home master alchemist

food; draught kinds beyond these two tiers; any crafting tree; draughts on the legacy (non-battle_v1) path.

title: Buildings show their level in town
description:
WHY
The five buildings already have real levels (GameSession.building_levels, cap 5), but in town they are identical grey boxes. The owner wants the town to feel alive and later to become a base builder. Upgrades should show. This is the first visible payoff of the staged art. See GAME_SPEC.md § The town hub.

BEHAVIOR
1. Each leveled building (Circle, Forge, TrainingHall, Sanctum, Reliquary) swaps its model by tier:
   - level 0: an empty plot or ruin
   - levels 1-2: small
   - levels 3-4: bigger
   - level 5: final

Built on ig-6m2.8.2 (accepted, not landed): each hall scene's Model is its level-5 gltf at a fitted base scale, inside a fixed 4.5 m Pick box. This bead adds only the lower tiers. Model sizes are measured from the .gltf bounds (accessor min/max through the node transforms), and they match 8.2's table where the two overlap.

PICKS (director's call)
1. Props (body item 4) move to a follow-up bead, filed after this bead's screenshots. There's no room for them:
   - A hall's hex is 6.0 m flat to flat (HEX_SIZE 3.46 m, pointy-top), and its box is 4.5 m. That leaves 0.75 m strips on the left and right. Those strips are the walker gap between neighbouring halls (HALL_HEXES q -2..2, r 0: 1.5 m, 0.9 m once grown by 0.3). The front point holds the WorkSpot (z 2.8). The back point is a triangle about 1.1 m wide at z -2.8.
   - Props have no collider, so a body walks through them.
   The tiers are the payoff. The screenshots show whether a hall still needs dressing, and the mapping note already lets the director swap in per-tier prop sets as a presentation-only change.
   If the director keeps props here, the smallest version is one prop per hall at (0, 0, -2.9), at the hexagon scale, the same at every tier, no collider, and not on the Pick layer.
2. Two cells of the mapping note change so that every tier fits the fixed box (item 5: the box stays; it's also the body's collider):
   - Level 0: building_destroyed at x3.0 overflows the box by 0.21 m (x max 0.820 x 3.0 = 2.46 > 2.25). Every hall's ruin is scaled to the same absolute size, 2.7: 4.16 x 3.53 m, 2.65 m tall. It fits every box, the Forge's 3.0 m height included.
   - TrainingHall L3-4: archeryrange at the base scale 2.85 overflows by 0.24 m (x 2.48, z -2.49). At x0.9 (2.565) it fits by 0.011 m (x 2.234, z -2.239).
   All other cells stand as the note wrote them.

1. THE TIERS (hub/town/town_view.gd)
- `static func hall_tier(level: int) -> int`: `clampi(ceili(level / 2.0), 0, 3)`. So 0 → 0 (ruin), 1-2 → 1 (small), 3-4 → 2 (bigger), 5 → 3 (final). A level over 5 stays final, and below 0 it's a ruin. (ceili of a float division, not `(level + 1) / 2`: the gate fails on the integer-division warning.)
- `const TIERS`: per leveled hall, in GameSession.building_levels index order (0 Circle, 1 Forge, 2 TrainingHall, 3 Sanctum, 4 Reliquary), three [model, factor] pairs for tiers 0, 1 and 2. Tier 3 is the scene's own Model. The factor multiplies the Model's transform, its base scale and any facing 8.2 gives it.

| Hall (base) | Tier 0 (L0) | Tier 1 (L1-2) | Tier 2 (L3-4) | Tier 3 (L5) = Model |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SummoningCircle (3.0) | destroyed x0.9 | tower_base x1.0 | tower_A x1.0 | tower_B |
| Forge (3.0) | destroyed x0.9 | blacksmith x0.75 | blacksmith x0.9 | blacksmith |
| TrainingHall (2.85) | destroyed x0.95 | archeryrange x0.75 | archeryrange x0.9 | barracks |
| Sanctum (3.0) | destroyed x0.9 | church x0.75 | church x0.9 | church |
| Reliquary (2.0) | destroyed x1.35 | castle x0.75 | castle x0.9 | castle |

  Files: hub/town/models/hexagon/building_{destroyed,tower_base_blue,tower_A_blue,blacksmith_blue,archeryrange_blue,church_blue,castle_blue}.gltf. All are staged already. Nothing is downloaded.
  Measured fits (half-widths against 2.25 m; tops against the box): Circle tier 1 1.74 / 4.50 m, tier 2 1.74 / 6.58 m; Forge tier 2 1.85 / 2.65 m; TrainingHall tier 1 1.87 / 3.83 m, tier 2 2.239 / 4.60 m; Sanctum tier 2 1.61 / 4.44 m; Reliquary tier 2 2.03 / 7.16 m; each ruin 2.22 / 2.65 m.

2. THE SWAP (the _show_stage pattern, town_view.gd:356-378)
- `show_buildings(buildings: Array[Dictionary], levels: Array[int] = [])`. For each building whose type is in TIERS and whose index is inside levels, it calls `_show_tier(node, hall_tier(level))`.
- `_show_tier`:
  - it swaps a "Tier" child only when the tier changes (a meta, as "Stage" keeps "stage"), so it's cheap on every pulse;
  - at tier 3 there's no Tier child, and Model is visible;
  - at tiers 0-2 Model is hidden, and the Tier child is the table's model with `transform = Model.transform.scaled_local(Vector3.ONE * factor)`.
- The empty default leaves every hall as its scene has it. That keeps the seven existing callers (tests and perf_baseline.gd:589) unchanged.
- The Stage and the tier never meet. Halls are never under construction (build_seconds is 0 for them, and SYSTEMS § Stone and construction says so), and _show_stage returns before touching Model when both old and new stage are -1 (:362-363).
- Pick, Shape, Label and WorkSpot aren't touched. So item 5 holds by construction: the click area, collider, label and routes are the same at every tier.

3. THE HUB (hub/hub.gd, one line)
- `_refresh_town` (:1056) passes the levels: `%Town.show_buildings(GameSession.town_buildings, GameSession.building_levels)`.

So the model changes in the same frame as the upgrade, and a reload builds the town at the saved tiers.

title: Ambient life: home heroes wander and use stalls (never saved)
description:
WHY
Owner, 2026-09-23: "we see our heros walking around, interacting with stalls and shops, and make it seem alive". Heroes who are home should be visible in town, doing small things. See ARCHITECTURE.md § The town is the interface: ambient heroes are views derived from the roster and are never saved.

BEHAVIOR
1. Show up to AMBIENT_HERO_CAP heroes who are home: on the roster, not busy (is_hero_busy), and not the body. Pick order: favorites, then higher rank, then lower instance_id. The order is stable, so the same heroes appear each visit.
2. Authored Marker3D spots under Town/Spots, one or more per building and stall. Each spot has metadata naming its clip (Interact, PickUp, Use_Item, Idle_B, or a Tools/Simulation clip once those are staged).
3. Each ambient hero walks between free spots in a straight line (Walking_A), plays the spot's clip for a few seconds, then picks another spot. No navmesh. Spots are placed so straight paths are clear.
4. Refresh on roster_changed and expeditions_changed:
   - a dispatched hero leaves
   - a returning hero appears
   - a killed hero vanishes
5. Clicking an ambient hero opens that hero's detail panel.
6. Nothing is saved. Positions and spots reset on every load.

PERF
Measure the FPS with the cap at 8, 12 and 16 on the owner's machine. Set AMBIENT_HERO_CAP to the highest value that holds 60 FPS, and mark it PROVISIONAL in the code comment and the bead notes.

ACCEPTANCE
- Tests:
  - the chosen set matches the pick order and the cap
  - busy heroes and the body are excluded
  - the set updates after a dispatch, a return and a kill_hero
  - to_dict() is identical before and after ambient heroes spawn
- A screenshot shows heroes at spots. Record the FPS numbers in the bead notes.
- BUILT: the import gate shows zero errors and zero warnings, and GUT is green.
- The scene<->script seam (spots, metadata, signals) makes a verifier pass mandatory.

FILES
- hub/town/town_view.gd, optional hub/town/town_ambient.gd (+ .uid)
- hub/town/town.tscn
- tests/unit/test_town_ambient.gd

NON-GOALS
saving positions; non-roster townsfolk; hero-to-hero interaction; schedules or needs; pathfinding.

title: Squad battle readability after KayKit swap: faction ring, corpse cue, cleric silhouette
description:
Design follow-up from the ig-ixj review (Opus::extra 1 game, 2026-09-23). The KayKit swap removed ALLY_COLOR/ENEMY_COLOR tint and DEAD_COLOR, which were the only faction and death cues on the old capsules.

Evidence: .agent-results/ig-ixj/battle_live.png (melee clump). Wide shots separate by palette, but a clump does not: crimson Skeleton_Mage hats sit next to purple hero Mage hats, and 10 dead skeletons look like 5 live ones.

Issues:
1. Faction cue: reviewer suggests a thin faction-coloured ground ring under every unit, reusing the selection-ring TorusMesh with 2 shared static materials (no per-unit material copies).
2. Corpse cue: a shared static material_overlay dim on dead units, or sink and hide corpses once the death clip ends.
3. Cleric reads as Mage (same model, wand vs staff only), so the healer is invisible at battle zoom. PROVISIONAL mapping from ig-ixj.
4. Cosmetic: Skeletons_Death hips slide about 0.85 world units back after the root pin (hips track kept on purpose), plus the fling, so corpses land 1.1-1.65 units from the sim spot.

Route: game-designer picks the cues, then implementer. Renderer only (combat/battle/battle_unit_view.gd). No sim changes. Perf: ig-ixj already costs about 1.9x render median at 60 units, so every cue must use shared materials.

One static mesh plus 2 static unshaded materials: ALLY_COLOR a8c9a8 and ENEMY_COLOR e87b68, the old capsule colors from da554c1^ (director: keep green/salmon, matches the HP bars). Hidden on dead, shown on downed. (2) Corpse cue: static 50%-black material_overlay (CORPSE_DIM) on a dead unit's meshes. The killing-hit flash keeps the overlay until it ends, then _clear_flash hands over to the dim. Both are marked PROVISIONAL (ig-hpu) in code, settled by a played build. Tests: test_every_unit_stands_on_a_shared_faction_ring_until_it_dies, test_the_killing_hit_flashes_before_the_corpse_dims, and _assert_dead_look now checks ring hidden + dim. Mutation 6/6 killed (.agent-results/ig-hpu/mutation.txt). Perf at 60 units (fallen_citadel, benchmark.gd from ig-ixj): render median before 3.385/3.284 ms, after 3.325/3.464 ms. +2%, inside run-to-run noise. Still about 1.8x the old 1.9 ms capsule baseline, no new cost. Screenshots before_/after_{wide,clump,corpses}.png, compare_corpses.png (corpse region about 25% darker). ITEM 3: CLERIC CUE = HAT OFF + HALO. Not folded into ig-4if: the Cleric must read while idle too (Mend is on an 8 s cooldown), so the static cue lives here.
Why: Mage.glb's Mage_Hat is its own skinned mesh, and it is the Mage's whole top-down read. Its brim is 1.86 x 1.97 model units, wider than the head (1.14) and the body (0.86). The camera looks down about 53 degrees (0,32,24 onto the rig), so from there a Mage is a big purple disc. With no hat, a Cleric's hatless purple head could pass for a hooded Rogue, so the halo adds the colour pop that says healer.
3a. Hat off (HeroModel, because it is the Cleric's look and town heroes will share it): the ally cleric look drops the Mage_Hat mesh. Free the node in HeroModel.build(), so it costs no skinning. Put the data in the look table (a 4th row field, or a small dropped-meshes const keyed by archetype), not in an archetype if. The Mage keeps its hat.
3b. Halo (BattleUnitView, because it is a readability marker like the faction ring):
  - A BoneAttachment3D on the "head" bone (the head bone rests at model y 1.24; the Mage_Head mesh top is at 2.16), holding a MeshInstance3D about 0.1 above the head top. That is a bone-local offset of about +1.0 up; tune it by eye.
  - Reuse the shared _faction_ring_mesh at y-scale 0.3, lying flat. Under the 0.75 model scale that is about 0.4 world radius, roughly the head's width.
  - One new static material: _halo_material = _flat_material(HALO_COLOR), HALO_COLOR = Color("fff1c4"), a warm white. It must not be the selection gold d4b65b or the ally ring green.
  - Cast shadow off.
  - Add the halo AFTER the _flash_meshes gather in _build_visual, so it never takes the hit flash or the corpse dim.
  - Visibility: shown when alive and when downed. Hidden when dead, like the faction ring.
  - Every cleric unit gets it. Enemies never spawn clerics.
  - Mark HALO_COLOR under the existing PROVISIONAL (ig-hpu) line.
Fallback (no need to ask): if the screenshot shows the hatless Mage_Head is open or broken on top, keep the hat, ship the halo alone, and report it.
Cost: -1 skinned hat mesh, +1 unshaded halo per cleric. Net no more draws, so no perf run is required.

Measured hips X/Z travel per clip (model units, then world at 0.75):

  - Death_B (ally downed) 0.23 forward / 0.18. A revive snaps the body back, so this one also pops.

title: Combat punch pack: hit-stop, lunge, squash, corpse fling, last-kill slow-mo, compact health bars
description: Owner picks 2026-09-23 (ideas 2,4,5,6,7) plus small health bars that don't clutter. View-only. The sim, snapshot and saves are untouched. Full spec in notes.
acceptance_criteria: See the dispatch brief in notes.
notes:
DISPATCH BRIEF (director, 2026-09-23). View-only. No creative work beyond this; ask instead.
FILES: combat/battle/battle_unit_view.gd, combat/battle/battle_view.gd, combat/battle/battle_vfx.gd, tests/unit/test_battle_unit_view.gd, tests/unit/test_battle_vfx.gd. Nothing else. NEVER touch battle_simulation.gd, battle_actor.gd, battle_state.gd, saves, .tscn, project.godot.
BUILDS ON ig-0gt (crit tick, red/yellow numbers, recoil on pivot x/z). Read its final code first.

OFFSETS RULE: recoil, lunge and fling all move the pivot on x/z. Keep a separate Vector3 offset per effect and set pivot.position = their sum (plus the death lift on y) in one place. No two tweens may write pivot.position directly.

2 HIT-STOP: on a hit event with critical=true, freeze the target's view animation (lerp + its tweens) for 0.06s. If a basic_attack event in the same render targets it, freeze that attacker too. Non-crit hits: no freeze.
4 LUNGE: on a basic_attack event where the attacker's archetype is not ranger/mage: lunge offset 0.3 toward the target over 0.07s, back to 0 over 0.15s (ease-out).
5 SQUASH: on a hit: pivot scale (1.15, 0.85, 1.15) back to ONE over 0.12s. On a crit: (1.25, 0.75, 1.25). Not on dead units once the death pose has started.
6 CORPSE FLING: on life alive->dead: fling offset slides along -facing during the 0.35s tip-over, 0.8 units if last_crit_tick advanced in that render, else 0.25, plus a small y arc peaking at 0.3. It must end at rest. A first-sight dead unit snaps (no fling).
7 LAST-KILL SLOW-MO: when a render takes the living enemy count from >0 to 0, the battle VIEW runs at 0.35x for 0.4s of real time. That covers unit lerps and every tween in units and vfx. NEVER use Engine.time_scale (it slows GameSession clocks for every expedition). NEVER scale the delta passed to BattleSimulation.advance in practice mode.
HEALTH BARS (replaces the current _hp_fill box):
- Billboarded, unshaded, drawn over geometry (no depth test) so bodies never hide it. Centered at y 2.2. 0.7 wide x 0.07 tall. Enemies with elite: 0.85 wide.
- Layers: a background 1a1a1a at alpha 0.6; a trailing damage chip f5e6a8 that eases down to the new value over 0.4s after a hit; a fill 6fcf6f for allies / e8483c for enemies.
- Visibility, to cut clutter: shown when hp < max_hp OR selected. Hidden at full hp. Hidden when dead. Hidden when downed (the downed marker covers that case).
- Heals: the fill rises immediately and the chip snaps to it.
TESTS: each effect's trigger and non-trigger case, the offsets-sum rule (a recoil during a lunge ends at zero), bar visibility rules, the chip trailing behavior (Tween.custom_step, no wall-clock waits), and slow-mo leaves the practice sim delta untouched.

title: Playtest timed expedition and recovery pacing
description:
## Objective
Determine whether the provisional timed expedition and active recovery pacing makes building multiple teams and recovering lost gear practical in a played session.

## Existing context
ig-6l4 implements concurrent reserved teams, finite and safe repeat orders, automatic rewards, and bulk management. docs/SYSTEMS.md defines base seconds 60/180/300, five-hero floors 15/45/75, square-root strength scaling, and the 5/team_size workload factor. Recovery uses 900 + 300*Reliquary active seconds and pauses on new losses. Automated formula examples are not playtest evidence.

## Acceptance criteria
Record a fresh three-pull save progressing to its second viable team; compare one geared squad with several squads; play a lost-gear recovery scenario with a surviving weak roster at low and high Reliquary levels. Record roster/gear, destinations, elapsed active time, income, idle periods, and decisions. Give an evidence-backed keep/change recommendation for the director. Do not change balance during the measurement. If later balance changes are authorized, run powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests\import_gate.ps1 and the full unit suite on that final state.

## Files allowed to change
.agent-results/ig-6l4-pacing/ evidence only; this Bead's notes. Production balance/spec edits need a separately accepted decision.

## Non-goals
No stamina, paid timers, new currencies, offline repeat chains, permadeath redesign, combat controls, or automatic destructive processing.

title: Timed expeditions, team presets, and bulk management
description:
Objective: replace click-speed expedition farming with concurrent timed dispatches so roster depth and equipped strength improve sustained returns. The user explicitly requested timers, named team presets, send-X-times/auto-repeat, and bulk resource management. This is Astra's proposed direction pending user decisions and a decision-complete Plan-mode specification; it is not an accepted implementation plan.

Each hero may participate in one active expedition. Separate teams run concurrently without an energy meter or arbitrary small dispatch cap. Equipped heroes and their gear are reserved while away, with no mid-run transfers or sacrifice. Show duration before dispatch; derive it from current team strength against mission difficulty with diminishing gains and a nonzero floor. Exact timing and reward tuning are provisional and must cover a fresh save with only three pulls and compare solo with full-team efficiency because current enemies scale with team size.

Preserve combat and permadeath: a past clear is history, not proof of safety. Derive any Safe label from conservative worst-case attrition for the current roster, gear, and zone, including retreat threshold, and validate it before trusting it. Named presets require durable hero identities rather than names or indices, show missing or busy members, and never silently substitute. Preset launch offers one run, a finite total run count, and eventually until-stopped looping. Repeat orders recheck availability and safety, stop on casualty, retreat, or an incomplete team, and support stop-after-current-run. Credit rewards automatically. A dispatch board shows team, zone, remaining time, completed/ordered runs, and cumulative rewards, with collectable reports for review.

Clock behavior awaits the user's async answer. Astra's proposed default is that dispatched missions finish while closed while repeats run only while open; alternatives are session-only timing or bounded repeats progressing offline. Do not assume an answer.

Recovery remains unresolved. The current global expedition-turn clock would let parallel or automatic returns rapidly expire lost gear. Before implementation, explicitly redesign expiry and damage aging while preserving a meaningful Reliquary benefit; do not silently retain or replace the existing rule.

Bulk QoL reuses existing batch salvage/sacrifice and filters. Add protection for favorites, preset members, away heroes, and equipped gear; selection by rank, type, slot, and availability; clear destructive previews with outputs; quantity/all-eligible salvage and sacrifice; and batch part conversion with a keep-at-least reserve. The user's word refine is ambiguous among salvage, part conversion, and enhancement; identify the intended meaning before creating any resource system. No automatic destructive processing by default.

Scope implementation only after design acceptance: (1) timed persisted dispatch, reservations, presets, and finite repeats as one complete player loop; (2) richer bulk management and advanced automation. Existing ig-544 (controlled playable expeditions) and ig-yzc (hop into a sent run) are related direction, but neither grants scope for this work and neither is changed by this epic.

Technical entry points are hub/hub.gd:_on_expedition_pressed/_do_expedition, hub/expedition/expedition.gd:resolve, systems/game_session.gd, systems/save_service.gd, and heroes/hero.gd. Saves are version 1 with no durable hero IDs or migration machinery, and current resolution performs multiple automatic saves. Design exactly-once rewards and casualties, deterministic restart behavior, version-1 migration, and stable completion ordering for concurrent returns. Keep the three-autoload cap, central kill_hero path, and SaveService ownership. Change the explicit no-clock/no-offline-accrual spec only through an accepted plan. In Default mode, do not implement this complex epic until a decision-complete Plan-mode plan is accepted or the user explicitly overrides that gate.

Eventual acceptance: run tests/import_gate.ps1 and the full GUT suite; add focused reservation, repeat, timer, and migration tests plus actual isolated-APPDATA save/reload checks for in-flight missions, duplicate-return prevention, and old saves; visually check populated and empty dispatch boards. Do not mutate the user's save, run concurrent Godot processes, or perform git operations, commits, or pushes. This design/source-inspection turn establishes no runtime proof.
notes:
ACCEPTED DESIGN — 2026-09-21 (user authorized implement-all; direct authorization governs proceeding)

Entry point: core worker starts at systems/game_session.gd + systems/save_service.gd, then deterministic combat/expedition rules and serialization. UI worker separately owns hub/hub.gd, hub/hub.tscn, theme/UI tests and docs; core worker must not edit those paths. Do not close this epic until all core, UI, verification, save/reload, and review gates are complete.

1. Identity/schema: Save version 2. Hero and Item gain stable random serialized instance_id:String and favorite:bool=false. Legacy v1 missing IDs migrate once. Names and indices are never identity. Persist GameSession team_presets:Array[Dictionary], expedition_orders:Array[Dictionary], expedition_reports:Array[Dictionary], recovery_clock_seconds:float, recovery_clock_paused:bool. Presets are {id,name,hero_ids:Array[String],zone_id}; preserve missing/dead references and never substitute. At the v2 trust boundary reject duplicate object IDs, malformed presets/orders, duplicate/invalid teams, unknown/locked dispatch zones, overlapping active teams, invalid finite/count/time/seed state, and do not overwrite canonical save on rejection.

2. Reservations/protection: one hero may be in at most one active order; unlimited disjoint orders. Shared backend guards prevent busy heroes from equip/unequip/rank-up/sacrifice/recovery/arena availability and prevent touching busy equipped gear. kill_hero remains the only roster removal path and must remain usable for expedition deaths; sacrifice guard precedes it. Preset/favorite membership protects heroes from destructive sacrifice; favorite/equipped items protect bulk salvage. Non-destructive equip/enhance remains allowed for non-busy favorites. Revalidate at commit.

3. Timing: combat_ratio=Hero.compute_team_power(team)/(zone.recommended_power*team.size()/5.0). full_team_seconds=max(zone.minimum_duration_seconds,zone.base_duration_seconds/sqrt(combat_ratio)); actual_seconds=ceil(full_team_seconds*5.0/team.size()). Reject empty/invalid/zero-power teams. Author Verdant 60/15, Ashfall 180/45, Sundered 300/75 seconds. Values are provisional pending play; do not alter current reward/combat tuning. Verify equal-gear 1-vs-5 throughput and fresh-three-hero pace.

4. Safety/repeats: forecast emulates worst-case loss damage across Wave.from_zone using exact max HP, rounding, cumulative HP, and non-boss <=25% retreat rule including all traits/stats. Safe only if every hero survives every wave and no retreat. Finite risky dispatch allowed with warning; infinite requires safe and rechecks before every repeat. total_runs is 1..999 including initial; 0 means infinite. Automatically bank every completed run and track cumulative stones/xp/items and runs_completed. Stop after casualty, retreat/failure, incomplete team, or stop_requested; stop means finish current. Captured membership/destination are immutable under preset edits.

5. Clock: persist per-order stable ID, deterministic run seed, initial duration and remaining_seconds. Use monotonic online delta; persist saved_at_unix for offline elapsed max(0, now-saved_at_unix). On load subtract offline time only from already-dispatched current runs; resolve each due run once, then start at most the next repeat at full duration in the open session. No recursive offline catch-up. Rollback gives zero offline progress; forward jump completes current run only. Stable due ordering is remaining time then order ID. Pulse about 0.25s; no per-frame save. Periodic timer/recovery save about 15s and durable dispatch/completion mutations. Pause-menu pause stops online delta; closing follows offline rule. UI observes backend scheduling and need not own it.

6. Exactly once: persisted seed drives deterministic local RNG through expedition/quick-resolve while preserving public resolve(team,wave) seam via helper/optional expedition entry. Defer existing signal-triggered saves during resolution and commit one atomic save containing casualties, cache, rewards, order advance, report. Atomic failure restores pre-transaction memory, preserves previous canonical save, sets notice, and cannot retry awards from mutated memory. Dispatch has the same durability. SaveService remains sole file owner; prevent from_dict/load autosave recursion and preserve newer-version refusal. Add actual isolated-APPDATA reload tests.

7. Recovery: turns remains historical completed/attempted expedition count only. Cache expiry moves to an active recovery clock that runs only in unpaused, active gameplay and never offline. Any new cache pauses recovery_clock_paused. acknowledge_recovery_losses unpauses all current losses. Cache stores its created recovery-clock value. Lifetime seconds=900+300*ReliquaryLevel; damage age converts elapsed active seconds to minutes and reuses 0.03 per unit, Reliquary -0.03/level, and power penalty. Preserve strict <0 expiration. Legacy turn age maps to elapsed active minutes while preserving remaining effective window and migrated caches start paused. Parallel returns/dispatch do not age caches. Recovery acknowledgment is independent from report retention.

8. Reports: retain newest 50. Each summarizes captured team/zone, outcome, casualty names, per-run and cumulative rewards, and stop reason. Rewards never depend on review.

Public backend API: GameSession.hero_by_id(id:String)->Hero; is_hero_busy(hero:Hero)->bool; is_hero_protected(hero:Hero)->bool; is_item_protected(item:Item)->bool; set_hero_favorite(hero:Hero,value:bool)->void; set_item_favorite(item:Item,value:bool)->void; save_team_preset(preset_id:String,preset_name:String,hero_ids:Array[String],zone_id:String)->String; delete_team_preset(id:String)->bool; dispatch_expedition(hero_ids:Array[String],zone_id:String,total_runs:int,team_name:String,preset_id:String='')->String; request_stop_expedition(order_id:String)->void; acknowledge_recovery_losses()->void. ExpeditionOrders.duration_seconds(team:Array[Hero],zone:ZoneDefinition,balance:BalanceTable)->float; safety_forecast(...)->Dictionary {safe:bool,reason:String}. Add `expeditions_changed` for timer/order UI refresh, separate from autosave roster_changed, plus explicit testable tick/offline entry points. Bulk API follows as a separate exact handoff; do not guess it.

Core ownership: heroes/hero.gd, equipment/item.gd, equipment/lost_cache.gd, combat/quick_resolve.gd, hub/expedition/expedition.gd, new hub/expedition/expedition_orders.gd, systems/game_session.gd, systems/save_service.gd, balance_table.gd, balance.tres, zones/zone_definition.gd and three zone definitions as needed, new systems/bulk_operations.gd, backend tests/unit and tests/save_roundtrip_check.gd. No hub UI/docs/tool/.godot/manual uid edits. No engine until director grants exclusive slot; no git or user-save access.
ACCEPTED BULK SCOPE — 2026-09-22

Refining means batch operations over the existing salvage, sacrifice, enhancement and part-conversion systems; no new resource system. Public API: GameSession.preview_bulk_salvage(item_ids:Array[String],quantity:int)->Dictionary; preview_bulk_sacrifice(hero_ids:Array[String],target_id:String,quantity:int)->Dictionary; preview_bulk_enhance(item_ids:Array[String],target_level:int,budget_parts:Array[int])->Dictionary; preview_bulk_conversion(rank:int,quantity:int,reserve:int)->Dictionary; commit_bulk_plan(plan:Dictionary)->bool. quantity=0 means all eligible/max convertible; positive is a deterministic exact limit. last_action_error:String is ephemeral.

Plans are read-only dictionaries with shared keys kind, valid, error, entries, excluded, cost_parts[8], gain_parts[8], essence_gain, resonance_gain, parameters. Entries carry stable IDs, names, rank and operation-specific before/after/spend/gain fields; excluded entries carry id/name/reason. Commit rebuilds from the current profile and refuses any stale eligibility, protection, membership, cost/output, Forge, target, gear, rank or resource change. One SaveService-backed memory/disk transaction commits the whole batch or rolls it all back on write failure. No generic action/plugin framework.

All pure selection/arithmetic lives in new static res://hub/bulk_operations.gd; GameSession supplies profile state and applies coordinated mutations. Reuse the existing single-item formulas. Salvage/sacrifice exclude favorites, preset members, busy heroes, equipped gear/fodder; sacrifice excludes recipient. Selected/displayed order is deterministic and quantity never fills from unselected resources. Preview exact parts/essence/resonance.

Enhancement permits favorite inventory items, bounds target by current Forge cap, accepts eight nonnegative per-rank budgets also capped by actual parts, and processes each selected item to target before the next. Skip target <= current with reason. No random/new enhancement mechanic. Conversion accepts source ranks 0..6, preserves reserve, computes max=floor(max(0,parts[rank]-reserve)/3), refuses positive quantity above max, spends 3 per output, and never cascades. Add focused backend tests for protection, stale plans, funds, budget/reserve and atomic failure.

title: Fix the 108 GDScript warnings left at Warn, then raise each type to Error
description:
WHY

A headless run never prints a warning at Warn, so new ones of these types creep in unseen. integer_division has a bug history (P2-19's trap, docs/TASKS.md:883).

THE SITES (type: count, where)
- static_called_on_instance 38: GameSession's static funcs called through the autoload (validate_saved_state, repair_rescue_timestamps). save_service.gd 2, tests 36 (test_battle_persistence 20).
- shadowed_global_identifier 16: game_session.gd 5, battle_simulation.gd 3, battle_job.gd 1, tests 7.
- confusable_local_declaration 14: hub.gd 8, quick_resolve.gd 1, game_session.gd 1, tests 4.
- shadowed_variable 12: battle_actor.gd 3, item.gd 3, hero.gd 3, ledger.gd 1, hub_ui_builder.gd 1, tests 1.
- integer_division 11: battle_simulation.gd 3 (row = index / columns; objective_enemy_count / 3 twice), bulk_operations.gd 1, hub.gd 1, town_rules.gd 1 (hex distance), game_session.gd 1 (minutes left), settings.gd 1 (window centering), tests 3. The director's read: all 11 look like intended floors.
- unused_parameter 6, shadowed_variable_base_class 5, incompatible_ternary 4, unassigned_variable 1 (test_battle_controls.gd "enemy"), int_as_enum_without_cast 1 (test_battle_controls.gd).

Owner domain: godot-tester (gates). Engine lane, any gap (P3).
design:
- Renames, underscores and casts only. No behavior change.
- integer_division: an intended floor gets @warning_ignore("integer_division") on its line (GDScript 4 has no integer-division operator). A site that meant a float is a bug: list it and stop (STATUS partial). Don't fix it here, since the fix changes numbers.
- static_called_on_instance: game_session.gd is an autoload with no class_name, so "call it from the type" needs a preload const in each file. If that is clean, do it. If not, keep this type at Warn (or Ignore) with a one-line reason in the gate comment. Implementer's call; say which.
- Each fixed type goes to Error (2) in project.godot's [debug] section, and tests/import_gate.ps1's comment moves it to the Error list.
- save_service.gd and game_session.gd are boundary #1 files: renames only there, no to_dict/from_dict key changes.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Measure first at HEAD, the way ig-4k2 did (one type at a time at Error): confirm the 108 sites in 10 types, or say what changed. Log under .agent-results/<this bead>/.
2. Each of the 10 types ends either with 0 sites and at Error in project.godot, or at Warn/Ignore with a one-line reason in tests/import_gate.ps1's comment. The comment's lists match project.godot.
3. integer_division: the report rules every site: an intended floor (annotated), or a float that was meant (listed, not fixed, STATUS partial).

title: Body-part damage: a badly hurt limb comes off, and town healing puts it back
description:
WHY

NOW
Only skeletons lose parts (ig-c9y.4). Heroes and flesh creatures bleed but keep their limbs, as ig-c9y says.

LATER (scope before any code)
- Heroes and NPCs track damage per body part.
- Too much damage to one part takes it off. What a lost arm or leg does in a fight is design's call.
- Potions and healing magic in town put it back: which building, what it costs, how long it takes (design).
- The injury is saved on the hero until it is healed.
- Which bodies: heroes and flesh enemies and creatures; town folk only if design wants it.

RISKY BOUNDARIES
- #1 save round-trip: a new saved injury on Hero, plus a legacy save without it.
- #4 combat seam: both resolve() paths agree on body-part damage, or an ADR says why only the squad sim has it.
- Permadeath: losing a part is not death. GameSession.kill_hero() stays the only way off the roster.
Needs design (GAME_SPEC, SYSTEMS) and an architect ADR before any code.

AFTER
ig-c9y (the part-mesh work in the view).

Its design left out dreams that need encounter records (ig-m6o.2.2.4) or meal records (ig-m6o.2.2.5) as proof. This bead holds them so they aren't lost. Filed 2026-09-24 on the director's order.

BEFORE BUILD (game-designer)
- One or two dreams proved by encounter records ({heroes, place, why}) or meal records ({diners, place}). Each gets § 5's parts, the owner's reason, its milestones and PROVISIONAL rows, written into SYSTEMS § The dream catalogue.
- Each new dream's place in the catalogue order, which the choice rule uses to break a tie inside one record.
- Eviction: ig-m6o.2.2.4 evicts encounter records before any routine battle, so a dream counted on them fades first at the cap. Pick formative events and counts that survive that, or say why the fade is acceptable.

RULED (ig-m6o.2.2.7; DECISIONS.md 2026-09-24 "Bonds stay derived", item 6)
- Derived from records. No saved dream field.
- One dream at a time per hero. The catalogue's choice rule applies: oldest formative record first, and the record that ends a dream never opens the next.

ACCEPTANCE (tests/unit, APPDATA redirected)
- Each new dream opens, advances each milestone, ends fulfilled and ends lost. Its place in the choice rule is tested.
- The four ig-m6o.2.2.7 dreams still pass their tests.
- The read cost for one hero at the cap, best of seven, is printed. It runs on refresh only, never per frame.
- No saved state. BUILT. Verifier pass mandatory: boundary #2.

NON-GOALS
Profession dreams (ig-m6o.2.2.8). Dreams revised by knowledge. Gossip. Rivals and other roles (ig-m6o.2.2.6).
design:
DESIGN (extra as game-designer, 2026-09-25; checked against HEAD 3fd43c1). Built on ig-m6o.2.2.7 (the catalogue, the dream shape, the choice rule), ig-m6o.2.2.4 (the encounter record {heroes, place, why}) and ig-m6o.2.2.5 (the meal record {diners, place}). All three are accepted and none is built, so this runs after them. Rules: DECISIONS 2026-09-24 "Bonds stay derived", item 6 (derived, one dream at a time, oldest formative record first). All numbers PROVISIONAL, under § Bonds and dreams' marker.

PICKS (director's call)
1. Two dreams, one per new record kind:
   - "Welcome them home" is meal-proved. Tablemates get a stake in a rescue they weren't on.
   - "Fight beside them" is encounter-proved. Town life turns into a team choice.
2. How they survive eviction (the bead's third question):
   - Welcome them home opens on a rescue battle (a tier 2 battle after 2.4's renumbering), not on a meal. Only its proof, the rescued hero's last meal before it, and its count are meals.
   - Fight beside them opens on a meeting (tier 0). Why that's acceptable is in section 4.
3. Fight beside them also ends "lost" if the pair meet dream_along_meetings more times without fighting together. Without that, two keepers the player never sends out together would hold it for ever, and one dream at a time means neither hero could open another. Keepers can be sent out (DECISIONS 2026-09-23 item 5), so the dream can always be fulfilled. The loss is a missed chance, not a stuck one.

1. THE DREAMS (SYSTEMS § The dream catalogue's format; X is the other hero, Z the zone)

**Welcome them home** (`welcome_home`). A tablemate came back from a rescue. The owner stayed home, and wants them back at the table.
- Opens: a rescue battle lists X in `rescued`, the owner isn't in that battle's `team`, and X's last meal before it was at the owner's table (the latest meal record listing X in `diners` also lists the owner). The first such X in `rescued` order.
  - Why "X's last meal", not "the owner's last meal": a stranded hero isn't home, so it misses meals. The owner's latest table before the rescue never has X at it.
  - Why "not in the team": with the owner in the team, the same record is the owner rescuing X (watch_over) or being rescued (life_debt). Those are the stronger stories, and this keeps the three apart.
- Desired change: X is home and well. Beneficiary: X. Methods: keep X home and at the table.
- Milestones: X was carried home from Z; eat with X again (n / `dream_welcome_meals`), meal records listing both after the rescue.
- Fulfilled: the count is reached. Lost: X dies.
- Owner's reason: a rescue is the game's big stakes moment ("a stranded force needs a rescue", GAME_SPEC). This gives the heroes who stayed home a part in it, and it shows who eats together. It also makes a small peace-or-war choice: the dream wants X home for about three live hours, and the player wants X back out.

**Fight beside them** (`fight_beside`). Two heroes who talk in town but have never shared a fight. The owner wants to go out with X.
- Opens: a meeting (an `encounter` record with the owner and X in `heroes`) that brings their meetings in the read to `dream_along_meetings`, while no earlier battle in the read has both in its `team`. The meeting count runs through the whole pass, so meetings held while another dream was open count too.
- Desired change: the owner and X fight side by side. Beneficiaries: both. Methods: the player puts them on one team.
- Milestones: got to know X in town (the meetings, shown as a number); fight beside X (n / `dream_fight_beside_battles`), battles with both in the team, routine too.
- Fulfilled: the count is reached. Lost: X dies, or they meet `dream_along_meetings` more times after the opening before the first battle together.
- Owner's reason: it's the mirror of the life debt. The life debt turns a battle into a town story. This turns town life into a team pick, and it's the first dream the player fulfils by choosing a team, from something that happened at home.

Catalogue order, for a tie inside one record: life_debt, watch_over, carry_name, be_worthy, welcome_home, fight_beside. The new two never tie:
- welcome_home needs the owner outside the battle's team, and life_debt and watch_over need it inside;
- carry_name and be_worthy open on died records;
- fight_beside is the only dream that opens on a meeting.
The record that ends a dream never opens the next (slice 1's rule). For example, X's death loses welcome_home and doesn't open carry_name, and the battle that fulfils fight_beside doesn't open a life debt even if it holds a save.

2. THE READ (history/bonds.gd, Bonds.dream; still one oldest-first pass per hero, on refresh only)
- The pass keeps three small maps beside 2.2.7's order set:
  - for each other hero, whether its latest meal was at the owner's table (set on every meal record: true for each diner when the owner dined, false otherwise);
  - meetings with the owner, per other hero;
  - fought-with: every hero that shared a battle team with the owner so far.
- Per record, that's one kind check. A meal costs up to 4 diners, and a battle the owner fought in costs up to its team size.
- The dream dict has 2.2.7's shape: `dream` names the id, plus state, X, Z where there is one, and the count.
- Legacy and gaps: a meal with no `diners`, an encounter with no `heroes`, or a rescue with no `rescued` reads as nothing. Records written before 2.4 and 2.5 have neither kind, so every older save reads exactly as 2.2.7 does.

3. THE PANEL AND THE LINES
- Bonds.dream_lines (the hub seam, hub.gd:683-695, unchanged):
  - welcome_home open: "Dream: welcome X home." / "  [x] X was carried home from Z." / "  [ ] Eat with X again (n/3)."; fulfilled: "Dream fulfilled: X is back at the table."; lost: "Dream lost: X died before coming back to the table."
  - fight_beside open: "Dream: fight beside X." / "  [x] Got to know X in town (4 talks)." / "  [ ] Fight beside X (n/3)."; fulfilled: "Dream fulfilled: fought beside X."; lost to a death: "Dream lost: X died before they fought together."; lost to time: "Dream faded: never fought beside X."
- The refresh: 2.4's social_recorded handler, step c), refreshes the whole bond-and-dream block, not only the bond line, when the selected hero is in a record. A meal or a meeting can now move a dream. The dream memo is already cleared in step a). That's one dream read (about 25 ms at the cap, SYSTEMS' Bond read cost row), at most once per tick, and only when the selected hero dined or met someone.
- Greetings (history/lines.gd; greeting_facts reads the speaker's dream, as 2.2.7 does):
  - "welcome_home": while it's open and X is the listener;
  - "fight_beside": while it's open and X is the listener.
  - {name} only, 5 lines each. The longest is 69 characters with a 14-letter name.
  - welcome_home: "Good to have you back at the table, {name}." / "Eat something, {name}. You're still pale from that place." / "Your seat waited for you, {name}. So did we." / "Slow down, {name}. There's more soup where that came from." / "We kept your bowl, {name}. Nobody else got to use it."
  - fight_beside: "Take me with you next time, {name}. I mean it." / "All this talk, {name}. I'd like to see you fight for once." / "Put in a word for me, {name}? I want to be on your team." / "One day we'll stand in the same line, {name}. Soon, I hope." / "You tell a good story, {name}. I'd rather be in the next one."
  - They go with the dream kinds (after the bond kinds; before 2.2.6's roles and 2.2.3's quirks). test_lines' SLOTS gains both kinds with ["name"].

4. EVICTION (the bead's third question)
- After 2.4, meetings and meals are tier 0 and go first at the cap. Routine battles are tier 1, and other battles tier 2.
- At 2.4 and 2.5's volume estimate (a 30-hero town at pace 6: about 12 meetings, 8 meals and 10 battles an hour, itself PROVISIONAL), the ledger fills at about 330 live hours. From then on, each new record evicts the oldest tier-0 one. So tier-0 records survive for a shrinking window: about 330 hours at the fill, about 50 at 900 hours, and none from about 1,000 hours. By then 10,000 records hold only battles and up, and a new meal or meeting leaves as it arrives.
- These two dreams live for a few live hours: three meals, or four meetings and three fights. So they read exactly until the window drops under that, near 1,000 hours.
- Past that, neither opens or advances, and one open on an evicted meeting drops out of the read. That's the ceiling the meeting and meal bond points already have ("both go first at the cap", § Encounters and shared meals). It's accepted, for the same reason: the fix is a Ledger budget for tier 0 (DECISIONS item 8), which is worth filing only when a real save nears the cap.
- fight_beside's "never fought together" can't be fooled early. Routine battles evict only after every tier-0 record is gone, and then there are no meetings left to open it.

5. BALANCE ROWS (balance_table.gd, balance.tres; SYSTEMS § The dream catalogue's table; PROVISIONAL)
| Row | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `dream_welcome_meals` | 3 | Three shared meals: about three live hours home together at `meal_interval_minutes` 60. Long enough to be a choice, short enough to see in one session |
| `dream_along_meetings` | 4 | Four meetings before the wish, and four more to let it go. A neighbour or coworker pair in a 30-hero town meets about 0.27 times an hour, so about 15 live hours; in a two-hero town, about 4. It's higher than the battle counts because meetings are the most common record, and a low count would crowd the battle dreams out of the one dream slot |
| `dream_fight_beside_battles` | 3 | Reused: fight_beside's counted milestone, as for the life debt and watch_over |

6. COST
- The read is still one pass per hero, on refresh only, never per frame or per pulse. The extra per-record work is above.
- The ACC extends 2.2.7's read-cost test (test_read_cost_at_the_cap): the capped ledger gains meetings, meals and each new dream's formative records. It prints one hero's read, best of seven, beside 2.2.7's number.

DOCS (after acceptance, marked designed and not built; SYSTEMS :993-994's "Dreams on encounter and meal records wait…" changes with the code)
- SYSTEMS § The dream catalogue: the two dreams in its format, their place in the order, the two rows and the eviction note.
- GAME_SPEC: nothing. § 5 describes dreams in general.

BOUNDARIES
- #2: dream_lines through the existing hub seam, 2.4's handler step c), and greeting_facts' two kinds. Sol reviews it.
- #1: no saved state (the ADR). A disk round-trip gives the same dream.
- #3, #4: untouched.

NON-GOALS: the bead's, plus: a line when a meeting is between a fight_beside pair (2.2.6 owns the meeting kind); dream notices; any change to how tables are seated.

ORDER: after ig-m6o.2.2.7, .4 and .5. It shares history/bonds.gd, history/lines.gd and hub.gd with ig-m6o.2.2.6 and .3, so it never runs side by side with them. Either order with 2.2.6 works; my pick is after it, so greeting_facts' parameter list settles once.

title: Determinism: full-precision floats in saves; tick-exact timers
description:
WHY
Two pre-existing numeric shortcuts surfaced in the ig-gy0.2 review (high1, 2026-09-24, nits 6 and 7):
1. SaveService writes floats at JSON default precision, so a battle reloaded from a checkpoint drifts about 1e-12 HP from one never saved. A tie on equal HP could break differently after a reload. Likely root-cause fix: JSON.stringify(..., full_precision = true) in SaveService, one argument; old saves still load. Verify the Godot 4.7 signature first.
2. Timers add 0.1 s ticks with no epsilon, so a 1.0 s lock or delay clears on the 11th tick (+10%), and an 8 s cooldown takes 81 ticks. Fix it in one place: count integer ticks, or compare with an epsilon.

ACCEPTANCE
- A checkpoint reloaded through disk finishes bit-identical to the unsaved battle. Tighten the gy0.2 persistence test from 'as written' to exact.
- A 1.0 s lock clears on tick 10.
- The goldens are re-baselined on purpose (the timer fix changes them), and the diff is reviewed.
- BUILT green. Boundary #1 review (Sol).
design:
DESIGN (extra, 2026-09-25; checked against 858b45d). Two one-place fixes. The ACC's line refs were taken at 3063ca6; the current ones are below.

1. SAVES AT FULL PRECISION
- systems/save_service.gd:40 becomes JSON.stringify(payload, "\t", true, true). sort_keys stays true, as today. The signature is already proven in this engine: tests/unit/test_battle_persistence.gd:205 (_exact_json) calls it.
- The self-check right after (:45-48) parses the same text, so it checks what load will read, as today.
- It is the only production stringify of game state. The ledger lines (:238, :262) stay at default precision: they are history, not sim state.
- Load needs no change. A default-precision save written by today's build parses the same way it does now.
- The test helper _json_round_trip is now at test_battle_persistence.gd:209-210. It gains "", true, true so the tests round-trip the way SaveService will. :121 writes a file with default precision on purpose (a legacy save), so it stays.
- Other tests stringify at default precision (test_attack_move:130, test_battle_cleric:89, test_battle_job:69 and :90, test_battle_rescue:276, test_catch_up:225). Leave them unless one goes red: they check shape, not bit-equality.

2. ONE COUNT-DOWN HELPER (combat/battle/battle_simulation.gd)
   static func _count_down(value: float) -> float:
       var left: float = value - BALANCE.battle_tick_seconds
       return 0.0 if left < TICK_EPSILON else left
- It replaces maxf(x - BALANCE.battle_tick_seconds, 0.0) at six sites in two functions:
  - _expire_effects_and_cooldowns (:463-475): attack_cooldown :465, skill_cooldowns :467, item_cooldown :468, ability_lock :469, and the stun/windup/telegraph _remaining keys :473;
  - _tick_statuses: :1269.
- That is every count-down. The count-ups already use TICK_EPSILON (tick loop :144-146, objective hold :799-800, carry :1961, combo window :1413). guard_remaining is a legacy key migrated into a status at load (battle_actor.gd:146-150), so it isn't counted here.
- Why it works: ten subtractions of 0.1 from 1.0 leave about 1.4e-16, which is > 0 today, so the lock needs an 11th tick. Under the epsilon it snaps to 0 on tick 10.
- The status damage ticks don't change count. _tick_statuses already fires with ceilf(x / period - TICK_EPSILON), so a 3 s bleed ticks 3 times before and after. What changes is that the status ends one tick sooner, so shields and damage reduction end on time.
- Saved timer fields stay in seconds. That is why this uses an epsilon and not integer ticks: no schema change, no migration.

3. TESTS TO TIGHTEN (current lines)
- test_skill_kits.gd:300 (the 1 s ability lock) clears on tick 10.
- test_skill_kits.gd:467 (`advance(state, 1.3)  # the countdown lands on tick 13`) and :488 become 1.2 / tick 12.
- test_battle_simulation.gd:18 advances 1.3 s for a round-trip check. It doesn't pin a timer, so leave it unless it goes red.
- test_knockback.gd:213-222: the workaround ("The file's floats are 14 digits (ig-85w)…"). Delete it. The disk path is then held to the unbroken fight, like the exact path above it.
- gy0.4's telegraph tests allow the extra tick (high1's note above). Tighten them too.

4. GOLDENS
- tests/fixtures/battle_checkpoint_pre_skills.expected.json is re-baselined.
- .agent-results/ig-gy0.1/ has golden_capture.gd, golden_compare.py and a before/after pair. Reuse that pattern: capture at HEAD, capture with the fix, and report the clear-time shift in the notes. Expect fights to end a little sooner (every cooldown is one tick shorter).

5. SAVE SIZE
- Full precision writes up to 17 significant digits instead of 14, so the file grows. Record the bytes before and after (ACC).
- ig-7sn.10 (the periodic save, 34-35 ms) measures save cost. If both are open, measure 7sn.10 after this lands, or its number goes stale.

6. DOCS: SYSTEMS.md :21, the 0.1-second tick paragraph, gains one sentence: a timer of t seconds ends on tick t / 0.1. (game-designer)

ORDER: every combat bead after this one measures on fixed timers, so running it early means one re-baseline instead of several. It touches battle_simulation.gd, so it runs alone there (not beside ig-gy0.5 or ig-gy0.6).

BOUNDARIES
- #1: the save text changes precision only; there are no new keys, and a legacy save still loads. Sol reviews it.
- #4: both resolve paths go through the same advance, so both get the fix at once. The digests move on purpose.
- #2, #3 untouched.
